title: Are QVC and HSN Destined to Die?
summary: This article questions the future of home shopping networks QVC and HSN in an era dominated by online retail and changing consumer preferences. Despite declining stock prices and revenue, the author highlights QVC's efforts, including a merger with HSN, improved online sales, flexible payment options, and strong customer service, suggesting these strategies might help them survive. The piece ultimately expresses hope for their continued existence.

title: eBay is more like the NYSE than Amazon, says Intercontinental Exchange CEO Jeffrey Sprecher
summary: Jeffrey Sprecher, CEO of Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), argued that eBay, an e-commerce giant, more closely resembles the New York Stock Exchange than Amazon. He suggested eBay should be viewed as a 25-year-old cash market for collectible goods, emphasizing business model similarities like matching buyers and sellers, data collection, and third-party partnerships. This perspective emerged as ICE clarified its discussions with eBay, which it ultimately ceased pursuing for strategic opportunities.

title: Uber is ready to join the FANG camp, analyst says after earnings
summary: Following its latest earnings report, an analyst suggested that Uber Technologies Inc. is ready to join the ranks of major internet companies like Facebook, Amazon, Netflix, and Google. RBC Capital Markets analyst Mark Mahaney proposed the acronym FANGU, adding Uber, as the company works towards profitability and leverages its scale. This optimism led to an 8% increase in Uber's stock price on Friday morning.

title: Matt Desch, CEO of Iridium Communications, Named to 2020 Wash100 for Driving Revenue, Tech Advancement
summary: Matt Desch, CEO of Iridium Communications, has been inducted into the 2020 Wash100 Award for his continuous efforts in driving revenue and advancing satellite, IoT, and cloud technologies. This marks his sixth consecutive Wash100 award, highlighting his significant impact on the government contracting sector through initiatives like Iridium's L-band broadband service, partnerships with Satelles and Amazon Web Services, and authorization for GMDSS satellite services. His leadership has led to substantial growth for Iridium, including a 12 percent revenue increase in Q1 2019 and a 25 percent rise in commercial IoT data subscribers.

title: Are video games a worthwhile investment?
summary: Raj Lala, CEO of Evolve ETFs, discusses the investment potential of the video game industry, explaining why he launched the HERO ETF to provide exposure to major gaming companies. He highlights the significant evolution of the industry's revenue model beyond simple sales, citing in-app purchases, subscriptions, and esports as key drivers. Lala emphasizes that gaming fits into Evolve's strategy of investing in disruptive technologies that will shape the future and advises financial advisors to understand the full ecosystem of the market.

title: Amazon’s Total Stock-based Compensation Expense, by Quarter
summary: This article analyzes Amazon's total stock-based compensation expense by quarter from 1998, highlighting significant increases, such as $1,840 million in Q4 2019, a 29.9% year-over-year rise. It notes Amazon's substantial workforce of approximately 798,000 employees as of December 2019 and provides background on Amazon's history and key offerings.

title: Tyler Technologies Tops $1B in Annual Revenue for First Time
summary: Tyler Technologies announced its annual revenue surpassed $1 billion for the first time in 2019, reaching $1.068 billion, a 16.2 percent increase from 2018. The company, a leading provider of public sector software, expects continued double-digit growth and aims for $2 billion in annual revenue, supported by its Connected Communities vision and strategic investments in cloud technologies and acquisitions.

title: Oracle’s Larry Ellison makes friends with his enemy’s enemy, hosting a fundraiser for President Trump
summary: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison is hosting a fundraiser for President Donald Trump, aligning with a shared adversary of Amazon and its CEO Jeff Bezos. Ellison's company has a fierce rivalry with Amazon's cloud computing wing, and Trump has openly expressed a desire to "screw Amazon." This move places Ellison among a few Silicon Valley figures who have publicly supported Trump, despite potential backlash from the tech industry.

title: How Blackstone became the world’s biggest corporate landlord
summary: Blackstone has grown to become the world's largest corporate landlord, accumulating $325 billion in real estate assets through strategic investments since going public in 2007. The firm employs both "opportunistic" (BREP) and "Core+" (BREIT) funds, focusing on distressed properties and stable rental income, respectively, while increasingly targeting warehouses in "last-mile infill" areas due to the e-commerce boom. Its ability to raise massive funds allows it to make large-scale deals with limited competition, shaping its investment strategy around fast-growing "knowledge centers."

title: This Growth ETF Continues Winning
summary: The article discusses the continued outperformance of growth stocks over value stocks in early 2020, driven by technology and consumer discretionary sectors. It highlights the SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 Growth ETF (SPYG) as a strong performer, noting its impressive year-to-date gains compared to the broader S&P 500 and S&P 500 Value Index. The piece also contrasts growth and value investing strategies and mentions significant inflows into SPYG.

title: Israeli VC Firm Grove Ventures Closes $120M Fund For Deep Tech Startups
summary: Israeli VC firm Grove Ventures announced the closure of its Grove Ventures II Fund (Grove II), raising $120 million to invest in early-stage, deep tech startups in Israel targeting European and US markets. The fund, which was oversubscribed, focuses on companies developing "hard-to-replicate solutions" across various sectors, led by serial entrepreneur Dov Moran. Grove Ventures aims to empower deep tech entrepreneurs to build international companies and address significant industry challenges with innovative technology.

title: Franklin-Legg Mason combo could produce nontransparent ETF powerhouse
summary: The pending merger of Franklin Resources and Legg Mason, while having a relatively small combined ETF asset base, could position them as a significant player in the nontransparent ETF space. This potential stems from Legg Mason's majority stake in Precidian Investments, a company licensing nontransparent ETF structures, which could give the merged entity a first-mover advantage as these new fund types are expected to launch soon. Nontransparent ETFs offer a new avenue for active mutual fund managers to enter the ETF market with potential benefits like lower costs and greater tax efficiency.

title: Piedmont Pays $396M for Dallas Galleria Office Towers
summary: Piedmont Office Realty Trust acquired the three distinctive Galleria office towers in Dallas for $396 million, marking the largest Dallas-Fort Worth office sale of the year. The transaction included over 1.4 million square feet of Class A office space, associated parking garages, and a 1.9-acre land parcel. This acquisition means Piedmont now owns the entire Galleria portfolio in Dallas, having previously acquired Galleria properties in Atlanta.

title: Beyond ESG: How Individuals Can Influence Corporations
summary: This article discusses how individuals can influence corporations beyond traditional ESG investing by leveraging their consumer choices, employment decisions, and advocacy. It highlights the rise of stakeholder capitalism and provides examples of how customers, employees, suppliers, communities, and shareholders have successfully pressured companies to adopt more responsible practices, leading to positive corporate behavior and potentially superior stock returns.

title: Expedia cuts 3,000 jobs, including 500 at new Seattle HQ — read the internal email to employees
summary: Expedia Group is laying off 3,000 employees, or 12 percent of its workforce, including 500 at its new Seattle headquarters, as part of an effort to "streamline and focus" the company under chairman Barry Diller. These cuts follow the ouster of the CEO and CFO and a commitment to address an "unhealthy and undisciplined" growth strategy, aiming for $300 to $500 million in annual cost savings. The layoffs are not linked to the coronavirus outbreak, though the company expects related profit reductions and will incur $135 million to $185 million in pre-tax charges this year.

title: Checkup for $30, Teeth Cleaning $25: Walmart Gets Into Health Care
summary: Walmart is entering the healthcare market by offering low-cost medical services such as $30 checkups and $25 teeth cleanings in its new Walmart Health centers. This initiative aims to capture a share of the $3.6 trillion health spending by leveraging its large customer base and providing accessible care, even for those without insurance. The retail giant's move positions it as a competitor to existing healthcare providers like CVS and Amazon in communities nationwide.

title: Comcast acquires free video streaming service Xumo
summary: Comcast announced its acquisition of Xumo, a free, ad-supported streaming service, positioning itself to compete in the growing ad-supported streaming market. This strategic move comes ahead of NBCUniversal's launch of its own streaming service, Peacock, which will also offer free, ad-supported content. The acquisition highlights the increasing trend of media companies investing in streaming services as consumers shift away from traditional pay TV.

title: Kraft Heinz invests in $110m Series B for cloud retail robotics startup Fabric
summary: Kraft Heinz, through its venture arm Evolv Ventures, invested in a $110 million Series B round for the cloud retail robotics startup Fabric. Fabric's technology provides automated fulfillment solutions for retailers facing increasing demand for fast e-commerce delivery. The funding will support Fabric's US expansion, aiming to address the challenges retailers face in efficient order fulfillment.

title: Prudential buys local Amazon distribution hub
summary: PGIM Real Estate, a branch of Prudential, has acquired a new Amazon distribution hub located in Antioch, Nashville. This 517,500-square-foot industrial building was developed speculatively, indicating strong confidence in the demand for industrial space in the Nashville market. Amazon is the current tenant, leasing the facility.

title: Walmart is developing a membership program to rival Amazon Prime
summary: Walmart Inc. is developing a new paid membership program called Walmart+ to compete directly with Amazon Prime. This service will expand on Walmart's existing grocery-delivery subscription and aims to attract and retain shoppers who might otherwise turn to Amazon. The initiative highlights Walmart's efforts to counter Amazon's dominance in online retail and customer loyalty.

title: Building operators eager for coronavirus info as one Seattle tower closed Monday
summary: F5 Tower in Seattle was closed for one day due to coronavirus concerns after an employee had contact with someone who tested positive for the virus. This closure highlights the growing concern among building operators seeking information as authorities anticipate an increase in cases.

title: HPE Confirms Discover Conference Still On, Cancels ‘Most’ Events Through April
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has decided to proceed with its annual Discover Las Vegas and Discover More London conferences, despite canceling or postponing most other events through April due to coronavirus concerns. Partners have expressed support for HPE's decision, emphasizing the need to continue business while taking prudent precautions. The company plans to shift resources to digital engagement for customers and partners.

title: Target's online sales surge as shoppers opt for pick up, delivery
summary: Target announced a 20% surge in digital sales, driven by increased use of its pick-up and delivery services. The retailer plans to expand its online offerings to include perishables like milk, wine, and beer for drive-up pickup, and will also experiment with even smaller store formats. Target also addressed concerns regarding the coronavirus, stating its impact on performance is not notable, but they are preparing for potential supply chain delays.

title: Carlyle Group’s $1.4 Billion Folly: Inside The Biggest Buyout Loss In Washington, D.C. Firm’s 33-Year History
summary: Carlyle Group's $1.4 billion equity investment in Acosta was completely wiped out, marking the biggest buyout loss in the firm's 33-year history. Acosta, a food broker, faced declining revenues due to shifting consumer preferences and aggressive cost-cutting by clients, leading to a bankruptcy filing despite Carlyle's efforts. The article highlights the growing trend of private equity firms trading companies among themselves and the risks associated with high debt levels in such deals.

title: Lawmakers ask Amazon, EBay to crack down on counterfeit sales
summary: House lawmakers are urging Amazon.com Inc. and EBay Inc. to take stronger action against third-party vendors selling fake, stolen, or unsafe goods on their platforms. The bipartisan request follows concerns about organized retail crime and counterfeit products, especially those originating from China. Both Amazon and EBay executives testified that they are investing in tools and supporting law enforcement to combat fraudulent listings.

title: Theme Lab: A Look Inside An Amazon Fulfillment Center
summary: This article details a "Theme Lab" visit to an Amazon Fulfillment Center, showcasing how robotics, IoT, AI, and human labor collaborate in the Stowing, Picking, Packing, and Shipping phases. It highlights the critical synergistic roles of these technologies and human expertise in achieving efficiency in e-commerce fulfillment. The article concludes by discussing related ETFs that track these disruptive technologies.

title: Watch Jessica Alba Put Her Product Prowess to the Test in ELLE's Beauty Haul
summary: Jessica Alba, co-founder of The Honest Company and Honest Beauty, takes on ELLE's "Beauty Haul" challenge. She demonstrates her clean beauty routine, shopping for products with a $150 budget and applying a full face of makeup in under 30 minutes. Alba highlights her favorite Honest Beauty products and explains her approach to clean beauty, emphasizing natural ingredients and avoiding fragrances.

title: Alliance Data: Is Three a Charm with a New CEO?
summary: Alliance Data, a private label credit card company, is facing significant challenges, including a ten-year stock low and rising charge-off rates, as a new CEO, Ralph Andretta, takes the helm. The article highlights the company's reliance on proprietary credit scores instead of FICO, a lack of innovation compared to competitors like Synchrony, and the need for a strategy to convert weaker credit accounts to branded network cards. The new CEO has initiated a "listening tour" to develop a strategic plan for the struggling firm.

title: Costco sales surge 11% as coronavirus fear prompts stockpiling
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported an 11% surge in sales due to customer stockpiling of essentials amid coronavirus fears, forcing frequent replenishment of items. The company also exceeded holiday-quarter expectations with a 28% increase in e-commerce sales and strong membership revenue, while acknowledging the continued rise in traffic into March. Analyst Garrett Nelson of CFRA Research considers Costco a primary beneficiary of coronavirus-related consumer stockpiling.

title: Champion Jumps to Amazon From Target for Discount C9 Brand
summary: Champion, owned by Hanesbrands Inc., has moved its C9 apparel line to Amazon.com Inc. after its agreement with Target Corp. ended. Amazon has entered into a two-year deal to offer the C9 line, marking the first time C9 will be available globally.

title: Burlington Stores walks away from e-commerce
summary: Burlington Stores is winding down its e-commerce operations, citing the difficulty of making a profit on low-priced items online, the challenge of replicating the "treasure hunt" experience digitally, and the strong performance of its physical stores. This decision comes despite the growth of e-commerce in other retail sectors, as Burlington focuses its resources on brick-and-mortar growth. The move sparks debate among experts about its long-term implications for the off-price retailer.

title: NetApp sinks claws into Talon Storage
summary: NetApp has acquired Talon Storage, a company specializing in caching software that connects branch offices to public cloud file servers. The acquisition aims to provide a unified footprint for unstructured data, enabling seamless access for users regardless of their geographical location. Talon's FAST software will allow NetApp to offer an indirect remote office/branch office (ROBO) presence without requiring on-premises NetApp filers.

title: HanesBrands Launches Popular C9 Champion Brand With Amazon in Multiyear Exclusive Agreement
summary: HanesBrands has launched its popular C9 Champion performance athleticwear exclusively on Amazon Fashion worldwide through a multiyear agreement. The value-priced line, which includes activewear, innerwear, and accessories for the whole family, aims to reach a broader global consumer base and complement the existing mainline Champion brand on Amazon.

title: Costco tells office workers
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is requiring its head office employees in Issaquah to report to work, despite public health requests to allow remote work. CEO W. Craig Jelinek stated that this decision is based on equity and fairness, as the majority of Costco employees work in stores and warehouses and do not have the option to work from home. This contrasts with companies like Amazon and Microsoft, which have allowed many office workers to work remotely amid coronavirus concerns.

title: Starbucks stores may go drive-thru only or limit seating to address coronavirus concerns
summary: Starbucks announced that some of its stores in the U.S. and Canada might transition to drive-thru only or limit seating to address concerns about the coronavirus pandemic. The company plans to make these decisions on a store-by-store basis and may temporarily close stores as a last resort. Starbucks has also expanded catastrophe pay for employees affected by the virus, and its shares have significantly dropped amid the outbreak.

title: Zero-Day Bug In Verisign And IaaS Services Allowed Registering of Malicious Domains With Homoglyph
summary: A zero-day bug found in Verisign and various IaaS services allowed cybercriminals to register malicious domains using homoglyphs, making them appear visually identical to legitimate sites. A researcher exposed the flaw, which had been actively exploited since 2017, and successfully registered imposter domains for major companies. While Verisign and Amazon have implemented mitigations, other services have yet to address the vulnerability.

title: Synchrony Financial agrees to 10-year deal to stay in Kettering
summary: Synchrony Financial, a major employer in Kettering, has secured a 10-year agreement to remain in the Kettering Business Park. The city extended a $675,000 Economic Development Incentive Grant for a five-year lease with a five-year option, with the company committing to maintain 1,900 full-time equivalent positions. This deal highlights Synchrony's significance to the local economy and the city's efforts to retain key businesses.

title: Bill Gates steps down from Microsoft board
summary: Bill Gates announced he is stepping down from the boards of Microsoft and Berkshire Hathaway to dedicate more time to philanthropy, focusing on global health, education, and climate change through the Gates Foundation. He will continue to serve as a technology advisor to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Gates, who co-founded Microsoft in 1975, remains one of the world's richest individuals.

title: WeRide resumes robotaxi service in China after COVID-19
summary: WeRide, an L4 AV smart mobility company based in Guangzhou, China, has resumed its robotaxi service with strict precautions after COVID-19. The company has implemented measures such as nucleic acid tests for safety drivers, daily health checks, mandatory mask-wearing, and vehicle sanitization after every two trips to ensure the safety of riders and drivers. WeRide, which partners with Amazon's AWS, emphasizes its R&D and claims to have one of the largest autonomous vehicle fleets among Chinese startups, having covered over 1,150,000 kilometers.

title: Amazon to hire 100,000 workers as online orders surge on coronavirus worries
summary: Amazon.com Inc announced plans to hire 100,000 warehouse and delivery workers in the United States to manage a significant increase in online orders due to the coronavirus outbreak. The company will also add $2 to its minimum $15 per hour wage for U.S. workers through April, an initiative expected to cost over $350 million across North America and Europe. Other retailers are also seeking new hires as consumers shift to online shopping and stock up on essential goods.

title: Canadian Solar secures €55m financing to build 151MW solar projects in Italy
summary: Canadian Solar has secured €55m ($60.6m) in financing from Intesa Sanpaolo for the construction of a 151MW portfolio of 12 solar projects in Italy. These projects, located in Sicily, Apulia, and Lazio, are expected to generate 287GWh of clean energy annually and are among the country's first subsidy-free utility-scale solar plants. The company also recently signed a PPA with Amazon for its Gunnedah solar plant in Australia.

title: Coconut water is the pandemic’s newest shortage
summary: Amid coronavirus concerns, sales of coconut water, particularly from Vita Coco, have surged significantly across the U.S., depleting typical stockpiles and straining supply chains. While other bottled waters are also in high demand, this trend raises concerns about potential supply disruptions if borders close, especially since coconuts are not grown in the US.

title: Broadcom Asserts Patents Covering ‘Crucial Aspects’ of Netflix Content Delivery
summary: Broadcom Corporation has filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Netflix, Inc. in the Central District of California, alleging that Netflix's streaming service infringes on nine of Broadcom's U.S. patents. The patents cover technologies crucial for reliable content delivery, efficient server use, and video encoding. Broadcom claims Netflix's infringement has harmed its set-top box business by drawing consumers away from cable television.

title: Reese Witherspoon’s Draper James and Land’s End Dive Into Swimwear
summary: Reese Witherspoon’s Draper James brand partnered with Land's End to launch a limited-edition women's swimwear collection. The collaboration combines Draper James' signature Southern-inspired prints with Land’s End's swim expertise, offering 23 pieces in sizes XS-3X. A portion of the proceeds from the collection will be donated to Girls Inc.

title: Marcus Corp. operates cinemas, hotels and restaurants. Here's how it's weathering the coronavirus pandemic.
summary: Marcus Corp., encompassing hotels and movie theaters, has been severely impacted by the coronavirus pandemic. CEO Greg Marcus is focused on financially preserving the company and supporting laid-off employees while navigating the unprecedented economic shock. Despite the challenges, Marcus believes the company's conservative financial approach will help it survive until business returns to normal.

title: Conduent Collaborates with Amazon Web Services to Help Government Agencies Scale Their COVID-19 Response
summary: Conduent announced that its Maven disease surveillance platform, configured for COVID-19 case management, patient outreach, and contact tracing visualization, is now available on Amazon Web Services (AWS). To support public health agencies, Conduent is waiving the software license fee for the Maven COVID-19 module through June 30, 2020, for qualified state and territorial-level agencies. This collaboration enables rapid and scalable deployment of critical tools to help "flatten the curve" by digitizing contact tracing and reporting.

title: Chipotle joins Starbucks, Amazon with coronavirus pay bump
summary: Chipotle announced a 10 percent pay increase for its hourly employees working between March 16 and April 12, joining companies like Starbucks and Amazon in providing additional compensation during the coronavirus pandemic. This initiative, along with updated emergency benefits, aims to show appreciation for workers during a time when many businesses are shifting to takeout or delivery-only operations. Other companies, including Albertsons, Kroger, Walmart, and McDonald's, are also offering similar support to their employees.

title: Maintaining a high-speed connection: A new playbook for cable growth
summary: This article outlines strategies for the cable industry to maintain growth, focusing on becoming a digital-first enterprise, doubling down on B2B growth, and becoming a leading smart-home player. It highlights the industry's strong current position while addressing looming long-term challenges such as regulatory risks and 5G competition. The authors emphasize the importance of strategic shifts to avoid becoming a "dumb pipe" and to continue increasing the value of customer relationships.

title: Social Media Moves to New Era of Growth
summary: Social media platforms are entering a new era of growth, shifting focus from user acquisition to maximizing revenue per user through targeted advertising and innovative technologies. New avenues like social commerce and AR/VR are being explored to diversify revenue streams. This evolution includes in-app purchases, live-streaming commerce, and augmented reality experiences to further engage users and drive monetization.

title: DoorDash Starts Delivering Toilet Paper and Other Groceries
summary: DoorDash, the largest food delivery app in the U.S., is expanding its services to include deliveries from convenience stores like 7-Eleven and Wawa. This accelerated rollout, prompted by the coronavirus pandemic, allows customers to order essential goods such as toilet paper and other packaged items. The company currently has over 1,800 convenience stores listed on its app across the U.S.

title: Home Depot Halts Sales of N95 Masks Amid Shortage, Company Says (Published 2020)
summary: Home Depot has halted sales of N95 masks at all of its North American stores and redirected them to healthcare providers and emergency responders due to the coronavirus pandemic. Other retailers like Lowe's and Target have also taken similar actions, while 3M, a mask manufacturer, has expressed concern over retailers continuing to sell protective gear. The move aims to address the critical shortage of personal protective equipment for frontline workers.

title: Jessica Alba's The Honest Company Has Donated 3 Million Diapers To Help Families In Need
summary: Jessica Alba's The Honest Company has donated three million diapers, 20,000 wipes, and 20,000 personal care products to families in need during the coronavirus pandemic. Alba emphasized that these donations address the critical needs of families facing difficult choices between essentials like diapers and food. Her husband, Cash Warren, also contributed through his company, Pair of Thieves, by donating profits to purchase relief supplies and masks for front-line workers.

title: EBay pledges $100M to help small businesses move online
summary: eBay has launched its "Up & Running" accelerator program, investing $100 million to help North American small businesses without an online presence transition to e-commerce. The program offers free basic eBay stores for three months, waived selling fees for up to 500 items, and provides marketing tools, discounted shipping, and educational resources. This initiative responds to the increased focus on e-commerce due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with 70% of small businesses reportedly lacking an online presence before the outbreak.

title: Infographic: Retailers’ cage-free egg pledges
summary: U.S. egg producers are converting to cage-free systems as North American retailers commit to sourcing only cage-free eggs. While some retailers already exclusively sell cage-free eggs, many others, including major grocery chains, are still in transition, with most aiming for completion by 2025 or 2026. This shift is also driven by new laws in several U.S. states requiring cage-free egg production and sales.

title: Uber Aids Idled Rideshare Drivers With Job Listings
summary: Uber is launching "Work Hub," an initiative to connect its rideshare drivers, who are experiencing diminished income due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with alternative job listings. These opportunities include roles within Uber, such as Uber Freight or Uber Eats, and with other companies like Domino’s, Shipt, and CareGuide, covering positions in food production, warehousing, and customer service. The company also encouraged drivers to join Uber Eats, which has seen increased demand, and is contributing to a Restaurant Employee Relief Fund.

title: SoFi acquires banking tech firm Galileo for $1.2 billion
summary: SoFi announced its acquisition of Galileo, a banking tech firm that powers companies like Robinhood and Chime, for $1.2 billion. The deal involves $875 million in SoFi shares, $75 million in cash, and $250 million in debt financing. SoFi plans to operate Galileo as an independent entity, providing white-label technology services globally, despite both companies recently experiencing turbulence.

title: BlackBerry uncovers hacker tools that it says opened data servers for a decade
summary: BlackBerry has released a report detailing how five separate groups linked to the Chinese government have been targeting Linux systems for a decade. These hackers have used novel techniques, including disguising malicious tools as advertising software, to exfiltrate vast amounts of data from servers. The report highlights a significant blind spot in cybersecurity, as Linux powers critical global infrastructure like stock exchanges and major cloud services.

title: Piper Sandler Completes 39th Semi-Annual Generation Z Survey of 5,200 U.S. Teens
summary: Piper Sandler completed its 39th semi-annual "Taking Stock With Teens" survey, revealing a 13% year-over-year decrease in self-reported teen spending to $2,300, the lowest since fall 2011, largely influenced by the COVID-19 pandemic. The survey of 5,200 U.S. teens highlighted food as the top spending priority and environmental concerns as the primary social/political issue, with "Coronavirus" ranking second. Key trends include Amazon's dominance in e-commerce, a significant drop in female cosmetic spending, and the continued popularity of Nike and lululemon in fashion, alongside TikTok's debut as a major social media platform.

title: Simply Good Foods builds inventories as Covid-19 boosts e-commerce sales
summary: Simply Good Foods Co. is increasing its inventory levels and reallocating marketing spend in response to altered consumer purchasing behavior caused by Covid-19, which has significantly boosted e-commerce sales. The company is moving from five-to-six weeks of stock to eight-to-ten weeks for its top SKUs to ensure safety stock and meet increased online demand for brands like Quest Nutrition and Atkins Nutritionals. This shift is expected to have a short-term impact of US$10-15m on cash flow, but the company remains confident in its supply chain.

title: Amazon stops accepting new online grocery customers amid surging demand
summary: Amazon is implementing new measures to manage surging online grocery demand, including placing new customers on a waitlist and shortening Whole Foods' public hours to prioritize online orders. The company is actively increasing capacity by hiring additional workers and transitioning a new store into an online order warehouse. Despite these efforts, Amazon acknowledges that high demand and social distancing may continue to make delivery windows challenging for customers.

title: Amazon Revenue by Year, Worldwide (In US$ Millions)
summary: This article provides a historical overview of Amazon's worldwide annual revenue from 1996 to 2019, highlighting its growth trajectory. It notes Amazon's achievement of reaching $100 billion in annual sales in just 21 years and its record revenue of $280,522 million in 2019. The article also includes a brief company profile of Amazon.com, Inc.

title: Amazon Total Operating Expenses by Quarter
summary: This article details Amazon's total operating expenses by quarter from Q1 1997 to Q4 2019, highlighting key growth periods and record highs. It notes that Amazon's operating expenses reached a record $83,558 million in Q4 2019, representing 95.6% of its total revenue, and provides context on the company's financial growth and history.

title: Pfizer’s digital chief: Technology can speed the race to a COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Lidia Fonseca, Pfizer's Chief Digital and Technology Officer, is leveraging technology to support the company's race for a COVID-19 vaccine, enabling remote work for thousands of employees and facilitating data sharing and collaboration with other biopharmaceutical companies. Her team built a "scientific cloud" on Amazon Web Services to centralize Pfizer's previously siloed data, dramatically increasing its value for research. Fonseca emphasizes technology's role in empowering scientists with information to make informed decisions and accelerate the development of life-changing breakthroughs.

title: 2019 Letter to Shareholders
summary: Jeff Bezos's 2019 Letter to Shareholders details Amazon's response to the COVID-19 crisis, highlighting efforts to support customers and employees, including safety measures, wage increases, job creation, and combating price gouging. The letter also covers Amazon's broader initiatives beyond COVID-19, such as The Climate Pledge for carbon neutrality and significant investments in job creation, employee training, and community programs. It contrasts the 2019 situation with Amazon's founding principles from the 1997 shareholder letter, emphasizing long-term focus and customer obsession.

title: Watch FAT Brands CEO on How The Coronavirus Impacted Business
summary: FAT Brands CEO, Andy Wiederhorn, discusses the varied impact of the coronavirus pandemic on his company's 400 franchised restaurants across eight different brands. He highlights the shift to delivery for burger and chicken restaurants, while casual dining and steak houses experienced significant declines. Wiederhorn also addresses concerns about food supply chains, the need for government support for small businesses, and anticipated changes in consumer behavior and restaurant operations post-pandemic.

title: Exclusive: Amazon deploys thermal cameras at warehouses to scan for fevers faster
summary: Amazon.com Inc has begun using thermal cameras at its warehouses to more quickly screen workers for fevers, a key symptom of the coronavirus. This represents an effort to maintain operations and contain the virus' spread without fully closing warehouses, a move that comes amid reports of infections at over 50 U.S. facilities and calls from unions to close buildings. The camera systems, which are faster and require less contact than forehead thermometers, are being deployed in warehouses near Los Angeles and Seattle, and at Whole Foods stores.

title: Large Cap Tech Stocks Continue to Throw Their Weight Around
summary: Large-cap tech stocks, particularly those in the Nasdaq 100, are demonstrating resilience and leading recovery efforts in capital markets amidst the coronavirus pandemic. Companies like Amazon and Microsoft are driving this trend, with the Nasdaq 100 showing a 1% year-to-date gain compared to the S&P 500's 11% decline. Investors can gain exposure through ETFs like FTEC, XLK, and RWLS, which offers a large-cap over small-cap strategy.

title: Wayfair Appoints Jim Miller as Chief Technology Officer
summary: Wayfair Inc. has appointed Jim Miller as its permanent Chief Technology Officer, a role he had held on an interim basis since August 2019. Miller, with extensive experience from Google, Cisco, and Amazon, will lead Wayfair's global tech operations and engineering team. He will also step down from Wayfair's board, a position he held for four years.

title: Geared Consumer Discretionary ETFs For An Altered Retail Landscape
summary: This article discusses how the COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered the retail landscape, impacting traditional retailers while boosting e-commerce giants like Amazon. It examines two leveraged ETFs, Direxion Daily Consumer Discretionary Bull 3X Shares (WANT) and Direxion Daily Consumer Discretionary Bear 3X Shares (PASS), as ways for active traders to play these trends. The article highlights that while consumer discretionary spending is projected to decline, WANT still offers appeal due to its significant Amazon exposure, while PASS benefits from the broader retail downturn.

title: Metlife buys giant Amazon fulfillment center in Shakopee
summary: Metlife has purchased an 860,000-square-foot Amazon fulfillment center in Shakopee, Minnesota, for $118 million. This distribution center was Amazon's initial major investment in the southwest metro area. The sale reflects significant activity in the commercial real estate market, with related articles discussing other large property deals.

title: Spotting A Winner Among Internet ETFs
summary: The article highlights the Global Internet Giants ETF (OGIG) as a strong performer among Internet ETFs, particularly due to the "staying in" theme accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. OGIG, with major holdings like Amazon, Alibaba, and Tencent, focuses on internet and e-commerce sectors with quality and growth potential. The fund benefits from the rapid shift to online retail and work-from-home trends, suggesting significant long-term growth potential.

title: Coronavirus pandemic and online media consumption: settling into the New Normal
summary: This article discusses how online media consumption in Europe has begun to level off after an initial surge during the early stages of the coronavirus pandemic lockdown. It highlights that the "new normal" has settled in, with some categories that saw initial growth, such as General News, Instant Messaging, Food/Groceries Retail, and Entertainment, now showing signs of fatigue as activity stabilizes. The piece also includes a timeline of key pandemic events in Europe leading up to the lockdowns.

title: IZEA Announces Twitch Influencer Marketing Workflow Support in IZEAx Unity Suite
summary: IZEA Worldwide, Inc. has launched beta support for Twitch influencer marketing workflows within its IZEAx Unity Suite, allowing marketers to integrate Twitch live stream sponsorships into their campaigns. This new feature enables standalone Twitch sponsorships or their inclusion in broader multi-channel initiatives, leveraging the platform's increased viewership due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The workflow was developed in collaboration with a Fortune 500 company and aims to connect brands with Twitch's captive audience, who show a higher propensity to purchase non-essential products.

title: Ford’s Lincoln And Rivian Cancel Electric SUV Plans, Citing COVID-19 Impact
summary: Lincoln, Ford's luxury brand, has canceled an electric SUV it planned to develop with startup partner Rivian, citing the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Although other collaborations between Ford and Rivian will continue, this specific project was halted due to difficulties exacerbated by the pandemic, including remote work challenges and delayed vehicle production. This decision comes as Ford invests heavily in electrification, but the future demand for electric vehicles remains uncertain given the collapse of the oil market and changes in regulatory incentives.

title: Build-A-Bear introduces online activity program
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop launched "Workshop Wednesdays," an online program providing creative activities and entertainment for families during the COVID-19 pandemic. The initiative includes new weekly activities, enhanced online Bear Builder features, and access to Build-A-Bear Radio and YouTube content. This move aims to maintain engagement with its core audience while physical stores are closed, as the toy industry faces challenges and Build-A-Bear itself furloughed staff due to the pandemic's impact.

title: Value Tilt – Don’t Give Up on Your Small-Cap Value Strategy
summary: This article argues against giving up on a small-cap value investing strategy despite recent underperformance. The author, Dr. Jim Dahle, explains the rationale behind factor investing in small value stocks, including risk and behavioral biases, and presents data indicating historical long-term outperformance. He discusses why now, given the undervaluation and underperformance of small-cap value, is a good time to stick with or even implement such a tilt, cautioning that it is a long-term decision.

title: C3 AI Accelerates AI Application Development on AWS by 26X
summary: This report details how the C3 AI Platform significantly reduces the complexity and time required to develop enterprise AI applications on AWS, accelerating development by a factor of 26x. It compares using only AWS native services versus incorporating the C3 AI Platform, highlighting the platform's ability to simplify infrastructure provisioning and reduce coding needs. The report, written by an independent system integrator, showcases the C3 AI Platform's effectiveness in increasing developer productivity and speeding up deployment.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | ICE Partners With Amazon, 3M to Identify Counterfeit Coronavirus Gear
summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is partnering with companies including 3M Co., Amazon.com Inc., and Pfizer Inc. to combat the influx of counterfeit coronavirus-related medical gear. ICE's intellectual-property unit announced this collaboration to identify suspicious shipments and remove fraudulent online listings. The companies have agreed to share information and best practices with the agency to curtail the trade of counterfeit masks, tests, and other equipment.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market Reports Pandemic Revenue Gains
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market Inc. reported a 16% year-over-year gain in net sales and a 10.6% boost in comparable-store sales for Q1 2020, largely driven by increased consumer demand during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company's net income rose to $92 million, a 64% increase, despite higher expenses due to increased worker pay, bonuses, and e-commerce fees. Sprouts' CFO noted uncertainty regarding future consumer behavior and market visibility for the remainder of 2020.

title: Shopify surges past Royal Bank for title of most valuable company in Canada
summary: Shopify Inc. has surpassed the Royal Bank of Canada to become the most valuable company in Canada, with its market capitalization exceeding $121 billion. The e-commerce firm's shares surged due to booming demand for its online selling platform during the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to higher-than-expected revenue in the first quarter of 2020. Despite a net loss, the company reported an adjusted profit and is working to support businesses moving online, although analysts express concerns about its valuation.

title: Middletown battery plant to close, cutting 200 jobs
summary: Clarios, a battery assembly plant in Middletown, will close in November 2020, resulting in the loss of about 200 jobs. The company, a global leader in lead-acid automotive batteries, will keep its distribution center in Middletown open and plans to modernize its U.S. operations and streamline manufacturing. This closure highlights the shift towards electric vehicles that use lithium-ion batteries, impacting the lead-acid battery market.

title: Target in talks to boost its same-day delivery ambitions by buying pieces of startup Deliv
summary: Target is acquiring technology assets from the same-day delivery service Deliv to bolster its same-day delivery capabilities and compete with rivals like Amazon and Walmart. The acquisition focuses on Deliv's technology for pooling multiple orders and routing them efficiently, and includes hiring Deliv's CEO and a subset of its team, as Deliv is in the process of shutting down operations. This move follows Target's previous acquisition of Shipt in 2017 to enhance its fast delivery services.

title: Hello Products Takes Natural Oral Care Mainstream
summary: Hello Products, a natural oral care brand recently acquired by Colgate-Palmolive, is expanding its offerings including a new line of CBD-infused products in Ulta Beauty stores. Despite the pandemic, the company has maintained growth in sales and operations, emphasizing self-care and natural ingredients. Hello Products aims to make natural, affordable, and effective oral care accessible to a wide range of consumers, appealing especially to younger demographics with its "naturally friendly" positioning.

title: News Outlets Want More Advertisers to Act Like Burger King (Published 2020)
summary: News organizations want more advertisers to emulate Burger King, which continued to run ads near coronavirus coverage by focusing its message on contactless delivery. Many companies used "blacklisting" to avoid articles with COVID-19 related terms, costing publishers significant revenue, while Burger King saw it as an opportunity to play a role in the crisis. This practice has had a devastating effect on ad-dependent news organizations during the pandemic.

title: Amid COVID-19, an E-Commerce World Arrives
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the growth of e-commerce, with several related ETFs, including the Global X E-commerce ETF (NasdaqGM: EBIZ), reaching record highs. The article highlights how consumer behavior shifts are driving this trend and suggests that e-commerce will continue to be a significant force in retail. EBIZ is noted for its broader e-commerce ecosystem exposure compared to rivals heavily reliant on Amazon.com.

title: Amazon to pay $11M to settle security search pay claim
summary: Amazon has agreed to pay $11 million to settle a class-action lawsuit from California workers who alleged they were not paid for time spent during mandatory security searches. The lawsuit claimed Amazon violated California labor laws by not compensating hourly warehouse workers for up to 30 minutes spent on security checks after clocking out. This settlement follows similar rulings and settlements against other companies in California regarding off-the-clock security checks, highlighting the state's stringent worker protection laws.

title: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt Cut Last Ties With The Company: Report
summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt officially severed all ties with Alphabet Inc. in February 2020, ending his 19-year tenure with the company. Schmidt, who had served in various executive roles since 2001, stepped down as a technology advisor, a move that coincided with his increased involvement in government roles. His departure also came amid criticism over his dual role as an advisor to the Pentagon while Alphabet competed for the JEDI contract.

title: PepsiCo Opens Two New eCommerce Outlets
summary: PepsiCo has launched two new direct-to-consumer websites, PantryShop.com and Snacks.com, to meet increased demand for food and beverage products amid the ongoing pandemic. These platforms offer curated "pantry kits" and a wide selection of snack products, enabling shoppers to order from home with convenient shipping options. The initiative underscores PepsiCo's focus on e-commerce and digital capabilities to meet evolving consumer needs.

title: Nvidia Unveils New Data Center Chips to Speed Pace of AI
summary: Nvidia Corp. announced new Ampere graphics chips and computers for AI processing in data centers, claiming a 20x performance increase over predecessors. These new chips are designed to handle both AI training and inference tasks, a capability that will bolster Nvidia's leadership in the growing AI market. The company is selling Ampere-based computers called DGX for $199,000 each, touting their superior performance compared to traditional Intel-based server arrays.

title: Amazon Stock Benefits If AWS Is Spun Off
summary: This article discusses the potential benefits for Amazon stock if its Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud business were spun off. The author suggests that AWS, with its faster-growing revenue and better margins compared to Amazon's e-commerce operations, could be worth more as a separate entity. The article also touches upon increasing government scrutiny on large tech companies like Amazon, Google, and Facebook regarding their dominance and potential monopolistic practices.

title: Goldman Sachs: new Co-Chief Officer and Chief Technology Officer
summary: Goldman Sachs has announced the appointment of Marco Argenti as Co-Chief Information Officer and Atte Lahtiranta as Chief Technology Officer. Argenti joins from Amazon Web Services, bringing over 30 years of technology experience, while Lahtiranta, with over 20 years of experience, joins from Verizon Media Group. They will work with George Lee to advance the company's engineering strategy and deliver innovative technology and data solutions.

title: How American Express uses Big Data to transform operations
summary: American Express leverages Big Data primarily for fraud detection and enhancing customer-merchant connections. With over 110 million AmEx cards and US$1 trillion in transactions, the company uses machine learning models and Hadoop infrastructure to analyze vast data flows in milliseconds. This strategy not only protects customer finances but also helps develop apps that benefit cardholders and encourage more businesses to accept American Express.

title: Home Depot expanding paid time off, doubling overtime pay
summary: The Home Depot Inc. has expanded paid time off for hourly workers, provided additional paid time off for high-risk employees, and offered weekly bonuses and double overtime pay to support its employees during the coronavirus pandemic. These actions resulted in a pre-tax expense of approximately US $850 million for the company. The initiatives focused on ensuring the safety and well-being of associates and customers while providing essential products.

title: 21st Century Fox completes asset divestment, creates Fox Corp
summary: 21st Century Fox has created Fox Corporation as a standalone company to divest assets in anticipation of its acquisition by The Walt Disney Company. Fox Corp will house Fox broadcasting network, Fox Sports, Fox News, and Fox Business Network, with Michael Nathanson projecting a significant portion of its earnings from Fox News. The new board members include Lachlan Murdoch, Paul Ryan, Chase Carey, Roland Hernandez, and Anne Dias.

title: Tech Moves: Qualtrics exec moves to Google; NHL Seattle expands team; former Amazon exec named Bluecrew CEO; and more
summary: This article details various "Tech Moves" in the Pacific Northwest, highlighting significant personnel changes across several companies. Key appointments include a former Qualtrics EVP joining Google, an ex-Amazon executive becoming CEO of Bluecrew, and new hires for the Seattle Center Arena project and NHL Seattle. Other notable moves include board appointments, new CROs, and executive leadership roles in marketing, finance, and engineering across the tech industry.

title: FedEx, Microsoft Join Forces Against Amazon for Package Shipping
summary: FedEx Corp. and Microsoft Corp. are collaborating to offer commercial shipping customers early warnings about potential delays due to weather, traffic, and other issues, directly competing with Amazon.com Inc. This new service, called FedEx Surround, will leverage Microsoft's cloud software and AI tools to provide real-time data to improve package movement, especially for high-priority shipments. The partnership aims to provide commercial customers with logistics tools that can serve as an alternative to Amazon for both small and large retailers.

title: 8x8 moves to Oracle Cloud from AWS amid explosive growth
summary: 8x8 migrated its core XCaaS platform from AWS to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) to meet explosive growth in demand for its communication solutions in 2020. This strategic move resulted in a 25% performance increase and network savings of over 80%, while enhancing global reach and allowing 8x8 to deliver its services more efficiently to millions of users worldwide. The company also leverages Oracle's Observability and Management Platform, including Logging Analytics, to monitor its IT environment and quickly resolve issues.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise plans cuts in jobs, executive pay to temper sales slump
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) announced plans to cut costs by US$1 billion by the end of fiscal 2022, including job cuts and executive pay reductions, following a decline in sales due to the coronavirus pandemic. The company reported a 16% revenue drop to US$6 billion in the recent quarter and is implementing measures like simplifying its product portfolio and consolidating offices to recover from supply chain disruptions. CEO Antonio Neri expects sales to recover sequentially but acknowledges the uncertainty of the economic downturn.

title: Expedia Group CEO Peter Kern: 'Google's a problem for everyone who sells something online'
summary: Expedia Group CEO Peter Kern criticized Google for its dual role as a competitor and a major source of customer traffic, stating it's an issue for all online sellers. Kern indicated a shift in strategy for Expedia to reduce its reliance on Google and performance marketing by improving internal merchandising and customer understanding. These comments follow Expedia's quarterly earnings report where marketing expenses dropped significantly, and the company reported a major reduction in business due to COVID-19.

title: Same Old Leadership Song Lifts These Leveraged ETFs
summary: Technology sector leadership is driving the stock market's recovery from March lows, benefiting leveraged ETFs like Direxion Daily Technology Bull 3X Shares (NYSE: TECL) and Direxion Daily Dow Jones Internet Bull 3X Shares (NYSE: WEBL). TECL is a triple-leveraged play on Microsoft and Apple, while WEBL offers a similar leveraged exposure to internet giants like Amazon, Facebook, and Netflix. Both ETFs have seen significant gains and investor interest due to the strong performance of their underlying tech and internet components.

title: Amazon Prime Air Seen Surging Fivefold, Rivaling UPS
summary: Amazon's Prime Air fleet is projected to grow fivefold to 200 planes in the next seven to eight years, potentially rivaling United Parcel Service Inc. This expansion, driven by the demand for faster home delivery, includes a significant $1.5 billion facility near Cincinnati designed to accommodate up to 100 planes and 200 daily flights, which could transform Amazon's ability to offer comprehensive domestic delivery services. While some analysts initially dismissed Amazon as a limited competitor due to its lack of a central hub, the new Cincinnati facility is seen as a pivotal investment for its long-term competitive aspirations.

title: CVS Health tests self-driving vehicle prescription delivery
summary: CVS Health is partnering with Nuro, a Silicon Valley robotics company, to test self-driving vehicle prescription delivery in the Houston area beginning next month. This marks Nuro's first venture into healthcare delivery, following previous partnerships for pizza and grocery delivery. The move by CVS Health, and rival Walgreens, highlights an industry trend to expand home delivery services amid Amazon's growing influence in retail.

title: Should You Buy or Sell Costco Stock?
summary: This article analyzes whether Costco stock (COST) is a good investment, weighing its strong performance during the pandemic and formidable business model against its high valuation and low dividend yield. It discusses Costco's growth in sales and membership, its "economic moats," and challenges such as rising costs and the need to scale up e-commerce operations. The article concludes that Costco is a wonderful company, despite its high price.

title: Target closing 6 stores 'until further notice' after protests compromise the safety of employees
summary: Target announced the temporary closure of six stores across the U.S. due to safety concerns stemming from protests, updating a decision that initially affected over 200 locations with adjusted hours over the weekend. The company is committed to reopening stores as soon as it is safe and is providing support to affected employees, including pay and the option to work at other locations. Target is also sending essential supplies to heavily impacted areas and its CEO expressed support for the protests against police abuse.

title: Parsons launches Intelligent Intersections traffic management and signal timing solution
summary: Parsons Corporation has introduced its new Intelligent Intersections solution, a software designed to reduce congestion and improve mobility in cities by using advanced analytics and existing sensor data. This tool automates the retiming of traffic signals, which can reduce congestion by up to 40% and annually decrease GHG emissions by 4.9 million tons and productivity losses by US$27 billion. The solution will be deployed in four US cities including Fort Smith, Arkansas; Austin, Texas; Westminster, Colorado; and Walnut Creek, California, in collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS).

title: Apple begins to sell Sonos as the speaker company accuses Google and Amazon of patent theft
summary: Apple has started selling the Sonos One SL Wireless Speaker online and in its stores. This comes as Sonos has publicly sued Google and accused Amazon of patent theft related to its streaming technology. The Sonos One SL speaker can stream Apple Music via Siri or AirPlay 2.

title: Synchrony Bank Review: High Interest Online Banking
summary: This review covers Synchrony Bank, an online bank offering high-interest deposit products, including savings, money market, and CD accounts, and various credit card options. It highlights the pros and cons of using an online-only bank, such as higher interest rates due to lower overhead but no physical branches. The article also touches on Synchrony's "Loyalty Perks" program and compares it to other online banking alternatives like CIT Bank.

title: Cisco Moves ACI Strategy Forward
summary: Cisco is advancing its hybrid cloud computing strategy with the release of version 5.0 of its Application Centric Infrastructure (ACI), adding support for AWS transit gateways and enhanced integration with Microsoft Azure and Kubernetes. This update aims to provide a centralized view of cloud resources and simplify configurations, offering IT teams networking services equivalent to those historically provided on-premises. The strategy emphasizes hybrid cloud management and automation, making networking services more accessible via APIs and GUIs, and fostering greater collaboration between NetOps and DevOps.

title: FedEx Follows UPS in Raising Delivery Prices Amid Package Surge
summary: FedEx Corp. is increasing its delivery prices for residential and large packages, mirroring an earlier move by UPS, in response to a surge in online orders during the coronavirus lockdown. Effective June 8, new charges will include an extra 30 cents per package for high-volume shippers, 40 cents for "SmartPost" parcels, and $30 for oversized packages. This adjustment reflects the ongoing impact of the pandemic on shipping volumes and operational costs.

title: National Grid Partners Announces New Investments in Two Security Leaders
summary: National Grid Partners announced new investments in two leading online security companies, 1touch.io and RiskIQ, to enhance data security and combat cyber threats. The investments, totaling $14 million and $15 million respectively, highlight National Grid's commitment to delivering a safer energy future. These security solutions are particularly relevant given the increased remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Real Networks' AI Facial Recognition Software IDs Familiar Faces in Streaming Movies and Personal Videos
summary: Real Networks has launched two new AI-powered facial recognition products: StarSearch for identifying actors in streaming movies and TV shows on platforms like Netflix and YouTube, and RealPlayer 20/20 for organizing personal video collections by individuals. These tools aim to address the common user query of identifying faces on screen, leveraging Real's Secure Accurate Facial Recognition (SAFR) software, which boasts high accuracy and low bias. The company envisions expanding the technology to more streaming services and enhancing personal video organization.

title: Amdocs transforms its own culture to help service providers move to the cloud
summary: Amdocs undertook a significant cultural and technological transformation, leveraging TM Forum's Open Digital Framework, to enable its customers to adopt cloud services faster. This involved shifting its portfolio to a cloud-native, microservices-based architecture, upskilling over 10,000 employees in DevOps, and increasing R&D velocity by over 50%. The successful internal transformation is now delivering tangible benefits for Amdocs' customers, such as Sprint, by speeding up time to market for new services and reducing operational costs.

title: US Cloud Data Firm NetApp To Acquire Israel’s Spot.io
summary: US cloud data services company NetApp is set to acquire the US-Israeli company Spot.io for an estimated $450 million. Spot.io helps businesses manage cloud workloads and slash computing costs for clients like Moovit, Ticketmaster, and Wix. This acquisition aims to establish NetApp's leadership in cloud management and infrastructure tools, promising significant cost savings for customers by combining their technologies into an Application Driven Infrastructure.

title: How Snowflake is challenging the cloud-native database giants
summary: This article examines how Snowflake Inc. is competing with major cloud providers like Amazon Web Services, Google, and Microsoft in the cloud-native database market. It analyzes customer spending data from Enterprise Technology Research (ETR) to demonstrate Snowflake's strong spending momentum across all three major clouds and discusses its strategy of being cloud-agnostic and prioritizing engineering investments. The piece concludes that Snowflake's specialized focus and native cloud architecture position it well for continued growth and a successful IPO despite competition from giants with vast R&D budgets.

title: Amazon sues to limit former AWS marketing VP Brian Hall’s new job at Google Cloud
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has filed a lawsuit against Brian Hall, a former VP of product marketing at Amazon Web Services Inc., to prevent him from taking a new role at Google Cloud due to a noncompete agreement. The lawsuit claims Hall's move risks exposing "valuable competitive information" related to Amazon's cloud product roadmap and strategy. Hall's lawyers argue the noncompete clause is overbroad and unenforceable, citing prior assurances from an AWS executive and Amazon's non-enforcement against another executive who joined a rival.

title: In Retreat, Wall Street Pulls Back From Rally (Published 2020)
summary: Wall Street experienced a retreat after a recent rally, with stocks falling on Tuesday despite the S&P 500 erasing its yearly losses on Monday. Concerns about a potential second wave of the coronavirus outbreak are affecting investor sentiment, even as global economies show signs of recovery and central banks provide support. This article summarizes key market movements and includes snapshots of news from companies like Chesapeake Energy and AMC.

title: Morgan Stanley's Gorman 'thrilled' with ETrade purchase
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman expresses immense satisfaction with the acquisition of ETrade, highlighting the online trading firm's technology, digital banking capabilities, and management team. He plans to retain the ETrade brand, possibly as "ETrade powered by Morgan Stanley," recognizing its value to clients. Gorman believes the deal expands Morgan Stanley's online platform, diversifies the company, and strengthens its digital offerings, particularly appealing to a younger demographic.

title: Rackspace rebrands (again) and repositions for digital transformation
summary: Rackspace has rebranded itself as Rackspace Technology and repositioned its strategy to focus on end-to-end technology solutions across four key areas, including cloud optimization, security, cloud-native enablement, and data modernization. This move follows a series of acquisitions and strategic partnerships, as the company prepares for a potential new initial public offering. The company aims to tackle the entire technology transformation lifecycle for its customers.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: Mitch Rubin, Stanley Druckenmiller, Lynwood Capital Management, Bow Street LLC, Ecolab Inc. (ECL), Ball Corporation (BLL), and More
summary: This article compiles various hedge fund and insider trading news, featuring fund managers like Mitch Rubin and Stanley Druckenmiller, and discussing their investment strategies and portfolio performance. It also covers several significant insider transactions in companies such as Ecolab Inc. (ECL) and Ball Corporation (BLL), and reports on the growth of crypto hedge funds in Gibraltar, new healthcare startups, and a regulatory charge against a penny stock trader for a manipulative scheme.

title: Here’s what that Capital One court decision means for corporate cybersecurity
summary: A recent court decision regarding Capital One's data breach mandated the bank to reveal a third-party incident response report, challenging the traditional attorney-client privilege over such documents. This ruling could significantly impact how companies contract cybersecurity firms and manage incident response, potentially making breach details public. Legal experts suggest this decision will prompt corporations to re-evaluate their agreements with security vendors to preserve legal protections.

title: Walmart buys tech from Carezone to help people manage their prescriptions
summary: Walmart has acquired technology and intellectual property from the start-up CareZone to enhance its health and wellness services, particularly in medication management. This acquisition includes bringing CareZone's engineering and product teams into Walmart, but Walmart is not purchasing CareZone's pharmacy business. The move is seen as a strategic step for Walmart to compete with Amazon in the pharmacy space and make healthcare more accessible and affordable for its customers.

title: Fact Check: Do Cruise Lines Pay US Taxes?
summary: This article clarifies whether cruise lines pay U.S. taxes, explaining that while they generally avoid federal income taxes due to international shipping agreements, they pay other significant taxes and fees. It details the tax amounts paid by major cruise corporations like Carnival Corp., Royal Caribbean Cruises, Ltd., and Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings, highlighting the relatively low effective tax rates compared to typical corporate rates. The article also debunks the myth that cruise lines sought a U.S. government bailout and notes that many profitable Fortune 500 companies also avoid federal taxes.

title: Oracle expects flat sales on fewer corporate software deals
summary: Oracle Corp. projects flat revenue in the current quarter due to delayed software purchases by corporate clients amid the coronavirus pandemic. The company, the world's second-biggest software-maker, reported a 6.3% decline in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, missing analyst estimates. Oracle is struggling to shift existing database customers to cloud-based offerings and compete with Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp.

title: Target permanently raises starting hourly pay to $15
summary: Target Corp. announced it is permanently increasing starting hourly wages for its workers to $15 beginning July 5, several months ahead of its original 2020 goal. This move comes after a temporary $2 wage bump for workers due to increased demand during the pandemic. The company will invest nearly $1 billion more this year in its workers, including a $200 bonus and extended COVID-19 benefits.

title: Salesforce Launches Government Cloud Plus, Achieves FedRAMP Provisional Authority to Operate at the High Security Impact Level
summary: Salesforce has launched Government Cloud Plus, a dedicated cloud instance for U.S. federal, state, and local government customers, achieving FedRAMP Provisional Authority to Operate (P-ATO) at the High Security Impact Level. This new offering provides enhanced security and compliance, running on AWS GovCloud (US), to help government agencies modernize their systems and deliver services more efficiently amidst evolving demands. Government Cloud Plus aims to reduce IT costs and complexity while offering the full power of Salesforce's Customer 360 CRM platform tailored for secure government use cases.

title: Amazon to hire 3,000 people in South Africa for customer service roles
summary: Amazon.com Inc. announced it will hire 3,000 people in South Africa this year for customer service roles, supporting customers in North America and Europe. These work-from-home positions, ranging from customer service associates to technical experts, will increase Amazon's permanent workforce in South Africa to 7,000. This expansion highlights South Africa's value proposition for global companies, following Amazon Web Services' launch of its first data center in Cape Town in April.

title: This NAACP-backed ETF will help you invest in companies that care about equality
summary: The Impact Shares NAACP Minority Empowerment ETF (NACP) allows investors to support companies committed to diversity and racial equality. Developed in partnership with the NAACP and Impact Shares, the ETF screens companies based on their practices in hiring, pay, promotion, and supply chains, with net proceeds going to the NAACP for social advocacy. With over $4 million in net assets and holdings in major companies like Amazon and Microsoft, the fund aims to achieve "social alpha" by investing in corporate leaders in social justice.

title: Montclair Woman Makes History At American Express, Joins Top Team
summary: Montclair resident Glenda McNeal has been appointed to American Express' executive committee, making her the first African American woman to hold such a position. Having served over 30 years with the company, McNeal’s elevation comes as a significant milestone, strengthening the committee's female representation. She will continue to lead strategic partnerships with major e-commerce, travel, technology, and retail companies.

title: Amazon Facing Class Action Alleging PFAS in Disposable Plates
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is facing a proposed class action lawsuit alleging that its disposable plates and bowls, advertised as compostable, actually contain PFAS "forever" chemicals. The plaintiff claims he purchased these products, which cost more than non-compostable alternatives, believing they were environmentally friendly and would not have bought them if he knew they contained PFAS. The lawsuit highlights concerns about the contamination of soil by these chemicals.

title: After 15 Years, Apple Prepares to Break Up With Intel (Published 2020)
summary: Apple is preparing to end its 15-year partnership with Intel, with plans to replace Intel processors in Macs with self-designed chips. This move, expected to be announced soon, signifies Apple's growing independence and determination to control its product manufacturing, a trend seen among other major tech companies like Facebook, Amazon, and Google. The new Mac chips are anticipated to arrive next year and will likely be manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.

title: American Express Names Glenda McNeal as the First Black Woman on its Executive Committee
summary: Glenda McNeal has been appointed as the first Black woman to join the Executive Committee at American Express, where she will bring her extensive expertise in strategic partnerships to help navigate global economic challenges. McNeal, who has a storied three-decade career, has overseen relationships with major Amex partners and serves on several boards. Her appointment also marks a record number of seven women on the committee, with leadership praising her diverse perspectives.

title: Sheltering-In and Shopping Online
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated the shift to online shopping, especially for softline retail sales, with e-commerce expected to account for 32% of softline sales in 2020. This shift is predicted to negatively impact brick-and-mortar retail margins due to cannibalized store sales and fixed costs, while benefiting e-commerce giants and brands with strong direct-to-consumer businesses. Morgan Stanley Research has raised its U.S. e-commerce estimates for both 2020 and 2021, emphasizing the long-term changes in consumer behavior.

title: Kroger CEO: Company's heavy tech investments vindicated. 'We made the right decision.'
summary: Kroger CEO Rodney McMullen stated that the company's significant investments in digital shopping initiatives have positioned it for future growth and allowed it to meet the increased demand during the coronavirus pandemic. He highlighted the vindication of their business model transformation and the expansion of digital capabilities, including new robotic delivery hubs. The company also announced a 12.5% increase in its quarterly dividend.

title: LATEST TECH NEWS: Verizon joins others to boycott Facebook. 4 other things and a trivia you need to know today, June 26, 2020
summary: This article covers five key tech news stories from June 26, 2020, including Verizon joining the boycott against Facebook due to hate speech concerns, Egyptian edtech OTO Courses securing new investment, Waymo and Volvo partnering on electric robotaxis, the opening of applications for the AppsAfrica Innovation Awards 2020, and Amazon's reported acquisition of self-driving startup Zoox for over $1 billion. It also includes a tech trivia question and answer about the beginning of computer engineering.

title: A Thank You bonus for Amazon front-line employees and partners
summary: Amazon announced a one-time "Thank You" bonus totaling over $500 million for its front-line employees and partners in recognition of their efforts during June 2020. The bonus amounts vary based on employment status and role, with full-time Amazon and Whole Foods Market employees, and Delivery Service Partner drivers receiving $500, and front-line leaders receiving $1,000, among others. Dave Clark, SVP WW Operations, expressed gratitude for their commitment to customers.

title: Special Feature: YouTube’s Evolution in the OTT Streaming Landscape...
summary: This article by Comscore and YouTube examines YouTube's significant growth within the evolving OTT streaming landscape, highlighting its increased reach in ad-supported households and substantial growth in CTV watch time. It also details how YouTube's unique user-generated content and extensive library are providing new opportunities for advertisers to target diverse audiences. The piece further explores emerging content consumption trends on the platform, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Santander appoints three leading technologists to support its strategy and digital transformation
summary: Santander has appointed R. Martin Chávez, Sebastian Gunningham, and Francisco D’Souza to key roles to bolster its digital transformation. Chávez will join the board as an independent director, Gunningham will chair Santander Consumer Finance and become vice chairman of Openbank, and D’Souza will be a strategic advisor for Santander Global Platform. These appointments aim to leverage their extensive technology and financial sector experience to drive Santander's digital strategy.

title: Target to open two-level store in former Boston Store space at Bayshore
summary: Target is scheduled to open a new two-level store in the former Boston Store space at the Bayshore shopping center in Glendale. This announcement was made by mall manager Cypress Equities on June 30, 2020. This development implies a significant revitalization for the Bayshore shopping center.

title: FedEx says coronavirus shopping helped offset commercial slowdown
summary: FedEx reported better-than-expected revenue and adjusted profit for its fiscal fourth quarter, despite a $334 million loss. The surge in residential deliveries due to increased online shopping during the coronavirus pandemic helped offset a significant slowdown in its commercial deliveries. The company incurred $125 million in COVID-19 related costs and will cut capital spending in the new fiscal year due to economic uncertainty.

title: Pollster with fake staff gave top grades to firms landing deals
summary: A firm named Black Book Market Research, led by Douglas Brown, whose rankings are used by major healthcare IT companies, is accused of using questionable methods. The company used fake staff on its website, lifts content from other research firms, and has a crowd-sourcing methodology experts compare to Yelp, which could lead to skewed results. Despite its claims of independence, Black Book is paid by the vendors it rates and has shown instances of working closely with companies like Allscripts to produce favorable rankings.

title: ‘Mad Men’ Rights Sold To Amazon/IMDb TV Globally, AMC & Starzplay In Complex Licensing Deal Made By Lionsgate
summary: Lionsgate has finalized intricate licensing deals for "Mad Men," bringing the iconic series to Amazon/IMDb TV globally, and back to its original network, AMC, and Starzplay. The agreement outlines various exclusive and non-exclusive international streaming windows, aiming to generate revenue comparable to its previous Netflix deal, which expired in June. The complete series on all platforms will include a blackface episode with a disclaimer explaining its historical context.

title: More Confirmation Online Retail Is Eating Traditional Retail's Lunch
summary: The Global X E-commerce ETF (EBIZ) saw significant growth in Q2, driven by companies like Amazon, Walmart, and Target, as online retail continues to take market share from traditional brick-and-mortar stores. Experts predict a sustained shift towards e-commerce, with U.S. online sales expected to reach $709.78 billion in 2020, representing 14.5% of total retail sales. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated this trend, making e-commerce a sticky theme for investors for years to come, despite a projected slight dip in share as consumers return to physical stores in 2021 before rising again in 2022.

title: Western Digital Launches SanDisk 1TB USB Type-C Pendrive for Smartphones
summary: Western Digital has launched a 1TB SanDisk Ultra Dual Drive Luxe USB Type-C Pendrive for smartphones in India, designed to help consumers easily transfer content between USB Type-C devices.
