This expansion is part of the company's continued investment in the APAC region and its strategy to enhance digitization plans for businesses globally, especially for its cloud solutions following its IPO. The new office will serve as a base for expansion into ASEAN markets, focusing on helping businesses leverage cloud technology for efficiency, productivity, and cost optimization.

title: Entertainment and Media Market to Witness Huge Growth by 2026 | Warner Media, Viacom, Alphabet
summary: A new research study by HTF MI titled "Global Entertainment and Media Market Report 2020" predicts significant growth in the entertainment and media sector by 2026. The report evaluates market trends, drivers, and investment structures, covering key players like Viacom, Alphabet, and Warner Media. It provides forecasts based on segments like product types (Amusement Park/Facilities, Animation, Films) and applications (Wire, Wireless) across various regions.

title: Marvell to buy Inphi in $10bn semiconductor deal
summary: Semiconductor company Marvell Technology Group is set to acquire Inphi Corp in a $10 billion cash-and-stock deal. The acquisition aims to strengthen Marvell's leadership in cloud infrastructure and expand its 5G presence, leveraging Inphi's expertise in fiber-optic data traffic and its customer base including Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Facebook. This move is part of a broader trend of consolidation within the semiconductor industry.

title: A Look Behind the Vimeo Brand
summary: This article explores Vimeo's unique position in the crowded video platform market, highlighting its focus on community, storytelling tools, and value proposition compared to competitors like YouTube. Author Bryan Elliott shares insights from his professional experience and an interview with Vimeo CMO Harris Beber, discussing Vimeo's features, OTT capabilities, and a new service connecting creators with video professionals. The piece also delves into the author's personal journey in content creation, including his early experiences in the entertainment industry and the inspiration behind his career path, concluding that now is an optimal time for video storytelling.

title: Analysis: In an epic pivot to the cloud, Microsoft makes Azure the linchpin of its future
summary: Microsoft's Azure cloud computing service is a central component of the company's innovation strategy, driving significant revenue growth and serving as a key differentiator from competitors focused on advertising. The company's overall financial performance is strong, with impressive growth across its three main business segments: Productivity and Business Process, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Microsoft's successful pivot to the cloud and its developer-centric approach have made it a leader in the tech industry, demonstrating remarkable spending momentum among its customers despite its large size.

title: Mukesh Ambani versus Jeff Bezos: A fight or a waiting game?
summary: The article details the struggle between Mukesh Ambani and Jeff Bezos for dominance in the Indian consumer market. This centers around Amazon's attempt to block Reliance Industries' $3.4 billion acquisition of Future Group assets, stemming from a previous agreement where Amazon had rights to acquire shares in Future Retail and a non-compete clause with Reliance. The dispute highlights potential issues for foreign investors in India and questions whether Amazon prefers rivalry or a sweeter deal with Ambani.

title: IndianoriginCEOs
summary: This article highlights 13 individuals of Indian origin who hold significant leadership positions in global IT companies. It showcases their roles, companies, and key achievements, underscoring the growing presence and influence of Indian-origin executives in the international tech industry.

title: Smart Offers: Sabre Partners With Google on AI-Powered Personalized Travel Tech
summary: Sabre, in partnership with Google, is launching an AI-powered "Smart Retail Engine" in early 2021 to offer personalized travel options. This technology aims to customize offerings for travelers, increase satisfaction, and boost industry revenue by leveraging AI and machine learning. The partnership seeks to transform customer experience and pricing in the travel sector.

title: Toyota-backed startup Pony.ai raises $267 mln in latest fundraising
summary: Pony.ai, a self-driving startup backed by Toyota, announced it raised $267 million in the initial phase of its latest fundraising round, valuing the company at $5.3 billion. This investment, led by Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board, aims to boost its presence in the United States and China and explore mobility services with Toyota. The company plans to use the funds for technology development and fleet expansion, including autonomous trucks.

title: Nest Wifi vs. Ubiquiti AmpliFi HD: Which should you buy?
summary: This article compares Google's Nest Wifi and Ubiquiti AmpliFi HD mesh Wi-Fi systems, detailing their strengths, weaknesses, and key differences. While Nest Wifi offers Google Assistant integration and WPA3 support, AmpliFi HD excels in coverage, QoS options, wired backhaul, and a free VPN solution. The article concludes that AmpliFi HD is generally the superior product due to its broader feature set and performance advantages.

title: Prisma Access: SASE Architected for Unprecedented Security and Scale
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Access service, combined with CloudGenix SD-WAN, offers a comprehensive SASE platform designed for unprecedented security and scale. Leveraging cloud-native architecture on AWS and Google Cloud, it provides extensive global coverage and ultra-fast security processing, proven by its ability to support massive increases in remote workers during the COVID-19 pandemic. The service has demonstrated rapid scalability, enabling major organizations like PwC, Schlumberger, and Flex to transition significant portions of their workforce to remote operations without disruption.

title: Google parent Alphabet turns to cat bonds for earthquake insurance
summary: Alphabet, Google's parent company, has entered the catastrophe bond market for the first time, seeking $237.5 million in earthquake insurance protection. This is facilitated through a Phoenician Re Ltd. cat bond transaction with capital market investors. The move highlights how major tech companies are utilizing the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market for efficient capacity to manage significant catastrophe exposures like California earthquakes.

title: 10 Websites to Make $100 per Day Working From Home (Without Investment!)
summary: This article lists ten websites that can help individuals earn $100 per day working from home without an upfront investment. It covers various online opportunities like freelancing, affiliate marketing, content creation, and online tutoring, detailing how each platform works and payment methods. The goal is to provide readers with diverse options to supplement their income or make a full-time living online.

title: Buy now! COVID-19 sparks Southeast Asian e-commerce boom
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly accelerated e-commerce growth in Southeast Asia, with spending expected to triple to over $300 billion by 2025. While online travel and transport were hit, overall digital adoption surged, bringing 40 million new internet users online in the region in 2020. Indonesia's digital economy is also projected to nearly triple despite the wider economic downturn.

title: Yelp CEO is encouraged by antitrust case against Google
summary: Yelp CEO Jeremy Stoppelman expressed encouragement regarding the U.S. antitrust case against Google, stating that it validates his long-held belief in Google's monopoly in internet search. Stoppelman alleges that Google abuses its dominant position by prioritizing its own content, harming competition and consumers. Despite initial pandemic-related challenges, Yelp reported better-than-expected sales in the third quarter and anticipates further improvement with a vaccine rollout.

title: How Microsoft and Sony’s new consoles improve game technology
summary: Penn professors and lecturers discuss the technological advancements in the new PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X consoles. Key improvements include solid-state hard drives (SSDs) for faster loading times and hardware-based ray tracing for photo-realistic graphics. The article also touches on the potential impact of streaming services on the gaming industry.

title: The Snowflake Story
summary: Snowflake Inc., founded in 2012, is a cloud-based data-warehousing company that came out of stealth mode in 2014. The company offers a data warehouse-as-a-service, running on major cloud platforms and enabling data storage and analytics for corporate users. Snowflake had a historic IPO on September 16, 2020, with shares more than doubling in value, leading to a $70.4 billion market valuation on its first day of trading.

title: Amazon shifts some voice assistant, face recognition computing to its own chips
summary: Amazon is transitioning some of the computing for its Alexa voice assistant and Rekognition facial recognition service to its custom-designed "Inferentia" chips. This strategic move aims to improve speed and reduce costs by moving away from third-party chip providers like Nvidia. The company reports a 25% improvement in latency and 30% lower costs for Alexa's text-to-speech tasks with the new chips.

title: Apple, Google, and LG Start Working on 6G Technology
summary: Apple, Google, and LG have joined the Next G Alliance, a group focused on developing sixth-generation (6G) communication technology. Established in October by ATIS, the Alliance aims to position North America at the forefront of 6G innovation, even as 5G technology has yet to become mainstream. The group is working towards making 6G a reality potentially ahead of Samsung's 2028 estimate.

title: Why Google, Amazon, and Nvidia are all building AI notetakers for doctors
summary: Google, Amazon, and Nvidia are developing AI-powered notetaking tools for doctors to address the time-consuming and often inaccurate process of medical transcription. These tools aim to improve the efficiency and accuracy of recording patient interactions and medical records, moving beyond existing methods that doctors find cumbersome or overly generalized. While some solutions are already available, tech giants are focusing on delivering more precise and sophisticated AI to streamline healthcare documentation.

title: Continuous Security for Google Cloud Artifact Registry
summary: Palo Alto Networks has integrated Prisma Cloud with Google Cloud Artifact Registry to provide continuous security for containerized applications. This integration helps organizations manage vulnerabilities, compliance, and runtime protection for their cloud-native applications on Google Cloud. Prisma Cloud supports container security across the build, deploy, and run stages of the application lifecycle.

title: 115 Amazon lobbyists. 1 works on climate
summary: Despite Amazon's public stance on climate action and its "Climate Pledge," an analysis reveals that only one out of its 115 lobbyists is focused on environmental issues. This raises questions about the company's commitment, with critics suggesting it may be "greenwashing." Other tech giants like Facebook also show similar discrepancies, while Microsoft, Apple, and Google appear to align their lobbying efforts more closely with their climate concerns.

title: Real-Time Payments Launch in Brazil
summary: Brazil has launched its national real-time payments platform, PIX, operated by Banco Central do Brasil. The system, which is available 24/7, aims to increase financial sector competition and has already processed significant transactions during its pilot phase. PIX utilizes ISO 20200, has no transaction limits, and has seen rapid adoption by financial institutions and companies like Uber.

title: Life360 and Google Collaborate to Bring Family Coordination Features to Google Assistant-Enabled Devices
summary: Life360 has partnered with Google to integrate its family coordination services into Google Assistant-enabled devices, including Nest smart speakers, Smart Displays, and Android/iOS phones. This collaboration allows Life360 members in the U.S., U.K., and Australia to use voice commands like "Hey Google, where's my family?" to check the real-time location of family members. The feature aims to enhance family safety and connectivity through convenient voice-forward experiences powered by Life360's Smart RealTime (SRT) technology.

title: WWE SuperCard Season 7 Now Available
summary: 2K Games has released Season 7 of WWE SuperCard, introducing new features, card tiers, and gameplay mechanics. The update includes Styles & Techniques, Super Moves, three new card tiers (Bio-Mechanical, Behemoth, Swarm), and an art refresh. Players can also earn rewards through dynamic Collections and participate in a new WarGames event.

title: Who’s a Very Good Pandemic Business? Chewy Is. Oh, Yes It Is
summary: Chewy (CHWY) has experienced phenomenal growth in 2020, becoming a top pandemic business as pet care surged. CEO Sumit Singh's 2019 compensation of $108.2 million placed him among the highest-paid executives, despite the company not yet achieving profitability in its nine years of existence. This success highlights the booming online pet supply market.

title: BREAKING: Johnson & Johnson finally unveils its new robot-assisted surgery system
summary: Johnson & Johnson has unveiled Ottava, its new robot-assisted surgery system designed for unrivaled flexibility and control with six arms integrated into the operating table. The company plans to begin verification and validation processes in 2021, followed by clinical trials in 2022, and aims to combine it with the FDA-cleared Monarch platform for minimally invasive procedures and targeted drug delivery. J&J remains optimistic about the medtech market's recovery post-pandemic, expecting double-digit operational sales growth in 2021.

title: BuzzFeed acquires news website HuffPost from Verizon Media
summary: BuzzFeed has acquired news website HuffPost from Verizon Communications Inc., marking further consolidation in the online media sector. This deal brings two properties, previously struggling for ad dollars, under the control of HuffPost's co-founder, Jonah Peretti, with Verizon also taking a minority stake in the combined company. The acquisition aims to leverage a more affluent and age-diverse audience and explore new monetization opportunities.

title: Phillips 66 adopts Google Pay at its gas pumps
summary: Phillips 66 is introducing Google Pay as a new payment option at its 7,000 gas stations across the U.S., including Phillips 66, Conoco, and 76 brands. This initiative, in collaboration with P97 Networks, will allow drivers to pay for fuel directly through the Google Pay app, eliminating the need to swipe credit cards at the pump. The company aims to enhance the fueling experience by integrating mobile commerce solutions for greater convenience.

title: Now that's multicloud: CIA awards multibillion-dollar contract to AWS, Microsoft, Google, Oracle and IBM
summary: The CIA has awarded its Commercial Cloud Enterprise (C2E) contract to Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Google, Oracle, and IBM, marking a significant shift to a multicloud strategy. This multibillion-dollar contract allows these five major public cloud providers to compete for task orders from the CIA and 16 other intelligence agencies across different security classification levels. This move aims to leverage the unique strengths of various providers for different workloads and enhance competition, contrasting with past single-vendor awards like the Department of Defense's JEDI contract.

title: The Value of Data in a Digital World
summary: This article discusses the increasing value of data in a digital world, contrasting it with the historical valuation of companies based on tangible assets. It explores why data should be considered an asset, despite current accounting rules, and proposes three approaches for data valuation: market-based, cost-based, and cash flow-based, providing examples for each. The article also touches on how data-rich enterprises can seize opportunities and mentions related ETFs that invest in data-centric technologies.

title: Cynergy Bank secures partnership with Google
summary: Cynergy Bank has partnered with Google and Wipro Limited to launch a "digital relationship bank" aimed at small business owners and professionals. This new platform, set to launch in early 2021, will combine digital banking services with personal relationship management, leveraging Google Cloud technology and Wipro's expertise. The collaboration seeks to enhance customer engagement and grow Cynergy Bank's customer base significantly by allowing relationship managers to act as growth advisors.

title: Android apps from Chinese internet giant Baidu found to leak sensitive data
summary: New research from Palo Alto Network's Unit 42 revealed that Android apps from Baidu, including Baidu Search Box and Baidu Maps, were leaking sensitive user data, potentially allowing users to be tracked. The leaked data included phone information such as MAC address, Android ID, IMSI, and IMEI. Following contact from Unit 42, Google removed the apps from Google Play in October, with a compliant version of Baidu Search Box returning in November, though Baidu Maps remains unavailable.

title: Android Apps Leaking Sensitive Data Found on Google Play With 6 Million U.S. Downloads
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 researchers identified several Android applications on Google Play, including Baidu Search Box and Baidu Maps, that were leaking sensitive user data like IMSI and MAC addresses, together accumulating over 6 million U.S. downloads. These data leaks, while not definitive violations of Google's policy, go against Android's best practices for handling unique identifiers. Google subsequently removed the identified Baidu applications globally, and a compliant version of Baidu Search Box has since been re-released.

title: Global Over the Top Market - Featuring 8*8 Inc., Alphabet Inc., and Amazon.com Inc. Among Others | Technavio
summary: The global Over the Top (OTT) market is projected to grow by USD 88.85 billion during 2020-2024, at a CAGR of almost 14%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing demand for cloud streaming services and the rising adoption of target advertisement-based streaming applications. Technavio's report provides a comprehensive analysis including market sizing, forecast, trends, growth drivers, challenges, and vendor analysis featuring key players like 8x8 Inc., Alphabet Inc., Amazon.com Inc., and Netflix Inc.

title: How Fiserv Is Working With Google Pay And ExxonMobil To Go ‘Beyond the Buy Button’
summary: Fiserv is leveraging its Carat platform to integrate digital and physical commerce, exemplified by a new partnership with Google Pay and ExxonMobil. This collaboration allows consumers to activate gas pumps and pay directly from their cars using Google Pay, with ExxonMobil able to push offers post-transaction. Fiserv aims for Carat to be a leading omnichannel solution for various merchants, enhancing quick-purchase experiences across diverse channels.

title: TSMC adopts 3D stacking tech for chips along with Google and AMD
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) is introducing a new 3D stacking technology called SoIC, developed with Google and AMD, to stack and link various chip types into a single package. This innovation aims to make chips more efficient and powerful, with a new factory in Miaoli, Taiwan, expected to begin mass production by 2022. Google and AMD are already testing these chips, and TSMC's move into advanced packaging seeks to serve premium clients and counter the slowing of Moore's Law, positioning it against competitors like Samsung and Intel.

title: Top-Selling Videogames of the Last 25 Years Show Mario and Call of Duty Rule
summary: A report on the top-selling videogames over the past 25 years reveals the dominance of franchises like Super Mario and Call of Duty. While new games are constantly released, sequels and reboots from major publishers such as Activision Blizzard, Electronic Arts, and Nintendo consistently lead sales charts. The article also highlights the significant growth of mobile gaming revenue and the burgeoning popularity of live-streaming and esports viewership.

title: Alphabet’s (Google’s) first catastrophe bond priced on-target at $237.5m
summary: Alphabet (Google's parent company) has successfully priced its first catastrophe bond, Phoenician Re Ltd. (Series 2020-1), at the target size of $237.5 million. This cat bond will provide Alphabet with California earthquake insurance protection through its captive insurer and Hannover Re, marking a significant step for a major tech company entering the catastrophe bond market for efficient risk transfer. The bond offers a 3% coupon to investors across a three-year term.

title: Is Zoom a Chinese Company?
summary: This article addresses the common question of whether Zoom Video Communications Inc. is a Chinese company, clarifying its U.S. base despite its founder's origins and global operations. It also delves into Zoom's history, its market competitors, and its freemium business model, particularly highlighting how the COVID-19 pandemic fueled its growth. The piece concludes by touching on Zoom's tax collection practices in the U.S.

title: How to Avoid Speed Bumps and Stay in the AI Fast Lane with Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure
summary: This article discusses the benefits of hybrid cloud infrastructure for AI development, combining the flexibility of cloud computing with the cost-effectiveness of on-premises systems. It highlights how NVIDIA DGX systems with Google Cloud's Anthos on bare metal can help organizations manage AI workloads efficiently, minimizing data gravity issues and supporting both rapid experimentation and scaling. The approach allows businesses to "own the base, rent the spike," ensuring continuous compute resource availability and optimal cost per training run.

title: How Cloud Is Democratizing RDMA Use in the Financial Services Industry
summary: The financial services industry is seeing Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) become more accessible due to cloud migration, enabling smaller firms to leverage a technology previously exclusive to large institutions. NASDAQ's move to the cloud by 2030 highlights this trend. RDMA's high performance and low latency capabilities can be applied beyond high-frequency trading to areas like risk modeling, portfolio rebalancing, and payments, democratizing advanced computing power.

title: Commercial real estate: Trends to watch in 2021
summary: The commercial real estate market in 2021 will be shaped by the lasting impacts of COVID-19 on leasing and transaction patterns, accelerating existing trends in industrial and retail sectors. While industrial real estate, driven by e-commerce, is expected to thrive with increased construction and higher rates, the office sector faces uncertainty with varied forecasts on vacancies due to work-from-home trends. Multifamily residential properties are also gaining investor interest, though downtown vacancies in some cities are attributed to factors like Airbnb conversions and a halt in immigration.

title: Judge throws out Trump rules limiting skilled-worker visas
summary: A federal judge in California has struck down two Trump administration rules that aimed to significantly reduce the number of H-1B visas issued to skilled foreign workers. The judge ruled that the government failed to follow proper transparency procedures and that its argument of an emergency response to COVID-19 job losses was unconvincing. This decision is seen as a significant relief for companies and current H-1B visa holders.

title: How to use Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant with Tile
summary: This article explains how to integrate Tile trackers with Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant smart home devices. It describes the setup process for enabling voice commands to find Tile devices, allowing users to locate misplaced items more easily.

title: Sanjay Sharma: Remixing the Mainstream From the Margins?
summary: In this interview, Sanjay Sharma, Founder and CEO of Marginal MediaWorks, discusses his journey from being a lawyer and screenwriter to a serial entrepreneur. He emphasizes how focusing on "fringe" cultures and underserved audiences has led to outsized value creation in the media landscape. Sharma covers his experiences building successful ventures like Machinima and All Def Digital, and how these inform his current work at Marginal MediaWorks, which focuses on genre storytelling from marginalized voices for a changing demographic.

title: WWE® SuperCard Season 7 Introduces Three-Ring Chaos with New WarGames Event
summary: WWE SuperCard Season 7 is set to introduce a new WarGames event on December 3rd, bringing a unique three-ring, three-round solo battling experience. Players will strategize their card decks to control rings, earning points to win, and can play at their own pace for various rewards. To celebrate the launch, players can claim a free pack containing an Adam Cole "Cataclysm" card and other in-game items from December 3rd to December 10th.

title: Alphabet (Google) returns for second cat bond to top up quake cover
summary: Alphabet, Inc. (Google's parent company) has issued a second catastrophe bond, Phoenician Re Ltd. (Series 2020-2), for $95 million, quickly following its initial $237.5 million transaction. This second cat bond further increases its California earthquake insurance coverage, attaching where the first bond exhausts, demonstrating Alphabet's satisfaction with the efficiency and pricing offered by the capital markets for risk transfer. The move highlights the growing appeal of catastrophe bonds for large corporations seeking diversified and cost-effective insurance solutions for significant exposures.

title: Deutsche Bank to Move ‘Heart’ of IT Systems Into Google’s Cloud
summary: Deutsche Bank AG has finalized a cloud computing agreement with Alphabet Inc.'s Google to migrate most of its data onto Google servers, aiming to modernize its IT systems and cut costs. This long-term contract is expected to yield a cumulative return on investment of 1 billion euros for Deutsche Bank and marks a significant step for Google into the European banking cloud market. The partnership also includes joint development of new financial products, with both companies planning to sell some of this technology as white-label products.

title: Chasing the hydrogen dream: Ballard on quest to transform long-haul transportation
summary: Ballard Power Systems, a Canadian pioneer in hydrogen fuel cell technology, is experiencing a resurgence in investor interest and market capitalization after a tumultuous history. The company, which specializes in fuel cells for heavy-duty transportation, is banking on global demand for clean energy and government initiatives to drive widespread adoption, despite past setbacks and competition from battery electric vehicles. With strategic partnerships and a focus on automation to reduce costs, Ballard aims for significant revenue growth from China, Europe, and North America in the coming years.

title: Deutsche Bank and Google Cloud sign pioneering cloud and innovation partnership
summary: Deutsche Bank and Google Cloud have formed a strategic, multi-year partnership to accelerate the bank's transition to cloud technology and co-innovate new financial products and services. This collaboration aims to improve resilience, speed up market delivery of new capabilities, and reduce costs for Deutsche Bank, while also exploring new lending products, unified retail interfaces, and enhancements to its Autobahn platform. The partnership signifies a move towards more intelligent data use and a flexible environment for delivering innovative banking solutions to clients.

title: Google removes some IAC browser extensions for 'policy violations'
summary: Google announced it has removed several browser extensions from IAC/InterActive Corp due to "policy violations" and is considering further enforcement actions. While internal Google investigators reportedly found IAC's extensions were deceptive, an IAC spokeswoman denied violations, stating Google had previously approved and profited from these products. The situation highlights ongoing tensions and competitive dynamics between the two companies.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Senator Seeks Answers From Google CEO Over IAC Feud
summary: Senator Ron Wyden (D., Ore.) has requested answers from Google CEO Sundar Pichai regarding the company's financial ties with IAC/InterActive Corp. This follows a Wall Street Journal article reporting that Google was considering penalties against IAC for Chrome browser extensions that allegedly did not deliver promised functions and instead directed users to advertising. Wyden's letter asks nine specific questions about the relationship between the two tech giants.

title: Popular Android apps like Grindr, OkCupid, and others vulnerable to major security flaw: Check Point
summary: A security flaw, CVE-2020-8913, rooted in Google's Play Core Library, continues to affect popular Android apps like Grindr, Bumble, Cisco Teams, and OkCupid, despite Google having issued a fix in April 2020. This vulnerability allows cybercriminals to inject and execute malicious code, potentially leading to the theft of sensitive user data, including login and financial details. Developers of the affected apps still need to implement the updated Play Core library to fully eliminate the threat, putting millions of users at risk.

title: The 2021 outlook for the booming SPAC market and traditional IPOs
summary: The article discusses the outlook for Special Purpose Acquisition Companies (SPACs) and traditional Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) in 2021, following a strong year for both in 2020. Despite initial criticisms, SPACs are gaining credibility with big-name sponsors and offering advantages like full transparency and an easy exit for investors. Experts believe there's room for both IPOs and SPACs to thrive in 2021, especially with an improving economy and market conditions.

title: Audio Quick Take: Aon’s Rakesh Inamdar on Being a Digital Leader
summary: This HBR Audio Quick Take features Rakesh Inamdar from Aon discussing how the company has achieved digital leadership through strategic technology investments in areas like big data analytics, elastic compute, and AI. Aon's focus on a resilient, scalable, and globally reachable digital infrastructure, including partnerships with companies like Equinix, allowed them to maintain operations efficiently, even during the COVID-19 pandemic. Looking ahead, Aon plans further investments in AI, Machine Learning, and 5G to drive future business insights and transform network connectivity.

title: Google Weighs Action in Search Against a Smaller Player
summary: Google is reportedly considering taking action against IAC in its search results, potentially penalizing the internet holding company. This consideration comes amid an ongoing federal antitrust probe into Google, with the tech giant citing deceptive marketing practices by IAC as the reason for its potential action.

title: Best Buy wants 1 in 3 new corporate hires to be people of color
summary: Best Buy announced a plan to have people of color fill one-third of its new corporate jobs over the next five years, aligning with similar diversity targets set by other major companies. This initiative is part of a broader $44 million diversity push, which also includes financial support for students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities and the establishment of "Teen Tech Centers" in underserved communities. Other companies like Google, Microsoft, Wells Fargo, and Starbucks have also committed to increasing racial diversity within their leadership and workforce by 2025.

title: GM's Cruise begins testing autonomous vehicles without human drivers in San Francisco
summary: GM's Cruise has started testing fully self-driving vehicles without human drivers in San Francisco, marking a significant milestone for the company and the autonomous vehicle industry. While a safety operator will initially remain in the passenger seat, this move signals Cruise's transition from research and development to commercialization. CEO Dan Ammann anticipates an "exciting year ahead" with further progress, eventually leading to public use after an employee test program.

title: The dark reality behind Slack’s billion-dollar sale to Salesforce
summary: The article discusses Slack's acquisition by Salesforce for $27.7 billion, framing it as a "defensive" move rather than a success story. It argues that Slack, despite its innovative product, was unable to compete against Microsoft's bundling of Teams, highlighting a broader issue of tech giants stifling smaller innovators through monopolistic practices. The author suggests that this trend threatens consumer choice and calls for a rebalancing of the playing field against unchecked corporate power.

title: Zepp Z review: An excellent watch hampered by two software flaws
summary: The Zepp Z smartwatch is reviewed as a well-built device with great health tracking features and strong battery life but is hindered by poor notification handling and a lack of a third-party app ecosystem. Despite its premium hardware and responsive software, these two software flaws prevent it from being a top contender, especially when compared to competitors like the TicWatch Pro 3 and Samsung Galaxy Watch 3.

title: Digital Ad Spending Poised for Exceptional Growth
summary: Digital ad spending is expected to see strong growth in 2021 and beyond due to increased online consumer activity during COVID-19. While major digital ad players like Snap, Pinterest, Twitter, and Spotify are considered overvalued, Facebook and Alphabet are viewed as reasonably valued and well-positioned to benefit from this trend. The shift towards e-commerce and increased time spent online has accelerated advertisers' move to digital channels, with direct-response ads providing a stable option during economic uncertainty, though brand marketing remains crucial for long-term customer value.

title: Google's YouTube, Gmail recover after global outage
summary: Google's YouTube and Gmail services have recovered after experiencing a global outage. The services resumed functionality following the widespread disruption. The article was published on December 14, 2020, by Reuters.

title: Google Picks Gray TV for 2021 News Innovation Challenge
summary: Gray Television has been selected by Google for its GNI Innovation Challenge for 2021 and will receive $200,000 in funding. This funding will support a multiplatform journalism project focused on health disparities in the Mississippi Delta and Appalachia regions of the U.S. Journalists from over 25 Gray TV stations, the D.C. News Bureau, and Gray’s National Investigative unit will collaborate on the project, aiming to give a voice to underrepresented populations and provide resources for health-related decisions.

title: Quantum computing applications for the energy industry
summary: This article explores the potential applications of quantum computing in the energy industry, discussing its fundamental principles like superposition and entanglement, and contrasting it with classical computing. It highlights specific areas where quantum technology, including quantum annealers and quantum-inspired computing, can provide solutions, such as simulating molecules for material science, solving complex combinatorial optimization problems in planning and logistics, and improving machine learning algorithms. The article emphasizes early opportunities for quantum computing in chemistry simulation and optimization due to current hardware limitations (NISQ devices) and looks ahead to future advancements.

title: Texas, nine US states accuse Google of working with Facebook to break antitrust law
summary: Texas and nine other US states have filed an antitrust lawsuit against Google, accusing it of illegally colluding with Facebook to dominate the online advertising market. The lawsuit seeks compensation for damages and "structural relief," potentially forcing Google to divest assets. This action is part of a broader push by regulators against alleged anti-competitive practices by major tech companies.

title: Apple Inc. stock rises Thursday, still underperforms market
summary: Apple Inc. (AAPL) stock increased by 0.70% on Thursday to $128.70, during a generally favorable trading session for the market where the NASDAQ Composite Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also rose. Despite this, Apple's stock closed below its 52-week high but outperformed some competitors like Microsoft and Alphabet. Trading volume was lower than its 50-day average.

title: Cloud recasts global data center switch market
summary: The global data center switch market is being reshaped by cloud providers and enterprise cloud makers, leading to a decline in traditional networking gear sales. White box switches, favored by large-scale cloud environments, saw significant growth while established vendors like Arista Networks, Cisco, and Juniper Networks experienced revenue drops. This shift demands that vendors reconfigure their products and software to be cloud-focused, addressing enterprise needs for independent management software and hybrid environments.

title: Yext CEO Howard Lerman returns to the OMR Podcast
summary: Yext CEO Howard Lerman returned to the OMR Podcast to discuss the current search landscape and the importance for companies to provide search alternatives to Google. Lerman emphasizes that brands need to optimize their websites for search to keep customers from going to Google and finding competitors, highlighting Yext's mission to revolutionize company search functions. He also discusses the company's $2 billion valuation.

title: Here Are Barron’s 10 Top Stocks for the New Year
summary: Barron's has released its list of 10 top stock picks for the upcoming year, as the S&P 500 expects a 17% return by the end of a remarkable year. Investors are optimistic about 2021, anticipating the end of the pandemic and significant improvements in corporate earnings. The article highlights key CEOs whose companies are included in these picks.

title: Burger King teams up with Google to add online ordering
summary: Burger King is partnering with Google to integrate online ordering across Google Search, Maps, and Pay, allowing customers to find locations, order, and pay directly through Google. This move targets over 5,000 restaurants nationwide and includes a 20% cashback offer for Google Pay users on orders over $10. The initiative aims to boost online sales and reach a broader customer base, especially as Burger King plans mobile-focused restaurant designs and drive-thru modernizations following a 7% decline in comparable sales in Q3 2020.

title: Tastemade acquires ChefsFeed — plus other L.A. tech news
summary: Tastemade has acquired ChefsFeed, adding 100 million viewers and 6,000 chefs to its platform. This news comes alongside other L.A. tech updates, including a new electric delivery vehicle from Canoo, Rocket Lab's final rocket launch of the year, and the launch of BümoWork, a co-working space for parents and children.

title: Google's antitrust mess: Here are all the major cases it's facing in the U.S. and Europe
summary: Google is facing multiple antitrust challenges globally, including three major lawsuits in the U.S. filed by federal and state governments in the past two months. These U.S. cases follow earlier probes and significant fines levied by the European Commission against Google for alleged anticompetitive practices related to shopping comparison, Android, and online advertising. While Google denies all allegations, these cases could lead to substantial resolutions, though any significant outcome is likely years away and may not immediately impact the company's stock price.

title: How cloud computing can speed materials design
summary: Cloud computing is dramatically accelerating materials discovery by enabling scientists to screen millions of virtual compounds and predict their properties in a fraction of the time previously required. This advancement, building on computational materials science successes like Gorilla Glass, allows for more efficient design of novel materials across various fields. The use of large-scale physics-based simulations on cloud platforms like Google Cloud generates high-quality training data, boosting machine-learning models for even faster and more accurate material predictions.

title: How to find photos on your phone? Here's how I do it.
summary: This article provides practical advice on organizing and finding photos on a smartphone, addressing a common issue for many users. The author shares his personal method, which involves using professional tools like Adobe Lightroom and various cloud storage services including Amazon Photos and SmugMug. It also highlights how others, like Kristin Metcalfe, leverage built-in features such as Apple's "Places" tool, and discusses the evolving landscape of photo storage services with Google Photos' upcoming changes.

title: The cloud polyglot
summary: The article introduces the concept of a "cloud polyglot," referring to individuals capable of managing multiple cloud infrastructures, both on-premises and hyperscalers. It highlights the challenges of user experience fragmentation across various cloud platforms despite their similar underlying services. The author proposes NetApp ONTAP data management software and NetApp Cloud Manager as a potential solution to achieve a unified experience for managing storage and data in hybrid, multicloud environments.

title: Google’s self-driving spinoff signals big Mountain View expansion with sublease
summary: Waymo, Google's self-driving car spinoff, is expanding its presence in Mountain View with a new sublease for office space. This marks the first time Waymo's South Bay corporate employees will be housed outside of its Googleplex headquarters. The move signals a significant expansion for the autonomous driving technology company.

title: Exclusive: Apple targets car production by 2024 and eyes 'next level' battery technology - sources
summary: Apple Inc. is reportedly advancing its self-driving car technology with a target to produce a passenger vehicle by 2024, featuring its own groundbreaking battery design. This initiative, known as Project Titan, aims for a mass-market personal vehicle, contrasting with rivals' focus on robo-taxis. The company's innovative "monocell" battery design and use of LFP chemistry are expected to significantly reduce costs and increase range, though challenges in manufacturing and potential pandemic-related delays could push production to 2025 or later.

title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai's passion is building AI to deliver on company's moonshot ideas
summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai faces increasing legal and legislative threats against the company, treating regulatory engagement as a full-time job. Despite these challenges, Pichai remains focused on refocusing Google on artificial intelligence and honing Alphabet's "moonshot" ventures, envisioning a future where AI forms a coherent conglomerate of their diverse projects. He emphasizes adapting to innovation and ensuring Google's acquisitions and widespread platforms ultimately benefit users, while acknowledging the ongoing work needed to combat misinformation and address ethical concerns within AI development.

title: Machine Translation Market 2020-2024 | The Globalization Of Business to Boost Market Growth and Post a CAGR of 19% | Technavio
summary: The machine translation market is projected to grow by USD 971.87 million between 2020 and 2024, at a CAGR of 19%, driven primarily by the globalization of business. While this trend creates significant opportunities, data privacy and security risks in online translation services pose challenges for market participants. The report identifies key vendors, segmentation by application and geography, and highlights the increasing localization of video content as a key driver.

title: Ad-Tech Company AdTheorent Reaches $1 Billion SPAC Deal to Go Public
summary: Ad-Tech Company AdTheorent is nearing a SPAC deal valued at approximately $1 billion to go public. The firm, which uses machine learning to optimize advertising campaigns without relying on sensitive personal data, joins other digital advertising companies in leveraging SPACs for public listing. This move allows AdTheorent to bypass the traditional IPO process.

title: Google employees form union in rare move for a US tech giant
summary: Employees of Google and its parent company, Alphabet, have formed a new union called the Alphabet Workers Union, in a rare move for a major US technology company. The union, supported by the Communications Workers of America (CWA), aims to address issues like compensation, employee classification, and the types of work Google undertakes. This initiative follows years of workplace confrontations and dismissals of employee concerns by executives.

title: Why Apple became a $2 trillion company in 2020, and what could come next
summary: Apple's market valuation soared to over $2 trillion in 2020, largely due to a significant re-rating of its services business by investors, which now accounts for roughly half of its total value. While the iPhone remains crucial, the company faces challenges with its streaming content, risks to its Google search licensing revenue, and an undefined strategy for the EV market. Analysts are optimistic about continued growth, but some caution about the stock's valuation, given the service's growth rate and potential threats to key revenue streams like the Google licensing deal and App Store commissions.

title: Google's iOS apps haven't been updated in weeks. Could Apple's privacy labels be the reason?
summary: Not a single one of Google's iOS apps has been updated in almost a month, a period considered unusually long for a major tech company. This lack of updates coincides with Apple's new mandate, which started on December 8, requiring developers to publish privacy labels for any new apps or updates submitted to the App Store. It appears that by not updating its apps since December 7, Google has avoided providing these privacy labels for its iOS applications, as indicated by the "No Details Provided" message on their App Store listings.

title: YouTube Restores News Corp-Owned TalkRadio’s Channel After Brief Suspension
summary: YouTube briefly suspended the channel of News Corp-owned U.K. radio station TalkRadio due to alleged COVID-19 misinformation, but reinstated it hours later after further review. The platform cited its policy against content contradicting health authorities but made an exception, while TalkRadio maintained its robust editorial controls. The incident follows YouTube's expanded policies on COVID-19 and vaccine misinformation.

title: Bell Media president Wade Oosterman announces restructuring in bid to reclaim lost advertisers
summary: Bell Media president Wade Oosterman announced a restructuring of the division, including several executive departures, in response to a significant drop in advertising revenue amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. This move aims to streamline operations and enable investment in new content and technology to compete in the evolving media landscape. The company reported a 16.4% decline in operating revenues in the third quarter, reflecting the challenges faced by the traditional media industry.

title: Livestream shopping is the next big thing in retail
summary: Livestream shopping, initially popularized in China, is rapidly gaining traction globally, fueled by the pandemic and evolving consumer behavior. Mike George, President and CEO of Qurate Retail and Chairman of the National Retail Federation, highlights how retailers are adopting this interactive video approach to engage customers, building on Qurate's nearly 40 years of experience with live video shopping. While offering dazzling possibilities like AI-curated content and virtual reality, success hinges on building lasting customer relationships and competitive economics rather than just technological flash.

title: Online Entertainment Market Expected to Witness High Growth
summary: The online entertainment market, valued at $183,067.0 million in 2019, is projected to reach $652,455.0 million by 2027, growing at a CAGR of 20.82% from 2021 to 2027. This growth is driven by increased competition and strategic partnerships, with key players including Netflix, Google LLC, Facebook, Tencent Holdings Ltd, and Sony Corp. The report provides detailed segmentation, competitive analysis, and regional estimates for the market.

title: Device-Based Hybrids Solution for Mobile Network Operators in Canada
summary: Comtech discusses its perspective on the Emergency Services Working Group's (ESWG) recommendations for implementing device-based hybrid location solutions for Canadian Mobile Network Operators (MNOs). The article highlights the importance of combining handset-based and network-based location data to provide the most accurate locations for 911 calls, especially in indoor environments. Comtech's solution involves AML End Point functionality and enhanced Location Platforms to integrate and compare various location results for optimal accuracy and cybersecurity.

title: Survey: 29% of people would rather quit than return to the workplace
summary: A survey by LiveCareer indicates that 29% of individuals would prefer to quit their jobs rather than return to a physical workplace, with over 60% desiring to continue working from home post-pandemic. While companies are preparing for employees to return, with some making it mandatory, experts suggest that flexibility and compromise, like hybrid models, might be offered. Employees hesitant to return are advised to communicate with their managers, especially if health is a concern, and be prepared to discuss flexible arrangements.

title: Tesla market value crosses $800 billion for the first time
summary: Tesla's market capitalization surpassed $800 billion for the first time, driven by a 5.6% jump in its shares. This surge also propelled CEO Elon Musk past Jeff Bezos to become the world's wealthiest individual. The electric automaker's valuation now dwarfs the combined market caps of traditional Detroit automakers, despite its production being a fraction of larger rivals.

title: Tesla market value crosses $800 billion for the first time
summary: Tesla Inc.'s market capitalization surpassed $800 billion for the first time, driven by a significant jump in its stock price on Friday. This surge has also propelled CEO Elon Musk to become the world's richest man, surpassing Amazon's Jeff Bezos. The company's valuation now places it among Wall Street's most valuable firms, despite its production volume being a fraction of larger automotive rivals.

title: These Hot Stocks Made This American Century's Best 2020 U.S. Diversified Stock Fund
summary: The American Century Focused Dynamic Growth Fund (ACFSX) was the top-performing U.S. diversified stock fund in 2020, up 73.63% compared to the S&P 500's 18.40%. The fund achieved this success by investing in high-growth companies like Amazon, Facebook, Alphabet, Tesla, Square, DocuSign, Nike, Chipotle Mexican Grill, and Chegg, focusing on those with high sustainable growth rates and strong fundamentals, consistent with CAN SLIM principles. Its strong performance has earned it repeated IBD Best Mutual Funds Awards.

title: Comcast among U.S. companies taking a tough line on campaign donations after election challenge, Capitol takeover
summary: Comcast Corp. has joined other major U.S. corporations in suspending campaign donations to the 147 Republican politicians who voted against certifying the presidential election results following the January 6th Capitol takeover. While companies like Google, Facebook, and Microsoft halted all political contributions, Comcast and Marriott specifically targeted those who voted against certification, condemning the violence and seeking to review their political giving policies. This move by several firms signifies a significant shift in corporate political donations, with some companies requesting the return of previous contributions.

title: Going Rogue – a Mastermind Behind Android Malware Returns with a New RAT
summary: Check Point Research (CPR) identified "Triangulum," a darknet figure who evolved from an amateur developer to a mastermind in Android malware. Collaborating with "HexaGoN Dev," Triangulum created and distributed various malware, including the advanced "Rogue" Mobile Remote Access Trojan (MRAT). Rogue can steal data, modify files, and uses Google's Firebase to mask its malicious activities.

title: Howard Alum & 1st Black Female Google VP Appointed to PagerDuty Board of Directors
summary: Howard University alumna Bonita Stewart, the first Black female vice president at Google, has been appointed to the Board of Directors at PagerDuty, Inc. Stewart brings over 20 years of experience in leading multi-billion dollar operations and accelerating digital technology adoption. She also has public company board experience with Pluralsight (NASDAQ:PS) and Decker Outdoor Corporation (NYSE:DECK), and her appointment is seen as a move towards greater diversity and inclusion in tech.

title: Explainer: What is Parler and why has it been pulled offline?
summary: Parler, a social media network founded in 2018 as a "free speech-driven" space, has been largely adopted by U.S. conservatives. It was taken offline after Amazon suspended its web hosting service, following similar bans by Apple and Google. These companies cited Parler's failure to prevent the spread of posts inciting violence, particularly after the U.S. Capitol unrest, leading Parler to sue Amazon.

title: Oracle Debuts Major Release Of Its Flagship Database, First Since 2019
summary: Oracle has launched its new 21c Database, the first major release of its flagship database since 2019, incorporating features from a planned 2020 version that was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The update includes over 200 enhancements such as automated machine learning, blockchain tables for immutability, and persistent memory capabilities. Additionally, Oracle is making its APEX low-code development tools available as a managed cloud service on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) to help developers build data-driven applications more quickly and affordably.

title: Alabama A&M Partners With Apple's Innovative Propel Center
summary: Alabama A&M University is partnering with the Propel Center, a new global campus in Atlanta supported by Apple, Southern Company, and Ed Farm. This initiative, part of Apple's $100 million Racial Equity and Justice Initiative, aims to provide HBCU students and faculty with access to innovative curricula, technology, career opportunities, and fellowship programs. The Propel Center will offer educational tracks in AI, machine learning, agricultural technologies, social justice, app development, and creative arts, with expert mentorship and internship opportunities from Apple.

title: New Google Union Triples in Size in First Week, But Faces Formidable Challenges
summary: The Alphabet Workers Union, a new Google union, has tripled its membership to over 700 workers in its first week, reflecting growing activism in Silicon Valley. The union aims to give employees more influence over company operations but faces significant challenges, including Google's historical resistance to unions and strategies to "fissure" its workforce through diverse employment statuses. Critics question its partnership with the Communications Workers of America and its status as a minority union, not yet recognized by the NLRB or Google.

title: China’s autonomous driving hopeful WeRide raises $310 million
summary: WeRide, a Guangzhou-based driverless car startup, has secured $310 million in a Series B funding round led by Yutong Group, a commercial vehicle manufacturer. The company plans to conduct fully autonomous tests of 'Robotaxi' and 'Mini Robobus' services in 2021 and focuses on developing software and sensors for car makers rather than manufacturing vehicles. This funding aims to accelerate R&D and commercialization of its self-driving technologies, with trials of its Mini Robobus expected this month.

title: World's top 10 most valuable companies
summary: Apple is the most valuable company globally, with a valuation of $2.12 trillion, followed by Microsoft and Amazon. The 2020 Hurun Global 500 report also highlighted that 51 Chinese companies made the list, with their total value increasing significantly. Electric carmakers Nio and Xpeng Motors, along with Beike Zhaofang, were among the top gainers in percentage growth.

title: Google Defends Against Allegations Of Collusion With Facebook On Ads
summary: Adam Cohen, Google's director of economic policy, has refuted claims of collusion with Facebook regarding ad-sharing agreements, calling allegations by Texas attorney general Ken Paxton "misleading." The defense comes after a New York Times expose detailed an antitrust lawsuit suggesting Google provided special advantages to Facebook. Cohen clarified that Facebook competes in a crowded online advertising space and that their Open Bidding program is not manipulated in Facebook's favor, constituting less than 4% of Google's display ads.

title: Reliance on cloud, APIs create confusion and introduce risk into software development
summary: A survey by Radware and Osterman Research reveals that businesses face significant challenges in securing software development due to increased reliance on cloud hosting and APIs. Less than half of companies have integrated security into their CI/CD pipelines, and many struggle with confusion regarding cloud provider responsibilities and API security. The report emphasizes the need for stronger partnerships between development and security teams, and greater investment in API security solutions to manage new attack vectors.

title: How Google Won the 2020 Super Bowl with its Loretta Ad
summary: Google's "Loretta Ad" was deemed the real winner of the 2020 Super Bowl, despite the Kansas City Chiefs winning the game. The emotional ad, which depicted an elderly man remembering his deceased wife using Google products, garnered significant views and positive emotional responses, making it "The Most Effective Ad of Super Bowl LIV." Experts suggest the ad's success stemmed from its relatable storytelling, which created an emotional connection between viewers and the brand, highlighting the importance of storytelling in marketing.

title: Microsoft Is Leasing The Most Data Center Capacity In US
summary: Microsoft led U.S. data center capacity leasing in 2020, with capacity tripling nationwide compared to 2019. The company leased 178 megawatts in Virginia alone and is expanding its global data center footprint to support Microsoft Azure. Other major leasers included Bytedance (TikTok), Facebook, Oracle, Google, and Twitter, driven by the shift to remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Global Data Center Market Research 2021-2025 | Market Impact Analysis due to COVID-19 | Technavio
summary: The global data center market is projected to grow by USD 519.34 billion between 2021 and 2025, with a CAGR exceeding 21%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing adoption of multi-cloud strategies and necessary network upgrades to support 5G technology. The report analyzes the market's components and geographical landscape, offering insights into market sizing, forecast, and vendor analysis, while also considering the impact of COVID-19.

title: How to Negotiate for a Higher Salary and Better Perks on a Job Offer
summary: This article provides detailed advice on how to effectively negotiate a job offer, including salary and benefits, based on insights from Candor cofounder Niya Dragova. Key strategies include starting the negotiation early, avoiding disclosing salary expectations upfront, thoroughly understanding the full benefits package, and always negotiating via phone or video calls with a collaborative approach. The piece emphasizes that negotiation is always possible, even during economic slowdowns, and rarely leads to a rescinded offer.

title: Retail marketers invest in livestreams to establish shopping’s ‘next normal’
summary: Retail marketers are increasingly using shoppable livestreams to engage consumers and drive e-commerce sales, especially as the pandemic keeps shoppers at home. Major brands like Ulta Beauty, Walmart, and Anne Klein are leveraging these interactive mobile experiences to demonstrate products and build direct customer relationships. The trend, already popular in Asia, is gaining traction in the U.S. with platforms like Amazon Live, Shoploop, and TikTok, showing significant growth potential.

title: Young Industry, Old Roots | The 9 Veteran Startups of Quantum Tech
summary: This article identifies and ranks nine veteran startups in the quantum technology space, challenging the common misconception about the oldest companies in the field. It highlights pioneers like D-Wave Systems, MagiQ Technologies, and even non-quantum-focused companies that pivoted into the sector, such as Oxford Instruments and High Precision Devices. The piece also acknowledges later entrants that established themselves despite early skepticism towards quantum technology.

title: Digital ad firm Taboola plans to go public via SPAC
summary: Digital ad company Taboola announced plans to go public through a merger with ION Acquisition Corp., a special acquisition corporation. The transaction, expected to close in Q2, will value Taboola at approximately $2.6 billion and result in the company trading on the NYSE under the symbol TBLA. CEO Adam Singolda emphasized the importance of the open web and Taboola's goal to expand recommendations beyond content to e-commerce, apps, and games across various devices.

title: Clarivate Launches Web of Science My Research Assistant Mobile Application
summary: Clarivate Plc launched Web of Science My Research Assistant, a new mobile application designed to help scientific researchers search, save, and share publication records from the Web of Science citation index. The app offers features like personalized feeds and reading lists, with both free and unlimited functionality available depending on the user's institutional affiliation. This initiative aims to improve the researcher experience by providing a more personalized service and fostering collaboration within the science community.

title: TikTok fixes privacy issue discovered by Check Point Research
summary: Check Point Research discovered a privacy vulnerability in TikTok's "friend finder" feature that could allow an attacker to link profile details with phone numbers, creating a database of users. This vulnerability primarily affected users who associated a phone number with their account. Check Point Research responsibly disclosed the issue to TikTok, which promptly deployed a fix to secure user data.

title: Businesses Gain Unparalleled Collaboration and Productivity With Motorola Solutions’ New Smart Radio
summary: Motorola Solutions announced the launch of its new MOTOTRBO Ion smart radio, designed to enhance collaboration and productivity for businesses. This smart radio combines reliable voice communication with broadband data, a full Android interface, and an open application ecosystem. It aims to integrate business workflows, leveraging capabilities like a 13-megapixel camera and a 4-inch touchscreen for various industries.

title: ServiceNow, Salesforce deliver vaccine management tech
summary: Salesforce and ServiceNow have both released new vaccine management tools to assist healthcare providers, public health agencies, and employers with COVID-19 immunization efforts. Salesforce's Vaccine Cloud offers appointment scheduling, data management, and follow-up communications, while ServiceNow's Vaccine Administration Management tool boasts customers including the state of North Carolina. These platforms aim to simplify the complex logistical challenges of mass vaccination, including supply chain tracking, consent management, and varying dosage requirements.

title: Buying Signavio, SAP gets into business transformation-as-a-service
summary: SAP has launched a new offering called "RISE with SAP," which aims to provide "Business transformation-as-a-Service" to help enterprises achieve digital transformation by moving to a cloud and subscription-based model. As part of this initiative, SAP is acquiring Signavio GmbH, a company specializing in business process intelligence, to enhance its capabilities in business process redesign. The RISE with SAP service bundles contracts, SLAs, operations, and support into a single subscription, with customers already operating under this model.

title: British Hedge Fund Billionaire Takes Climate Fight to S&P 500
summary: Billionaire hedge-fund manager Christopher Hohn is funding a campaign to compel major S&P 500 companies to publish carbon-emission reduction plans and subject them to shareholder votes. Frustrated by slow corporate action on climate change, Hohn aims to achieve this with at least 100 companies by the end of 2022, using both voluntary engagement and proxy battles. His firm, TCI Fund Management Ltd., has already filed resolutions with companies like Alphabet Inc. and Charter Communications Inc., with similar efforts in Europe and Australia.

title: Google to stop using Apple tool to track iPhone users, avoiding new pop-up warning
summary: Google has announced that its iPhone apps, including Maps and YouTube, will cease using Apple's IDFA tool for personalizing ads. This move comes as Apple prepares to enforce new tracking transparency rules that would require apps to obtain explicit user consent via a pop-up warning, which Google aims to avoid. While Google's core ad business may not be significantly impacted due to its logged-in user base, the company warns that publishers and advertisers relying on its mobile ad software will likely see weaker results without IDFA access.

title: Television makers see brighter prospects
summary: China's television manufacturing industry expects an 8.4% revenue increase to 131.1 billion yuan ($20.3 billion) in 2021, driven by new-generation flat-panel display technologies and consumption upgrades. Despite a 9.1% unit sales drop in 2020 due to COVID-19, online sales soared, and larger, intelligent TVs along with advanced display technologies like 8K, QLED, OLED, and Micro LED are fueling market growth and competition among manufacturers.

title: Google & Facebook laws just a back rub for News and Nine
summary: The article argues that proposed Australian laws aimed at making Google and Facebook pay for news content are merely a "back rub" for large media companies like News Corp and Nine, rather than a genuine effort to protect consumers or promote quality journalism. Author Kim Wingerei suggests alternatives to financial penalties, such as licensing search engines and regulating social media platforms as publishers, to address their market power, privacy issues, and the spread of misinformation. He views Google's threat to withdraw services from Australia as a real, albeit last-resort, consequence.

title: Amazon, Alphabet and Salesforce are all investing in a $28 billion company that crunches big data
summary: Databricks, a company specializing in big data processing and AI model deployment, has raised $1 billion in new funding, bringing its valuation to $28 billion. Prominent investors include Amazon Web Services, Alphabet's CapitalG, Salesforce Ventures, and existing investor Microsoft. This investment highlights the recognition from top cloud providers of Databricks' potential, similar to Snowflake, in helping companies manage and analyze large datasets.

title: Ford bets on Google Cloud for its digital transformation
summary: Ford has announced a new partnership with Google, making Google Cloud its preferred cloud provider. This collaboration will bring Android Automotive to Ford and Lincoln vehicles starting in 2023 and aims to digitally transform Ford's operations from product development to manufacturing and supply chain management using Google Cloud's AI tools. The partnership also seeks to leverage data for new monetization opportunities and improve customer experiences.

title: Microsoft's Bing ready to step in if Google pulls search from Australia, minister says
summary: Australia's Communications Minister Paul Fletcher stated that Microsoft's Bing is prepared to take over if Google follows through on its threat to withdraw search services from Australia due to the proposed mandatory news code. Fletcher downplayed Google's threat, emphasized that the government would not back down on the code, and highlighted Microsoft's strong interest in expanding Bing's presence in the Australian market. The minister reiterated that companies operating in Australia must comply with its laws.

title: Pandemic cloud migration push to have lasting impact
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated cloud migrations in 2020, leading to permanent changes in enterprise cloud strategies and spending habits. Gartner and IDC reports indicate a substantial increase in public cloud spending and a shift towards cloud-first approaches, driven by the need for cost optimization and commercial elasticity. The adoption of multi-cloud strategies and new billing models from vendors like IBM further reflect the lasting impact of the pandemic on cloud computing.

title: ‘Bad Bets’: Antitrust Class Action Alleges Major Brokerages, Hedge Funds, Clearinghouses Conspired Against Ordinary Investors
summary: An antitrust class action lawsuit alleges that major brokerages, hedge funds, and clearinghouses conspired to prevent non-professional investors from controlling their investments during a social media-driven price surge. The complaint asserts that these entities disabled buy features on trading platforms for certain "meme stocks" like GameStop, forcing retail investors to sell at lower prices and artificially reducing stock values to mitigate losses from their short positions. The lawsuit seeks to represent investors who purchased specific securities and were impacted by the alleged anticompetitive conduct between January 1, 2021, and the cessation of the illicit activities.

title: Apple, Its Control Over the iPhone, and The Internet
summary: This article examines Apple's extensive control over the iPhone ecosystem and its implications for the internet, competition, and future digital economies. It argues that Apple's policies, while leading to success, inhibit innovation and create anti-competitive barriers for developers and users through its App Store, payment systems, and technology decisions. The author suggests regulatory intervention to force competition in app distribution and payments, allowing users to download apps from any source and developers to use alternative payment solutions.

title: White & Case Advises Deutsche Bank on Strategic Partnership with Google Cloud
summary: Global law firm White & Case LLP advised Deutsche Bank AG on a strategic, multi-year partnership with Google Cloud. This partnership aims to accelerate Deutsche Bank’s transition to cloud services and facilitate the co-innovation of new products and services. White & Case provided comprehensive advice on contractual, regulatory, IP, and data protection aspects of the transaction.

title: Google Settles With Labor Department for $3.8 Million over Hiring, Pay Discrimination Claim
summary: Google has settled with the U.S. Department of Labor for $3.8 million over allegations of systemic discrimination in compensation and hiring practices affecting women software engineers and Asian applicants. The settlement addresses pay disparities at Google’s offices in Seattle, Kirkland, and Mountain View, and hiring discrepancies at San Francisco, Sunnyvale, and Kirkland locations between 2014 and 2017. As part of the agreement, Google will pay back wages and interest to over 5,500 individuals, commit funds for future pay equity adjustments, and enhance its non-discrimination policies.

title: EX-99.2
summary: CCC Information Services Inc. is set to go public through a SPAC merger with Dragoneer Growth Opportunities Corp. in a deal valuing the IT provider for car insurers at $6.5 billion. The total deal, including debt, is worth $7 billion, confirming an earlier Wall Street Journal report. The transaction, expected to close in the second quarter, will generate nearly $1 billion in proceeds for CCC, which plans to invest in software research and development.

title: Here’s how the FAANG companies stack up this earnings season
summary: This article examines the performance of FAANG companies during the latest earnings season, highlighting their continued impressive growth in revenue and display of pricing power. Despite their large size and the challenges posed by the pandemic, these companies maintained successful growth strategies in the fourth quarter and throughout the previous year. The piece underscores the dominance of FAANG stocks in earnings reports.

title: World’s Fastest-Growing Cloud Vendors: #1 Google, #2 Oracle, #3 Microsoft & ServiceNow, #5 Amazon
summary: The article identifies the five fastest-growing major cloud vendors based on their Q4 growth rates and revenue. Google Cloud led with 46.5% growth, followed by Oracle, Microsoft, ServiceNow, and Amazon Web Services, collectively generating about $37 billion in Q4 cloud revenue. The author emphasizes the significance of these growth rates in the context of the unprecedented expansion of the cloud market and its profound global impact on various industries and daily life.

title: BNY Mellon, Google Cloud technology to predict Treasury settlement failures
summary: BNY Mellon has partnered with Google Cloud to develop AI and machine learning technology aimed at predicting U.S. Treasury settlement failures for its clients. This new technology can predict around 40% of eligible settlement failures with 90% accuracy, helping to mitigate liquidity problems in the $22 trillion U.S. Treasury market. The model analyzes supply and demand, trading velocity, and counterparty activity to make these predictions.

title: Chris Lyons: Where Tech Meets Culture
summary: Chris Lyons, head of Andreessen Horowitz's Cultural Leadership Fund, discusses how the fund connects Black cultural leaders with tech companies and elevates African-American creators in the tech industry. He explains the rationale behind the fund, its unique all-African-American LP structure, and its mission to foster entrepreneurship and generational wealth within the Black community by increasing access and exposure to technology and venture capital. Lyons also shares his personal journey from audio engineer to Silicon Valley investor, emphasizing the importance of networking and service.

title: Global Payments and Google Form Strategic Partnership to Reimagine Digital Payments
summary: Global Payments and Google have announced a multi-year strategic partnership to transform digital payments for merchants worldwide. This collaboration involves Global Payments migrating its merchant acquiring technology to Google Cloud and becoming Google's worldwide merchant acquiring provider. The partnership will also focus on co-selling opportunities and product innovation, integrating Google's public APIs with Global Payments' software to offer a comprehensive suite of cloud-based solutions to merchants.

title: Employee activism gives life to tech union organizing
summary: The rise of employee activism in the tech sector significantly correlates with increased union organizing efforts. Unlike traditional unionization focused on wages, these tech unions prioritize social issues and values alignment, as seen with groups like the Alphabet Workers Union. While organizing highly skilled workers remains challenging, experts believe a shift in professional identity perception and a broader trend of political activism moving into corporations are driving this change, despite typical corporate resistance to unionization.

title: Why Archer, a flying taxi company you've never heard of before, just listed on the NYSE with a $3.8 billion valuation
summary: Archer, a Palo Alto-based flying taxi company, is going public through a SPAC merger with Atlas Crest Investment Corp., achieving a valuation of $3.8 billion. The company has secured significant backing from United Airlines and Stellantis (Fiat Chrysler), with United committing to purchase $1 billion worth of its future aircraft. Archer plans to develop electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft (eVTOLs) for short-range urban travel, with an ambitious target to begin operations by 2024.

title: Introducing your 2021 Marketo Engage Champions!
summary: Adobe has announced its 2021 Marketo Engage Champions, marking the 10th anniversary of the program. This elite group comprises Marketo Engage experts and advocates who share their knowledge, support others, and provide feedback to Adobe's product teams. Champions benefit from career development, speaking opportunities, and connections within the Marketo Engage community.

title: Expedia Group pulls Vrbo from Google’s vacation rental metasearch product
summary: Expedia Group has removed Vrbo from Google's vacation rental metasearch product because the company found the investment unproductive and the customer experience not valuable. CEO Peter Kern stated that Vrbo is seeing strong direct traffic and the company is focusing on more profitable ways to drive traffic and increasing brand marketing for its alternative accommodation brands. Expedia Group's financial results for Q4 2020 showed significant revenue and gross booking decreases, though trends were improving by January.

title: Salesforce Embraces Flexible, Remote Work for Post-Pandemic
summary: Salesforce announced a new flexible work policy for its employees post-pandemic, offering options including flexible schedules, full-time remote, or fully office-based work. This move aims to boost equality, broaden talent search beyond traditional city centers, and remove hurdles for employees, following similar trends among other tech giants. The company plans to redesign its offices for collaboration and will implement health screenings for those returning to physical workspaces.

title: Data gathering: University of Delaware’s virtual Big Data conference convened experts on emerging analysis techniques
summary: The University of Delaware's virtual "Big Data in Railroad Maintenance Planning" conference, held in December 2020, brought together over 260 participants to discuss emerging data science approaches for railroads. Experts presented on using predictive analytics and AI to prevent locomotive engine failures, enhance crossing safety, detect trespassing, and predict broken rails. The conference highlighted how Big Data can transform vast amounts of railroad information into actionable intelligence for improved safety, operations, and maintenance.

title: Alphabet, Microsoft, Qualcomm protest Nvidia's Arm acquisition - Bloomberg News
