summary: Alphabet, Microsoft, and Qualcomm have reportedly lodged complaints with U.S. antitrust regulators regarding Nvidia's proposed acquisition of Arm Ltd. Nvidia had previously announced a deal with SoftBank Group in September to purchase Arm. This development indicates significant opposition from major tech companies over the acquisition.

title: Bumble CEO: 'If you want to behave poorly, you cannot do it here'
summary: Bumble CEO Whitney Wolfe Herd emphasizes the dating app's strict zero-tolerance policy against hate speech and toxic behavior, including body shaming, racism, and homophobia. The company, which recently went public, aims to hold users accountable for their actions online, reflecting Herd's personal mission to empower women and curb harmful conduct. Bumble has also supported legislation against cyberflashing and plans to expand its services to support women through various life stages.

title: Spotify set for uphill battle in South Korea
summary: Spotify recently launched its service in South Korea, a market already dominated by local music streaming services like Melon, Genie Music, and Flo. Despite its global presence, Spotify faces challenges including a lack of content from major Korean artists due to an unconfirmed deal with Kakao M, and increasing competition from both established local players bolstering their services and new contenders like Clubhouse. The company hopes to succeed by offering tailored playlists, a vast catalog, and launching podcast services, but its success is not guaranteed in this competitive landscape.

title: Sonos One vs Apple HomePod: Which smart speaker should you buy?
summary: This article compares the Sonos One and Apple HomePod smart speakers to help consumers decide which one to purchase. It evaluates them based on price, multi-room system compatibility, music service support, control methods, and loudness. The Sonos One typically comes out ahead for versatility and value, while the HomePod is preferred for Apple users with larger rooms and deeper pockets.

title: Apple wins victory as North Dakota votes down bill that would regulate app stores
summary: The North Dakota state senate has voted down a bill that would have required app stores like Apple's and Google's to allow developers to use their own payment processing software, thereby avoiding the up to 30% fees charged. This decision is a win for Apple, which argued that its tight control over the App Store is essential for user safety and product integrity. The proposed legislation, despite being defeated, highlights ongoing debates at state and federal levels regarding the commercial power of tech giants and their app store policies, fueled by efforts from groups like the Coalition for App Fairness.

title: An Interview With Twilio CEO Jeff Lawson
summary: This article features an interview with Twilio CEO Jeff Lawson, author of "Ask Your Developer," discussing how companies can harness the power of software developers to win in the 21st century. Lawson emphasizes the "build or die" philosophy, where software development is a core competency for modern businesses and highlights the importance of organizing companies into small, autonomous teams and empowering developers to solve business problems rather than just implementing prescribed solutions. The interview also touches on Twilio's own practices, including requiring all employees to build an app, and the company's focus on markets outside of China.

title: Another giant podcast buy: iHeartMedia to acquire Triton Digital for $230m
summary: iHeartMedia has announced its agreement to acquire Triton Digital for $230 million, a move that further consolidates its position in the audio advertising technology and podcasting space. Triton Digital is an Advertising Technology SaaS platform specializing in audio streaming, podcasting, and metrics, operating in over 50 countries. This acquisition follows iHeartMedia's recent purchase of Voxnest and other investments, highlighting a trend of significant podcast and audio tech buyouts in the industry.

title: Deloitte to acquire The Working Group Inc. to enhance digital and cloud transformation
summary: Deloitte is acquiring Toronto-based digital consulting firm, The Working Group Inc. (TWG), to boost its digital and cloud transformation capabilities for mid-market and large clients. This acquisition aims to enhance Deloitte's global digital strategy and expand its offerings in product strategy, design, and engineering. TWG's team of 150 employees will integrate into Deloitte Canada's Consulting practice, strengthening its position as a leader in Canadian digital transformation.

title: News Corp signs news partnership deal with Google
summary: News Corp has finalized a global news partnership with Google, encompassing a subscription platform, advertising revenue sharing, and the development of audio and video journalism. This extensive deal concludes years of tension between Rupert Murdoch's media empire and the tech giant, especially in Australia, where Google had threatened to cease operations due to proposed content laws. The agreement follows similar deals News Corp struck with Apple and Facebook, marking a significant win for media companies seeking compensation for their premium content from large digital platforms.

title: Google and J.B. Hunt Announce Strategic Alliance to Accelerate Innovation in Transportation and Logistics
summary: Google and J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc. have announced a multi-year strategic alliance to accelerate J.B. Hunt's digital transformation and collaborate on next-generation supply chain platform technology. By leveraging Google Cloud's AI and ML tools, J.B. Hunt aims to enhance its J.B. Hunt 360° platform, enabling greater efficiency, visibility, and predictive analytics in the transportation and logistics industry. This partnership seeks to digitally transform the shipping experience for shippers, carriers, and service providers, ultimately creating a more efficient transportation network in North America.

title: J.B. Hunt Enlists Google to Match Carriers With Shippers
summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. is partnering with Google to leverage AI and machine-learning models to enhance its freight-matching segment. This collaboration aims to improve the pairing of shippers with carriers on its J.B. Hunt 360 platform. The goal is to help shippers predict supply and demand and enable carriers to estimate future fuel and transportation costs more accurately, strengthening J.B. Hunt's brokerage business amidst competition from digital-only rivals.

title: J.B. Hunt Teams up with Google for Next-Generation Supply Chain Technology
summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services is partnering with Google Cloud in a multi-year strategic alliance to enhance its J.B. Hunt 360 platform. This collaboration will leverage Google's artificial intelligence and machine learning tools to improve supply chain visibility, efficiency, and real-time decision-making for shippers and carriers. The initiative aims to centralize data and build upon J.B. Hunt's existing efforts to transform the logistics industry with advanced technology.

title: Clean200 Surges Ahead of MSCI ACWI Global Index, Leaves Index of Dirty Energy Companies in the Dust
summary: The seventh update of the Carbon Clean 200 report by As You Sow and Corporate Knights reveals that Clean200 companies, focused on clean energy, significantly outperformed the MSCI ACWI broad market index and the MSCI ACWI/Energy Index of fossil fuel companies. Since its inception on July 1, 2016, through January 31, 2021, the Clean200 generated a total return of 113.41%, compared to 78.67% for the broad market and a -13.83% for fossil fuel companies. This report highlights the strong financial performance of sustainable solutions and the market's growing confidence in the clean energy sector.

title: Understanding the mobile experience on T-Mobile’s standalone 5G network
summary: Opensignal analyzed the impact of T-Mobile's standalone (SA) 5G network launch on August 4, 2020, on user experience. The study found that SA 5G significantly increased 5G Availability, especially in rural areas, and improved latency. However, download speeds on SA 5G were slower than on non-standalone (NSA) 5G due to T-Mobile's focus on extending reach with its 600 MHz band and limitations of early 5G smartphone chipsets, which are expected to improve with newer models supporting carrier aggregation.

title: J.B. Hunt, Google partner to develop new supply chain technology
summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. and Google have formed a multi-year partnership to accelerate J.B. Hunt's digital transformation and develop next-generation supply chain technology, leveraging Google's Data Cloud and AI/ML tools. This collaboration aims to enhance J.B. Hunt 360, centralize data, improve efficiency, and provide predictive analytics for the logistics industry. Analysts from Stephens Inc. see this alliance as a significant driver for J.B. Hunt's strategic plan and their long-term position as a digital disrupter in the transportation sector.

title: JB Hunt partners with Google, as real-time visibility becomes trucking commodity
summary: J.B. Hunt has announced a multi-year partnership with Google Cloud to enhance its J.B. Hunt 360 digital platform. The collaboration aims to improve visibility, leverage AI and machine learning for predictive analytics, and develop new solutions for real-time data and predictive modeling. This initiative responds to the industry's need for greater transparency and efficiency in the backdrop of tight capacity and driver shortages.

title: Waze's ex-CEO says app could have 'grown faster' without Google
summary: Noam Bardin, the former CEO of Waze, stated that the navigation app's growth was stifled under Google's ownership, suggesting it could have grown faster independently. He cited Google's promotion of Google Maps over Waze, Waze's financial losses, and Google imposing constraints while copying Waze's ideas. This sentiment reignites antitrust concerns regarding Google's 2013 acquisition of Waze.

title: Google parent-backed health insurance start-up eyes massive IPO
summary: Oscar Health, a health insurance start-up backed by Google's parent company Alphabet Inc., is preparing for an initial public offering (IPO) aiming to raise up to $1.05 billion. Share prices are expected to range between $32 and $34, potentially valuing the company at $6.7 billion. Founded in 2012 by Mario Schlosser, Josh Kushner, and Kevin Nazemi, the tech-driven insurer has seen significant growth, especially in virtual health services during the COVID-19 pandemic, and seeks to replicate the public market success of other venture-backed insurers.

title: Arrastrados por Banco Supervielle, el S&P Merval perdió 3,3% y los ADR cayeron hasta 10%
summary: On February 22, 2021, the S&P Merval index fell 3.3%, primarily driven by a significant drop in Banco Supervielle shares. Argentine ADRs also experienced declines of up to 10%, while the country risk rose by 0.9%. This downturn mirrored negative trends on Wall Street, influenced by rising US Treasury bond yields and inflation concerns.

title: S|W: The SaaS Weekly – Uberize the workforce
summary: This S|W: The SaaS Weekly newsletter covers various SaaS industry news, including Benevity securing new investments, Boast.ai receiving a $100 million credit facility for R&D tax credits, and RocketRez raising an $8.4 million Series A round. The article also touches on broader topics like the gig economy's expansion, Google's talks with Canadian publishers, and Dropbox's financial shift due to remote work.

title: ADT and DISH Network Partner to Bring Smart Home Security to More Customers
summary: ADT Inc. and DISH Network Corporation announced a partnership where DISH will provide marketing, sales, and installation services for ADT smart home security products. This collaboration expands ADT's reach to existing and potential subscribers, particularly in rural and exurban areas, leveraging DISH's nationwide network and its subsidiary OnTech Smart Services. The partnership aims to offer integrated smart home and security solutions to DISH's more than 20 million subscribers.

title: Security top of mind for digital transformation projects
summary: A new ASUG and Onapsis survey reveals that security is a top concern for SAP customers undertaking S/4HANA migrations and other digital transformation projects, especially when moving to the cloud. The survey indicated that these modernization projects have not been significantly slowed by the COVID-19 pandemic. While cloud providers handle some security aspects, organizations remain responsible for data security and for addressing the unique complexities and vulnerabilities of SAP applications in a hybrid IT environment.

title: Google, Trustpilot, TripAdvisor – the challenge of online reviews
summary: This article discusses the growing challenge businesses face with online reviews on platforms like Google, Trustpilot, and TripAdvisor. It highlights the difficulty in managing negative reviews, particularly those that are defamatory or stray into data protection issues. The piece prominently features the English High Court case of Summerfield Browne Ltd v Waymouth, where a law firm successfully sued a former client for a defamatory Trustpilot review, resulting in £25,000 in damages and an order for review removal.

title: LG opens WebOS TV platform to third-party TV manufacturers
summary: LG Electronics has announced that its webOS TV platform will now be available to other TV brand partners, making it no longer exclusive to LG products. This move follows a significant overhaul of webOS, showcased at CES 2021, and has already garnered commitments from approximately twenty TV manufacturers globally. LG aims to expand the webOS ecosystem by partnering with major streaming services and leveraging its acquisition of Alphonso Inc. for enhanced user experience.

title: Viewpoint: J.B. Hunt, Google team up to build another supply chain platform
summary: J.B. Hunt and Google have partnered to leverage Google Cloud’s AI and machine learning tools with J.B. Hunt’s logistics expertise to create a more efficient North American transportation network. This collaboration aims to accelerate J.B. Hunt's digital transformation and develop next-generation supply chain platform technology. The partnership is expected to evolve J.B. Hunt 360 from a transaction platform into an innovation platform by enabling supply-side innovations, which are crucial for disrupting traditional freight brokerage.

title: Why Are Google and Facebook Now Okay with Australia’s News Media Bargaining Code?
summary: Google and Facebook have come to terms with Australia's News Media Bargaining Code, which mandates payment to news publishers. While initially opposed, their agreements with major news organizations and the inclusion of a compulsory mediation stage have made the legislation more palatable. The Code aims to address the significant bargaining power imbalance between digital platforms and news media, potentially leading to substantial financial contributions for journalism, though concerns remain about media diversity and the focus on larger publishers.

title: Google Sued for Refusing to Redeem Google Play Gift Cards
summary: Google and Alphabet, Inc. are facing a class-action lawsuit for allegedly refusing to redeem Google Play gift cards in accordance with California law. The lawsuit claims Google erects barriers to redemption, including demanding detailed purchase information, which can render gift cards "impossible" to use, especially for recipients of gifts. The plaintiff, who experienced these issues, alleges that Google's conduct violates California's Gift Card Law, Unfair Competition Law, and constitutes a breach of contract, seeking class certification, restitution, damages, and other relief.

title: Google Cloud Big Data: Build a Big Data Architecture on GCP
summary: This article explores how to build a big data architecture on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), highlighting its suitability for massive data storage and parallel processing. It details various GCP services like BigQuery, Dataflow, and Dataproc, which support big data analytics. The article also provides best practices for data ingestion, using streaming inserts, and organizing resources with nested tables for optimized performance and cost efficiency.

title: Palo Alto Networks appoints Anil Valluri as regional VP - India and SAARC
summary: Palo Alto Networks has appointed Anil Valluri as the regional vice president for India and the SAARC region. Valluri, previously with Google India, will focus on driving growth, expanding the company's technology footprint, and building strategic alliances. He brings extensive experience from his prior roles, including eight years as President for NetApp in the India and SAARC region.

title: Manbang Group loads up billion-dollar IPO
summary: Manbang Group, a China-based trucking services provider backed by Tencent, SoftBank, and Alibaba, has confidentially filed for a US IPO aiming to raise at least $1 billion. The company, also known as Full Truck Alliance, operates an online platform for truck bookings and was valued at nearly $12 billion in its last funding round in November 2020, where it secured $1.7 billion. Previous investors include Alphabet’s CapitalG unit, Vision Fund, and various other capital firms.

title: Wearable Device Maker Huami Steps Out of Xiaomi’s Shadow
summary: Huami Corp. is rebranding outside China to Zepp Health Corp. and changing its ticker symbol to ZEPP, indicating a strategic move away from its long-standing relationship with Xiaomi. This rebranding is supported by a series of global acquisitions, investments, and partnerships aimed at establishing its own identity and improving its financial margins, which have been pressured by its association with Xiaomi. Despite declaring independence, Huami recently extended its "most preferred partner" status agreement with Xiaomi, highlighting a cautious approach to separation.

title: Exclusive: Infosys wins $500 million all-digital deal from Google
summary: Infosys has secured a nearly $500 million deal from Google to provide customer experience and engineering support for Google's products. This engagement signifies Infosys's increased collaboration with major tech companies. The scope of work includes customer experience, language support, business process requirements, and data management.

title: Companies That Prioritize Workforce Investment and Training Outperform Those That Don’t
summary: This article highlights that companies investing in workforce development and training outperform those that do not, based on an analysis of Russell 1000 companies. The top quintile of companies in terms of Workforce Investment and Training scores outperformed the bottom quintile by 5.01% over the past year. This underscores the importance of employee advancement, skills development, and educational opportunities for improved business outcomes like productivity and customer satisfaction.

title: Arizona House passes bill that threatens Apple and Google's app stores
summary: The Arizona House of Representatives passed a bill (HB 2005) that would compel app stores, specifically targeting Apple and Google, to allow app makers to use their own payment processing software to bypass the 15-30% fees charged. The legislation, which passed 31-29, is a setback for Apple and Google but a victory for groups like the Coalition for App Fairness. While the bill still requires Senate approval and the governor's signature, it highlights ongoing legislative efforts to regulate app store policies following criticism of their alleged anticompetitive practices.

title: Murphy’s Law: Fiserv Had ‘Most Overpaid’ CEO
summary: A new study by "As You Sow" found that former Fiserv CEO Jeffery Yabuki was the 15th most overpaid CEO in 2020, making 428 times the average worker's salary. His annual compensation was $27.6 million, $13.8 million more than deemed appropriate, highlighting the growing wealth gap. The report also identified Sundar Pichai of Alphabet Inc. and David M. Zaslov of Discovery, Inc. as the top two most overpaid CEOs, with shareholder opposition to such pay packages increasing.

title: KT and LG U+ buy into OneStore, the Google Play killer
summary: South Korean mobile carriers KT and LG U+ have acquired stakes in One Store, a local app market, joining SK Telecom to challenge the dominance of Google Play and Apple App Store. This strategic investment aims to bolster the domestic IT ecosystem and comes as foreign app markets face increasing criticism over their in-app payment policies. One Store saw a significant increase in transaction volume and turned a profit for the first time in 2020, benefiting from the controversy surrounding Google's 30 percent commission policy.

title: BUZZ, the ETF of Social-Media Darlings, Drops in Trading Debut
summary: The VanEck Vectors Social Sentiment ETF (BUZZ) began trading, aiming to capitalize on the retail-investing trend and the influence of social media buzz on stock performance. This ETF includes stocks like Tesla and DraftKings, aiming to capture the "new era of investing" where information is sourced and shared online.

title: Google won’t use other web tracking tools after phasing out cookies
summary: Google has announced it will not create or use alternative web tracking technologies after phasing out third-party cookies from its Chrome browser next year. This move is intended to address growing data privacy concerns and reshape online advertising practices. While Google will not replace cookies with other individual tracking methods, it will continue to explore ways for businesses to target large, anonymous groups of users with shared interests.

title: Stock Prices & Quotes with Live Stock Market Charts
summary: This article provides real-time stock prices, quotes, live stock charts, and historical information for publicly traded companies. It features a comprehensive list of top stocks by market capitalization, including major technology and financial firms, along with their current prices, daily changes, volume, and P/E ratios. The platform also offers market data for total market cap, BTC dominance, 24h volume, BTC price, S&P 500, gold, and USD/EUR exchange rates.

title: Westside Pavilion transforms into a Google office campus
summary: The former Westside Pavilion shopping mall is being redeveloped into a Google-anchored office campus called One Westside, a $475-million project by Hudson Pacific Properties and Macerich. The Gensler-designed office space will span 584,000 square feet, making use of the mall's existing structure, and is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2022. Google has signed a 14-year lease for the entire property upon its completion.

title: Liberty Media CEO Sees Amazon Driving Big Tech’s TV Sports Rights Ambitions
summary: Liberty Media CEO Greg Maffei believes Amazon is leading the charge for Big Tech platforms to acquire more international sports rights, driven by their increasing involvement in agreements like NFL games. Maffei highlighted the growing seriousness of Amazon's investments in sports content and predicted other tech giants would follow suit. He also noted that the break up of the cable bundle and pressure on regional sports networks are contributing factors to Silicon Valley's pursuit of global sports rights.

title: The Sonos Roam is a small, portable smart speaker for $169
summary: Sonos has unveiled its smallest and most portable smart speaker to date, the Sonos Roam, priced at $169. This lightweight device, weighing under a pound, is designed for on-the-go use and features an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance, as well as Qi wireless charging compatibility. It boasts enhanced sound quality with Automatic TruePlay Tuning, connects via Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and supports over 100 streaming services and multiple voice assistants.

title: WWE® SuperCard Celebrates 25 Years of “Stone Cold” Steve Austin with New Content Available Now
summary: 2K has announced new content for WWE SuperCard to celebrate the 25th anniversary of "Stone Cold" Steve Austin's WWE debut. Throughout March, players can enjoy new items and events, including a "Stone Cold" Steve Austin cardback, his iconic jean shorts, and a "Stone Cold" Fusion event starting March 9th to create Special Edition cards.

title: Zwift Adds Twitter’s Pichette, Lululemon’s Burgoyne to Board
summary: Online fitness platform Zwift has appointed Patrick Pichette, current chairman of Twitter, and Celeste Burgoyne of Lululemon to its board of directors. Pichette is a partner at Inovia Capital, an investment firm that has backed Zwift. The company's CEO, Min, stated that a public markets debut is anticipated in the future, and Zwift plans to launch equipment, including an indoor bike, in 2022.

title: The 10 most innovative companies in consumer electronics
summary: This article highlights the top 10 most innovative companies in consumer electronics, showcasing how they adapted and thrived during the pandemic by releasing useful new products. It features companies like Corning, Apple, and Samsung alongside newer players such as Raspberry Pi, Tempo, and Aira. The piece details Corning's advancements in Gorilla Glass and Ceramic Shield, emphasizing their impact on device durability.

title: How Google’s New Career Certificates Could Disrupt the College Degree (Exclusive)
summary: Google is launching new career certificate programs on Coursera in project management, data analytics, and user experience design, aimed at bridging skills gaps and providing high-paying job qualifications without requiring a college degree. These programs are designed to be completed in six months or less and are supported by need-based scholarships and partnerships with over 130 employers committed to hiring graduates. Google is also enhancing its search engine to help job seekers find opportunities based on education and experience levels, including "no degree" options, contributing to economic recovery and addressing unemployment exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: Epidemic Sound valued at $1.4bn as Blackstone joins $450m investment round in Swedish company
summary: Swedish music company Epidemic Sound has secured a $450 million funding round, including investment from Blackstone Growth and EQT Growth, valuing the company at $1.4 billion. The new capital will be used for continued international expansion, customer acquisition, enhancing user experience, and investing in music and digital offerings. Epidemic Sound's business model involves licensing rights-cleared production music and generating royalties from streaming services, with a commitment to pay 50% of streaming revenue to composers.

title: Technology and the Free Press: The Need for Healthy Journalism in a Healthy Democracy
summary: This article by Brad Smith, Vice Chair & President of Microsoft, discusses the critical relationship between technology and a healthy free press in a democracy. It highlights how technology, particularly the dominance of companies like Google in digital advertising and content aggregation, has negatively impacted the financial viability of journalism, especially local news. Smith advocates for a multi-faceted solution involving continued evolution within journalism, greater responsibility from tech companies, and government intervention through legislation modeled after Australia's recent law to restore competition and support news organizations.

title: GM-backed Cruise to buy self-driving start-up Voyage
summary: GM's majority-owned autonomous vehicle subsidiary Cruise has announced its agreement to acquire self-driving car start-up Voyage. Voyage CEO Oliver Cameron will join Cruise as vice president of product, and most of Voyage's 60 employees are expected to transition to Cruise. This acquisition marks a continued consolidation within the autonomous vehicle sector as Cruise focuses on launching a robotaxi business in San Francisco.

title: The Future of Work is here – ready?
summary: The article discusses the accelerated shift to flexible and hybrid work models due to the pandemic, highlighting a study by Deloitte commissioned by Liberty Global. It explores themes such as the need for new "meta skillsets" in an automated world, the importance of agile leadership and clear communication, and the opportunity for greater diversity and inclusion through flexible work arrangements. The article also touches upon the evolving role of the office as a hub for collaboration and innovation, while acknowledging the need for a "skills revolution" to address potential societal divides in the new economic landscape.

title: Facebook strikes deal with Murdoch’s News Corp in Australia
summary: News Corp, owned by Rupert Murdoch, has reached a content-supply deal with Facebook in Australia, making it the first major media outlet to do so under Australia's new media laws. The agreement follows a dispute last month where Facebook temporarily blocked all media content in Australia due to the new regulations. While terms were not disclosed, both parties expressed satisfaction with the landmark deal, which aims to transform the economics for journalism.

title: Apple v. Iancu: Oral Argument on Motion to Dismiss and Plaintiff Summary Judgment Motion, PTAB Litigation Blog
summary: This article discusses the oral argument in the case of Apple v. Iancu, focusing on motions to dismiss and for summary judgment. The lawsuit, filed by major tech companies, challenges the PTAB's "Fintiv" rule, which allows for discretionary denial of patent institution petitions when parallel litigation exists. The plaintiffs argue the rule exceeds statutory authority, is arbitrary and capricious, and was adopted without proper rulemaking procedures.

title: Imperva Snags Akamai’s Micheal McCollough To Lead Channels
summary: Imperva has hired Micheal McCollough, formerly Akamai's global channel chief, to lead and expand its channel business, with a focus on becoming a channel-first company. McCollough aims to strengthen relationships with public cloud providers, enhance services for existing partners, and leverage the company's acquisition of jSonar. He plans to incentivize partners through new programs, potentially driving almost all new business through the channel and increasing their involvement in services and support.

title: Google debuts A2 VMs powered by Nvidia A100 GPUs, its largest cloud instances yet
summary: Google has announced the general availability of its new Compute Engine A2 virtual machines, powered by Nvidia's Ampere A100 Tensor Core GPUs. These A2 VMs are notable for being the first in the world to integrate up to 16 Nvidia A100 GPUs into a single instance, making them the most powerful single-node GPU offering from any public cloud provider. Designed for demanding machine learning and high-performance computing workloads, Google claims they offer significant performance improvements and cost efficiencies compared to previous generations.

title: Twitter share price history in recent times
summary: This article provides a historical overview of Twitter's share price performance since its 2013 IPO, detailing key events that impacted its stock movements. It covers the company's origins, monetization strategies, and significant ups and downs, including earnings reports, user growth challenges, acquisition rumors, and strategic announcements. The piece highlights how various factors, from initial market reception to technical glitches and ambitious growth plans, influenced investor sentiment and Twitter's valuation over time.

title: Clarivate celebrates BD’s culture of innovation
summary: Clarivate has named BD to its Top 100 Global Innovators 2021 list for the sixth time, recognizing the company's significant investment in innovation and its commitment to protecting intellectual property. BD invests over a billion dollars annually in innovation, contributing to advancements in medical technology, and holds approximately 27,000 active, issued patents worldwide. The recognition highlights BD's ongoing efforts to advance global health through pioneering solutions and a robust intellectual property portfolio.

title: Coral South FLNG Project, Rovuma Basin, Mozambique
summary: The Coral South FLNG Project involves the development of the Coral Sul floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) facility in the Coral South field, located in Area 4 of the Rovuma Basin off Mozambique. Operated by Eni, the project aims to monetize gas reserves and is expected to start production in 2022. The article details the project's financing, contractors, and the technical specifications of the FLNG unit.

title: Invesco QQQ ETF releases Augmented Reality experience powered by 8th Wall for its NCAA basketball campaign
summary: Invesco QQQ ETF launched an augmented reality (AR) experience called 'QQQ Hoops AR' for its NCAA men’s college basketball championship campaign, in partnership with NBA legend Grant Hill, 8th Wall, and COFFEE Labs. This WebAR experience allows users to virtually shoot hoops in their living rooms and see the potential investment value of their in-game earnings through the Invesco QQQ ETF. The campaign features a web-based AR game accessible on smartphones without an app download, aiming to engage sports fans and showcase financial principles.

title: Google Cloud Pricing vs AWS: A Fair Comparison?
summary: This article provides a detailed comparison of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Amazon Web Services (AWS) pricing for compute instances and storage. It highlights differences in market positioning, on-demand and reserved VM pricing, and various storage options, noting where direct comparisons can be misleading due to differing structures. The article also discusses cost optimization strategies using NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP.

title: Iconic American Automaker Ford Motor Says Employees Can Work From Home ‘Indefinitely’ With Its Newly Redesigned Hybrid In-Office And Remote Model
summary: Ford Motor Company announced a new progressive, flexible, hybrid work model allowing approximately 30,000 white-collar employees to work from home indefinitely with flexible hours. The company plans to redesign its corporate office interiors to be versatile for collaborative work, driven by a survey showing 95% of office workers prefer self-determined work arrangements. This shift aligns Ford with other major corporations embracing remote work, leading to an exodus from big cities to more affordable locations and potential benefits for both employees and companies.

title: Quantum Brilliance unveils diamond-based quantum accelerator that can run at room temperature
summary: Quantum Brilliance has emerged from stealth mode to introduce the world's first diamond-based quantum accelerator that operates at room temperature. This innovation eliminates the need for extreme cooling or complex laser systems, which are typically required by existing quantum computers. The company aims to make quantum computing an "everyday technology" by developing hardware that can be installed in various environments, including data centers and even laptops, and will soon install its first accelerator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Center.

title: Brinker International's Virtual Brand, It's Just Wings, Integrates With Google To Offer New Pickup Option
summary: Brinker International's virtual brand, It's Just Wings, has integrated with Google to provide a new pickup option for its customers. Guests can now easily order and pick up their favorite wings directly through Google Search and Google Maps from over 1,000 participating kitchens nationwide. This integration aims to enhance the digital guest experience by offering convenience, value, and a seamless ordering process with contactless payment options.

title: Newfound Popularity of Thematic ETFs
summary: Thematic ETFs, which invest in baskets of stocks benefiting from emerging trends, technology, or evolving economic landscapes, have seen a significant surge in popularity since October 2020, with AUM growing by 132%. Despite this growth, the article highlights potential risks associated with these ETFs, including the reversal of investor enthusiasm impacting fund flow and performance, the concentrated holdings of individual stocks within the ETFs, and the potential for misleading diversification that may dilute thematic exposure and justify higher fees. Investors are advised against chasing "hot" ETFs without understanding their underlying holdings and potential risks.

title: A virtual ride-along in Waymo Via’s latest Class 8 autonomous truck
summary: Waymo Via demonstrated its fourth-generation Level 4 autonomous Class 8 trucking software on freeways outside Phoenix, with an editor's note clarifying it was fourth, not fifth generation. The system, based on the Waymo Driver used in passenger cars, features higher-resolution lidar and 360-degree camera sensors, but is still "years away" from mass production. While Waymo Via works towards scaling its autonomous trucks, the article also mentions competitors like TuSimple, Plus, PACCAR, and Daimler Trucks, highlighting the varying development stages and market approaches to autonomous trucking.

title: Moncef Slaoui Departs Galvani Bioelectronics Board of Directors
summary: Moncef Slaoui was terminated as Chair of the Galvani Bioelectronics Board of Directors, effective immediately, after allegations of sexual harassment and inappropriate conduct were substantiated by an investigation initiated by the GSK Board. Christopher Corsico has been appointed the new Chair, and Amy Altshul has also joined the Board. GSK emphasizes its commitment to a safe and respectful workplace and its zero-tolerance policy for sexual harassment and abuse of leadership.

title: Fastest-Growing Major Cloud Vendors: Google #1, Oracle #2, Microsoft and ServiceNow #3
summary: Google Cloud leads as the fastest-growing major cloud vendor, while Oracle shows significant hypergrowth, ranking second. Microsoft and ServiceNow are tied for third. The article analyzes the cloud revenue growth rates of the world's top cloud providers, noting the impressive performance of Google and Oracle, and scrutinizing slower growth figures from IBM and SAP.

title: AI is boring - or is it?
summary: This article argues that the term "Artificial Intelligence" is overused and often misapplied to simple technologies, creating inflated expectations. Despite the hype, the author, Christian Ott, emphasizes that the underlying AI technology is genuinely transformative, particularly in industries like automotive and manufacturing. He concludes that the real challenge and value of AI lie in effective data management from edge to core to cloud, allowing for scalable and impactful implementations.

title: Toyota VS Apple: The Age of EV Battles Unlatches the Door to Smart Cars
summary: The electric vehicle (EV) market is seeing an influx of traditional automakers and tech giants like Apple and Baidu, creating a new battleground for smart cars. Toyota, the world's leading automaker, is positioning itself with AI-based software development and strategic partnerships to compete against these tech companies, focusing on a "making friends" approach similar to Google's Android strategy. While Apple boasts significant financial and brand power, Toyota believes its collaborative ecosystem for automotive technology gives it an edge in the complex and responsibility-heavy auto industry.

title: YouTubers to battle it out in Malaysia’s 1st virtual sports day
summary: YouTube Malaysia, in collaboration with MyGameOn and IGN SouthEast Asia, is organizing "Pesta Game," Malaysia's first virtual sports day, which will feature local YouTubers competing against each other. The event, powered by Samsung Galaxy A52 | A72, was initially postponed due to the pandemic and will be streamed live in Bahasa Malaysia on Media Prima's YouTube channels and participating YouTubers' individual channels from March 27 to 28. Viewers can also win prizes and join in-game live sessions with their favorite creators.

title: After Spotlight, Snapchat Is Ripping Off Another Core Feature Of TikTok!
summary: Snapchat is reportedly developing a new feature called "Remix," which is similar to TikTok's Duets, allowing users to create new content from friends' snaps by reacting or adding their own video alongside the original. This feature follows Snapchat's earlier launch of Spotlight, a TikTok-like scrollable video feed. The company has confirmed that Remix is currently in external testing, with potential for integration into other parts of the app like Spotlight.

title: US chip giant Nvidia to recruit 600 engineers in Israel to boost AI prowess
summary: Nvidia, the US gaming and computer graphics giant, announced plans to hire 600 hardware and software engineers and chip designers in Israel. This recruitment drive aims to bolster the company's AI-based technologies. Following its acquisition of Mellanox Technologies, Nvidia already employs over 2,400 people across seven R&D centers in Israel, making it the company's largest R&D operation outside the US.

title: T-Mobile to wind down live TV services, offer YouTube TV
summary: T-Mobile is discontinuing its live TV service, TVision, on April 29th and will instead direct its wireless customers towards Google's YouTube TV. This decision comes after the company struggled to make its "skinny bundle" profitable, facing rising fees from programmers and intense competition in the virtual pay-TV market. This marks T-Mobile's second failed attempt to establish itself in the pay-TV industry.

title: U.S. Supreme Court weighs TransUnion bid to nix 'terrorist list' lawsuit
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court is considering narrowing a class-action lawsuit against TransUnion, where thousands sought damages after being incorrectly flagged as matching names on a government list of suspected terrorists and drug traffickers. The credit reporting company is appealing a lower court's ruling which upheld a $40 million jury verdict. Justices questioned whether all class members suffered a "concrete injury," a requirement for such lawsuits, particularly for those whose information was not publicly disclosed.

title: As Ad Spending Explodes, Look to These Communications ETFs
summary: The U.S. advertising market is projected to grow significantly in 2021 as businesses increase spending to recover from the pandemic, with an anticipated 15% expansion excluding political advertising. This resurgence is driven by stimulus measures and economic recovery, particularly benefiting digital ad platforms like Facebook and Google. Investors can capitalize on this trend through communication services ETFs such as XLC, FCOM, and VOX, which include major players in the digital advertising space.

title: Infosys and LivePerson Announce First-of-its-Kind Partnership to Drive Customer Experience Transformation for the World's Biggest Brands
summary: Infosys and LivePerson have formed a strategic partnership to revolutionize customer experience by integrating Infosys Cobalt with LivePerson's Conversational Cloud and AI. This collaboration aims to help major brands enhance customer and employee interactions through AI-powered conversations across various messaging channels. The initiative is expected to drive higher sales, improve customer satisfaction, and reduce operational costs for enterprises.

title: YouTube Music's Android users more than double on-year in Feb: data
summary: YouTube Music saw its Android user base in South Korea more than double year-on-year in February, reaching 2.61 million users. This surge positioned it as the second-most popular music streaming platform in the country, behind local giant Melon. The growth signals a shift in the Korean music streaming market, which is now facing increased competition from foreign players like Spotify.

title: Google Promises Not to Muzzle Staff on Pay, Settling Labor Case
summary: Google has settled a labor case, agreeing not to restrict employees from discussing their pay and working conditions. This agreement stems from a complaint filed by the Alphabet Workers Union, which represents staff and contractors at the company. The settlement requires Google to post a notice affirming workers' rights to discuss wages, bonuses, hours, and working conditions.

title: Bilibili’s $123 million investment in TapTap plans to revolutionize game distribution in China
summary: Chinese video-sharing website Bilibili has invested $123 million in TapTap, aiming to disrupt traditional game distribution channels in China. TapTap stands out by not charging a commission on in-app purchases, a direct challenge to the commission models of major app stores like Huawei, Xiaomi, Google, and Apple. This move allows Bilibili to diversify its revenue and directly compete with giants like Tencent, Huawei, and Xiaomi in the highly competitive Chinese gaming market.

title: Indian states tussle to retain jobs as economy slows
summary: Amid an economic slowdown and job losses from the pandemic, a growing number of Indian states are implementing laws that mandate local hiring, creating internal trade barriers. These policies, like Haryana's 75% job quota for locals in private companies with monthly salaries under 50,000 rupees, aim to address unemployment but raise concerns among businesses regarding ease of doing business and potential constitutional violations. Critics argue that such measures act as a short-term political fix and could deter investors and hinder overall economic growth.

title: OLB Group Adds QR Code Acceptance to Its Gateway
summary: OLB Group has integrated dynamic QR code acceptance into its cloud-based OmniSoft platform and SecurePay gateway to meet the demand for contactless payment options. This feature allows merchants, especially small and mobile businesses like tradesmen, to accept various digital payments including Apple Pay, Google Pay, and cryptocurrency, using just their phone. The company continues to expand its payment processing capabilities, having recently added social media app payments and cryptocurrency, with plans for PayPal wallet support.

title: New Fabs Crop Up Globally in 2021 as Chip Crisis Continues
summary: Amidst the ongoing global chip crisis affecting various industries, several major semiconductor manufacturers are announcing significant expansion plans. Intel is investing $20 billion in two new fabs in Arizona and launching Intel Foundry Services, while GlobalFoundries is committing $1.4 billion to boost its global production capacity. SK Hynix has also received approval to build a massive $106.35 billion fab complex in South Korea, primarily for DRAM production.

title: Google Wins Multibillion Dollar Copyright Fight With Oracle in Supreme Court
summary: The Supreme Court ruled in favor of Google in its multibillion-dollar copyright dispute with Oracle concerning Google's Android operating system. The 6-2 decision, delivered by Justice Stephen Breyer, determined that Google's use of Java API code constituted fair use, overturning a lower court ruling. This ruling may impact software copyright protections by providing developers more flexibility to build upon existing products.

title: First Look: The New Sonos Roam Speaker Is Versatile but Pricey | Reviews by Wirecutter
summary: The article provides a first look at the new Sonos Roam speaker, highlighting its versatility as a portable Bluetooth speaker, a smart speaker with voice activation, and an integrated part of a Sonos multiroom system. While impressed by its sound quality and portability, the review notes its high price ($170) and short battery life as potential drawbacks. The Sonos Roam is presented as an ideal entry point for those looking to start a multiroom speaker system.

title: Google Won. So Did Tech. (Published 2021)
summary: The Supreme Court ruled in favor of Google in its decade-long legal battle with Oracle, deeming it permissible to copy computer code in certain instances related to Android's operating system. This decision provided relief to the technology industry, affirming the standard practice of using application programming interfaces (APIs) to ensure compatibility across different technologies. The ruling left some fundamental questions about API copyright unanswered but solidified Google's position.

title: Meet the highest paid CEO in S&P 500, Paycom’s $211M man
summary: Chad Richison, the founder and CEO of Paycom Software Inc., was awarded compensation valued at $211 million in 2020, making him the highest-paid CEO in the S&P 500 based on disclosures so far. This compensation package, centered on restricted shares, could be worth over $2 billion if Paycom's stock price significantly increases, demonstrating a performance-based alignment with shareholder interests. Richison's equity award is contingent on the company's share price more than doubling and reaching specific targets within the next decade.

title: JPMorgan’s Chief Sees a Boom Coming (Published 2021)
summary: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon predicts a potential economic boom extending into 2023 driven by excess savings, deficit spending, infrastructure plans, and vaccine-induced euphoria, though he warns of potential inflation and aggressive interest rate hikes. He also addresses concerns about the growing influence of shadow banking and big tech in finance, China's perception of American decline, and the complexities of addressing climate change. Dimon's annual letter also touched on remote work reducing office space needs, cybersecurity spending, and specific tax loopholes he believes should be closed.

title: New Wormable Android Malware Spreads by Creating Auto-Replies to Messages in WhatsApp
summary: Check Point Research discovered a new wormable Android malware on Google Play disguised as a fake Netflix app named "FlixOnline." This malware spreads by automatically replying to incoming WhatsApp messages with a malicious link, and is designed to steal credentials, spread misinformation, or distribute further malware. Users are advised to remove the application if infected and change their passwords, and to be cautious of suspicious links even from trusted contacts.

title: Arista simplifies network management in latest CloudVision
summary: Arista Networks has updated its CloudVision software to simplify cloud-based network management through a new graphical user interface and built-in workflows. The CloudVision 2021 upgrade also improves AI-powered analytics for identifying network congestion and offers enhanced application monitoring for popular services like Microsoft 365, Salesforce, and Zoom. These enhancements aim to reduce IT complexity, especially for managing remote workers, and compete with simpler offerings from Cisco and Juniper.

title: New android malware disguised as Netflix app spreads via WhatsApp message auto-replies
summary: Check Point Research (CPR) has discovered new Android malware, disguised as a Netflix app called FlixOnline, spreading via WhatsApp messages with an auto-reply feature. The malware aims to steal credentials and spread further by offering a fake "free Netflix premium" service. CPR disclosed its findings to Google, which subsequently removed the app, but advises users to be cautious of suspicious links and install security solutions.

title: Moj, ShareChat-parent latest to join Unicorn club, raises $502 million in latest funding round
summary: Mohalla Tech, the parent company of Moj and ShareChat, has achieved unicorn status after raising $502 million in a funding round led by Lightspeed Ventures and Tiger Global. This investment values the company at over $2.1 billion. The capital will be used to expand its user base, improve its platform, and strengthen its creator community, amid a growing trend of Indian startups joining the unicorn club in 2021.

title: Ubiquiti Promised Premium, Secure Routers; Then They Were Hacked
summary: Ubiquiti, a company specializing in networking hardware, experienced a security breach that compromised customer data. The incident highlights the risks associated with cloud-based hardware that forces users to create online accounts, a trend also seen with products from Amazon and Google. Security experts suggest that locally controlled hardware is a more secure alternative, as it offers users more control over their data and privacy.

title: Today In Retail: PriceSmart’s Revenues Increase 3.4 Pct; Handy Collaborates With Gotham Properties
summary: PriceSmart reported a 3.4 percent increase in total revenues for the second quarter of fiscal 2021, and Handy partnered with Gotham Properties to offer home services to tenants. Additionally, Levi Strauss plans to open new stores and expects a 25 percent rise in first-half sales, while UPS is acquiring electric vertical takeoff aircraft to enhance delivery efficiency and reduce emissions.

title: P&G reportedly testing Chinese workaround to Apple’s privacy changes
summary: Procter & Gamble is participating in a test in China of a method to collect iPhone data for ad targeting, as a potential way to circumvent Apple's new privacy features. This initiative, developed with the China Advertising Association, uses "device fingerprinting" technology (CAID) to track online consumers, which violates Apple's app rules. As a major advertiser, P&G is seeking alternative audience tracking methods to maintain ad efficiency given that many consumers are expected to opt out of device tracking.

title: NVIDIA CEO Introduces Software, Silicon, Supercomputers ‘for the Da Vincis of Our Time’
summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang unveiled a comprehensive vision for the future at GTC, highlighting advancements in AI, automotive, robotics, and virtual worlds. He introduced new hardware like the Grace data center CPU, BlueField-3 DPU, and NVIDIA Atlan for automotive, alongside significant software developments such as NVIDIA AI, Omniverse, and various AI acceleration libraries. Huang emphasized NVIDIA's evolution into a computing platform company offering solutions across GPUs, CPUs, and DPUs, and a robust software ecosystem to empower researchers and enterprises.

title: Manager Question of the Month: How Active Fund Managers Cope With Index Concentration
summary: This article discusses the challenges active fund managers face due to increasing index concentration, particularly in U.S. large-cap growth benchmarks dominated by a few technology companies. It explores how managers adapt their strategies, including considering a switch from diversified to nondiversified funds, and the trade-offs involved in maintaining performance against highly concentrated indexes while adhering to SEC diversification rules. The piece highlights various approaches taken by investment firms like T. Rowe Price and Wellington Management.

title: The Fastest-Growing Sport Might Surprise You
summary: Esports are rapidly growing, attracting a massive global viewership and disrupting traditional sports. Despite its significant growth and investment from companies like Amazon (who bought Twitch for $970 million in 2014), the esports market is still early in its development, valued at $1.1 billion in 2021. Investors can gain exposure to this industry through ETFs like the Global X Video Games & Esports ETF (Nasdaq: HERO).

title: Televisa to Merge its Media, Content and Production Assets with Univision in Landmark Transaction, Creating the Premier Global Spanish-Language Media Company
summary: Grupo Televisa and Univision Holdings, Inc. announced a definitive transaction agreement to combine Televisa’s content and media assets with Univision, forming the largest Spanish-language media company globally: Televisa-Univision. This merger will create a premier media entity with extensive content libraries and production capabilities to serve the underserved global Spanish-language streaming market. The transaction is valued at $4.8 billion from Televisa's content assets, including cash, equity, and other sources, and is partially financed by a $1 billion Series C preferred investment led by SoftBank Latin America Fund.

title: TELEVISA Y UNIVISION COMBINAN ACTIVOS EN MATERIA DE CONTENIDOS
summary: Grupo Televisa and Univision Holdings Inc. have announced a definitive agreement to combine Televisa's content assets with Univision, forming the largest Spanish-speaking media group globally. This new entity, Televisa-Univision, will leverage the combined content libraries and production capabilities to target the 600 million Spanish speakers worldwide, supported by strategic partners like SoftBank, Google, and The Raine Group. Televisa will maintain control over its broadcasting concessions in Mexico and telecommunications businesses, while increasing its stake in Univision.

title: Cogent Communications signs lease for T5@Minneapolis data center
summary: Cogent Communications has signed a lease with Legacy Investing for space in the T5@Minneapolis data center, located within the Sleep Number Corp. headquarters building in downtown Minneapolis. This is described as a significant signing for the data center, which is owned and operated by Legacy Investing.

title: Alianza entre Televisa y Univision crea un gigante de contenidos de habla hispana
summary: Grupo Televisa and Univision Holdings have merged their content assets to create the largest Spanish-language media group, focusing on a new streaming platform targeting 600 million Spanish speakers. Televisa will receive USD 4.8 billion and become the largest shareholder with 45% of the new Televisa-Univision, which also secured USD 1 billion in strategic investments from partners like Google and SoftBank. The new entity is projected to achieve USD 4 billion in sales and USD 1.6 billion in EBITDA, positioning it for digital transformation and global content leadership.

title: Dollar Tree Launches Retail Media Network
summary: Dollar Tree has launched a new retail media network called Chesapeake Media Group, aiming to connect CPG brands with its customers through personalized digital experiences. This initiative, powered by Swiftly and Aki Technologies, allows brands to leverage data insights for targeted advertising on the Family Dollar mobile app and FamilyDollar.com. The move positions Dollar Tree alongside other major retailers like Kroger and Walmart in the growing retail media space, with a focus on delivering value to brands and shoppers.

title: Rackspace Technology Defines a New Category in Cloud Services
summary: Rackspace Technology (NASDAQ: RXT) has launched Rackspace Elastic Engineering, a new service model designed to help customers build and operate modern cloud environments. This new approach shifts from traditional fixed-scope managed services to providing flexible, modern, cloud-native engineering services through dedicated "Pods" of architects and engineers. Rackspace Elastic Engineering aims to support customers in their cloud-native transformations and DevOps-focused operating models across AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform.

title: Wipro clocks its best quarterly results in a decade in Q4 FY21
summary: Wipro announced its best fourth-quarter results in nearly a decade, with profit and revenue increasing by 27% and 3.4% respectively, driven by significant deal wins. The IT major forecasted a 2-4% growth for the quarter ending June, signaling a potential double-digit expansion, and won over $1.4 billion in deals including a potential $1 billion large deal. Despite rising attrition rates, Wipro plans to invest in talent, including hiring over 18,000 freshers, to sustain its growth momentum.

title: The curious case of Google Pay's disappearing American Express cards has been fixed
summary: American Express cards disappeared from Google Pay for many customers due to an expired certificate issue. Google confirmed the problem, and while cards won't automatically reappear, users can now re-add them manually without further issues. American Express also confirmed the resolution and apologized for the inconvenience.

title: Zscaler Acquires Trustdome for Cloud Security Posture Management Boost -
summary: Zscaler is acquiring Trustdome to enhance its cloud security posture management (CSPM) capabilities, aiming to help MSSPs, MSPs, and customers mitigate security risks across major cloud platforms. Trustdome's Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM) platform will strengthen Zscaler's existing CSPM offerings by providing granular governance over data, applications, and services in public cloud environments. This acquisition comes amidst booming demand for CSPM solutions, with market revenues projected to reach $9 billion by 2026.

title: Reuters introduces online paywall in digital-subscriber push
summary: Reuters is implementing a paywall for its website, Reuters.com, at a cost of US$34.99 per month. This move aligns it with other business news publications like Bloomberg.com and The Wall Street Journal, which already charge for digital access. The initiative aims to attract digital subscribers and was announced shortly after Alessandra Galloni was named Reuters' first female editor-in-chief in its 170-year history.

title: El behind the scenes Televisa-Univision
summary: Televisa and Univision announced a multi-million dollar agreement to create the largest Spanish-language content company globally, focusing on the Spanish-speaking streaming market. The deal, valued at $4.8 billion for Televisa, involves international partners like Google and SoftBank, and made Televisa the largest shareholder with 45% of the shares. The announcement led to a significant 22-25% stock increase for Televisa and garnered positive public and governmental attention, highlighting the potential for content production in Spanish.

title: Microsoft to invest $1 bln in Malaysia to set up data centres - Malaysian PM
summary: Microsoft Corporation announced a $1 billion investment over the next five years in Malaysia to establish its first "datacentre region" in the country. This initiative is part of a new partnership program with the Malaysian government and local companies, aiming to boost the nation's digital economy and provide digital skills training for up to a million Malaysians. The investment follows Malaysia's efforts to attract foreign direct investments after a significant decline last year.

title: Digital connectivity helps Manchester wine bar thrive online during UK lockdown
summary: Salut Wines, a Manchester-based wine bar, successfully pivoted to an online model during the UK lockdown thanks to reliable digital connectivity provided by Virgin Media. Owner Sara Saunby leveraged ultrafast broadband to set up an online shop and host virtual wine tastings, which proved highly popular and expanded their customer base across the UK. The business plans to continue these online offerings even after reopening, recognizing the significant role technology plays in its resilience and growth.

title: Synchronoss CEO still has high hopes for RCS in U.S.
summary: Despite the dissolution of the Cross Carrier Messaging Initiative (CCMI), Synchronoss Technologies remains optimistic about the future of Rich Communications Services (RCS) in the U.S., with CEO Jeff Miller believing in its eventual success and interoperability. The company, which was contracted to provide the RCS platform for CCMI, is now focusing on one-on-one partnerships with carriers who are still bullish on the technology. Synchronoss sees a significant opportunity for brands to engage consumers through RCS, with a model similar to its successful deployment in Japan, offering a richer, more interactive experience than traditional SMS.

title: Sunnyvale real estate mega-deal makes Google, big developer neighbors
summary: Tishman Speyer completed a major real estate transaction in Sunnyvale, acquiring seven parcels from NetApp for $365 million, making them neighbors with Google. This deal includes four large office buildings and amenities, giving Tishman Speyer significant control in a prime Silicon Valley tech area. Google also owns adjacent properties, suggesting potential long-term redevelopment plans for both entities in northern Sunnyvale.

title: Synopsys Tackles SoC Design with Unified Circuit Simulation Flow
summary: Synopsys has launched PrimeSim Continuum, a unified circuit simulation workflow designed to address the increasing complexity and scale of heterogeneous System-on-Chip (SoC) designs across various applications. This all-in-one solution integrates multiple simulation engines including PrimeSim SPICE, PrimeSim Pro, PrimeSim HSPICE, and PrimeSim XA, providing a seamless simulation experience with improved productivity and ease of use. PrimeSim Continuum leverages next-generation architectures and heterogeneous computing to optimize resource utilization, aiming to reduce verification times from days to hours, as demonstrated by early access customers like Kioxia and partners like Samsung and Nvidia.

title: UiPath IPO raises $1.3 billion by pricing shares above marketed range
summary: UiPath Inc. and its shareholders raised $1.3 billion in an initial public offering, pricing shares above the marketed range at $56 each, valuing the company at $29 billion. This valuation is below its February funding round valuation of $35 billion, partly due to a dip in software stocks. The company, founded in Romania, has grown significantly and its CEO, Daniel Dines, retains significant voting power.

title: Marvell closes on $10 billion Inphi deal, expanding data center and 5G business
summary: Marvell Technology has completed its $10 billion acquisition of Inphi after receiving approval from Chinese regulators, expanding its reach into data centers and 5G network infrastructure. CEO Matt Murphy noted the deal's overwhelmingly positive global customer support. The acquisition will enhance Marvell's growth in key markets such as 5G, cloud, and automotive, and Inphi's former CEO, Dr. Ford Tamer, has joined Marvell's board.

title: The ARKW ETF: Leading the Future of Advertising
summary: The ARK Web x.0 ETF (ARKW) is an actively managed ETF focused on disruptive growth and internet-driven themes, including internet advertising. The article highlights ARKW's leverage to the increasing shift towards digital advertising, particularly as retail footprints decline. It projects significant growth in US digital ad spending, suggesting its critical role in the future economy.

title: The Need for Continuous and Dynamic Threat Modeling
summary: This article emphasizes the importance of continuous and dynamic threat modeling in DevSecOps environments, moving beyond static, point-in-time assessments. It highlights how agile development and cloud deployments remove traditional checks and balances, necessitating real-time monitoring for architecture drift. The authors propose methods to transform operational views into dynamic threat models, contextualize security requirements, and continuously monitor for deviations from baseline security.

title: Here's how much money you'd have if you bought $1,000 worth of Netflix stock in 2011
summary: This article examines the significant return on investment for Netflix stock over the past decade. A $1,000 investment in Netflix in 2011 would have grown to over $15,000 by April 2021, far outpacing the S&P 500, Google, and Apple. Despite recent subscriber growth concerns, analysts believe Netflix is well-positioned for the long term due to its first-mover advantage and extensive content investments, even amidst increasing competition from other streaming services.

title: Mr. Cooper secures deal with Google Cloud for mortgage servicing platform
summary: Mr. Cooper Group has partnered with Google Cloud to develop a new digital mortgage servicing platform. This platform will leverage AI and machine learning to automate loan documentation processes, aiming to make mortgage servicing easier for homeowners and improve operational efficiency. The collaboration builds on Mr. Cooper's existing technological investments and aims to make these advancements available to the broader industry.

title: Double down on health and fitness with Garmin’s Venu 2 Series GPS smartwatch
summary: Garmin announced the Venu 2 and Venu 2S GPS smartwatches, designed to help users achieve a healthier lifestyle with new features like fitness age, advanced sleep tracking with sleep score, and numerous health monitoring tools. The Venu 2 series offers over 25 built-in sports apps, enhanced battery life, and smart features for daily convenience. Available in two sizes, these smartwatches are priced at $399.99 and aim to provide deeper insights into overall wellness.

title: JFrog Expands Cloud DevOps Announces The Availability Of JFrog DevOps Platform Enterprise+ On the Google Cloud Marketplace As A SaaS Subscription
summary: JFrog has announced that its DevOps Platform Enterprise+ subscription is now available on the Google Cloud Marketplace as a SaaS offering. This allows Google Cloud customers to easily deploy the full Enterprise+ capabilities, including JFrog Artifactory, Xray, Distribution & Hybrid Edges, and Pipelines. The integration aims to provide a secure, flexible, and cost-effective platform for accelerating enterprise application delivery.

title: Nature as a building block for Microsoft’s new Silicon Valley Campus
summary: Microsoft's new Silicon Valley campus in Mountain View, California, is designed as an ecologically integrated site, earning it a spot on the COTE Top Ten list for its sustainable features. The campus incorporates water reuse, clean energy production, carbon reduction, and native ecology restoration. Key elements include an extensive solar panel system, an integrated water management system for net-zero non-potable water, and the use of Cross Laminated Timber to reduce its carbon footprint.

title: Alphabet Discloses New Top Lawyer’s $51 Million Pay Package (2)
summary: Alphabet Inc.'s chief legal officer, J. Kent Walker Jr., received a total compensation package valued at $50.9 million last year, according to a proxy statement. This included a base salary of $655,000 and stock awards worth over $50.2 million, which will vest over four years. Walker currently holds over $11.4 million in Alphabet stock and has sold more than $9.6 million since December.

title: Apple and Google Are Killing the (Ad) Cookie. Here’s Why
summary: Apple and Google are implementing separate changes that will effectively end the use of third-party advertising cookies, significantly altering how marketers track online activity and target ads. Apple is requiring app developers to gain user permission for tracking across apps and websites, while Google is developing a cookie alternative that allows for targeted advertising without relying on individual web history. Both tech giants cite privacy as the driving force behind these changes, though Google also emphasizes balancing privacy with the financial viability of web publishing.

title: What do Apple’s new privacy settings mean for you?
summary: Apple is rolling out new privacy settings requiring app developers to explicitly ask users for permission to track their browsing habits across other apps and websites. This change is expected to significantly impact the mobile advertising market as many users are anticipated to decline tracking, potentially reducing ad effectiveness and revenue for businesses and publishers. The move has created a rift with companies like Facebook, which argues it will harm small businesses.

title: Google (GOOGL) stock hits all-time high on Q1 2021 earnings, announces $50 billion buyback
summary: Alphabet (Google's parent company) reported record Q1 2021 earnings, with revenues of $55.31 billion and EPS of $26.29, significantly beating analyst estimates. Google's stock hit an all-time high of over $2400/share in after-hours trading following the announcement. The company also announced a new $50 billion share repurchase program for its Class C capital stock.

title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) 4th Earnings: What to Expect
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is set to report its first-quarter fiscal 2021 earnings, with expectations rising due to strong performance from rival Intel and increasing chip demand. Analysts predict earnings of 44 cents per share on $3.21 billion in revenue for the quarter, largely driven by gains in datacenter revenue and PC demand, where AMD has been taking market share from Intel. The company's gross margin growth and the recent Xilinx acquisition are also expected to contribute to its continued momentum.

title: Alphabet reports big earnings beat as revenue grows 34%
summary: Alphabet reported significant beats on earnings and revenue for the first quarter of 2021, with revenue growing 34% year-over-year. The company's stock rose over 4% in after-hours trading, also driven by a new $50 billion stock buyback program. YouTube ad revenue saw a nearly 50% increase, contributing to the strong financial performance.

title: Huya agrees five-year, £224m broadcast deal for Chinese League of Legends
summary: Chinese livestreaming platform Huya has secured an exclusive five-year media rights deal worth approximately £224 million for League of Legends esports in China. The agreement with TJ Sports, a joint venture between Tencent and Riot Games, covers the League of Legends Pro League (LPL), League of Legends Development League (LDL), and LPL’s All-Star event from 2021 to 2025. This significant deal highlights the immense value of esports media rights, especially for popular titles in major markets like China.

title: Senators ask Google about phone call to Match on day before testimony
summary: Senators Amy Klobuchar and Mike Lee have sent a letter to Google seeking details about an alleged call made to Match Group, the maker of Tinder, prior to its legal officer's testimony regarding Google Play app store practices. Match's chief legal officer stated that Google employees contacted Match after his testimony became public, questioning why it differed from previous earnings call comments. The senators expressed deep concern over potential witness intimidation, threatening severe repercussions for any attempts to retaliate against those speaking out on policy issues.

title: Alphabet Inc (GOOGL) Q1 2021 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: This is a transcript of Alphabet Inc.'s Q1 2021 earnings call. Key topics include strong financial performance driven by increased online activity and advertiser spend, significant growth in Google Cloud, and continuous investment in AI, Search, YouTube, and other ventures like Waymo. Executives discuss strategies for various segments, including evolving retail and travel advertising, and emphasize financial sustainability and long-term growth.

title: Highwoods Properties Inc (HIW) Q1 2021 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Highwoods Properties Inc. (HIW) reported Q1 2021 FFO of $0.91 per share and increased its full-year FFO outlook, driven by improved leasing activity and strong performance in its Sunbelt markets. The company also announced plans to acquire a portfolio of office assets from Preferred Apartment Communities for $769 million, funded by selling $500-600 million in non-core assets. Executives highlighted rising office utilization rates, significant job growth announcements in their key markets like Raleigh and Nashville, and continued optimism for long-term growth.

title: Microsoft plans to take a smaller cut from developers in its games store. (Published 2021)
summary: Microsoft announced that it will decrease the revenue cut it takes from independent developers publishing PC games on its online store, starting in August. The fee will drop from 30 percent to 12 percent, allowing developers to keep 88 percent of their revenue. This move aims to make Microsoft's store more competitive with platforms like Steam and Epic Games, and comes amid increased scrutiny over app store fees faced by companies like Apple and Google.

title: I'm Not Turning Off App Tracking On My iPhone, Because I’m A Total Cuck
summary: The author humorously explains her decision to not disable app tracking on her iPhone, despite Apple's new privacy feature allowing users to opt out. She describes herself as a "datacuck" who enjoys personalized ads and wants to see "how far this goes" when it comes to data collection, contrasting her personal choice with the recommended smart privacy practices. The article satirically delves into the perceived benefits of targeted advertising while acknowledging the serious implications of data privacy and Facebook's track record.

title: Vodafone teams up with Google Cloud on data analytics
summary: Mobile operator Vodafone Group Plc and Alphabet Inc's Google Cloud have formed a strategic partnership to jointly develop data services. This collaboration will involve about 1,000 workers creating "Nucleus," a cloud-based storage and analytics portal for Vodafone's data, and developing "Dynamo" for data transport across countries. The companies also aim to offer consultancy services to other multinational businesses for moving data to the cloud.

title: Snap Accelerator Boosts Startups
summary: Snap Inc.'s Yellow accelerator program provides funding, mentorship, and networking opportunities for startups at the "intersection of creativity and technology." The article highlights how Yellow aids companies like Givingli Inc. and Elly Health Inc. in their growth and fundraising efforts. The program culminates in a Demo Day where startups present to potential investors.

title: Google to power Virginia data centers with 24/7 clean energy from AES
summary: AES has signed a 10-year agreement to exclusively supply 24/7 clean energy to three Google data centers in Virginia, utilizing a 500-MW portfolio of resources. This partnership aims to decarbonize Google's operations in the state and sets a precedent for other companies seeking to eliminate carbon from their energy supply. The AES portfolio will require approximately $600 million for its clean energy projects.

title: Apollo’s $5bn bet on Yahoo aims to go beyond advertising
summary: Apollo Global Management's $5 billion acquisition of Verizon's media unit, now called Yahoo, aims to expand beyond advertising into new ventures like subscription services and sports betting. The deal includes brands such as AOL and TechCrunch, with Apollo seeking to leverage Yahoo's extensive user base and iconic assets. While Verizon struggled to make the media division profitable, Apollo plans to apply its expertise in managing diverse investments and potentially reorganize the new entity for growth.

title: AES to supply Google data centers in Virginia with 24/7 renewable energy
summary: AES has signed a 10-year agreement to supply Google's Virginia-based data centers with 24/7 carbon-free energy. This partnership will involve the construction of approximately 500 MW of renewable energy and storage projects, ensuring that Google's data centers will operate at 90% carbon-free capacity on an hourly basis. This initiative supports Google's goal of achieving 100% carbon-free energy operations by 2030 and represents a $600 million investment to generate 1,200 jobs.

title: How wearable technology is transforming wellbeing in the workplace
summary: Wearable technology, ranging from smartwatches to specialized helmets and goggles, is increasingly being adopted in workplaces to enhance employee wellbeing and performance.
