summary: Executive Network Partnering Corp., a SPAC co-founded by Paul Ryan, Alex Dunn, and Solamere Capital, successfully priced an upsized $360 million IPO, offering 14.4 million units at $25 each. The company, led by CEO Alex Dunn, plans to focus on businesses where its network and operational background will provide a competitive advantage. It will list on the NYSE under the symbol ENPC.U, with Evercore ISI acting as lead manager.

title: -Morgan Stanley doesn't expect trading boom to continue
summary: Morgan Stanley's CFO Jonathan Pruzan stated that the bank does not anticipate its sales and trading and investment banking business to perform as well in the third quarter as it did in the second quarter, despite good August activity. The bank expects net interest income in its wealth management business to decline slightly but is on track to complete its E*Trade acquisition in Q4. Pruzan also noted the bank's capital strength offers flexibility for future strategic opportunities in investment management.

title: Broadstone Net Lease, Inc. Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Broadstone Net Lease, Inc. (BNL), an internally-managed real estate investment trust, announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 33,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock at $17.00 per share. Trading on the NYSE under "BNL" was expected to begin on September 17, 2020, with the offering closing on September 21, 2020. The net proceeds are intended for debt repayment and general business purposes, including future acquisitions.

title: Webull Review (2023): A Free Stock App — But Better Than Robinhood?
summary: This article provides a comprehensive review of Webull, a free stock trading app known for $0 commissions on stock, options, and ETF trades. It highlights Webull's impressive technology, advanced trading platforms, and research tools, comparing it to competitors like Robinhood and TradeStation. The review also covers Webull's pros and cons, fee structure, safety measures, and account opening process, concluding that it's ideal for active DIY investors and those focused on stocks and ETFs.

title: ‘It has to have an impact’: What Citi’s new CEO means for other women on Wall Street
summary: Jane Fraser's appointment as CEO of Citigroup marks a historic milestone as the first woman to lead a major Wall Street bank, sparking optimism about the future for other senior women in finance. This promotion, while significant, highlights that increasing female representation in top executive roles is a slow process requiring intentional effort from companies and boards. Despite progress, there is still a considerable journey ahead to achieve true gender diversity, especially for women of color, in corporate leadership.

title: Top Comcast exec to become lead independent director at JPMorgan Chase
summary: Comcast Corp. executive Steve Burke has been appointed as the lead independent director of JPMorgan Chase & Co. Burke will be succeeding former ExxonMobil CEO Lee R. Raymond in this role. This move brings a prominent media executive into a key leadership position at one of the largest financial institutions.

title: How Morgan Stanley is linked to deforestation in the Amazon
summary: An investigation reveals that Morgan Stanley, a major shareholder in Brazil's second and third-largest meatpackers, Marfrig and Minerva, is linked to illegal deforestation in the Amazon. Despite calls for reform and increasing deforestation, Morgan Stanley resists changes to its investment policies, with its suppliers found to be involved in illegal deforestation and employing slave-like labor conditions. The bank's policy on socio-environmental issues does not include specific measures for the livestock supply chain or for deforestation in general, prompting criticism from environmental organizations.

title: Autonomía financiera: las ventajas de las cajas de ahorro para menores de edad
summary: BBVA Argentina is promoting financial literacy and independence among young people by offering savings accounts for minors. These accounts come with a debit card and online banking access, allowing adolescents to manage their own money, make transfers, and use ATMs. This initiative aligns with Argentina's National Financial Education Plan to build a healthy and responsible economy by fostering good financial habits from a young age.

title: The Last Handful Of U.S. Deutsche Bank Employees Never Have To Set Foot In 60 Wall Street Again
summary: Deutsche Bank has informed its U.S. employees that they will not need to return to their 60 Wall Street office, with many able to work from home until July 2021 or move to a new office in Columbus Circle. This decision comes as American offices remain largely empty due to the pandemic, contrasting with other banks pushing for a return to in-person work. The bank plans to move 5,000 of its 8,000 U.S. employees to the new Columbus Circle headquarters by 2021.

title: Got Gold? Bottom-Barrel Rates to Last for Years to Come
summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to keep near-zero interest rates until at least 2023, creating a favorable environment for gold, which recently hit an all-time high of $2,070 an ounce. Some analysts predict gold could reach $7,000 by 2025 due to continued quantitative easing and the low opportunity cost of holding gold in a negative-yield bond environment. Gold mining stocks, while up significantly this year, still have attractive upside potential compared to their 2011 highs and are showing improving valuations relative to the broader market.

title: Why are bank branches gobbling up Charlotte’s hottest real estate?
summary: Despite a national trend of bank branch closures since the recession and increased digital banking, new bank branches, including Fifth Third Bank and JPMorgan Chase, are rapidly opening in Charlotte's fast-growing and expensive neighborhoods. Banks view these high-tech, modern branches as crucial for connecting with customers, building loyalty, and attracting newcomers to the competitive Charlotte banking market even as they acknowledge a shift towards digital transactions for basic needs. The article also notes how even Bank of America and Wells Fargo are adapting their physical presence, with BofA modernizing existing centers and Wells Fargo opening "digital-first" Express Centers.

title: CBK bars digital mobile lenders from CRB listing
summary: The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) has prohibited unregulated digital mobile lenders from submitting names of loan defaulters to credit reference bureaus (CRBs) and has halted the blacklisting of borrowers with debts under Sh1,000. This decision comes in response to widespread public complaints about the misuse of the credit information sharing mechanism by digital lenders. Consequently, only regulated financial institutions can now blacklist defaulters, and a stimulus package introduced during the pandemic has suspended CRB listing for defaults from April 1 for six months, requiring clearance for those previously blacklisted for amounts below Sh1,000.

title: Morgan Stanley Narrows Recruiting-Attrition Gap, Hires $5 Mln UBS Duo
summary: Morgan Stanley is close to reversing its net outflow of financial advisors, with CFO Jon Pruzan highlighting that net recruiting is now "much closer to zero." The firm recently hired a $4.8 million producing duo from UBS, Gerald Crum and Darren Hugo, as part of its selective re-entry into the recruiting market. This increased focus on recruiting high-producing advisors aims to make Morgan Stanley a "destination of choice" for financial advisors again.

title: JPMorgan International Bond Opportunities ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:JPIB)
summary: The JPMorgan International Bond Opportunities ETF (JPIB) offers investors a means to achieve total return through active management of a broad bond portfolio covering developed and emerging markets outside the U.S. Launched in 2017, JPIB has assets under management of $1.79 billion and a dividend yield of 4.66%. The ETF's stock performance shows a 1.4% increase year-to-date in 2026, and its top holdings include various government bonds and money market funds.

title: Global banks defy U.S. crackdowns by serving oligarchs, criminals and terrorists
summary: A joint investigation by ICIJ and BuzzFeed News reveals that global financial giants like JPMorgan Chase, HSBC, Standard Chartered Bank, Deutsche Bank, and Bank of New York Mellon continued to move trillions of dollars in suspicious funds for oligarchs, criminals, and terrorists, despite U.S. crackdowns and previous fines. The "FinCEN Files" expose a broken enforcement system where major banks often fail to report suspicious transactions until years later and rarely face criminal prosecution. This lax oversight allows illicit money to flow freely, enabling corruption, fraud, and organized crime worldwide, often affecting vulnerable populations.

title: Pittsburgh becomes a battleground for national banking powerhouses
summary: Pittsburgh is becoming a battleground for national banking giants Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase, which are expanding their physical presence in the market historically dominated by PNC. While PNC still holds the largest market share, its dominance has slightly decreased. Smaller community banks in the area are relying on strong customer relationships and personalized service to compete against the national powerhouses, who offer a more complete product suite.

title: Banks bludgeoned by $2 trillion suspicious transfers bombshell
summary: A cache of leaked documents revealed that several major global banks, including HSBC, Standard Chartered, Deutsche Bank, and JPMorgan Chase, transferred over $2 trillion in suspect funds between 1999 and 2017. The FinCen files sparked fresh concerns about money laundering and led to calls for industry reforms, with some banks' shares falling significantly. Despite the revelations, some analysts believe the reports may not have a lasting impact on the banking sector, while banks stressed their efforts to enhance compliance.

title: Broadstone Net Lease, Inc. Announces Closing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Broadstone Net Lease, Inc. (BNL), an internally-managed REIT, announced the closing of its initial public offering of 33,500,000 shares of Class A Common Stock at $17.00 per share, generating estimated net proceeds of $533.5 million. The company plans to use the proceeds to repay borrowings and for general business purposes, including future acquisitions. BNL's shares began trading on the NYSE under the ticker symbol "BNL" on September 17, 2020.

title: Bank of America making presence known in central Ohio
summary: Bank of America has rapidly expanded its presence in central Ohio, becoming the fifth-largest bank in the region by deposits within a year of opening its first Columbus office. This growth is attributed to its focus on supporting clients and the community, with plans for further expansion across Ohio. The article also notes a significant increase in total deposits across central Ohio, indicating consumers and businesses are hoarding cash due to economic uncertainty.

title: From bailout debacle to global dominance: Inside the turnaround at UBS
summary: This article details the remarkable turnaround of UBS under former CEO Sergio Ermotti, transforming it from a scandal-ridden bank on the brink of collapse to a global wealth management powerhouse. Ermotti's strategy involved slashing the investment banking division, focusing on wealth management, and rebuilding trust with ultra-wealthy clients, leading to significant capital growth and profitable years. The bank's resilient business model, particularly its strong wealth management focus and healthy loan book, has positioned it well even amidst economic challenges like the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: BlackRock, JPMorgan climate votes at odds as new rules loom
summary: Top U.S. asset managers BlackRock Inc and JPMorgan Chase & Co showed differing levels of support for climate-related proxy resolutions this year, with BlackRock backing only about 10% compared to JPMorgan's roughly 50%. This divergence occurred as new rules loom and shareholder advocacy groups criticize BlackRock for not aligning its voting record with its stated commitments on climate matters. The article highlights the ongoing debate and varying approaches among financial institutions regarding environmental shareholder proposals.

title: Despite Trevor Milton's resignation, some analysts remain confident in Nikola
summary: Nikola Corp. founder Trevor Milton's resignation following fraud allegations led to a share price dip, but analysts like Cowen Inc. and J.P. Morgan view his departure as a positive development for the electric vehicle maker. They believe Milton's exit will reduce "drama" and allow the company to focus on its core business and partnership with General Motors under the leadership of new Executive Chairman Steve Girsky.

title: ODNI Blamed Syrian Banks, but Did the West’s Deutsche Bank Facilitate ISIL Finances in Mosul?
summary: This article investigates suspicious money transfers totaling billions of dollars through Deutsche Bank and Bank of America to Iraqi banks during the peak of ISIS's control in Iraq. It questions why these transfers were permitted despite ISIL's financial activities and sanctions, especially given Deutsche Bank's history of fines for money laundering and sanctions violations. The report highlights the bank's deep ties with the Iraqi government and Kurdistan, scrutinizing its continued involvement despite recurring controversies.

title: HSBC Stock Pummelled by Financial Crimes Report, China ‘Unreliable Entity’ List
summary: HSBC's Hong Kong-listed shares plunged to a decade-low after reports of the bank's involvement in facilitating criminal activities and concerns it might be added to China's "Unreliable Entity List." The bank was named in a report by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists for allegedly aiding a massive Ponzi scheme, even while on probation with U.S. regulators. Additionally, investors fear potential sanctions from the Chinese government due to claims HSBC provided information related to the detention of Huawei's CFO.

title: Warren Buffett Partner’s Forgotten Warning Still Haunts Stock Market
summary: This article revisits a prophetic warning from Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett's longtime partner, about the dangers of "idiot booms" fueled by excessive credit and monetary expansion, comparing them to heroin use for the economy. The author suggests this warning from 2009 is highly relevant to the current stock market, especially given Berkshire Hathaway's recent underperformance and the "craziness" seen in events like the WeWork fiasco. Munger's insights imply that the market's current high valuations are artificial and unsustainable, supporting Buffett's conservative approach of holding cash.

title: Selective Insurance Adds New Independent Directors to Enhance Board Expertise
summary: Selective Insurance Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: SIGI) announced the appointment of four new independent members to its Board of Directors, effective September 23, 2020, to enhance board expertise and diversity. These new directors bring extensive experience in areas such as sales, branding, digital marketing, finance, fintech, and corporate development, aligning with Selective's commitment to innovation and customer experience. Their addition expands the board from 13 to 17 members, supporting the company's strategy for profitable growth through high-tech, high-touch insurance solutions.

title: Ventas Acquiring Genesis Towers Complex in $1B Deal
summary: Ventas Inc. is acquiring the Genesis Towers, a 721,000-square-foot life sciences complex in South San Francisco, for approximately $1 billion. The seller is a joint venture between Bain Capital and Phase 3 Real Estate Partners, Inc., with the acquisition being funded by $415 million in financing from Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase. The complex includes both lab and office space across three buildings, with the north tower 91% occupied and the south tower fully leased.

title: JPMorgan set to pay nearly $1 bln in spoofing penalty -source
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM.N) is expected to pay almost $1 billion to settle market manipulation investigations by U.S. authorities concerning its trading of metals futures and Treasury securities. This settlement would resolve a long-standing regulatory issue for the bank and represents a significant win for government efforts against illegal trading techniques like spoofing. The agreement with the Department of Justice, SEC, and CFTC could come as early as this week and is not anticipated to restrict the bank's business operations.

title: Vanguard Enters ESG Fixed Income Market with Launch of US Bond ETF
summary: Vanguard Group launched its first ESG-focused ETF for US investors, the Vanguard ESG U.S. Corporate Bond ETF (VCEB), to meet growing investor demand in the fixed income ESG market. The ETF tracks the Bloomberg Barclays MSCI U.S. Corporate SRI Select Index, which screens out companies involved in certain controversial activities and includes those with at least a BBB ESG rating. This new offering expands Vanguard's suite of ESG products, which began over 20 years ago.

title: Two locals make annual list of top performing U.S. small-cap banks and thrifts
summary: Two local banks, Meridian and Parke, have been named to investment firm Piper Sandler’s annual list of top-performing U.S. small-cap banks and thrifts. This exclusive list includes only 35 U.S. banks with a market cap below $2.5 billion that meet rigorous criteria related to growth, profitability, credit quality, and capital strength.

title: Keep Calm and Stay Long: This Gold Price Correction Is Normal and Healthy
summary: Frank Holmes argues that the recent gold price correction is normal and healthy, attributing it to the metal's inherent volatility and short-term market dynamics. He highlights significant inflows into gold-backed ETFs during the dip, negative real rates, and unprecedented money printing as factors supporting gold's long-term outlook. The article also discusses the robust economic activity in Texas, advancements in the precious metals streaming industry, and other market updates.

title: Goldman Sachs to Move 100 Workers From London Ahead of Brexit
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is relocating just over 100 staff members from London to other European cities in preparation for Brexit. These employees, working in areas like sales and trading, deal-making, and private wealth management, are being asked to move to EU offices including Paris, Frankfurt, Milan, and Madrid by January 1. This move reflects intensified discussions within the firm as they adapt to post-Brexit operations.

title: Mapa del sector bancario: las crisis fomentan una mayor concentración del mercado
summary: The article discusses the increasing concentration in the Spanish banking sector, driven significantly by the 2008 financial crisis and the current economic impact of the coronavirus. It highlights how the number of banks and savings banks has drastically reduced through mergers, acquisitions, and absorptions, leading to a few large entities dominating the market. Experts suggest this trend will continue, with implications for employment, branch closures, and customer services, though opinions vary on the impact on competition.

title: Keep Calm and Stay Long: This Gold Price Correction Is Normal and Healthy
summary: The article discusses the recent gold price correction, explaining it as a normal and healthy part of gold's volatility. It highlights strong investor inflows into gold-backed ETFs during the dip and features insights from industry leaders on the continued positive outlook for precious metals. Additionally, it touches on the economic strength of Texas and market manipulation in the gold market.

title: Weibo-owner Sina to go private in $2.6 bln deal with CEO-led firm
summary: Sina Corp, owner of social media platform Weibo, is set to go private in a $2.6 billion deal with CEO Charles Chao's holding company, New Wave. The offer price represents an 18% premium over the stock's closing price before the initial offer. This move aligns with a trend of Chinese companies delisting from U.S. exchanges amid rising tensions between the two countries.

title: Global oil and gas company
summary: This article details how a global oil and gas company, challenged by liquidity inefficiencies and counterparty risk due to its extensive global treasury operations, centralized its U.S. dollar position with J.P. Morgan. J.P. Morgan's "Follow-the-Sun" and "Against-the-Sun" sweep solutions enabled regional consolidation and active investment of excess cash in London. This resulted in full visibility and control over USD balances, optimized yields, and adherence to risk guidelines for the company's treasury team.

title: JPMorgan to pay $920M for manipulating bond, metals markets
summary: JPMorgan Chase has agreed to pay $920 million in fines and penalties for manipulating the precious metals and U.S. Treasuries markets. The bank admitted that its traders used a tactic called "spoofing" over an eight-year period, where they sent trading signals with no intention of executing the trades to influence market direction. This illegal activity aimed to profit from artificial market movements and undermined market integrity, according to U.S. financial regulators and the Department of Justice.

title: A leader in agribusiness, food products and fertilizer
summary: This article highlights how J.P. Morgan provided a comprehensive liquidity management and electronic payment solution for a global corporate giant in the agribusiness, food products, and fertilizer sectors. The solution, which involved a zero-balance structure and a global and local earnings credit rate (ECR) program, helped the company optimize liquidity, reduce transactional costs in Mexico and the U.S., and enhance visibility and control over its cash flows. As a result, J.P. Morgan Mexico became the company's main payment and cash concentration bank, managing most of its cash flows effectively.

title: JPMorgan lent $5 billion to women entrepreneurs over the last year, halfway to its $10 billion commitment
summary: JPMorgan Chase has committed $5 billion to women small business owners over the last year, reaching the halfway point of its three-year, $10 billion lending commitment announced in 2019. This initiative is part of their broader "Women on the Move" program, which also includes investments in and support for organizations benefiting women, especially in light of the disproportionate impact of the coronavirus pandemic on women entrepreneurs. The bank aims to help female entrepreneurs scale their businesses, find new revenue streams, and manage their finances.

title: JPMorgan to pay $920 mln for manipulating precious metals, treasury market
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has agreed to pay over $920 million and admitted wrongdoing to settle U.S. market manipulation probes concerning its trading of metals futures and Treasury securities. This landmark multi-agency settlement, the largest ever imposed by the CFTC, addresses "spoofing" activities conducted between 2008 and 2016, with some trades made on JPMorgan's own account and others facilitating hedge fund clients. The agreement involves fines, restitution, and disgorgement, and includes a Deferred Prosecution Agreement with the Justice Department, staving off criminal prosecution.

title: Goldman Shuffles Consumer Banking, Asset Management Executives
summary: Goldman Sachs has announced executive reshuffles, promoting Stephanie Cohen to co-head the consumer banking and wealth management division, making her the first woman in years to run a major division at the firm. The company is also combining its money-managing arm with its private-equity business, to be run by Eric Lane and Julian Salisbury. These changes reflect CEO David Solomon's efforts to simplify the firm's structure into four main businesses to improve performance and investor understanding.

title: JPMorgan slammed with $920m penalty over market manipulation
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has agreed to pay over $920 million in penalties for market manipulation involving spoofing by 15 traders across its precious metals and Treasury desks. This record sanction from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission is part of a three-year deferred prosecution agreement with the Justice Department, addressing actions that caused over $300 million in losses to other market participants. The bank admitted wrongdoing and stated that the individuals involved are no longer with the firm.

title: Chase gets federal approval to build Albuquerque branches
summary: JPMorgan Chase has received federal approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to build two new branches in Albuquerque. This expansion is part of Chase's previously announced $20 billion, five-year plan initiated in 2018.

title: PNC opens first retail branch in Greater Boston
summary: PNC Bank has opened its first retail branch in Greater Boston, located at 55 Boylston St. in Chestnut Hill. This is the first of five planned locations for the Pittsburgh-based banking giant in the region for 2020, signaling an expansion into the Boston market.

title: Citigroup’s new stock-trading chief is cutting jobs in effort to revive the flagging business
summary: Citigroup's new global head of equities trading, Fater Belbachir, has begun cutting senior U.S. trading personnel as part of a broader effort to revive the bank's underperforming equities business. These initial cuts, which include three managing directors, are expected to expand to lower-ranked workers and international operations. The move aims to improve margins and address the business's consistent failure to meet performance targets, contrasting with larger rivals like JPMorgan Chase.

title: HPE overhauls treasury operations to gear up for growth
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has transformed its treasury operations in Asia Pacific with J.P. Morgan to simplify its banking and account structure, enhance liquidity, and improve process efficiencies. This overhaul addresses complexities from past restructuring and aims to reduce bank accounts by up to 40% while automating processes and improving yields on idle funds. The solution integrates J.P. Morgan’s Virtual Account Management, Unitized Time Deposits, and Virtual Branch solutions with HPE’s internal systems for better cash visibility and cost savings.

title: Morgan Stanley Starts Real Estate Search in London for New Quarters
summary: Morgan Stanley is searching for a new London headquarters, seeking at least 600,000 square feet of office space. This move signals confidence in London's long-term office market despite current sentiment about remote work. The bank is considering options in both the east London financial district and the City of London, potentially consolidating its current 800,000 square feet across two Canary Wharf buildings into a single, modern premises.

title: JPMorgan Finds More Than 500 Workers Got U.S. Virus Relief Funds
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s internal investigation revealed that over 500 of its employees received Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) funds intended for pandemic relief, with dozens of these instances deemed fraudulent. This discovery at the largest U.S. bank prompted a thorough probe into the misuse of taxpayer assistance. The findings highlight the scope of the issue and the firm's efforts to address the widespread abuse of the program.

title: IRSA buscará reestructurar su deuda en dólares
summary: IRSA will present a proposal to its creditors to restructure its debt of US$181 million, which matures on November 15, adhering to BCRA regulations. This comes as the BCRA has called on companies with foreign currency debt exceeding US$1 million monthly to present restructuring plans. The proposal must include a maximum 40% access to the exchange market and a two-year extension for the remaining payments.

title: Private Equity Firm Blackstone Actually Had a Sub-Zero Tax Rate Last Year
summary: Blackstone, the world's largest private equity firm, reported a sub-zero effective income tax rate in 2019 despite billions in profits, a result attributed to its conversion to a C corporation following Trump's 2017 tax cuts. CEO Stephen Schwarzman has donated nearly $25 million to Republican campaigns, aiming to preserve these tax breaks which significantly benefit Blackstone. Democrats, including Joe Biden, have pledged to raise corporate tax rates, posing a threat to Blackstone's profitability under its new corporate structure.

title: Goldman Sachs to go ahead with "modest" job cuts after coronavirus pause
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc plans to proceed with a "modest number of layoffs" after pausing job cuts due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The bank is reportedly looking to cut about 400 jobs, or roughly 1% of its workforce, primarily targeting back-office roles as part of an earlier reorganisation aimed at improving efficiency. This comes as the U.S. Federal Reserve curbed big bank capital distributions through the end of the year, affecting share buybacks and dividends for major banks.

title: Lithia Announces Pricing of Public Offering of Common Stock
summary: Lithia Motors, Inc. announced the pricing of its public offering of 3,181,819 shares of Class A common stock at $220.00 per share, with an option for underwriters to purchase additional shares. Concurrently, Lithia announced a private offering of $550 million aggregate principal amount of 4.375% senior notes due 2031, an increase from the previously announced size. The offering is expected to close on October 5, 2020.

title: JPMorgan Chase DPA Provides Insight into Government’s Assessment of Compliance Programs
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. settled criminal charges related to market manipulation, resulting in a deferred prosecution agreement (DPA) and over $920 million in penalties. The DPA incorporates recent updates from the DOJ and SEC regarding corporate compliance programs, particularly emphasizing the use of data for effective monitoring and root cause analysis. This settlement highlights the government's focus on companies' abilities to learn from past misconduct and adapt their compliance programs accordingly.

title: Rise of platforms calls for a different kind of bank
summary: The article discusses how platform business models, which leverage digital technologies to connect independent parties and facilitate exchange, are transforming industries. It highlights the strong valuations of companies employing these models and explores the challenges and opportunities they present for businesses and their transaction banking providers. J.P. Morgan outlines its approach to supporting clients on their platform journey, emphasizing stability, innovation, comprehensive product coverage, and strong banking relationships.

title: Why JMST: Solve Income Challenges With an Ultra-Short Municipal Bond ETF
summary: The article highlights the JPMorgan Ultra-Short Municipal Income ETF (JMST) as a solution for investors seeking tax-exempt income with low risk, especially during periods of market volatility and low interest rates. JMST targets portfolio duration of less than one year, focuses on high-quality, ultra-short municipal bonds, and is actively managed to identify opportunities and mitigate risks. It is presented as an alternative to cash for higher income and a de-risking option compared to longer-term bonds.

title: A Goldman Sachs partner will join Galaxy Digital to help bridge the gap between Wall Street and crypto
summary: Damien Vanderwilt, a Goldman Sachs partner and global head of FICC Execution Services, is joining Galaxy Digital as co-president and head of global markets at the start of 2021. He will leverage his Wall Street network to expand Galaxy's business across its various units, including trading and investment banking. This move aims to bridge the gap between traditional finance and the growing digital asset market, as Galaxy sees increased interest from macro hedge funds and pensions.

title: Bank of America Stands by Pledge of No Layoffs This Year
summary: Bank of America plans to uphold its promise of no staff layoffs in 2020, as stated by CEO Brian Moynihan. This commitment stands in contrast to several other major banks, including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase, which have resumed job cuts amidst the pandemic. The bank will continue to manage its headcount through attrition alone.

title: As Goldman, JPMorgan resume cuts, Bank of America reiterates no-layoff vow
summary: As Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase resume job cuts, Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan reiterated the bank's commitment to no layoffs for the year. This comes as other major banks like Citi and Wells Fargo have also restarted workforce reductions, with the industry on pace to cut over 80,000 positions in 2020. Moynihan highlighted Bank of America's strategy of relying on attrition and its progress in diversity initiatives.

title: KKR-backed Academy Sports and Outdoors raises $203 million in IPO - source
summary: Academy Sports and Outdoors, backed by KKR, raised $203 million in its IPO by selling shares at $13 each, below its target range of $15-$17. The IPO valued the company at $1.1 billion, despite a surge in demand for at-home leisure activities during the coronavirus pandemic which significantly boosted its e-commerce sales. Shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the symbol "ASO".

title: Chart of the Week: JUST Industry Leaders Maintain Their Performance Upside Through the Recovery
summary: This article highlights the continued outperformance of "JUST Industry leaders" compared to the Russell 1000, even through market volatility and recovery periods. These companies, identified by JUST Capital for prioritizing stakeholders, demonstrate similar volatility but stronger downside protection and upside gains. The piece also notes the success of JUST Capital's investable indices, such as the JUST US Large Cap Diversified Index and its ETF, in delivering significant returns.

title: Treasury Services: 5 trends driving the payment revolution
summary: This article by J.P. Morgan outlines five key trends revolutionizing the payments landscape: explosive connectivity, digital innovation, the rise of emerging markets, the availability of multiple payment methods, and demographic changes. It emphasizes how corporate treasurers can leverage these trends and associated data to elevate their strategic role within businesses, driving frictionless experiences and efficient capital use.

title: Malaysia's Mr DIY secures IPO investors, including BlackRock - sources
summary: Malaysian home-improvement retailer Mr DIY has secured over a dozen cornerstone investors, including BlackRock Inc, AIA Group Ltd, and J.P. Morgan Asset Management, for its upcoming market debut. The IPO is expected to raise 1.5 billion ringgit ($360.75 million), marking one of Malaysia's largest market listings in over three years. The company has seen significant interest due to its strong performance during the COVID-19 pandemic, as consumers spent more time and money on home improvements.

title: JPMorgan Chase to Pay Nearly $1 Billion to Settle Trade Manipulation Charges
summary: JPMorgan Chase has agreed to pay nearly $1 billion to settle charges of manipulative trading of US Treasury securities brought by the CFTC and SEC. The charges include "spoofing" over an eight-year period, resulting in a record $920.2 million CFTC fine and a $35 million SEC fine. By paying these fines, JPMorgan avoided criminal wire fraud charges from the Department of Justice.

title: Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Truist remain deposit leaders in Sarasota-Manatee
summary: Bank of America maintained its lead as the largest bank by customer deposits in the Sarasota-Manatee region, marking its tenth consecutive year at the top. Despite its merger, Truist Bank narrowly missed unseating Wells Fargo for the second position, with only a $90.3 million difference in deposits. The region saw an overall increase of $3.1 billion in deposits, partly attributed to investors seeking the security of insured bank deposits.

title: How treasury and payments organizations can stay vigilant against cyberattacks
summary: The global shift to remote work has significantly increased cybersecurity vulnerabilities, with a 63% rise in cyberattacks since the pandemic began. David Leach of J.P. Morgan highlights the exploitation of less secure home networks and supply chain disruptions by bad actors. Organizations are urged to implement stringent controls, educate employees on identifying threats like financial malware and social engineering, and leverage advanced security technologies and banking partnerships to protect against fraud.

title: Ecopetrol ingresó a activos recomendados de Bancolombia
summary: Bancolombia has updated its recommended investment portfolio for the fourth quarter of 2020, adding Ecopetrol to its list of advised stocks. This decision was influenced by Ecopetrol's over 40% year-to-date devaluation and a promising fundamental recovery outlook, which presents attractive entry opportunities. The new recommended basket also includes Nutresa, Cementos Argos, Preferencial Grupo Aval, and Grupo Argos, aiming for a diversified approach given the high market volatility.

title: Today In Digital-First Banking: BoA Launches Life Plan; United Airlines, Chase Roll Out United Gateway Card
summary: Bank of America has introduced its Life Plan program for digital financial planning. Concurrently, United Airlines and Chase Card Services have launched a new no-annual-fee United Gateway credit card, offering travel miles for various purchases. Additionally, NCR Corp. has upgraded its ATM operating software with the "Activate Enterprise NextGen ATM infrastructure," aiming to integrate ATMs further into the digital age.

title: C4 Therapeutics Announces Closing of Initial Public
summary: C4 Therapeutics, Inc. announced the closing of its initial public offering, raising $209.76 million before deductions. The offering included the full exercise of the underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares, totaling 11.04 million shares at $19.00 per share. Jefferies, Evercore ISI, BMO Capital Markets, and UBS Investment Bank served as joint book-running managers for the offering.

title: Comcast Corporation Promotes Dalila Wilson-Scott to Executive Vice President and Chief Diversity Officer
summary: Comcast Corporation announced the promotion of Dalila Wilson-Scott to Executive Vice President and Chief Diversity Officer, reporting to Chairman and CEO Brian L. Roberts. In this new role, effective immediately, Ms. Wilson-Scott will oversee all Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion activities for the corporation, while also continuing to lead the Comcast NBCUniversal Foundation and the company's community impact work, including a $100 million commitment to social justice and equality. Her responsibilities will also include digital equity efforts and building partnerships to provide skills training for under-resourced communities.

title: OXIGEN Beverages Inc. Announces $15 Million Series B Funding With Marquee Investors
summary: OXIGEN Beverages Inc. has secured $15 million in Series B funding, attracting a diverse group of celebrity and business leaders as investors, including Stephen Curry, Brett Eldredge, and Kevin Love. The company, which has seen 300-400% year-over-year growth, plans to use the capital to boost brand awareness through marketing and scale national distribution. OXIGEN is known for its pH-balanced, oxygen-boosted water made from 100% recycled plastic and has launched a "Recover + Rise" campaign supporting frontline workers.

title: JPMorgan Chase Commits $30 Billion to Advance Racial Equity
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced a new commitment of an additional $30 billion over the next five years to advance racial equity and provide economic opportunity to underserved communities, particularly Black and Latinx communities. This initiative will address key drivers of the racial wealth divide through promoting affordable housing, growing Black- and Latinx-owned businesses, improving financial health and access to banking, and accelerating investment in employees and building a more diverse workforce. The firm also committed to providing $2 billion in philanthropic capital over the next five years, with an emphasis on supporting Black- and Latinx-led organizations.

title: Inside Morgan Stanley's $7 billion deal for Eaton Vance
summary: Morgan Stanley is expanding its financial services offerings with the $7 billion acquisition of money manager Eaton Vance, following its $13 billion purchase of E-Trade. These acquisitions, including Solium Capital Inc., are part of CEO James Gorman's strategy to diversify the firm beyond investment banking and retail brokerage, aiming for younger, less affluent, and tech-savvy clients, and bolstering its wealth management business with more fee-based revenues and ESG offerings. The deal is expected to increase Morgan Stanley Investment Management's AUM to nearly $1.2 trillion, despite some concerns about execution risks due to the rapid succession of large acquisitions.

title: Morgan Stanley to Buy Eaton Vance for $7 Billion - WSJ
summary: Morgan Stanley announced its acquisition of Eaton Vance Corp. for $7 billion, marking a continued shift away from risky trading operations towards steadier money management businesses. This deal comes shortly after completing its $11 billion takeover of E*Trade Financial and is part of CEO James Gorman's decadelong strategy to double down on wealth and asset management. The acquisition will nearly double Morgan Stanley's managed assets and strengthen its position in specific product areas like municipal bonds and sustainable investing, making it a $1 trillion money manager.

title: U.S. Bank closing branches, including several in the Nashville area
summary: U.S. Bank is closing a handful of branches in the Nashville area, all of which are located inside grocery stores. This action by U.S. Bancorp follows similar trends and comes amidst other banking news in the Nashville market, including expansion plans by competitors.

title: Bank of America's plan in Columbus: Keep going
summary: Bank of America is continuing its expansion in Central Ohio, having opened its first Columbus branch on Morse Road in July 2019. The bank's market leader discussed plans for further growth in the region, focusing on a technology-centered design to attract customers.

title: Symcor helps to accelerate digital transformation in the COVID-19 era and beyond
summary: Symcor, a joint venture of Canada's top financial institutions, played a crucial role in helping the Canadian financial services sector respond to the COVID-19 pandemic by quickly deploying fraud detection solutions and digitizing operations. The company specializes in payment processing, customer communications, and fraud detection, assisting large organizations across various sectors. Symcor anticipates a continued acceleration of digital transformation and aims to be a key player in the future of open banking in Canada, ensuring data security and accessibility.

title: A roadmap for driving innovation in corporate treasury
summary: This article outlines a roadmap for corporate treasury teams to embrace innovation amidst rapid technological change. It suggests five key attributes for success, including education on emerging technologies, involvement in the innovation process, embracing experimentation with Minimal Viable Products (MVP), leveraging internal and external partnerships, and adopting a self-disruption mindset. The article emphasizes that banks are uniquely qualified partners in this innovation journey, highlighting J.P. Morgan's commitment with significant technology investments and collaborative initiatives.

title: Got my first job! Working as a software engineer at JPMorgan Chase & Co.
summary: Cesar Villa Garcia, an FIU alumnus, shares his experience securing his first job as a software engineer at JPMorgan Chase & Co. He discusses how crucial his coursework and involvement in university organizations like Upsilon Pi Epsilon (UPE) were in his career development. Villa Garcia also offers advice for job seekers and elaborates on the daily life and challenges of his role in the financial industry.

title: Actualización: Cemex recauda fondos en emisión internacional para pagar deuda
summary: Cemex, a Mexican cement company, issued $1 billion in senior guaranteed notes in the international market at a 5.200% rate with a 10-year term to pay down debt and for general corporate purposes. This private placement, which closed on September 17, involved several legal advisors for Cemex and the initial purchasers. The company plans to list these notes on the Irish Stock Exchange for trading on Euronext Dublin, following a similar bond issue in June.

title: China’s Ping An-Backed Lufax Files for $3 Billion U.S. IPO
summary: Lufax Holding Ltd., a Chinese online wealth management platform backed by Ping An Insurance Group, has filed for a U.S. IPO aiming to raise about $3 billion. This move comes as the company shifts away from its P2P lending origins and follows another Ping An-backed fintech listing (OneConnect Financial Technology), amidst a backdrop of rising U.S.-China tensions. The company reported a net profit of 7.27 billion yuan for the first half of 2020.

title: Ant Group Goes Public
summary: Ant Group is preparing for a dual listing in Shanghai and Hong Kong, aiming to raise $35 billion with a $225 billion valuation, potentially becoming the world's largest IPO. The company, a Chinese fintech giant controlled by Jack Ma, operates online payment, lending, insurance, and money-market funds, and plans to comply with new Chinese central bank regulations. Despite US-China friction, major global banks are underwriting the IPO, which will offer investment opportunities through direct share purchases, Alibaba, or related ETFs.

title: Ford and General Electric are headed back to the double digits, Jim Cramer says
summary: Jim Cramer predicted that Ford and General Electric's stocks are poised to return to double-digit prices. He believes Ford is a stronger buy, citing its clearer value play, better momentum, and rebounding core auto market. Both companies have recently received upgraded ratings from analysts and are showing "green shoots" after years of decline due to strategic errors and other market factors.

title: P&G Shareholders Send Resounding Message Calling for Diversity Disclosure
summary: Procter & Gamble shareholders voted 37% in favor of a resolution from As You Sow, demanding greater disclosure on diversity data related to employee promotion, recruitment, and retention. Investors are concerned P&G's extensive advertising campaigns on race relations may be perceived as exploitative without accompanying internal diversity metrics. This shareholder action highlights a demand for concrete data to demonstrate the effectiveness of P&G's diversity, equity, and inclusion programs, contrasting with other companies that have agreed to increased reporting.

title: Citi execs silent on cost of risk overhaul
summary: During their Q3 earnings call, Citigroup executives, including CEO Michael Corbat and CFO Mark Mason, largely withheld details on the anticipated cost and timeline for overhauling the company's risk management and internal controls. This silence came despite recent enforcement actions and a $400 million civil penalty from the Federal Reserve and OCC. While acknowledging the multi-year effort and current spending of $1 billion, they emphasized improving profitability and shareholder returns under new CEO Jane Fraser, who will ultimately lead the transformation.

title: JPMorgan sticks with plan to build giant New York headquarters
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is proceeding with its plan to build a new mammoth headquarters in New York, despite uncertainties about future office occupancy due to the coronavirus pandemic. CEO Jamie Dimon stated the building is a 50-year investment, not a short-term decision, even though current office attendance is low. The bank plans to adapt floor plans and believes it has flexibility in managing its real estate.

title: Eaton Vance Deal Enables Customization by Morgan Stanley's Advisors
summary: Morgan Stanley's $7 billion acquisition of Eaton Vance will significantly benefit its advisors by enabling greater customization of product offerings, particularly through Eaton Vance's Parametric unit which specializes in highly customizable SMAs for tax harvesting and capital preservation. The deal also strengthens Morgan Stanley's investment options with Eaton Vance's fixed income teams for various securities. While the acquisition aims to enhance revenue and investment platforms, questions remain regarding how Morgan Stanley will manage potential conflicts of interest and integrate the businesses to maintain advisor independence in product selection.

title: Lauren Hobart appointed to Yum! Brands board
summary: Lauren R. Hobart, president of Dick’s Sporting Goods Inc., has been appointed to Yum! Brands Inc.'s board of directors, effective Nov. 12. Her leadership experience and knowledge from retail and consumer products companies, particularly her work in digital transformation and e-commerce at Dick's, are highlighted as valuable assets for Yum! Brands' growth and innovation.

title: Wells Fargo earnings fall short of estimates as low rates hit interest income
summary: Wells Fargo reported disappointing third-quarter earnings, missing analyst estimates with 42 cents per share against a Refinitiv forecast of 45 cents. The bank's net interest income declined by 19% due to historically low interest rates, though revenue of $18.86 billion surpassed expectations. Despite the challenges, Wells Fargo showed some positive signs with lower credit loss provisions and increased noninterest income, but its stock remained down significantly year-to-date.

title: Goldman's trading business returns to former glory during pandemic stress
summary: Goldman Sachs reported its best quarterly performance in a decade, largely driven by a 29% jump in trading revenue during the pandemic. The bank's limited exposure to consumer lending, unlike its rivals, proved to be an advantage. Analysts consider its current business mix, with strong capital markets leverage and a small, high-quality loan portfolio, to be well-suited for the current economic climate.

title: Goldman’s Pandemic Hot Streak Continues in Third Quarter
summary: Goldman Sachs reported a near-doubling of its third-quarter profit, reaching $3.62 billion on revenue of $10.78 billion, significantly exceeding analyst forecasts despite the ongoing pandemic and recession. This strong performance, driven by trading revenue increases, highlights Wall Street's continued profitability amidst broader economic challenges. While banks' "Main Street" arms also show resilience, concerns about a potential double-dip recession and prolonged high unemployment remain.

title: Dallas Orgs Get $7M of JPMorgan Chase's $10M Investment in Texas to Sustain Equal Access to Opportunity
summary: JPMorgan Chase is investing $10 million in Texas, with $7 million dedicated to Dallas organizations like The Commit Partnership, Dallas ISD, Dallas College, and UNT Dallas, to advance racial equity and create career pathways for underserved communities. This significant philanthropic effort aims to prepare Texans for the future workforce and address economic disparities, particularly for Black and Hispanic young adults. The investment builds on JPMorgan Chase's previous commitments and focuses on inclusive economic recovery through education, skills training, and policy solutions.

title: Royal Caribbean Raises $500 Million Through Stock Offering
summary: Royal Caribbean Group has successfully raised $500 million through a public stock offering, diluting shares by just over 3%. The cruise giant also announced a separate private offering of $500 million in senior convertible notes. Both offerings are expected to close on October 16, 2020, with the proceeds designated for general corporate purposes.

title: Truist posts $1.1B profit, continues merger-related job cuts and branch closures
summary: Truist reported a $1.1 billion profit for the third quarter of 2020, a significant increase from the previous year. The Charlotte-based bank is continuing to implement merger-related cost-cutting measures, including closing 104 branches and eliminating 769 jobs during the quarter, with plans for further consolidation in 2021. Despite the pandemic, the company is on track to achieve $1.6 billion in cost savings by 2022.

title: Morgan Stanley tops analysts' revenue estimates by $1 billion on stronger-than-expected trading
summary: Morgan Stanley exceeded analysts' revenue and profit estimates for the third quarter of 2020, primarily driven by strong performance in its Wall Street trading operations. The bank's profit jumped 25% year-over-year, and its total revenue hit a post-financial crisis record. CEO James Gorman highlighted the firm's balanced business model and its recent strategic acquisitions in wealth management and investment management as key to its success.

title: Array Technologies Raises $1.05B in Upsized IPO
summary: Array Technologies, a solar energy tracking solutions manufacturer, successfully raised $1.05 billion in an upsized initial public offering. The company's common stock began trading on the Nasdaq under the symbol "ARRY," with an enterprise valuation estimated at $2.8 billion. Array increased its IPO size twice, selling 47.5 million shares, though it will not receive funds from shares sold by its parent company.

title: Massachusetts bank Eastern Bankshares raises $1.8 billion in mutual-to-stock conversion and Nasdaq listing
summary: Eastern Bankshares, a Massachusetts bank, successfully raised $1.8 billion through a best-efforts subscription offering as part of its conversion from a mutual holding company to a publicly-traded stock corporation. The company began trading on the Nasdaq under the symbol EBC on October 15, 2020, achieving a market value of $1.9 billion at its $10 subscription price. Eastern Bankshares sold 179.3 million shares and donated an additional 7.5 million shares to its charitable foundation.

title: First Citizens, CIT Group Merger Will Create $100B Bank
summary: First Citizens and CIT Group announced an approximate $2.2 billion all-stock merger deal, which will create the 19th largest U.S. bank with over $100 billion in assets. Frank Holding Jr. of First Citizens will retain his roles as chairman and CEO of the combined company, while Ellen R. Alemany of CIT will become vice chairwoman and serve on the new board. The merged entity will be headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, and operate under the First Citizens name and NASDAQ ticker symbol FCNCA.

title: 'FinCEN Files' leaker harmed US anti-laundering regime and should be prosecuted, say bankers
summary: Bank compliance officers are calling for the prosecution of the individual responsible for leaking over 2,000 highly confidential suspicious activity reports (SARs) that led to the "FinCEN Files" news articles. They argue that the leak undermines trust in the SARs system, which is crucial for the U.S. fight against illicit financial transactions, and necessitates re-evaluation of how banks file these sensitive documents to maintain partnerships with law enforcement. Authorities are investigating the source of the leak, which has raised concerns about the efficacy and future of the anti-money laundering regime.

title: Pandemic presents a ‘terrific opportunity’ for BMO executive’s plans to digitize
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has prompted Bank of Montreal (BMO) chief strategy and operations officer Cameron Fowler to accelerate the bank's digitization efforts. Despite initial surges in digital adoption easing, Fowler aims to embed new digital tools across all BMO divisions and redefine workspace needs and branch functions. This strategic shift is expected to save hundreds of millions of dollars and modernize the bank's operations.

title: 5 of the Cheapest Business Class Awards to Europe
summary: This article identifies five of the cheapest business class award options for flights from the U.S. to Europe, highlighting international mileage programs that offer more competitive rates than U.S.-based airlines. It details specific airlines like Iberia, Turkish Airlines, ANA, Virgin Atlantic, and British Airways, outlining their award costs, routes, and methods for earning miles. The piece emphasizes leveraging airline partnerships and strategic mile transfers to achieve more affordable business class travel to Europe.

title: Array Technologies, Inc. Announces Closing of Initial Public Offering
summary: Array Technologies, Inc. announced the closing of its upsized initial public offering of 54,625,000 shares of common stock at $22.00 per share. The company's common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol "ARRY" on October 15, 2020. Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and J.P. Morgan acted as joint book-running managers for the offering.

title: Cardlytics Helps Banks Increase Customer Engagement and Deepen Business Banking Relationships by Powering Loyalty Programs
summary: Cardlytics, founded by Scott Grimes and Lynne Laube, helps banks leverage valuable customer data to power loyalty programs, increasing customer engagement and bank profits. The Purchase Intelligence™ platform strengthens banks' roles in commerce by providing relevant, measurable marketing and has expanded to over 2,000 financial institutions, including major partners like Chase, Bank of America, and PNC. Cardlytics prioritizes security by using anonymized data, ensuring sensitive customer information never leaves the bank, and has paid over $350 million in cash back rewards to customers.

title: At JPMorgan Chase, Mental Health Is Front and Center
summary: JPMorgan Chase prioritized mental health and well-being for its diverse global workforce, implementing initiatives long before the pandemic. Utilizing programs like "Coping Connections" and expanding family care, the company supported employees through pandemic challenges, racial injustice conversations, and childcare needs. Leadership buy-in and existing infrastructure allowed for a rapid pivot to address these evolving needs, highlighting a deep commitment to employee welfare.

title: SEC Updates Regulatory Framework for Fund of Funds Arrangements, but Private Funds Remain Subject to Limits on Purchases of Investment Company Shares (Investment Management)
summary: The SEC has updated its regulatory framework for fund of funds arrangements by adopting rule 12d1-4 and related amendments, aiming to streamline the investment process for registered funds. While these changes offer more flexibility for registered investment companies, private funds will continue to face the existing 3 percent limitation on investing in registered funds under sections 3(c)(1) and 3(c)(7) of the 1940 Act. Private funds must maintain policies and procedures to monitor adherence to this limit, and registered funds should update their compliance programs accordingly.

title: UBS Profit Doubles on Trading Surge
summary: UBS Group AG announced that its net profit nearly doubled in the third quarter due to a surge in client trading and deal-making, enabling the company to free up cash for dividends and share buybacks amidst the pandemic. This strong performance, particularly in its investment bank and wealth-management units, highlights the growing divergence between European banks during the health crisis. The results were achieved as CEO Sergio Ermotti approaches the end of his term.

title: Essent increases credit facility
summary: Essent Group Ltd has increased its credit facility from $500 million to $625 million, which includes an increase in its revolving credit facility and an additional non-amortising term loan. This move enhances the Bermudian-based mortgage re/insurer's capital and liquidity position, with borrowings available for working capital and general corporate purposes. The amended terms and extended maturity to October 2023 reflect Essent's strong financial profile and provide added financial flexibility.

title: JP Morgan Chase announces $7 million commitment to Nashville career pathway programs
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced a $7 million commitment to Nashville as part of its New Skills at Work investment. This funding aims to support career pathways for underrepresented students in the city. Nashville is one of six cities to receive this investment from the company's global initiative focused on addressing the demand for skilled workers.

title: After Helping Shepherd Pandemic Loans, Banks Now Brace for Regulatory Risks
summary: Banks that participated in the U.S. government's Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) are facing increasing regulatory scrutiny and legal risks despite their initial role in distributing $525 billion in pandemic loans. Concerns include potential violations of application rules, inadequate documentation, and "know your customer" compliance, as the government begins to forgive loans and fraud inquiries mount. Major lenders like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America have warned investors about these impending challenges.

title: GDS Holdings hosts Hong Kong IPO in bid to raise $1.8bn
summary: GDS Holdings, a Chinese data center company, is launching an IPO on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to raise $1.8 billion. The company plans to sell 160 million Class A ordinary shares at approximately $11 each, with a portion offered to Hong Kong investors and the rest internationally. Proceeds from the IPO will primarily fund data center expansion and R&D efforts.

title: Canyon Bicycles Said to Draw Takeover Interest From Carlyle, KKR
summary: Canyon Bicycles GmbH, a German bike manufacturer, has reportedly attracted takeover interest from several private equity firms including Carlyle Group and KKR & Co. The company could be valued at over 500 million euros, as investors seek to capitalize on the increased demand for bicycles. Other buyout firms like Advent International, Apax Partners, General Atlantic, and Permira are also said to be interested.

title: As Quibi Shutters, So Goes Nearly $2 Billion in Major Hollywood Investments
summary: Quibi, the mobile streaming startup led by Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman, is shutting down just six months after launching, resulting in the loss of nearly $2 billion in investments from major Hollywood studios and other financial entities. The company struggled to attract subscribers, falling far short of its targets, partly due to its launch coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic which disrupted its intended use case. Quibi plans to wind down operations, sell its assets, and return remaining funds to its investors.

title: Wells Fargo to Eliminate 401(k) Match for High-Paid Employees–Sources
summary: Wells Fargo & Co. is eliminating the 401(k) retirement account match for employees earning $250,000 or higher, as part of its expense reduction efforts. The bank aims to emphasize support for lower-paid employees and will introduce new efforts to seed retirement plans for those making less than $75,000 annually. Despite not anticipating significant savings from this change, it represents a broader measure taken by the bank to address financial pressures and past scandals.

title: Morgan Stanley Issues $1 Billion Social Bond Aimed at Supporting Affordable Housing
summary: Morgan Stanley announced the issuance of a $1 billion social bond, with proceeds dedicated to supporting affordable housing projects in the United States for low- and moderate-income individuals and families. This initiative aligns with the firm's strategy to use market-based solutions for sustainability challenges and leverage capital markets to strengthen communities. The social bond was issued under Morgan Stanley’s new Social Bond Framework, which details the criteria for eligible projects, including those contributing to UN Sustainable Development Goals.

title: PHOTOS: U.S. Bank debuts Pineville branch as local retail expansion continues
summary: U.S. Bank has opened a new branch on Pineville-Matthews Road in Pineville, continuing its local retail expansion efforts. This move is part of the bank's broader strategy to increase its presence in the Charlotte area. The article includes photos of the new branch.

title: Capital One Opens Wallet on Credit Performance
summary: Capital One has provided a detailed look into the performance of its consumer debt portfolio, showing an "eye-popping" improvement in third-quarter credit. The domestic credit card delinquency rate (30 days plus) fell to 2.21%, a significant decrease from the previous quarter. This positive trend offers some reassurance to investors regarding banks, though it provides less insight into the broader consumer economy.

title: Does Capital One Offer Student Loans?
summary: Capital One does not offer student loans, prompting individuals to seek alternatives for private student loans or refinancing. The article suggests exploring options from other banks, credit unions, online lenders like Ascent, College Ave, and Earnest, and state-based agencies. It also emphasizes exhausting federal financial aid opportunities before considering private loans due to their unique benefits.

title: iCapital Network® Leverages U.S. Success to Accelerate International Growth
summary: iCapital Network announced significant milestones in its international expansion, hiring industry veterans Marco Bizzozero and Tom Slocock to lead its growth in Europe and Asia. The company also plans to acquire a 65-person technology team in Portugal and open new offices in Lisbon, London, and Singapore. This expansion builds on iCapital's success in the U.S. and aims to meet the increasing global demand for private market investments.

title: Covid-19: Lloyds Bank allows staff to work remotely until spring next year
summary: Lloyds Banking Group has extended its remote working policy for most staff until at least spring 2021 due to the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic and rising case numbers in the UK. This decision aligns with government guidelines, affecting two-thirds of its 65,000 employees, with customer-facing roles continuing in branches. The bank is also navigating cost pressures, including recent job cuts and efforts to convert branch space into offices to adapt to the pandemic's impact.

title: JPMorgan creates new unit for blockchain projects, says the technology is close to making money
summary: JPMorgan has created a new business unit called Onyx dedicated to its blockchain and digital currency efforts, as JPM Coin is now being used commercially for international payments. The bank believes blockchain technology is nearing commercialization and real profitability after years of research and development. Onyx aims to address inefficiencies in wholesale payments, including cross-border transactions and paper check processing.

title: Inscripta Appoints Sri Kosaraju as President and CEO
summary: Inscripta, a digital genome engineering company, has appointed Sri Kosaraju as its new President and CEO, succeeding Kevin Ness. Kosaraju brings extensive experience from his previous roles at Penumbra and J.P. Morgan, and as a board member for 10x Genomics, positioning him to lead Inscripta during the commercial launch of its Onyx™ digital genome engineering platform. The change in leadership aims to accelerate the company's efforts to revolutionize gene editing and biological discovery across various industries.

title: Aditya Puri retires, Sashidhar Jagdishan takes over as HDFC Bank MD-CEO
summary: Aditya Puri, the long-serving MD and CEO of HDFC Bank, has retired after 26 years, with Sashidhar Jagdishan taking over the role. Puri's retirement aligns with RBI regulations on a private bank CEO's tenure not exceeding 70 years. Jagdishan, who has been with the bank since 1996, played a significant role in the bank's growth.

title: Shinhan closing in on HSBC to be top foreign bank in Vietnam
summary: Shinhan Bank Vietnam is on track to become the leading foreign bank in Vietnam, driven by strong performance, advanced digital services, and an aggressive localization strategy. The bank's net profit saw significant growth despite the global pandemic, placing it in fierce competition with HSBC Vietnam. Shinhan's focus on retail banking services, expansion of its network, and support for Korean SMEs in Vietnam have been key factors in its success.

title: Dave & Buster’s Announces Closing of $550 Million Senior Secured Notes Offering by its Subsidiary Dave & Buster’s, Inc.
summary: Dave & Buster's Entertainment, Inc. announced the closing of a $550 million senior secured notes offering by its subsidiary, Dave & Buster's, Inc. The proceeds from the 7.625% senior secured notes due 2025 will be used to repay outstanding amounts under its Term Loan Facility and drawings under its Revolving Credit Facility. J.P. Morgan acted as lead book running manager for the private offering.

title: Texas Capital Bancshares names JPMorgan executive Rob Holmes as its new CEO
summary: Texas Capital Bancshares has appointed Rob C. Holmes, a JPMorgan Chase & Co. executive, as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective January 2021. Holmes will replace Larry L. Helm, who took on the role after a proposed $5.5 billion merger with Independent Bank fell apart earlier in the year. The Dallas-based bank struggled earlier in 2020 but saw a turnaround in the third quarter after Helm took over.

title: Fifth Third names president, sparking succession speculation
summary: Fifth Third has promoted Tim Spence to president, leading to speculation that he is being groomed to succeed current CEO Greg Carmichael. Spence, 41, will oversee all business lines and regional banking, and previously served as executive vice president and head of consumer banking, payments and strategy. This move mirrors leadership succession discussions at other major banks like Citi and JPMorgan Chase.

title: What Counts as Race Discrimination? A Suit Against JPMorgan Is a Test (Published 2020)
summary: Wanda Wilson, a former secretary at JPMorgan Chase, has sued the bank alleging race discrimination and retaliation after what she described as racially driven bullying by a colleague and an inadequate response from management. JPMorgan denies the allegations, stating it denies engaging in any race discrimination, harassment, or retaliation. A judge has recently ruled that the two sides should engage in mediation.

title: JPMorgan Chase Rebrands Its Wealth Business
summary: JPMorgan Chase is reorganizing its wealth management business and in effect, rebranding it. This change is part of an initiative that began late last year. The article details these branding changes within the company's wealth management sector.

title: En sintonía con Wall Street, el S&P Merval perdió 6,8%
summary: The S&P Merval index fell by 6.8% in line with Wall Street's decline, while Argentine American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) also saw significant drops. This financial downturn was attributed to concerns over a second wave of coronavirus and upcoming US presidential elections. Additionally, Argentina's country risk increased, and bonds in dollars continued to fall, while the financial dollar retreated against the stable official dollar.

title: Indexed investment - A new perspective on investing in China's bond market
summary: China's bond market, now the world's second largest at 109 trillion yuan (US$16.3 trillion), is increasingly appealing to international investors due to its strong returns, diverse offerings, and low correlation with other major markets. Indexed investment in RMB bonds is rapidly growing, with a significant increase in domestic bond index funds and overseas-listed RMB bond ETFs. ChinaBond Indices, managed by a CCDC subsidiary, is highlighted as the leading and most accurate provider of RMB bond indices, offering unique advantages to investors looking to capitalize on China's bond market opportunities.

title: DoubleVerify Announces $350 Million Investment from Group Led by Tiger Global Management
summary: DoubleVerify announced a $350 million investment from a group led by Tiger Global Management, including Fidelity, BlackRock, and Neuberger Berman. Providence Equity Partners will remain the majority investor. The investment will be used to purchase shares from existing shareholders and support DoubleVerify's continued growth, particularly in media performance optimization and Connected TV analytics.

title: The Son of Former Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy Helped Trump Secure Loans at Deutsche Bank
summary: Justin Kennedy, son of former Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy, helped Donald Trump secure nearly $700 million in loans from Deutsche Bank in 2005 for a Chicago skyscraper, despite Trump's history of loan defaults. This connection fueled rumors of a "White House charm offensive" to encourage Justice Kennedy's retirement, paving the way for Brett Kavanaugh's appointment. The article also mentions another son, Gregory Kennedy, and his alleged meeting with Kellyanne Conway regarding his father's happiness after Trump's election.

title: JPMorgan Chase Elects Phebe N. Novakovic to its Board of Directors
summary: JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM) announced the election of Phebe N. Novakovic, Chairman and CEO of General Dynamics Corporation, to its Board of Directors, effective December 7, 2020. Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO of JPMorgan Chase, highlighted Ms. Novakovic's respected executive status and deep knowledge in defense, intelligence, technology, and cyber as valuable additions to the company. Ms. Novakovic expressed enthusiasm about joining the talented board and contributing her experience to the firm's continued success.

title: Should you buy a bank ETF or build your own?
summary: Experts suggest that investors might be better off building their own portfolio of Canadian bank stocks rather than investing in a bank ETF, primarily due to the low number of stocks involved (the "Big Six") and the ability to save on management fees with commission-free trading platforms. While some bank ETFs offer leveraged or income-boosting strategies, historically, these have often underperformed or incurred higher fees. The article highlights that building a DIY portfolio of the Big Six banks can be a cost-effective and straightforward approach for Canadian investors.

title: Ravin Dajee, Managing Director of Absa Bank (Mauritius) Limited
summary: Ravin Dajee, Managing Director of Absa Bank (Mauritius) Limited, navigated the bank through the significant rebranding from Barclays to Absa and managed the challenges posed by the 2008 financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic. He emphasizes the bank's commitment to being a partner for corporates expanding into Africa, leveraging partnerships with Société Générale and MIGA. Dajee also highlights the crucial role of digital transformation and personalized banking experiences in the evolving financial landscape, while reaffirming Absa Bank (Mauritius)'s strong performance and dedication to national development.

title: Capital One to let most US call-center workers stay remote after pandemic
summary: Capital One announced that most of its U.S. call-center employees for cards will permanently work from home after the pandemic, increasing the remote workforce from 20% to 90%. This decision aligns Capital One with other card networks like Synchrony Financial and American Express, departing from the repopulation efforts of branch-heavy banks like JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs. CEO Richard Fairbank emphasized employee well-being and the success of a multi-year technology transformation enabling this shift.

title: This Bank Wants to Use Animal Crossing to Sell You on Financial Services
summary: Ally, a financial services company, hosted a sponsored island in Animal Crossing to market its banking and investment services to millennials. The campaign aimed to connect with a demographic less engaged with traditional banking by showcasing financial products within the game's context, emphasizing wealth management and investing as easy and accessible. The article critiques this marketing approach as a manifestation of the financialization of games and the gamification of finance, aiming to define how millennial consumers "should" act in a capitalistic system.

title: American Express pledges $1B toward racial, gender equality
summary: American Express has committed $1 billion to advance racial and gender equality, with a significant portion dedicated to doubling spending with diverse and minority-owned suppliers to $750 million annually by 2024. The company also announced it achieved 100% gender pay equity worldwide and aims to support Black-owned businesses, female entrepreneurs, and non-profit organizations led by underrepresented groups. This pledge follows similar commitments from other financial institutions in response to recent social justice movements.

title: Calculating Interest in International Arbitration: How Is Interest Determined?
summary: This article discusses how interest is determined in international arbitration, distinguishing between pre-award and post-award interest and the different types of interest (simple vs. compound). It highlights the wide discretion arbitrators have in determining interest rates, often guided by agreements between parties or commercial benchmarks, and provides examples from various ICSID cases. The piece also examines factors influencing interest rate selection, such as investment risk and currency.

title: Dayton area business people hired, promoted
summary: This article details recent hirings and promotions among business professionals in the Dayton area. Key appointments include Tony Boddie at Merchants Bank of Indiana, new volunteer officials at Day Air Credit Union, and Tara Marlow as CEO of the Boys & Girls Club of Dayton. Additionally, Dr. Isaac Koh joined Soin Family Practice Center, and Jocelyn Spencer Rhynard was reappointed to the Ohio School Boards Association’s Federal Relations Network.

title: Marvell Acquires Inphi in Cloud and 5G Push
summary: Marvell Technology Group announced its acquisition of Inphi Corp. in a cash-and-stock deal estimated at up to $10 billion, aiming to accelerate growth in cloud and 5G infrastructure. This move will create a "U.S. semiconductor powerhouse" by combining Inphi's silicon photonics for optical interconnects with Marvell's copper interconnects, expanding Marvell's footprint in the networking industry. Analysts view the deal positively, noting it will increase Marvell's exposure to data center and 5G markets and diversify its offerings.

title: JPMorgan Chase warns of upcoming fine over internal controls
summary: JPMorgan Chase has disclosed that it anticipates a civil money penalty from a regulator due to historical deficiencies in internal controls and auditing within its advisory business. This comes shortly after a significant $920 million fine for market manipulation.
