The bank is currently in discussions with the undisclosed regulator to resolve the issue, and this type of enforcement action is becoming more common among federal regulators for major banks concerning internal control lapses.

title: Capital One, JPMorgan Chase top J.D. Power’s small-business satisfaction survey
summary: A J.D. Power survey revealed that small businesses' satisfaction with their banks increased in 2020, particularly for larger businesses and those approved for the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP). Capital One and JPMorgan Chase emerged as top performers in various regions, though overall satisfaction varied significantly between business sizes and PPP outcomes. The survey highlights that banks successfully delivered for many during the pandemic but need to refine approaches for smaller businesses.

title: This Indian banker is the world’s best, says The Economist
summary: The Economist has named former HDFC Bank CEO Aditya Puri as the "world's best banker" for delivering over 16,000% cumulative returns to shareholders during his tenure. HDFC Bank, launched in 1994, is now the world’s 10th most valuable bank, surpassing Citibank and HSBC. Puri's success is attributed to his vision, attention to detail, focus on Indian consumers and firms, and strategic investment in technology.

title: Deutsche Bank Luxembourg announced management changes
summary: Deutsche Bank announced significant management changes for its Luxembourg subsidiary, Deutsche Bank Luxembourg S.A., and the Luxembourg branch of Deutsche Bank AG. Frank Krings will transition to the Supervisory Board, while Frank Rückbrodt will become CEO of Deutsche Bank Luxembourg S.A. and Chief Country Officer for Luxembourg. Alexander Ilgen will take over as Chairman of the Supervisory Board.

title: Videocon-ICICI case: ED chargesheets Chanda Kochhar, others, with ‘5 trunks’ of supporting documents
summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has filed a chargesheet against former ICICI Bank CEO Chanda Kochhar, her husband Deepak Kochhar, and Videocon Group chief Venugopal Dhoot in an alleged money laundering case. The case involves an illegal sanctioning of loans worth Rs 1,875 crore to Videocon Group during Chanda Kochhar's tenure, with a portion of the loan allegedly transferred to Deepak Kochhar's company, NuPower Renewables. The ED has provisionally attached assets worth Rs 78.15 crore belonging to the Kochhar family.

title: How Our Clients Help Veteran Communities | JPMorgan Chase
summary: JPMorgan Chase supports veteran communities through the New Markets Tax Credit (NMTC) Program, investing in various community facilities and businesses. These projects provide essential services like healthy food, healthcare, education, and social support to veterans, particularly those who are homeless, at risk, or disabled. The article highlights several client organizations, including Three Square Food Bank, Southwestern Oregon Community College, Community Healthcare Network, Paul's Place, Meals on Wheels San Francisco, Salvation Army Harrisburg, and John E. Alexander South Wood County YMCA, demonstrating diverse approaches to veteran assistance.

title: JP Morgan to Pay $800,000 in Back Wages in Lawsuit Over Women's Wages
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has agreed to pay at least $800,000 in back wages to 93 women as part of a 2017 lawsuit alleging the company underpaid women compared to men in the same positions. In addition to the back wages, JPMorgan will allocate $9 million over five years for compensation adjustments. The lawsuit, brought by the US Department of Labor, highlighted an ongoing struggle for pay equity in the US, where women continue to earn significantly less than men.

title: HDFC Bank appoints Ramesh Lakshminarayanan as CIO
summary: HDFC Bank has appointed Ramesh Lakshminarayanan as its new Group Head – Information Technology, with the designation of Chief Information Officer (CIO). In this role, he will be responsible for the bank's technology strategy, strengthening foundational technology, enhancing digital capabilities, and leveraging AI/ML solutions. Lakshminarayanan previously served as Chief Technology and Information Officer at CRISIL and has over 25 years of experience in the industry.

title: JPMorgan Chase’s QuickAccept first step to building SMB ecosystem
summary: JPMorgan Chase's QuickAccept payment acceptance solution, built on WePay technology, is the first step in the bank's vision to create a comprehensive ecosystem for small- to medium-sized businesses (SMBs). The solution offers SMBs real-time, fee-free access to funds accepted at the point of sale, a key differentiator in a competitive market. JPMorgan Chase aims to integrate payment acceptance with other financial services, leveraging its banking infrastructure to provide a one-stop-shop for diverse SMB needs.

title: What executives at Pioneer Bank, Bank of Greene County made in 2020
summary: This article discusses the compensation of executives at Pioneer Bank and Bank of Greene County for the year 2020. It notes that strong bank performances in 2020 led to increased total compensation for almost every named executive at Albany-area banks with fiscal years ending in June 2020.

title: Sallie Mae lays off 100+ in Delaware in restructuring
summary: Sallie Mae laid off 105 employees in Delaware as part of a company-wide restructuring to cut costs and boost operating efficiencies amid a disrupted higher education market. The layoffs represent 6% of the company's total workforce and incurred $24 million in restructuring expenses, primarily for severance and benefits. Despite the cuts, Sallie Mae is actively hiring in Delaware and its CEO stated the restructuring is to align the business with strategic imperatives and strengthen the company for 2021.

title: Van Eck targets China’s retail fund market
summary: Van Eck has submitted an application to the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) to establish a public mutual fund company in mainland China, aiming to tap into the RMB 17.8trn retail mutual fund market. The firm plans to offer ETF products, including thematic ETFs, and multi-asset allocation solutions, leveraging its extensive experience in Chinese capital markets since 1992. Additionally, Van Eck intends to apply for a Qualified Domestic Limited Partnership (QDLP) license, allowing it to raise funds in China for offshore investments.

title: Bank of Montreal hires new CFO from U.S. rival
summary: Bank of Montreal has appointed Tayfun Tuzun as its new chief financial officer, poaching him from U.S. rival Fifth Third Bancorp. Current CFO Tom Flynn will transition to a vice-chair role, focusing on client relationships. The appointment comes amidst other leadership changes, including a new general counsel and digital leadership, as BMO aims to bring in fresh talent and refine strategies while maintaining stability.

title: Private Prison Stocks Drop as the Reality of Biden’s Win Sinks In
summary: Following President-elect Joe Biden's victory, stocks for the two largest private prison companies, GEO Group and CoreCivic, significantly dropped as Biden campaigned on ending the federal government's use of private prisons. These companies heavily rely on federal contracts for over 50% of their revenue. While ending Bureau of Prisons contracts might be straightforward, dismantling immigration detention in private facilities, which accounts for about 70% of ICE detainees, presents a more complex challenge due to its deep entrenchment within federal operations.

title: Ex-SoFi CEO’s company Figure seeks national bank charter
summary: Figure Technologies, a fintech founded by former SoFi CEO Mike Cagney, has applied for a national bank charter through the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC). The company, which specializes in home equity lines of credit on a private blockchain, aims to cut compliance costs and expand its consumer product offerings nationwide by consolidating under one regulator. This move follows a trend of fintechs seeking national charters, including Cagney's previous company, SoFi, and highlights ongoing debates within the industry regarding regulatory oversight for non-bank entities.

title: JP Morgan to conduct pay analysis, pay $9.8M to settle DOL claim that it underpaid women
summary: JP Morgan Chase & Co. has agreed to pay $9.8 million to resolve charges by the U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) that it underpaid women in certain functions since 2012. The settlement includes $800,000 in back pay and interest, plus $9 million set aside for annual pay adjustments over five years starting in 2021. The company will also conduct pay equity analyses for U.S. employees to address pay equity for women and minorities.

title: Mibanco llegó a Colombia
summary: Mibanco has officially entered Colombia through the merger by absorption of microcredit bank Bancompartir and Encumbra (Edyficar S.A.S). This integration aims to expand financial inclusion, promote formal savings, and consolidate Mibanco's presence in areas with limited credit access, leveraging a portfolio of over COP 840 billion and more than 492,000 clients. Mibanco plans to reach 700,000 clients in the next three years, establishing itself as a key player in Colombia's microcredit market.

title: HDFC Bank aims to grow merchant payments base to 20 million in 3 years
summary: HDFC Bank plans to expand its merchant network from 2 million to 20 million within the next three years. This expansion is supported by the upgraded Smart Hub platform, which offers various digital tools like a digital ledger, billing software, and inventory management. The bank intends to cross-sell loans and credit cards, including 'buy now, pay later' options, to further drive growth and deepen digital payment penetration across India.

title: Japanese banks to hit profit goals as stimulus curtails bad loans
summary: Japan's three largest banks, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, and Mizuho Financial Group, are expected to meet their annual profit targets. This is largely due to massive government and central bank aid that has controlled bad loan costs by spurring lending and supporting companies during the pandemic-fueled recession. Additionally, a rise in investment banking has helped offset the impact of low-interest rates on lending profitability both domestically and internationally.

title: Irsa y Cresud: contundente apoyo al canje de sus ON
summary: IRSA and Cresud successfully concluded their debt exchange offers, receiving strong support from investors. IRSA achieved a 98.31% acceptance rate for its bonds totaling US$178 million, while Cresud saw an 88.41% acceptance for US$65 million. The exchange involved the issuance of new series of negotiable obligations with varying maturity dates, enabling the companies to navigate restrictions imposed by the BCRA on foreign currency debt payments.

title: Summary Of Executive Moves In Global Wealth Management - September 2020
summary: This article summarizes executive appointments and changes in the global wealth management sector across various regions (International, Asia-Pacific, North America) during September 2020. Key firms like BNY Mellon, State Street, Deutsche Bank, HSBC, Citi Private Bank, and Raymond James made significant hires and promotions in roles ranging from portfolio managers and CIOs to regional heads and client strategists, reflecting a dynamic period of talent movement in the industry.

title: Northeast Ohio is about to get another public company: Sotera Health
summary: Sotera Health, a Broadview Heights-based company providing lab services to the medical device and pharmaceutical industries, announced plans for an initial public offering (IPO) expected to raise over $1 billion. The company intends to sell 46.6 million shares priced between $20 and $23, valuing it at nearly $6.4 billion. Sotera Health will list on Nasdaq under the symbol "SHC" and will use the proceeds for working capital and debt reduction.

title: RBC, TD remain on "too big to fail" list
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) and TD Bank continue to be listed as Canada's only global systemically important banks (G-SIBs) by the Financial Stability Board (FSB) in its 2020 update. Both banks remain in the lowest "bucket," indicating their additional capital and oversight requirements. The updated list also saw several major U.S. banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and Wells Fargo, move to lower risk categories, while China Construction Bank moved to a higher bucket.

title: Medical sterilization firm Sotera Health looks to raise $1.07 bln in IPO
summary: Medical sterilization firm Sotera Health Co, backed by private equity firms Warburg Pincus and GTCR, aims to raise up to $1.07 billion in its initial public offering. The company plans to sell 46.6 million shares at $20 to $23 each, targeting a valuation of $6.38 billion. This IPO follows a previous attempt to sell the company in 2018, which was abandoned due to lawsuits alleging health problems near one of its factories.

title: Carnival Files To Raise $1.5 Billion Through Equity Offering
summary: Carnival Corporation has announced a $1.5 billion "at-the-market" equity offering to address its significant cash burn, which reached over $500 million per month. The company reported a $2.8 billion loss in Q3 2020 and saw a 99.5% revenue drop compared to the previous year. This offering, in conjunction with J.P. Morgan Securities and Goldman Sachs & Co., aims to provide a less expensive capital-raising option as the cruise industry works towards a gradual restart in early 2021.

title: DoorDash files for its long-awaited IPO
summary: DoorDash has filed for its IPO, expected between Thanksgiving and Christmas, with Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan leading the offering. The company reported a $149 million net loss on $1.9 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2020, but saw significant order growth amidst the pandemic. Shareholder details and future outlook, including the impact of COVID-19 on growth rates, are also outlined.

title: JPMorgan Chase to expand to Mississippi, build branches in Jackson
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced plans to open its first Mississippi branch in Jackson's Highland Village Shopping Center by April 2021, creating eight to 10 new jobs with entry-level positions starting at $15 an hour plus full benefits. This initial branch is part of a larger strategy to expand into the Jackson metro area, driven by the region's recent economic growth and the bank's existing client base in Mississippi.

title: LPL Affiliate Gladstone Hires $2-Billion Morgan Stanley Team
summary: Gladstone Wealth Management, an LPL Financial affiliate, has recruited a team of advisors, John W. Gallagher and Mark T. Levin, from Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, bringing with them $2 billion in assets and $5 million in annual revenue. This move represents Gladstone's largest recruitment to date and allows the advisors to operate with greater independence and a higher payout level. They plan to expand their business by leveraging Gladstone's partnership model and LPL's open architecture platform.

title: PNC Bank Buying BBVA USA Bancshares for $11.6 Billion
summary: PNC Financial Services Group is acquiring BBVA USA Bancshares for $11.6 billion, a deal expected to close in mid-2021. This acquisition will create one of the largest banks in the U.S., with a significant presence across 29 of the 30 largest markets and an estimated $560 billion in assets, ranking it as the seventh-largest American bank. The transaction will see existing BBVA USA branches converted to the PNC Bank name and its customers transitioned to the PNC platform.

title: Spain's BBVA exits U.S. in $11.6 bln deal with PNC
summary: Spain's BBVA is selling its U.S. business to PNC Financial Services Group Inc for $11.6 billion in cash, marking one of the largest global bank deals this year and another European retreat from the U.S. market. The sale is expected to consolidate the U.S. banking sector and sparked speculation that BBVA might use the proceeds to acquire a rival bank in Spain. This deal also creates an American bank with nearly $560 billion in assets and a presence in two dozen states.

title: Home Depot to buy back HD Supply in $8 bln deal
summary: Home Depot announced its acquisition of HD Supply Holdings Inc. for approximately $8 billion, aiming to regain control over the industrial materials wholesaler it spun off over a decade ago. The deal, offering $56 per share, seeks to expand Home Depot's reach into building utility and maintenance products, with the company expecting the acquisition to be accretive to earnings in 2021.

title: Banco Santander Is Reportedly Planning to Shut Down Up to 1,000 Branches, May Cut 4,000 Jobs
summary: Banco Santander is reportedly planning significant cost-cutting measures in Spain, including the closure of up to 1,000 branches and the elimination of 4,000 jobs. These actions are a response to economic challenges from the COVID-19 pandemic, low interest rates in the euro zone, and a growing consumer shift to digital banking. The bank, along with other European lenders, is struggling to adapt to these market changes and maintain operational efficiency.

title: BBVA sells U.S. subsidiary to PNC for $11.6 billion
summary: BBVA has agreed to sell its U.S. subsidiary to PNC for $11.6 billion in cash, a transaction that will significantly enhance BBVA's financial position and provide flexibility for capital deployment and shareholder distributions. The deal, valued at 19.7 times the unit's 2019 earnings, excludes BBVA's broker dealer and New York branch, allowing BBVA to continue serving corporate and institutional clients in the U.S. PNC will become the fifth-largest bank in the U.S. by assets after the transaction closes, which is expected in mid-2021.

title: The FICO Credit Score Range and How It Applies to Your Credit Cards
summary: This article explains the FICO credit score range (300-850) and how it impacts credit card options, including APRs, credit limits, and eligibility for cards. It categorizes FICO scores into five ranges from "Exceptional" to "Very Poor" and provides tips on how to improve and maintain good credit scores, emphasizing timely payments and managing credit utilization. The authors stress that while scores from various sources may differ, their directional movement generally aligns.

title: The Home Depot Announces Agreement to Acquire HD Supply Holdings, Inc.
summary: The Home Depot announced its agreement to acquire HD Supply Holdings, Inc. for approximately $8 billion in cash. This acquisition aims to accelerate sales growth by positioning The Home Depot as a premier provider in the MRO marketplace, serving multifamily and hospitality end markets. The transaction is expected to be accretive to earnings per share in fiscal 2021 and is anticipated to close during The Home Depot's fiscal fourth quarter, which ends January 31, 2021.

title: Home Depot (HD) Buying HD Supply (HDS) In $8 Billion Deal
summary: Home Depot (HD) announced it is reacquiring HD Supply Holdings Inc (HDS) in an $8 billion deal, paying $56 per share. HD Supply, a national distributor of maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) products, was spun out of Home Depot over a decade ago. The acquisition is expected to close in Q4 of Home Depot’s fiscal year and will be funded through cash on hand and debt, with projections for the deal to be accretive to earnings in fiscal 2021.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | PNC Financial Services to Buy U.S. Arm of Spain’s BBVA for $11.6 Billion
summary: PNC Financial Services Group Inc. has agreed to acquire the U.S. operations of Spain's BBVA for $11.6 billion. This deal marks one of the largest bank mergers since the financial crisis, poised to establish the fifth-largest U.S. retail bank with over $550 billion in assets.

title: PNC buys Houston-based BBVA USA for $11.6 billion
summary: PNC Financial Services Group has agreed to acquire BBVA's Houston-based U.S. banking operations for $11.6 billion, positioning it to become the country's largest regional bank. This acquisition allows PNC to expand into Texas and California, using funds from its BlackRock Inc. stake sale, while providing BBVA with capital for potential acquisitions and an exit from a business that has weighed on its earnings. The deal, expected to close by June, will boost PNC's earnings and significantly expand its presence across the southern and southwestern U.S.

title: Spain's BBVA Sells US Arm To PNC In $11.6 Billion Deal
summary: PNC Financial Services Group, which previously divested its stake in BlackRock, has agreed to acquire the US arm of Spain's BBVA for $11.6 billion. This acquisition will expand PNC's presence across 29 of the 30 largest markets in the US, adding substantial deposits and loans. The deal, expected to close in mid-2021, aims to be significantly accretive to PNC's earnings and generate over $900 million in cost savings.

title: PayPal Partners with Even to Provide New Tools to Improve the Financial Health of its Workforce
summary: PayPal has partnered with Even, an on-demand pay platform, to enhance the financial well-being of its U.S. employees. This initiative allows staff to access earned wages early, budget, and save through a mobile app, building on PayPal's efforts to increase the net disposable income of its hourly and entry-level workers. PayPal also plans to extend similar services internationally and is advocating for broader corporate focus on worker financial health with other organizations.

title: Think Private Prison Companies Are Going Away Under Biden? They Have Other Plans
summary: Despite the election of Joe Biden, who pledged to curb private prisons, major companies like CoreCivic and GEO Group are well-positioned to continue profiting. They have been aggressively diversifying their business models, shifting away from traditional prisons towards other government contracts such as commercial real estate, electronic monitoring, and halfway houses, and capitalizing on growing needs for immigration detention and re-entry services. This strategic pivot ensures their financial stability even as the political climate changes regarding mass incarceration.

title: Saudi Aramco gets $8 billion with jumbo five-part bond deal
summary: Saudi Aramco successfully raised $8 billion through a five-part bond deal, receiving $48.1 billion in order; this marks a significant move by the world's largest oil producer to secure cash amid low oil prices and to fund its substantial dividend payments and the acquisition of a 70% stake in Saudi Basic Industries (SABIC). The bond placement is part of a broader trend of Gulf issuers tapping international debt markets to address pandemic- and oil price-related financial pressures. The sale included tranches ranging from three to 50 years, with the 50-year bond being the longest-dated international debt issued by Saudi Arabia to date.

title: Pimco full of confidence: Targets annual double digit growth in the Nordics
summary: Pimco aims for annual double-digit growth in its Nordic business by focusing on wholesale, alternatives, and ESG strategies, as well as working closely with regional banks. The asset manager sees strong potential due to the increasing need for active management in fixed income and higher-yielding strategies amidst low government bond yields. This growth strategy includes expanding its reach within regional banks through various channels and emphasizing its ESG offerings, which recently secured a significant mandate from a Danish pension fund.

title: Desglobalización bancaria
summary: BBVA's strategic move to sell its US operations and propose a merger with Banco Sabadell signifies a shift towards "desglobalización" and a "back to basics" approach, focusing on its traditional Spanish market. This strategy aims to improve solvency and achieve synergies to counter low banking profitability in Spain and Europe, despite increasing market concentration. The article also notes that while national market share will rise, competition in sub-markets and from non-bank digital entities will mitigate potential negative effects.

title: J.P. Morgan Launches New Equity ETF In BetaBuilders Suite, BBSC
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management has expanded its BetaBuilders suite with the introduction of the JPMorgan BetaBuilders U.S. Small Cap Equity ETF (BBSC). This new ETF aims to offer low-cost exposure to the small-cap U.S. equity market through an indexed approach, closely tracking the Morningstar US Small Cap Target Market Exposure Extended Index. The launch emphasizes J.P. Morgan's commitment to providing efficient, diversified portfolio building blocks for investors.

title: European Customer Experience Index, 2020: How Banks And Insurers Can Connect CX With Business Impact
summary: This article discusses the findings from Forrester's European Customer Experience Index, 2020, focusing on how banking and insurance companies can link customer experience (CX) to business impact. It highlights that CX leaders achieve faster revenue growth and cost reductions, but many financial services firms struggle to quantify this value. The research, based on a survey across several European countries, reveals that direct banks outperform incumbents in CX, while most insurers offer mediocre and undifferentiated experiences, underscoring the need for these firms to prioritize CX improvements to drive financial performance.

title: GoodRx Shares Plunge After Amazon Announces Online Pharmacy
summary: GoodRx Holdings Inc. shares plunged nearly 28% after Amazon.com Inc. announced its entrance into the online pharmacy market, including a service offering steep prescription drug discounts to Prime customers. This move led to an immediate downgrade of GoodRx stock by a JPMorgan Chase analyst and raised concerns about GoodRx's operating margins due to potential price competition. Amazon's offering, which includes online purchasing for home delivery and discounts that could rival GoodRx's, positions it as a significant competitor in the prescription drug market.

title: People are Stopping Toxic Pipelines and Terminals
summary: This article highlights the growing movement to stop fossil fuel expansion projects, emphasizing the success of Indigenous communities and environmental organizations in delaying or halting toxic pipelines and terminals. It details various ongoing struggles against projects like the KXL Pipeline, Dakota Access Pipeline, fracked gas terminals in Texas, Line 3 Pipeline, Coastal GasLink pipeline, and Trans Mountain Pipeline, crediting people power and financial pressure on banks and insurers. The article underscores challenges to corporate power and calls for continued action against fossil fuel financing.

title: Why FuelCell Energy Should Consider Yet Another Capital Raise
summary: FuelCell Energy's stock has seen a significant surge, fueled by investor interest in alternative and renewable energy, despite a history of declining revenue and operating losses. Given this newfound market enthusiasm, the article suggests that FuelCell Energy should consider another capital raise, similar to Plug Power's recent successful offering, to secure operating and growth capital without significant stock punishment. This opportunistic move would leverage investor willingness to overlook dilution in the current market climate.

title: Giant Halliburton building to be demolished this week
summary: The former Halliburton building in west Houston, a 585,000-square-foot structure, is set for demolition this week to make way for a mixed-use redevelopment. Built in the late 1970s for Brown & Root, a Halliburton subsidiary, the vacant building's materials will be repurposed, and Gensler will design the new project. The property is owned by a local investment group led by Lawrence Wong, with Johnson Development Services providing fee development services.

title: Reddit Welcomes Paula Price to Board of Directors
summary: Reddit announced the appointment of Paula Price to its Board of Directors. Price brings over 30 years of experience as a finance leader with expertise in public company finance, board governance, and risk management from major brands like Macy's and JPMorgan Chase. CEO Steve Huffman highlighted her experience with transformative growth and passion for Reddit's mission as key reasons for her appointment.

title: The brand value of equality: five women from JPMorgan on what works
summary: This article features five women leaders from JPMorgan Chase discussing the importance of equality and why the company invests in it. It highlights their perspectives on the brand value derived from fostering an equitable environment. The piece was published by The Female Quotient in collaboration with Ad Age.

title: NISN - NiSun International Enterprise Development Group Co Ltd Stock Price and Quote
summary: This article provides a stock price quote and financial data for NiSun International Enterprise Development Group Co Ltd (NISN), including market capitalization, insider ownership, and performance metrics. It also lists recent news releases and operational updates detailing the company's expansion into various sectors like edible oil trading, corn supply, and gold business.

title: The independent artist market is exploding in China – with NetEase and Tencent battling to woo the best indie acts
summary: The independent artist market in China is rapidly expanding, leading to a fierce competition between major streaming platforms Tencent Music Entertainment (TME) and NetEase Cloud Music to attract and support indie artists. Both companies are investing heavily in programs that offer financial incentives, professional services, and exclusive opportunities to independent musicians, driving significant growth in artist numbers and original content on their platforms. This battle for indie artists is seen as a crucial factor for future market share dominance in the Chinese music industry.

title: ETFs Answer Investor Appetite for Small Caps
summary: Small-cap stocks, as tracked by the Russell 2000 index, showed strong performance in late summer and early fall, outperforming the Nasdaq 100. This shift indicates investors are looking beyond megatech and the pandemic, seeking diversification and more reasonable valuations in smaller companies. Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) like the iShares Russell 2000 ETF (IWM) are proving to be cost-effective and flexible tools for institutional investors to gain exposure to the small-cap market.

title: Fifth Third Bank plots next branch in Charlotte amid fast-paced retail expansion
summary: Fifth Third Bancorp is planning to open another retail branch in Charlotte, continuing its rapid expansion in the region. This news comes as the bank has been actively growing its presence in the Charlotte market, a strategy that has been highlighted by its CEO. The ongoing expansion indicates a significant focus on retail banking growth in the area.

title: UPDATE: Bank of America Says Access to Merrill Accounts Has Been Restored
summary: Bank of America's Merrill Lynch wealth management platform experienced widespread technology outages for about four hours on Tuesday, preventing advisors from wiring client funds and confirming stock executions, and blocking self-directed Merrill Edge customers from accessing their accounts. While a bank spokesman confirmed services were restored, the incident led to significant customer frustration and financial losses for some, highlighting persistent issues with brokerage platforms during active trading periods. This outage follows several similar incidents for Merrill and other firms, prompting clients to consider switching brokers.

title: Watch Room for China's E-Commerce Operators To Grow, JPMorgan's Yao Says
summary: Alex Yao, co-head of Asia technology, media, and telecommunications (TMT) research at JPMorgan Chase & Co., believes there is still significant growth potential for China's e-commerce operators. He discussed this outlook with Rishaad Salamat and Juliette Saly on "Bloomberg Markets: Asia." The interview covers the continued expansion opportunities within the Chinese e-commerce sector.

title: JPMorgan Chase Unit to Pay $250 Million Penalty Over Poor Internal Controls
summary: A unit of JPMorgan Chase & Co. has been fined $250 million by a top banking regulator for deficiencies in its internal controls and audit practices. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency cited the bank's weak risk-management and insufficient framework for avoiding conflicts of interest. This penalty follows a separate $920 million settlement related to allegations of misconduct in the precious metals and Treasury markets.

title: Quincecare: recent challenges to the duty
summary: This article discusses recent legal challenges to the Quincecare duty, which requires financial institutions to refrain from processing payment instructions if they suspect fraud. It examines two key cases, Hamblin v World First Ltd and Stanford International Bank Ltd v HSBC Bank plc, highlighting how the duty extends beyond traditional banks to other businesses handling client monies and its application in insolvency scenarios for the benefit of creditors. The author concludes that Quincecare claims are likely to become more frequent, particularly in light of increasing fraud and insolvencies.

title: Hurun China 500 Most Valuable Private Companies 2020
summary: The Hurun Research Institute, in association with Shimao Haixia, released the Hurun China 500 Most Valuable Private Companies 2020. Tencent surpassed Alibaba to become China's most valuable private company, with its value increasing 75% to US$743 billion. The report highlights the rapid growth of the new economy, with healthcare emerging as the top industry and Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Hangzhou concentrating half of the top companies.

title: Pinterest (NYSE: PINS) Stock is a Real Influencer Play
summary: Pinterest (NYSE: PINS) showcased strong performance in Q3 FY 2020, exceeding analyst expectations for both EPS and revenue, largely due to its increasing global user base and its unique, non-intrusive approach to e-commerce and advertising. Analysts subsequently upgraded the stock, citing its growth initiatives, international expansion, and "brand-safe" environment that attracted advertisers. The article suggests opportunistic pullback levels for investors looking to capitalize on Pinterest's momentum as a "dual narrative play" benefiting from both user growth during the pandemic and an advertising rebound.

title: ETF of the Week: SPDR S&P 500 ESG ETF (EFIV)
summary: This article discusses the SPDR S&P 500 ESG ETF (EFIV), highlighting its methodology for selecting companies based on environmental, social, and governance factors, and its strong performance compared to the broader S&P 500. It also delves into the growing interest in ESG investing, driven by factors like informed investors, wealth transfer, and the category's recent outperformance, projecting significant asset growth in ESG ETFs by 2030.

title: RXIL's First Trade Credit Insurance Transaction in Sandbox with Tata AIG, ICICI Bank and YES Bank
summary: Receivables Exchange of India (RXIL) has successfully initiated the first Trade Credit Insurance (TCI) backed transaction in a Sandbox environment with Tata AIG as insurer and ICICI Bank and YES Bank as financiers. This pioneering transaction aims to enhance financiers' ability to assign credit limits to corporates and improve liquidity for MSMEs by enabling discounting of invoices from lower-rated corporate buyers. The adoption of TCI on TReDS is expected to digitize credit insurance and significantly boost the platform's throughput.

title: JPMorgan Chase Appoints Financial Services Vet Reggie Chambers As New Head of Investor Relations
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has appointed Reggie Chambers as its new Head of Investor Relations, effective January 1, 2021. Chambers, a financial services veteran, will replace Jason Scott, who is moving to a new role as head of Global Technology Finance. Chambers previously served as Chief Administrative Officer for Chase Consumer Banking and will report to JPMorgan Chase CFO Jennifer Piepszak in his new role.

title: Bank of Butterfield appoints Sonia Baxendale to its board
summary: The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son has appointed Sonia Baxendale to its board as an independent director. Baxendale brings extensive experience from her role as president and CEO of the Global Risk Institute and previous senior leadership positions in retail banking and wealth management at CIBC. Her appointment coincides with Leslie Godridge's departure and is expected to provide invaluable insight into emerging risk factors affecting the global financial services industry.

title: Women Of The C-Suite: Eva Huston of ‘Duck Creek Technologies’ On The Five Things You Need To…
summary: Eva Huston, CSO of Duck Creek Technologies, discusses her career path from investment banking to her current executive role. She shares insights on leadership, diversity in executive teams, overcoming challenges faced by women executives, and the importance of authenticity. Huston emphasizes that success comes from helping others find their value and making a positive impact on the community.

title: NPCI raises ₹81.64 crore equity capital from 19 new shareholders
summary: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has raised ₹81.64 crore in equity capital from 19 new investors, who now collectively hold a 4.63% stake. This move expands NPCI's shareholder base to 67 entities, including various types of banks and payment companies. The shareholding restructuring was recommended by a 2016 Finance Ministry committee to diffuse shareholding, though several top banks still hold significant stakes due to mergers.

title: Blackstone, JD.com among bidders for FANCL Asia business -sources
summary: Blackstone and JD.com are among more than 10 bidders for CMC Holdings, the sole distributor of FANCL's skincare products in Asia outside Japan. Chris Chan, the owner of CMC, appointed Morgan Stanley to sell the business, which is valued at close to $1 billion. The interest in FANCL's Asia business highlights investor confidence in a consumer market recovery in the region, particularly in China.

title: JPMorgan, Lloyds Set Sights on Starling Bank, Times Reports
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Lloyds Banking Group Plc are reportedly interested in acquiring Starling Bank Ltd., a British challenger bank, according to The Times. This potential acquisition could mark the first major merger between an established lender and a startup in the UK. JPMorgan is preparing to launch a consumer bank in the UK, while Lloyds is reportedly interested in Starling's technology.

title: Hudson Pacific and CPP Investments Acquire Seattle Tower from JPMorgan Chase
summary: Hudson Pacific Properties and CPP Investments have jointly acquired a Seattle tower from JPMorgan Chase. This acquisition signifies a strategic investment in the real estate market of Seattle, involving two major investment entities. The deal highlights their continued focus on commercial properties.

title: JP Morgan, Lloyds Bank express interest in buying Starling Bank
summary: JP Morgan Chase and Lloyds Banking Group are reportedly interested in acquiring the British challenger bank, Starling Bank. JP Morgan's interest is tied to its upcoming UK consumer bank launch, while Lloyds is particularly interested in Starling's technology. Starling Bank's CEO, Anne Boden, has expressed her ambition for the bank to go public and stated she would never sell to a large bank.

title: PNC Makes Pittsburgh into a Banking Powerhouse
summary: PNC Bank has become the fifth-largest bank in the U.S. and the largest regional bank after acquiring the U.S. operations of Spanish bank BBVA for $11.6 billion. This acquisition expands PNC's footprint across the West Coast and Sun Belt, increasing its assets to $564 billion and giving it a presence in 29 of the 30 largest metro markets. This strategic move solidifies Pittsburgh's position as a national player in financial services.

title: Citigate Apartments sold for $90 million
summary: The Citigate Apartments at 8451 Gate Parkway in Jacksonville, Florida, were sold to New York-based The Blackstone Group for $90 million on November 25, 2020. This transaction marks the second-largest multifamily real estate sale of 2020. The 444-unit property, built in 2009, offers various amenities and unit types, with rents ranging from $1,278 to $1,768.

title: Why ExxonMobil and Chevron Should Merge
summary: ExxonMobil and Chevron have both endured difficult business conditions in 2020 due to weak oil prices and the pandemic. Analyst Paul Sankey suggests a merger between ExxonMobil and Chevron could create a more resilient and efficient "mega-major" oil company, potentially named Chevron, allowing for cost reductions and stability for ExxonMobil's dividend. This comes as Chevron recently surpassed ExxonMobil in market capitalization for the first time.

title: Zambia shows how the West must lend like China, says Mark Mobius
summary: Veteran emerging markets investor Mark Mobius argues that Western lending to Africa needs to adopt a China-like approach, focusing on infrastructure projects rather than supporting government bureaucracies. He suggests that such a shift, coupled with more conditionality from institutions like the IMF, could help African nations, including Zambia, address debt crises and foster economic development. Mobius, a professional optimist, also highlights Africa's potential to benefit significantly from technological progress and the shift towards a deflationary world.

title: Every major US bank has now come out against Arctic drilling
summary: All major US banks, including Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Chase, Wells Fargo, Citibank, and now Bank of America, have committed to not financing oil and gas exploration in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR). This decision follows pressure from environmentalists concerned about the impact on the indigenous Gwich’in people and endangered species. The Trump administration's efforts to sell drilling leases in ANWR face challenges from these financial decisions and President-elect Joe Biden's opposition to Arctic drilling.

title: Companies that support LGBTQ-inclusive policies outperform: Credit Suisse
summary: A Credit Suisse analysis highlights that companies supporting LGBTQ-inclusive policies have historically outperformed the broader market. These firms, including Apple and Tesla, attract and retain talent more easily, and show stronger revenue growth and cash flow. While not proving causation, the report indicates a strong correlation between LGBTQ inclusivity and better financial performance.

title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon: How my grandfather inspired my career in finance – 'he loved stocks' and 'read a lot'
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon attributes his interest in finance and several key personal habits, like extensive reading and a strong ethical compass, to his paternal grandfather, Panos Papademetriou. His grandfather, an immigrant who became a successful stockbroker, inspired Dimon's career path. Dimon continues to apply these lessons, emphasizing EQ and ethics in his professional life, in addition to intellectual ability.

title: Citizens CEO Bruce Van Saun talks Covid, competition, cuts and national digital expansion
summary: Bruce Van Saun, CEO of Citizens Financial Group, discussed the challenges of 2020 and the company's future strategy, which includes branch cuts and a national digital expansion that differentiates itself from competitors like Chase and PNC. The article also references related news about Citizens' third-quarter charge-offs, social equity commitment, and branch closures.

title: Seattle Trophy Office Tower to Change Ownership in $625M Deal
summary: Hudson Pacific Properties and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board are acquiring the 668,000-square-foot 1918 8th Ave. building in Seattle for $625 million from investors advised by J.P. Morgan Asset Management. The LEED Platinum-certified property, 98 percent leased with Amazon as the anchor tenant, is expected to close by year-end. Hudson Pacific will hold a 55 percent stake and manage leasing and construction.

title: JPMorgan Chase To Buy Boston FinTech 55ip
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management announced its agreement to acquire FinTech 55ip, a company specializing in tax-smart investment strategies for financial advisors. 55ip will continue to operate independently with J.P. Morgan's support, aiming to enhance automated advisor technology and improve client outcomes. This acquisition reflects the growing need for intelligent, automated tools in the financial advisory sector.

title: JPMorgan is buying fintech start-up 55ip to help financial advisors offer tax-efficient portfolios
summary: JPMorgan Chase's asset management division is acquiring 55ip, a fintech startup that helps financial advisors automate the creation of tax-efficient portfolios. This acquisition marks JPMorgan's first since CEO Jamie Dimon indicated the company was looking for takeovers earlier in the year. The two companies had previously partnered in October to assist advisors in tax-efficient portfolio management.

title: LPL to Buy Waddell & Reed’s Brokerage Business for $300 Mln
summary: LPL Financial Holdings will acquire Waddell & Reed's independent brokerage business for $300 million from Macquarie Asset Management, which is buying Waddell & Reed for $1.7 billion. The deal involves integrating Waddell’s approximately 900 brokers and $63 billion in client assets onto LPL’s platform by mid-2021. LPL anticipates the acquisition will add at least $50 million in EBITDA within a year, assuming a 70% client asset retention rate.

title: CIBC Announces Appointment of Katharine Stevenson as Chair of the Board
summary: CIBC announced the appointment of Katharine B. Stevenson as Chair of the Board, effective April 8, 2021, subject to her election as a director. Ms. Stevenson has been an independent director since 2011 and will succeed The Honourable John P. Manley, who is retiring. She brings extensive corporate governance experience and a background in financial executive roles in telecommunications and banking.

title: HDFC Bank's digital outages: 7 key takeaways from RBI action
summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has taken supervisory action against HDFC Bank due to frequent digital banking outages, instructing the bank to halt new digital launches and credit card customer sourcing. This unprecedented move by the RBI highlights concerns about the reliability of digital channels and the pressure banks face to rapidly introduce new digital products without adequate testing. The article outlines seven key points, including the first-time nature of RBI's action, the recurrence of such issues in HDFC Bank and other financial institutions, and the significant challenge this poses for HDFC Bank's new management in restoring customer confidence.

title: High-Producing Boston Broker Joins Kestra After Morgan Stanley Departure
summary: Jonathan Lonske, a former high-producing broker from Morgan Stanley Wealth Management in Boston, has joined Kestra Investment Services after being dismissed from Morgan Stanley for allegedly using unapproved client-prospecting software. Lonske, along with two other advisors from his former team, Tara Schutz and Mary Flanigan, will set up an independent practice with Kestra. Kestra, which works with around 1,700 independent brokers, has been actively recruiting advisors from employee-model firms, noting an acceleration of wealth managers leaving such models recently.

title: HDFC Bank Ordered by RBI to Suspend New Digital Products on Outages
summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has ordered HDFC Bank to temporarily suspend new digital product launches and onboarding of new credit card customers. This action follows a series of digital outages experienced by the Indian lender over the past two years. The bank's CEO has assured customers it is working to resolve the issues, highlighting the rare nature of such a step by the regulator amidst a surge in online transactions in India.

title: New Re/Insurer ‘Vantage Risk’ Launches, Led by Former Arch, AXA XL Executives
summary: A new re/insurance group, Vantage Group Holdings Ltd., has launched with $1 billion of equity capital from The Carlyle Group and Hellman & Friedman. The company is led by CEO Greg Hendrick, former CEO of AXA XL, and Dinos Iordanou, retired president and CEO of Arch Capital Group Ltd., as non-executive chairman. Vantage Risk will initially offer property catastrophe and specialty reinsurance and plans to launch insurance products in Bermuda and North America in 2021.

title: Re/Insurance Firm Vantage Announces Launch
summary: Vantage Group Holdings Ltd. and its wholly-owned subsidiary Vantage Risk Ltd. have officially launched, led by CEO Greg Hendrick and Non-Executive Chairman Dinos Iordanou. The new re/insurance entity, backed by $1 billion in equity capital from The Carlyle Group and Hellman & Friedman, aims to address shrinking capacity and evolving risks in the industry with a focus on technology, robust analytics, and experienced leadership, planning to expand into insurance products in 2021.

title: Can You Get International Bank Fees Refunded from Washington Trust?
summary: This article discusses the issue of international bank fees charged by Washington Trust and other financial institutions, particularly for online purchases made from home that are classified as foreign transactions. It explains how these fees are applied, offers advice on how consumers can avoid them, and outlines steps to seek refunds directly from banks. The piece also highlights the potential for legal action through class-action lawsuits if internal resolution attempts are unsuccessful, mentioning ongoing investigations into Washington Trust and other banks regarding alleged wrongful charges.

title: Where JPMorgan Chase and Snap See Innovation’s Next Steps
summary: JPMorgan Chase and Snap shared insights on their innovation and transformation strategies at the AWS re:Invent virtual conference. JPMorgan Chase, with its massive scale and legacy, is undertaking a modernization effort involving cloud migration, AI, and data warehousing. Snap, a cloud-native company, focuses on adopting new innovations quickly for cost savings and performance improvements, while AWS CEO Andy Jassy highlighted the continued evolution of computing modes.

title: JPMorgan Chase Expanding Economic Opportunity For Black Americans
summary: JPMorgan Chase has launched a new initiative called 'Advancing Black Pathways (ABP)' to bolster wealth and provide various opportunities for Black Americans. The program focuses on investments in financial, educational, career, and business arenas, aiming to address persistent financial inequities and the racial wealth gap. ABP will concentrate on strengthening education and job training, promoting fair professional opportunities, and improving the financial well-being of Black families and businesses, including a $6.65 million 'Entrepreneurs of Color Fund'.

title: Stripe: the Amazon of finance?
summary: The article discusses Stripe's ambition to become the "Amazon of finance" by expanding its financial services beyond merchant checkout APIs to a platform of platforms through its new Stripe Treasury offering. This new venture involves partnerships with banks like Goldman Sachs and Citigroup to provide checking accounts and business banking services, positioning Stripe as a potential rival to digital banks and banking-as-a-service platforms. The key focus is on enabling businesses like Shopify to offer embedded financial services to their merchants, leveraging Stripe's API layer to connect them to the banking system.

title: Kookmin Bank Bets Big on Crypto with New Partnerships
summary: Kookmin Bank, South Korea's largest bank, has entered the cryptocurrency space by investing in Korea Digital Asset (KODA), a new digital asset management company. This move, in partnership with firms like #Hashed and Haechi Labs, will enable KB to launch digital asset custody services, anti-money laundering, and OTC trading services. The bank also aims to expand into crypto deposit, lending, and payments, making early moves in cryptocurrency and blockchain adoption in Asia.

title: Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America diverge on bonuses
summary: Major banks in the U.S. are taking different approaches to employee bonuses, reflecting a divergence in compensation strategies. Morgan Stanley is issuing a one-time $1,000 bonus to about half its employees, primarily those earning less than $150,000. JPMorgan Chase is considering increasing variable compensation for traders by 15% to 20%, while Bank of America's senior executives suggested maintaining bonus pools for sales and trading at previous year levels despite revenue growth.

title: Wynn Macau Ltd grants share options to five directors
summary: Wynn Macau Ltd has granted share options for 4,780,000 ordinary shares to five directors as part of its share option scheme. This action follows the company's recent announcement of a US$216 million loss for Q3 2020 due to COVID-19 travel restrictions. The shares, priced at HK$0.001 each, have a nine-year exercise period, allowing directors to exercise up to 20% of their options annually, with provisions for unexercised amounts from previous years.

title: Get Defensive With Quality Bond Exposure Via IIGD
summary: Despite increased COVID-19 cases, the capital markets are showing less uncertainty, making quality corporate bond exposure attractive. The Invesco Investment Grade Defensive ETF (IIGD) offers access to U.S. investment-grade bonds with high credit ratings and shorter maturities, generating a 5.88% year-to-date gain. With tightening credit spreads and a potentially stable political landscape, corporate bonds could continue to perform well.

title: How Bill.com, The Boring Bookkeeper Of Fintech, Became One Of 2020’s Hottest Stocks
summary: René Lacerte, after being pushed out of his first startup, built Bill.com over 13 years into a company now valued at $10 billion, with its stock increasing more than fivefold since its IPO. Despite its "mundane" function of helping small businesses pay bills, Bill.com has become one of 2020's hottest stocks, benefiting from the acceleration of online transactions during Covid-19 and a strong network strategy. The company faces high expectations, trading at 50 times next year's expected revenue, requiring continued "Steady Eddie" growth.

title: Former Fifth Third executive takes role at nation’s largest bank
summary: Byna Elliott, a former Fifth Third Bank executive, has taken on a new role as Head of Advancing Black Pathways at JPMorgan Chase Bank. This move sees a prominent banking leader transition to a significant position at the nation's largest bank, focusing on advancing Black communities.

title: C3.ai Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering
summary: C3.ai, a leading enterprise AI software provider, announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 15,500,000 shares of Class A common stock at $42.00 per share, aiming to raise $651 million. The shares were expected to begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange on December 9, 2020, under the ticker symbol "AI" and the offering was slated to close on December 11, 2020. Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, and BofA Securities are lead book-running managers.

title: Banks look at ‘explainable’ AI systems to boost consumer trust
summary: Financial institutions are investing in "explainable" artificial intelligence (AI) to address concerns about algorithmic bias and lack of transparency in automated decision-making. This technology aims to make AI decisions more traceable and understandable for auditors, regulators, and consumers, helping to build trust and mitigate issues like discrimination in loan denials. While explainable AI offers solutions to the "black box" problem, experts caution that poorly structured data can still lead to skewed outcomes, emphasizing the need for continuous fine-tuning and good governance.

title: Colliers acquires veteran Cboe, CME real estate rep Holly Duran's firm
summary: Colliers International Chicago has acquired Holly Duran Real Estate Partners, a boutique brokerage firm specializing in financial sector tenant representation. Holly Duran, a veteran real estate adviser for the Chicago Board Options Exchange and Chicago Mercantile Exchange, will join Colliers as a principal and financial services lead. The acquisition strengthens Colliers' tenant representation practice and comes at a time when smaller brokerage firms are often absorbed by larger companies in the real estate industry.

title: Seer Announces Closing of Initial Public Offering and Full
summary: Seer, Inc. announced the closing of its initial public offering, raising approximately $201.3 million gross proceeds. The offering included the full exercise of underwriters' option to purchase additional shares, totaling 10,592,106 shares of Class A common stock at $19.00 per share. Seer's Class A common stock began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "SEER" on December 4, 2020.

title: Goldman Sachs to Acquire 100% of China Securities Joint Venture - WSJ
summary: Goldman Sachs is moving to acquire full ownership of its securities joint venture in China, Goldman Sachs Gao Hua Securities Co. This move deepens the New York-based bank's investment in the world's second-largest economy, following a 17-year partnership with a domestic brokerage. The firm is applying with Chinese regulators and has signed an agreement to acquire the remaining 49% share it doesn't already own.

title: Dimon asks bankers for M&A ideas
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon is actively seeking acquisition ideas, particularly in software, fintech, or overseas. He encouraged investment bankers to bring him potential deals, assuring them of fees. This comes as competitor Morgan Stanley has completed major deals, and JPMorgan itself recently acquired fintech company 55ip to expand offerings for financial advisors.

title: Planning Ahead: J.P. Morgan International Private Bank CEO Nicolas Aguzin Q&A
summary: Nicolas Aguzin, CEO of J.P. Morgan’s International Private Bank, discusses the bank's response to the pandemic, highlighting the swift adoption of digital interaction with clients and the acceleration of operational enhancements. He notes a strong investment appetite in Asia, particularly in sectors like digital, technology innovation, healthcare, and sustainable investments, and emphasizes the enduring value of holistic financial advice in a low-interest-rate environment.

title: You can have it all — just not all at once, says first woman to head major Wall Street bank
summary: Jane Fraser, the first woman CEO of a major Wall Street bank (Citigroup), advises that career success and personal life balance are achievable, but not necessarily all at the same time. She emphasizes that young people should not rush their careers, which are measured in decades, and that collecting diverse experiences is more valuable than solely focusing on upward promotions. Fraser also highlighted the importance of putting employees first, a philosophy she aims to continue at Citigroup.

title: Starbucks names Mellody Hobson as board chair
summary: Starbucks Corp. has appointed Mellody Hobson as the head of its board, making her the first African American woman to chair a Fortune 500 company. Hobson, co-chief executive of Ariel Investments, has been on Starbucks' board for over 15 years and takes over from Myron Ullman. This appointment highlights Corporate America's push for increased diversity in senior leadership roles.

title: Nature Conservancy Hooked Corporate America on an Empty Climate Solution
summary: The Nature Conservancy, the world's largest environmental group, is accused of selling "meaningless" carbon offsets to major corporations like JPMorgan, Disney, and BlackRock. These offsets are based on preserving forestland that was never actually threatened with deforestation. Critics argue that this practice allows companies to claim significant emissions reductions without making genuine changes to their operations, undermining efforts to combat climate change.

title: Quality over quantity: Building high quality equity portfolios
summary: This article discusses the importance of quality investing, focusing on building equity portfolios with strong, consistent companies. It explores historical research supporting quality as a long-term investment strategy, how "quality" is defined through profitability, financial solvency, and accounting consistency, and how J.P. Morgan Asset Management implements these principles in portfolio construction. The piece highlights the JPMorgan U.S. Quality Factor ETF (JQUA) as an example of a cost-effective and tax-efficient way to gain exposure to high-quality companies.

title: Moody’s revisa ratings de bancos como Bradesco, BB, Santander, Itaú e Caixa
summary: Moody's announced on December 11, 2020, that it revised the ratings of 28 Brazilian banks including Bradesco, Santander, Itaú Unibanco, BNDES, Caixa, and Banco do Brasil. The decision was primarily motivated by changes in the methodology for foreign and local currency ceilings, resulting in elevated long-term foreign currency deposit ratings for most banks. An exception was ING Bank N.V. (São Paulo), which saw its local currency classification downgraded.

title: NPS, Hines set up $1.5 bn build-to-core strategy JV - KED Global
summary: The National Pension Service (NPS) has formed a $1.5 billion build-to-core joint venture with US-based real estate firm Hines. This partnership will focus on upgrading defective properties in core locations globally. This venture follows NPS's recent collaborations with other global institutions, including a $2.3 billion JV with Allianz SE, as NPS seeks to expand its alternative asset portfolio amidst challenges in conducting onsite due diligence for international investments.

title: Kevin Greenard: Ensure you have the maximum deposit insurance
summary: This article explains the different types of banking institutions in Canada, including Schedule I, II, and III banks, and credit unions, along with their respective deposit insurance protections provided by the Canadian Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) and the Credit Union Deposit Insurance Corporation (CUDIC). It highlights the critical differences in coverage limits, especially for GICs, and advises investors, particularly those with credit union accounts, to be aware of how transitions to federal regulation can impact their insurance coverage. The author emphasizes the importance of structuring investments to maximize deposit insurance and avoid unnecessary risk exposure.

title: Huntington to acquire TCF Bank in deal creating top 20 bank valued at $22 billion
summary: Huntington Bancshares Inc. is acquiring TCF Financial Corp. in an all-stock deal valued at $22 billion, creating a combined bank that will be a top 20 U.S. bank with approximately $168 billion in assets. The combined entity will operate under the Huntington name, maintaining dual headquarters in Detroit and Columbus, Ohio, with TCF shareholders receiving 3.0028 shares of Huntington for each TCF share they own. The deal is expected to close in Q2 2021 and bring significant cost savings and a "significant commitment to Detroit and Michigan."

title: Huntington and TCF Financial to merge in $22 billion deal
summary: Huntington Bancshares and TCF Financial Corp. are merging in an all-stock deal valued at $22 billion, creating a regional bank expected to rank in the top 10 nationally. The Huntington brand will survive, and the combined company will maintain dual headquarters in Columbus, Ohio, and Detroit, with a significant commitment to Michigan including jobs and community investments. The merger is expected to close in the second quarter and result in approximately $490 million in cost savings.

title: State Street, UBS weigh merger of asset-management units
summary: State Street and UBS are reportedly in talks to merge their asset-management businesses, a move that would create a larger entity capable of competing with industry leaders like BlackRock. This isn't the first time the two banks have considered such a tie-up, with previous discussions occurring in 2012 and again earlier in 2020. The potential merger highlights a broader trend in the financial industry where smaller players are looking to combine or sell their asset-management units to gain scale and cut costs amidst digitization and increased competition.

title: ‘Keep it simple’: Aditya Puri on HDFC Bank’s path to market leadership
summary: This interview with former HDFC Bank CEO Aditya Puri discusses how the bank achieved market leadership through customer-focused innovation and disciplined risk management. Puri emphasizes the importance of simplicity, a strong customer focus, and technology-led innovation while maintaining a "first among equals" culture. He shares insights into risk management strategies, adapting to the digital era, and empowering employees, highlighting the bank's consistent strong performance and future outlook for India.

title: Huntington Bancshares to merge with TCF Financial in all-stock deal
summary: Huntington Bancshares and TCF Financial have agreed to an all-stock merger, creating a company with an estimated $22 billion market value. The deal, expected to close in Q2 next year, aims to boost Huntington's earnings per share by 18% in 2022. This merger reflects a trend of regional U.S. lenders pursuing growth through acquisitions amidst softer financial regulations.

title: JPMorgan Chase Bank Wrongly Charged 170,000 Customers Overdraft Fees. Federal Regulators Refused to Penalize It.
summary: JPMorgan Chase wrongly charged 170,000 customers overdraft fees due to a software glitch, but federal regulators, specifically the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), opted for a private reprimand instead of public penalties. This article reveals that since 2017, the OCC under the Trump administration has quietly rebuked at least six banks for similar overcharging practices, often overruling front-line examiners who sought public fines. The report highlights how this approach has kept abuses by major banks like American Express, U.S. Bank, Zions Bank, Union Bank, and First Horizon largely out of public view.

title: Goldman Sachs Asset Management Acquires Gold ETF 'AAAU'
summary: Goldman Sachs Asset Management (GSAM) has completed its acquisition of the Perth Mint Physical Gold ETF, now renamed the Goldman Sachs Physical Gold ETF (AAAU). The ETF will continue trading on NYSE Arca, offering investors exposure to physical gold with a competitively priced 18 basis points expense ratio. GSAM plans to leverage its global platform and resources to enhance the product, which is part of its strategic expansion into high-quality ETFs.

title: Wall Street Likes the Huntington-TCF Deal. Expect More Regional Bank Marriages in 2021.
summary: The merger between Huntington Bancshares and TCF Financial is being met with enthusiasm on Wall Street. Analysts anticipate this deal will pave the way for more regional bank consolidations in 2021. This trend suggests a period of significant M&A activity within the regional banking sector.

title: Plumas Bank celebrating 40 year anniversary
summary: Plumas Bancorp, the parent company of Plumas Bank, is celebrating its 40-year anniversary of providing financial services. Chairman Daniel E. West and CEO Andrew J. Ryback acknowledge the bank's growth to over $1.1 billion in assets, its 13-branch network, and its commitment to community banking and client service. The bank was also recognized by Raymond James, S&P Global Market Intelligence, and The Findley Reports for its strong performance.

title: Bancos fecham agências no Brasil no maior ritmo em três anos
summary: Os bancos brasileiros estão fechando agências no ritmo mais rápido em três anos, impulsionados pela pandemia de Covid-19 que acelerou o uso de canais digitais e intensificou a competição com fintechs. No período de 12 meses até novembro, foram fechadas 1.444 agências, representando um aumento de 78% em comparação com o ano anterior, o maior corte desde 2017. Essa adaptação tecnológica também resultou na eliminação de mais de 72.500 empregos bancários desde 2013, apesar dos investimentos significativos em tecnologia, gerando críticas sobre a distribuição dos lucros com a sociedade e os funcionários.

title: Northern Trust, Fidelity join small club managing crypto assets
summary: Northern Trust and Fidelity Digital Assets are expanding their cryptocurrency custody services, with Northern Trust partnering with Standard Chartered to form Zodia, a UK-based fintech. Fidelity, which launched Fidelity Digital Assets in 2018, is now collaborating with BlockFi for collateralized crypto loans. Both companies are navigating regulatory concerns and technological challenges to provide secure and established custody solutions for digital assets to meet growing institutional demand.

title: Bitcoin breaks above $20,000 for the first time ever
summary: Bitcoin surged past $20,000 for the first time in history, driven by increased demand from institutional investors and significant investments from prominent figures like Paul Tudor Jones and Stanley Druckenmiller. Major financial firms are also expanding into crypto market data services, further legitimizing the digital currency. This rally is seen by crypto evangelists as sustained institutional buying rather than speculative retail investment.

title: JPMorgan Chase Won't Give to Biden's Inauguration but Will Donate to Charity Instead
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it will not donate to President-elect Joe Biden's inauguration, a shift from its contribution to Donald Trump's 2017 inauguration. Instead, the company will give $300,000 to food banks in Wilmington, Delaware, Oakland, California, and Washington, DC, citing hardships from the COVID-19 pandemic. This decision comes as other corporations, like Boeing, are pledging up to $1 million for Biden's significantly scaled-down inauguration, which offers perks for large corporate donors.

title: PPP Loans: Accounting Treatment vs. Valuation Treatment
summary: This article explores the differing accounting and valuation treatments of Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans. It details how PPP loans are accounted for as debt under ASC 470 or as government grants, depending on forgiveness expectations, and explains how valuation firms assess these loans for fair market value, often removing them from the balance sheet if forgiveness is highly probable. The article highlights that while accounting takes a conservative approach by treating them as debt, appraisers can adjust based on the likelihood of forgiveness.

title: Who's Moving Where In Wealth Management? - Alex Brown, Morgan Stanley, Others
summary: This article details recent executive moves in the North American wealth management sector. Alex Brown, a part of Raymond James, recruited Mark J Pomerantz from Morgan Stanley, adding to its significant advisor hires. Additionally, Principle Wealth Partners appointed three senior wealth advisors, Theresa V Donatelli, Romaine A Macomb, and J Addison McAraw, along with senior client service managers, expanding their client assets under management to $1.7 billion.

title: At FDA’s request, Penumbra recalls catheter device after 14 patient deaths
summary: Penumbra has recalled its Jet 7 Xtra Flex catheter device, used for removing blood clots in stroke patients, at the FDA's request following 14 reported patient deaths and 200 medical device reports. The recall led to a 7.3% drop in Penumbra's stock, and the company expects a revenue hit of less than $20 million in the fourth quarter. Despite the setback, analysts believe Penumbra is well-positioned for future success, with other products and new launches planned to mitigate the impact.

title: SouthState Bank, formerly CenterState, Adds Jacksonville-based Middle Market Team, Attracts Top Commercial Banking Talent
summary: SouthState Bank, formerly CenterState, announced the addition of a Jacksonville-based Middle Market Banking team and expanded its Commercial banking talent across its six-state footprint. This strategic move aims to enhance services for commercial middle market companies, leveraging the bank's increased size and presence in key growth markets following its merger. The new team members bring extensive experience from various prominent banking institutions, solidifying SouthState Bank's commitment to growth and customer service.

title: LeBron James Family Foundation Buys Tangier to Expand I PROMISE School Offerings
summary: The LeBron James Family Foundation has purchased Akron's Tangier Restaurant & Cabaret to establish a multi-use complex called "House Three Thirty." This new facility will provide family programming, financial services, a sports complex, dining, retail, and event spaces, all aimed at supporting the I PROMISE School initiatives. The project, set to open in 2022, will offer job training and community services, with partnerships from JPMorgan Chase, DICK’S Sporting Goods Foundation, Old El Paso, and J.M. Smucker Co.

title: Citigroup to offer up to 12-week sabbaticals to staff
summary: Citigroup is introducing a new benefits package that includes offering employees up to 12-week sabbaticals and the ability to volunteer for charities for up to four weeks on full pay. This initiative stems from a review of bankers' work-life balance, prompted by the successful shift to remote working during the coronavirus pandemic. The scheme will initially roll out to US employees before being extended to UK staff, with other major firms like Standard Chartered and JP Morgan also reviewing their flexible working policies.

title: Lee R. Raymond to resign from JPMorgan’s Board of Directors
summary: Lee R. Raymond has announced his resignation from JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s Board of Directors, effective December 31, 2020. JPMorgan clarified that his departure is not due to any disagreements with the company. Raymond previously served as Chairman and CEO of ExxonMobil and Exxon Corporation.

title: Jaime Guardiola, el banquero tenaz
summary: Jaime Guardiola, a banker with a long career at BBVA and later Sabadell, is highlighted for his tenacious leadership during turbulent financial times. He successfully expanded BBVA's international presence and, upon returning to Spain, transformed Sabadell into a top Spanish bank by acquiring distressed entities. Despite challenges like the TSB acquisition post-Brexit, his legacy includes pioneering solutions for mortgage defaults and leaving Sabadell in a leading position amidst new crises.

title: Morgan Stanley Hires Merrill ‘Growth’ Champ in California
summary: Morgan Stanley has recruited Benjamin J. Meyers, a 33-year-old financial advisor from Merrill Lynch in La Jolla, CA. Meyers, known for his aggressive cold-calling strategy, generated $1.5 million in annual revenue from a $200 million book and was a consistent recipient of Merrill's Excellence in Growth Award. His move signifies Morgan Stanley's continued active recruiting efforts, a practice they had previously paused, and highlights a debate within the industry regarding cold-calling effectiveness and wirehouse vs. RIA models.

title: JPMorgan Chase Board Member Lee Raymond to Leave
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced that Lee Raymond, its longtime lead independent director and former Exxon Mobil chief, will be leaving the board at the end of the year. Raymond has served on the board for over 30 years and recently faced a campaign to remove him due to climate-change concerns. He has been the lead independent director since 2001.

title: JPMorgan Chase Longtime Board Member Lee Raymond to Leave
summary: Lee Raymond, a longtime lead independent director at JPMorgan Chase & Co. and former Exxon Mobil Corp. chief, is leaving the bank's board at the end of the year. His departure follows a campaign by environmental groups and institutional investors seeking his removal due to climate-change concerns. Mr. Raymond had served on the board for over 30 years.

title: Former Exxon chief Lee Raymond to retire from board of JPMorgan Chase
summary: Lee Raymond, former CEO of ExxonMobil and a long-serving director at JPMorgan Chase, is retiring from the bank's board following pressure from environmental activists. While JPMorgan stated his retirement was unrelated to climate issues, activist groups view it as a win, urging the bank to now overhaul its fossil fuel financing. Raymond had been a director for 33 years and the lead independent director for 19 years.

title: How Aditya Puri built HDFC Bank, brick by brick
summary: This article features an exclusive conversation with Aditya Puri, the former CEO of HDFC Bank, detailing his 26-year tenure. Puri discusses his approach to leadership, institution-building, and change management, highlighting the bank's culture, customer focus, and strategic vision. He emphasizes that HDFC Bank's success was a collective effort and outlines future growth opportunities, particularly in semi-urban and rural India.

title: UBS hires $1.7B duo from Goldman Sachs
summary: UBS has recruited advisors Scott Belveal and Adam Lambert from Goldman Sachs, who previously managed $1.7 billion in client assets. This move follows several other significant hires for UBS, including a team from JPMorgan overseeing $9 billion and a Merrill Lynch team managing $920 million. Belveal and Lambert will join UBS in Philadelphia along with their team, focusing on ultra-high-net-worth clients.

title: JP Morgan hires Citigroup veteran to lead digital commercial payments
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co has hired Lisa Davis, a veteran from Citigroup Inc, to lead its digital commercial payments division. Davis, who previously headed Citigroup's startup incubator, will replace Sairam Rangachari as head of channels. This move is part of JP Morgan's ongoing effort to strengthen its commercial payments business, following other key hires in the sector.

title: Rotich says investor returns from Eurobond to be tax free
summary: Kenya's Treasury has waived tax on interest payments from its Sh132 billion Eurobond to attract foreign investors. Finance secretary Henry Rotich also exempted the issue's arrangers—Barclays Bank PLC, J. P. Morgan Securities PLC, and Standard Bank PLC—from taxes on their fees. This move aims to make the Eurobond, intended to refinance debt and fund infrastructure, more appealing, especially as Kenya prepares for marketing roadshows in Europe and the US.

title: STI highlights from 2020
summary: The Straits Times Index (STI) experienced an 8% decline in 2020 through December 2nd, but its Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) saw significant growth, with combined assets under management (AUM) nearly doubling to S$2.08 billion. This growth was driven by increased investor participation, especially in the June and September quarters. The article also highlights the impact of new joiners like Keppel DC Reit and Mapletree Industrial Trust, and the cornerstone role of local banks, DBS, OCBC, and UOB, despite their initial declines.

title: Informe sobre la rentabilidad de la banca en Chile
