The $3.5 billion deal has faced delays and scrutiny from federal regulators, leading to discussions about modified structures and financial terms. Both companies remain committed to the strategic rationale of the merger, though analysts suggest a price renegotiation might be necessary to reflect the timeline and any required changes for regulatory approval.

title: The US is a core market for UBS and its Financial Advisors | UBS United States of America
summary: This article highlights why UBS considers the US a core market for its wealth management business and financial advisors. It addresses common misconceptions about UBS's US operations, emphasizing its global scale, client-centric approach, and focus on supporting financial advisors with extensive resources and direct access to senior leadership. The piece also underlines UBS's leading position in wealth management and its commitment to continued investment in the US market, citing its high productivity per advisor and comprehensive service offerings.

title: Emerge to Launch 10 Sustainable ETFs That Are All Run by Women
summary: Emerge is launching 10 new sustainable ETFs, with each fund managed by women. These funds, listed on both the Cboe BZX Exchange in the US and the NEO Exchange in Canada, will invest in equity securities while excluding categories like gambling and chemical weapons. Emerge, Canada's first women-owned investment fund firm, also plans to debut a program called EMPWR to encourage more women to become investment managers for sustainability-focused funds.

title: Citigroup hires three for China securities business - source
summary: Citigroup has hired three bankers for its planned China securities business: Kenneth Koo as CEO, Rochelle Wei to lead its futures unit, and John Lu to head the onshore equities business. This move follows Citigroup's application for a mainland Chinese securities license last year, reflecting its efforts to expand its presence in the Chinese market.

title: JPMorgan Chase Invests in J2 Ventures
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has made a strategic investment in J2 Ventures, a venture capital firm founded by U.S. Army veteran Alexander Harstrick and Jonathan Bronson, Ph.D. This investment is part of JPMorgan's Project Spark Initiative, which aims to provide capital to venture funds managed by emerging alternative managers with military service. J2 Ventures focuses on deep technology companies with applications in both government and private sectors, managing approximately $100 million in capital and including investments in companies like Oura Ring and Tasso Inc.

title: Meet Wall St. thought leaders at Hankyung conference in NYC
summary: The Korea Economic Daily (KED) is hosting the "HANKYUNG Global Market Conference NYC 2022" in October, bringing together top Wall Street portfolio managers, analysts, and South Korean investors. The conference will feature prominent figures like Howard Marks and Eric S. Rosengren, covering investment strategies, macroeconomic risks, and emerging asset classes such as blockchain and NFTs. It also includes exclusive networking opportunities, a guided art tour at Christie's, and a visit to "Billionaires Row."

title: Deutsche Bank’s Chadha Sees 25% US Stock Slump if Recession Hits
summary: Deutsche Bank strategists, led by Binky Chadha, predict a potential 25% decline in US stocks if the economy enters a recession. They cite declining company profits, high stock valuations, and looming recession risks as major challenges for the equity market. Despite these risks, investor positioning in equities is currently low.

title: Longtime Adams Funds CEO Mark Stoeckle to retire; successor named
summary: Mark E. Stoeckle is retiring as CEO of Adams Funds, with James P. Haynie slated to take over. Stoeckle successfully guided Adams Funds through significant market volatility, including the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: SK Closes Sale of NuCera Solutions to Chase
summary: An affiliate of funds advised by SK Capital Partners has completed the sale of NuCera Solutions to Chase Corp. for $250 million. NuCera, a leading producer of specialty polymers, will be integrated into Chase's Adhesives, Sealants and Additives reporting unit. This acquisition is seen by Chase as transformational for its strategic growth, expanding its presence in high-growth end markets.

title: KeyCorp stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: KeyCorp's stock (KEY) rallied by 4.05% to $18.49 on a strong trading day, outperforming competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Wells Fargo & Co., and PNC Financial Services Group Inc. This gain marked the stock's second consecutive day of increases, although it remained $8.68 short of its 52-week high. The trading volume for KeyCorp also exceeded its 50-day average.

title: J.P. Morgan Asset Management Expands Sustainable Thematic ETF Suite with Launch of CIRC, UPWD & BLLD
summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (JPMAM) has expanded its active sustainable thematic ETF suite with the launch of three new funds: JPMorgan Sustainable Consumption ETF (CIRC), JPMorgan Social Advancement ETF (UPWD), and JPMorgan Sustainable Infrastructure ETF (BLLD). These ETFs aim to provide clients with access to alpha opportunities by investing in companies addressing major global trends related to sustainable consumption, social advancement, and sustainable infrastructure. The funds leverage JPMAM's extensive research capabilities and active management approach to offer tailored stock selection in the growing sustainable investing market.

title: Morgan Health invests $20M in home diagnostics company LetsGetChecked
summary: Morgan Health, JPMorgan Chase's healthcare business unit, has invested $20 million in the home diagnostics startup LetsGetChecked as part of its Series D-2 funding round. LetsGetChecked provides at-home tests for various conditions, including sexual health, cholesterol, diabetes, and COVID-19, and has recently expanded into genomics and made several acquisitions. This investment aims to improve timely access to clinical testing and support the company's growth in the competitive home diagnostics market.

title: Several Large US Companies Quietly Rolling Back COVID-19 Vaccine Mandate
summary: Several major U.S. companies, including Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan & Chase Co., and Cisco, are discreetly reversing their COVID-19 vaccine mandates. Experts note that the rationale for such mandates has weakened significantly since 2021. This move comes after the Supreme Court blocked the Biden administration's broad mandate for companies, though a limited mandate for healthcare workers remains.

title: JPMorgan Agrees to Buy Payments Fintech Renovite
summary: JPMorgan Chase has announced its agreement to acquire Renovite, a cloud-based payments technology company. This move comes as JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has previously identified fintech as a significant competitive threat to traditional banks. The acquisition reinforces JPMorgan's focus on strengthening its position in the evolving financial technology landscape.

title: Tages Helios II cashes in a 1.1 bn euro jumbo green loan. Meanwhile the new Helios Net Zero Fund is on the market and Tages’ private debt fund is ready for investing – BeBeez International
summary: Tages Helios II has secured a €1.1 billion green loan, the first for Tages, provided by a consortium of eight banks for financing renewable energy projects. Concurrently, Tages Capital SGR is launching a new fund, Tages Helios Net Zero, with a €750 million fundraising target to develop greenfield renewable energy projects. Additionally, Tages' private debt fund, established a year ago, is set to become operational, expanding the firm's investment vehicles.

title: Dividend-Stock Deep Dive: Banks and Capital Allocation
summary: This article discusses dividend policies and capital allocation strategies for banks, featuring an interview with Eric Compton of Morningstar Equity Research. It covers why banks cut dividends, the impact of post-financial crisis regulations and stress tests, the flexibility offered by stock buybacks versus dividends, and the minimal effect of the new 1% excise tax on buybacks. The discussion also highlights specific bank stock picks, including Citigroup, JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, and KeyCorp, based on valuation, dividend yield, and growth potential.

title: JP Morgan Chase’s Rhea Marpu: Helping to boost security and diversity
summary: Rhea Pritham Marpu, Vice President for JPMorgan Chase, plays a critical role in boosting the cybersecurity posture of the largest bank in the U.S., overseeing data protection for over 300,000 internal users within a zero-trust architecture. Beyond her technical contributions, Marpu is dedicated to promoting diversity by leading mentorship programs and representing JPMorgan Chase at women in tech conferences. Her work highlights the blend of technical expertise and human skills essential for robust security and career development in the financial industry.

title: Powell Says Money Not Important for Inflation
summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell contends that high inflation is due to the pandemic and that monetary aggregates are no longer important for inflation. Former Bank of England Governor Mervyn King rebutted this view, asserting that "money matters" and that central bankers have been wrong to ignore the link between money supply and inflation. The article also includes Adrian Day's comments on Osisko Gold Royalties Ltd.'s recent copper royalty acquisition and lists several gold and silver mining companies as "Best Buys."

title: AIG Announces Pricing of Corebridge Financial, Inc. Initial Public Offering
summary: American International Group, Inc. (AIG) announced the pricing of the initial public offering (IPO) of Corebridge Financial, Inc. at $21 per share. The offering involves AIG selling 80 million shares of Corebridge common stock, expecting to generate approximately $1.7 billion in gross proceeds. Corebridge shares are set to begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "CRBG" on September 15, 2022.

title: What credit score do you need to qualify for the American Express Gold Card?
summary: The American Express Gold Card is a popular travel rewards card offering significant benefits for dining and grocery purchases, including a generous welcome offer and statement credits. While Amex doesn't publicly state a minimum credit score, applicants generally need a "good" FICO score of 670 or higher to qualify. Other factors like payment history, amounts owed, and credit history length also influence approval.

title: Surviving the pandemic and developing the next generation of leaders
summary: The Sadie Nash Leadership Project (SNLP), a nonprofit focused on empowering young women and gender-expansive youth, successfully navigated the pandemic with the help of two PPP loans secured through Chase. This support allowed SNLP to expand programming, provide emergency grants, and continue training future social justice leaders. JPMorgan Chase's broader initiatives, including over $40 billion in PPP relief and a $12.7 billion commitment to women entrepreneurs, underscore its dedication to supporting small businesses and underserved communities.

title: TD Bank and DailyPay team for real-time earned wage access
summary: TD Bank has partnered with DailyPay, an on-demand pay solution provider, to offer its clients' employees real-time access to earned wages before their scheduled payday. This partnership aims to ease financial burdens caused by inflation and unforeseen expenses, allowing workers to access their earnings when needed. DailyPay's solution integrates with existing payroll systems, converting time worked into net earnings accessible through a bank account or card.

title: Comerica Bank Is Building a New Business and Innovation Hub at The Star in Frisco
summary: Comerica Bank is constructing a new Business & Innovation Hub at The Star in Frisco, slated to open in late 2023 or early 2024, which will house approximately 300 employees and feature an innovation center and "tech genius bar." This expansion aims to enhance cross-functional collaboration and meet evolving needs, complementing its downtown Dallas headquarters. The facility will be located in a new Class A+ tower at 17 Cowboys Way and is designed by HKS Architects.

title: AIG unit Corebridge Financial's IPO prices at low end of range to raise $1.6 billion and mark biggest IPO of the year so far
summary: AIG's life insurance unit, Corebridge Financial Inc., priced its initial public offering at $21 a share, the low end of its anticipated range, successfully raising $1.68 billion. This makes it the largest IPO of the year despite a challenging market environment and a recent selloff in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The shares are set to begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "CRBG."

title: Trump Media’s Merger Delay Puts $1 Billion Financing Deal in Doubt (Published 2022)
summary: A $1 billion financing deal for Trump Media & Technology Group's Truth Social platform is in jeopardy due to a merger delay. The agreement, intended to finance the social media company, is set to expire on September 20, potentially allowing hedge funds and wealthy investors to withdraw their commitments. This situation arises because the shell company aiming to merge with Trump Media has postponed the merger completion deadline.

title: Kosciusko County Court News
summary: This article provides a comprehensive overview of recent legal proceedings in Kosciusko County. It details judgments from small claims, civil collections, evictions, mortgage foreclosures, and plenaries. Additionally, it lists infractions from Superior Court III, recent marriage licenses issued, and marriage dissolutions filed, offering a snapshot of local court activities.

title: Still holding up a decade later? An insight into the effectiveness of the Etridge Protocol
summary: This article assesses the effectiveness of the Etridge Protocol, established in the case of Royal Bank of Scotland plc v Etridge (No 2) [2001] UKHL 44, which revitalized the law of undue influence and clarified the duties of banks and solicitors. The author, Oliwia Maliszewska, discusses the pros and cons of the protocol, particularly its low threshold for notice which aids in swiftly identifying undue influence and protects vulnerable parties. However, she also highlights disadvantages such as the lowering of standards in post-Etridge case law by judicial creativity and the challenges posed during the Covid-19 pandemic for in-person consultations, underscoring the need for reform.

title: AIG’s Corebridge Is Year’s Largest IPO at $1.7B
summary: AIG's life insurance and retirement division, Corebridge Financial Inc., successfully raised $1.68 billion in its initial public offering, marking the largest IPO of the year despite significant market volatility. AIG sold 80 million shares at $21 each, valuing Corebridge at $13.6 billion, with all proceeds going to AIG as the company seeks to focus on its property and casualty business. This listing also represents the biggest U.S. IPO of 2022, surpassing TPG Inc.'s $1.1 billion listing in January.

title: JPMorgan Ultra-Short Income ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:JPST) $JPST
summary: This article provides details on the JPMorgan Ultra-Short Income ETF (JPST), including its current price ($50.58), key statistics, ETF overview, and expenses. It highlights that JPST is an actively managed fund investing primarily in investment-grade fixed income securities with a short effective duration, aiming to maximize income and preserve capital. The article also lists recent news headlines related to JPST, shareholder information, and its top holdings.

title: Rail News - CN's Tracy Robinson has her eye on growth opportunities. For Railroad Career Professionals
summary: CN President and CEO Tracy Robinson discussed the railway's focus on growth opportunities and operational efficiency after her first half-year in the role. She highlighted strong Q2 2022 results, anticipated record demand for the remainder of the year, especially in western Canada, and CN's strategic investments in infrastructure and staffing to support this growth. Robinson emphasized running a tight and efficient operation to ensure growth translates to improved bottom-line performance, with particular focus on intermodal expansion in key ports.

title: Tobias Heilmaier joins Santander as head of SCIB Germany
summary: Santander Corporate and Investment Banking (Santander CIB) has announced the appointment of Tobias Heilmaier as the new head of Santander CIB in Germany, effective December 1st. Heilmaier brings over 17 years of experience from JP Morgan and Goldman Sachs, where he held significant leadership roles. His appointment aims to strengthen Santander CIB's position in the dynamic German market and further consolidate its regional offering in Europe.

title: Nikko unveils metaverse ETF in Hong Kong
summary: Nikko Asset Management has launched a new actively managed metaverse thematic equity ETF in Hong Kong, the NikkoAM Metaverse Theme Active ETF, listed in HKD (3091 HK) and USD (9091 HK). The ETF offers exposure to companies globally involved in developing and enabling the metaverse, with estimated ongoing charges of 1.25%. This new offering joins the CSOP Metaverse Concept ETF (3034 HK) and the Samsung Asia Pacific ex NZ Metaverse Theme ETF (3172 HK) in the Hong Kong market.

title: Hashdex Launches ’33 Act Bitcoin ETF With DEFI
summary: Hashdex, a cryptocurrency asset manager, has launched the Hashdex Bitcoin Futures ETF (DEFI), the world's first bitcoin futures ETF registered under the Securities Act of 1933. Developed with Teucrium Trading and Victory Capital Management, DEFI will be available on NYSE Arca from September 16, offering investors regulated exposure to the digital asset class with a different tax treatment than ’40 Act Bitcoin futures ETFs. This launch signifies Hashdex's commitment to providing innovative and regulated products globally, building on its work with the Nasdaq Crypto Index and other crypto offerings.

title: Horizon Kinetics Inflation Beneficiaries ETF (NYSEARCA:INFL) Holdings Boosted by Lowe Wealth Advisors LLC
summary: Lowe Wealth Advisors LLC increased its stake in Horizon Kinetics Inflation Beneficiaries ETF (INFL) by 7.3% in the second quarter, making it their 8th biggest position. Other institutional investors like Flow Traders U.S. LLC, Newman Dignan & Sheerar Inc., Wedbush Securities Inc., and JPMorgan Chase & Co. also modified their holdings, with JPMorgan Chase & Co. significantly raising its stake. The ETF's shares traded down recently, with a 1-year low of $27.26 and a 1-year high of $34.84.

title: JPMorgan reduces credit to China's Tsingshan and metal clients globally
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has significantly reduced its lending to China's Tsingshan Holding Group, a major nickel producer, and other metal clients across Europe and Asia, following a risk review. This decision comes after Tsingshan's involvement in a major nickel crisis on the London Metal Exchange in March, where nickel prices soared. The move by JPMorgan, a prominent player in metals finance, is causing a tightening of credit and liquidity within the metals sector, further exacerbated by rising interest rates and global recession fears.

title: Kinross shares soar on buyback deal with activist fund Elliott Investment
summary: Kinross Gold Corp. has reached an agreement with activist investor Elliott Investment Management LP to significantly increase its share buyback program. The mining company committed to repurchasing US$300-million of its stock this year and pledged to use 75 percent of excess cash for buybacks over the next two years, leading to an 11 percent jump in its share price. This move addresses the perceived undervaluation of Kinross stock and is a result of "constructive discussions" with Elliott.

title: United Community Bank’s CEO Lynn Harton Sees Two Dimensions to Leadership
summary: Lynn Harton, CEO of United Community Bank, defines leadership as having a positive vision and followers, emphasizing continuous personal growth. United Community Bank, known for its customer service and having $24.2 billion in assets, fosters employee development through programs like Career Pathing and Leadership Academy. Harton aims for United to be a "legendary bank" recognized by employees, customers, and shareholders.

title: The Global Real-Time Rail Ecosystem (Part I)
summary: This article, Part I of a series, explores the global landscape of real-time payment rail modernization. It highlights Canada's modernization journey and reviews faster payment systems in the UK, Australia, Hong Kong, and the United States, detailing the innovative services built upon these infrastructures. The article emphasizes that while the introduction of Real-Time Rails (RTR) is a significant step, it is merely the beginning of a broader modernization process with extensive economic implications.

title: Tencent Music shares debut on Hong Kong stock exchange
summary: Tencent Music Entertainment Group's shares began trading on the Hong Kong stock exchange at HK$18 ($2.29) as part of a secondary listing. This move makes it the latest US-listed Chinese firm to pursue a dual listing in Hong Kong, aiming to mitigate delisting risks in New York amid a dispute between Washington and Beijing regarding auditing papers. The company did not raise new capital in this transaction, with its shares opening flat compared to its US stock.

title: Major U.S. banks threaten to leave Mark Carney's climate alliance - FT
summary: Major U.S. Wall Street banks, including Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and Bank of America, are reportedly threatening to leave Mark Carney's Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ). The banks fear legal risks associated with the alliance's strict decarbonisation commitments and potential lawsuits, especially concerning upcoming U.S. SEC climate-risk disclosure rules. They also expressed concerns about a lack of government action on climate change and disproportionate membership from top carbon-emitting countries.

title: Houston-based space tech company to go public via SPAC merger
summary: Houston-based space exploration company Intuitive Machines plans to go public through a SPAC merger with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp., valuing the combined company at $815 million. Anticipated to close in Q1 2023, the deal will list Intuitive Machines on Nasdaq under the ticker LUNR. The company, which has a $262 million backlog in NASA contracts and a history of significant revenue growth, is also expanding its facilities and has secured $105 million in capital commitments to fuel future growth in the expanding space exploration market.

title: Bank CEOs push back on capital requirements in Capitol Hill hearings
summary: CEOs from seven of the largest U.S. banks, including JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America, engaged in two days of public hearings on Capitol Hill. They addressed various topics such as inflation, racial equality in home lending, regulatory burdens, and their perspectives on an impending economic slowdown. A key point of discussion was their pushback on capital requirements.

title: Bank executives warn lawmakers of lending risk among nonbanks
summary: Bank executives testified before the House Financial Services Committee, warning lawmakers that less stringent regulations on nonbank lenders are shifting significant lending, particularly in mortgages, outside the traditional banking system. They argued that current capital requirements put banks at a disadvantage and could pose risks during an economic downturn, as nonbanks may not have sufficient capital to cover losses. Despite their concerns, some lawmakers expressed skepticism, noting that banks have remained highly profitable despite post-2008 financial crisis regulations.

title: Shorting Bonds? The Case for a Seldom-Used Tactic
summary: A new research paper argues that rising interest rates present an ideal opportunity for investors to consider shorting bonds, a seldom-used tactic. Despite historical investor hesitancy, with rates turning around and bond prices falling, 2022 has shown profitability for shorting government bonds. The paper by Kathryn Kaminski of AlphaSimplex suggests that when rates are increasing, shorting bonds can often be profitable and even boasts a generally positive Sharpe ratio.

title: US bank CEOs say they would stop working with China in event of Taiwan attack
summary: Top US bank CEOs stated they would cease operations in China if the US government instructed them to do so following a Taiwan invasion by mainland forces. This commitment was made during a House of Representatives Financial Services Committee hearing where lawmakers questioned their institutions' business ties to both Russia and China. The CEOs of JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Citigroup, US Bancorp, PNC Financial, and Truist were present.

title: Richard Jones leaves Lloyds Banking Group to join Motonovo
summary: Richard Jones, current managing director of motor and leasing at Lloyds Banking Group, will depart to join Motonovo Finance as of early 2023. Jones brings over 20 years of experience, including leading Black Horse Motor Finance and unifying transport businesses within Lloyds. His new role will see him on Motonovo's executive committee, reporting to CEO Steven Cooper, with a focus on expanding their market share.

title: Three law firms advise Tencent Music’s homecoming listing on HKEX
summary: Davis Polk, Han Kun Law Offices, and Maples Group advised Tencent Music Entertainment Group on its secondary listing by introduction on the HKEX. This listing strategy, which involved no new share issuance or fund raising, was supported by Tencent Music's strong cash flow. Freshfields and CM Law Firm advised the joint sponsors, JP Morgan and Goldman Sachs, while Slaughter and May advised Tencent Holdings, Tencent Music's parent company.

title: Lawmakers Grill the Big Banks on Zelle, Interest Rates, and Overdraft Fees
summary: Lawmakers recently questioned the CEOs of seven major banks during annual oversight hearings. Key topics included the economy's state, diversity efforts, electronic payment scams like those involving Zelle, and issues related to interest rates and overdraft fees.

title: Bank CEOs questioned on consumer protections, social issues
summary: Bank CEOs faced a second day of questioning on Capitol Hill regarding consumer protections and social issues. Senate Democrats pressed for more consumer safeguards amidst high inflation, while Republicans questioned banks' involvement in social issues. Topics included overdraft fees, Zelle fraud, and banks' stances on abortion costs, gun rights, and environmental policies.

title: Credit Suisse Mulls Sale of Latin American Wealth Business, Excluding Brazil
summary: Credit Suisse Group AG is considering selling its Latin American wealth management operations, excluding Brazil, as part of a broader restructuring effort. The bank is reportedly in discussions with potential buyers, including Banco Santander SA and Intesa Sanpaolo SpA, to offload this segment which includes operations in countries like Mexico and Colombia. This move aligns with Credit Suisse's strategy to focus on its top 20 markets and exit non-core businesses to improve profitability.

title: Questioning CEOs of America’s Largest Banks on Efforts to Block Gun Purchases, Legal Commerce
summary: Senator Kevin Cramer questioned the CEOs of major U.S. banks during a Senate Banking Committee hearing regarding their commitment to processing transactions for legal goods and services, particularly in light of pressures to block gun purchases. Senator Cramer specifically challenged the banks on a new Merchant Category Code for gun and ammunition stores and sought assurances that legal transactions would not be discriminated against. All seven bank CEOs present committed to processing transactions for legal goods and services, including guns and ammunition.

title: PRME IPO News - Gene editing biotech Prime Medicine files for an estimated $200 million IPO
summary: Prime Medicine, a biotech company specializing in gene editing therapies, has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) aiming to raise an estimated $200 million. The company is developing one-time curative genetic therapies using its Prime Editing technology, with 18 preclinical programs targeting various conditions like sickle cell disease and Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Prime Medicine plans to list on the Nasdaq under the symbol PRME.

title: How to earn more money from your savings now that banks are raising interest rates
summary: The Federal Reserve has raised interest rates, leading banks to offer higher returns on savings accounts. However, many banks do not proactively inform existing customers about new, higher-yielding accounts, so consumers must shop around or ask their bank to transfer funds to better accounts. Online-only banks often provide higher interest rates due to lower overhead and increased competition for deposits.

title: Banc of California acquires Deepstack in payment processing play
summary: Banc of California has acquired Deepstack Technologies for $24 million in a cash and stock deal to expand its business into payment processing, targeting ISVs, e-commerce marketplaces, fintechs and other merchants. This acquisition aims to provide predictable fee income, capture a larger share of revenue per transaction, and offer a full suite of payment solutions to existing and new business clients. The bank expects to integrate Deepstack’s technology by Q4 and plans to leverage client payment insights for credit purposes, with all Deepstack employees joining Banc of California.

title: Why Japanese Equities Are “The Lone TINA Trade”
summary: The article argues that Japanese equities represent the "lone TINA trade" (There Is No Alternative) as bond yields rise in most other countries, but remain negative in Japan. With a weakening yen and attractive valuations, Japanese stocks offer significant investment potential, particularly for those hedging against currency fluctuations. WisdomTree Japan Hedged Equity Fund (DXJ) is highlighted as a vehicle to capture these opportunities.

title: Wall Street firms hit with $2 billion in fines in WhatsApp probe
summary: U.S. regulators have levied over $2 billion in fines against more than a dozen Wall Street firms, including Citigroup, Bank of America, and Goldman Sachs, for failing to monitor employees' communications on unauthorized messaging apps like WhatsApp. These penalties, which include $1.1 billion from the SEC and $710 million from the CFTC, represent the largest-ever fines against U.S. banks for record-keeping lapses. The probes highlighted the widespread use of unapproved channels for work-related communication, even by senior supervisors, which undermined regulatory scrutiny.

title: PNC buys restaurant point-of-sale firm Linga
summary: PNC Financial Services Group has acquired Linga, a Naples, Florida-based point-of-sale (POS) and payments solutions firm specializing in the restaurant industry. This acquisition will expand PNC's corporate payments capabilities and enhance its treasury management platform by integrating Linga's cloud-based operating system, online ordering, and QR code-based menu features. Linga will continue to operate with its existing management team and founder, Onur Haytac, reflecting a broader trend of banks investing in fintech to meet evolving consumer demands for contactless payments.

title: As interest rates rise, is cash king again?
summary: With rising interest rates, "cash is king" again for short-term savings, but experts advise caution. While savings rates are improving, inflation still outpaces them, leading to a loss in real value. For long-term investors, the stock market is still expected to outperform cash, and the US dollar is currently considered the only safe haven asset offering both value and higher yields.

title: Dynasty Financial Partners Closes a $50 Million Credit Facility from RBC Capital Markets and a Consortium of Lenders to Power Growth and Strategic Initiatives
summary: Dynasty Financial Partners, a leading provider of outsourced solutions for RIAs, has secured a $50 million revolving credit facility. This facility, led by RBC Capital Markets, UMB Bank, and J.P. Morgan, with participation from Citibank and Goldman Sachs, will be used to enhance Dynasty's technology, intellectual capital, and support for its network partners. The company aims to fuel continued growth and strategic investments through this new financing arrangement.

title: JPMorgan doubles down on UK retail bank Chase
summary: JPMorgan plans to double the workforce at its UK retail bank Chase to at least 2,000 within two years, despite initial losses and investor skepticism. The bank has attracted one million customers and over 10 billion pounds in deposits since its launch and aims to expand its offerings with lending products and integrate its investments business Nutmeg. This move signals JPMorgan's commitment to building a full-service international digital bank, despite a challenging market and competition.

title: CIBC adviser managing $400 million joins Stratos
summary: Kenneth J. Gimbel, who managed over $400 million at CIBC Private Wealth Management, has joined Stratos Wealth Advisors. With more than 50 years of experience, Gimbel specializes in developing tailored asset management programs for large and complex trusts and investment relationships. He was previously a partner at Geneva Investment Management before its acquisition by CIBC.

title: CEO Says He’s Been “Praying for Inflation” Because It’s an Excuse to Jack Up Prices
summary: Iron Mountain CEO William Meaney candidly admitted at an investor event that he has been "praying for inflation" because it allows the company to significantly increase prices and expand profit margins. This admission highlights how corporations use inflation as a pretext to raise prices beyond increased costs, leading to record-high corporate profits. The article contrasts this corporate strategy with the Federal Reserve's approach to curb inflation by aiming to reduce wages and increase unemployment.

title: Regions Bank to repay customers $141 million in illegal overdraft fees
summary: Regions Bank has been ordered to repay $141 million to customers for illegally charging overdraft fees between 2018 and 2021, even after telling customers they had sufficient funds. This marks the second time in a decade the bank has been penalized for such practices, highlighting an ongoing issue with "surprise overdraft fees" across the financial industry. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau also fined Regions an additional $50 million.

title: CFPB fines Regions $191M on overdraft practices
summary: The CFPB has fined Regions Bank $191 million for charging "illegal surprise" overdraft fees between 2018 and 2021. The penalty includes a $50 million fine and $141 million in restitution to customers affected by "authorized-positive" fees, which the bank states it eliminated over a year ago. This action highlights ongoing regulatory scrutiny of overdraft practices, with other banks also modifying or eliminating such fees.

title: City Announces LaSalle Street Reimagined Program In The Loop
summary: The City of Chicago has launched the "LaSalle Street Reimagined" program to revitalize the LaSalle Street corridor in The Loop. This initiative utilizes the LaSalle Central Tax Increment Financing (TIF) district, offering financial incentives for residential conversions within existing structures to address high office and retail vacancies. A key requirement for developers is to designate 30 percent of proposed units as affordable, catering to various Area Median Income levels, while also preserving architectural features and improving public infrastructure.

title: 12 tips for mitigating cyberattacks
summary: This article by JPMorgan Chase provides 12 recommendations for organizations to mitigate cyberattacks, drawing on best practices from the National Security Agency (NSA). The tips cover areas such as software updates, account access control, disaster recovery planning, network segregation, and leveraging multi-factor authentication. The article emphasizes the importance of continuous review, updates, and proactive defensive strategies in a constantly evolving cyberthreat landscape.

title: Watchdog recommends punishment for SMBC Nikko over alleged manipulation
summary: Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission, has recommended administrative punishment for SMBC Nikko Securities. This recommendation follows alleged market manipulation that led to indictments of former executives. The watchdog found insufficient compliance within the brokerage unit of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, suggesting measures such as temporary business suspensions or orders to improve internal controls.

title: HSBC to review Canary Wharf tower HQ, consider new London base
summary: HSBC is reviewing the future location of its global headquarters in London, ahead of its lease expiring at the 45-floor tower in Canary Wharf in early 2027. The review will consider options including renovating the current building or relocating to a new London base, while confirming the HQ will remain in the city. This move aligns with a broader trend of banks downsizing office space and HSBC's own commitment to reduce its office footprint by 40%.

title: UK banks told to reimburse customers tricked by scams
summary: The Payment Systems Regulator (PSR) in the UK has proposed new rules that would require banks to reimburse customers within 48 hours for losses over 100 pounds incurred from "authorised push payment" (APP) scams, which are Britain's largest type of payment fraud. The reimbursement bill would be split between the sending and receiving banks, with a maximum claim of one million pounds and a claim period of no less than 13 months. This move aims to significantly increase the reimbursement rate for APP scam victims, currently at 46%, to over 95%.

title: Exclusive: JPMorgan to hire about 2,000 engineers even as economy softens
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co plans to hire approximately 2,000 engineers worldwide by the end of the year, despite a challenging economic environment. JPMorgan's global chief information officer, Lori Beer, highlighted that the bank views this hiring initiative as a strategic investment, positioning the company as a stable employer amidst economic volatility, and aims to attract talent away from tech companies that are currently slowing hiring or cutting jobs. The new roles will span various areas including software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, and cloud computing, supporting the bank's significant technology spending plan of $14.1 billion this year.

title: 2.6 million helped by Banco Santander’s financial education initiatives in three years
summary: Banco Santander's financial education programs have benefited 2.6 million people in the last three years (2019-2021) and are on track to exceed its financial inclusion target of 10 million people by 2025. These initiatives, which include projects like "Finanzas para Mortales" in Spain and similar programs in other countries, aim to provide basic financial concepts, promote informed decision-making, and contribute to the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals. The bank focuses on financially vulnerable groups, employing employee volunteers and collaborating with NGOs and other institutions to make growth inclusive through financial literacy.

title: Bancos concretan venta de Nexus a española Indra
summary: Chilean banks, including Banco de Chile, Banco Itaú, BancoEstado, and BCI, have finalized the sale of their stake in Nexus, a company processing credit card transactions in the country, to Minsait Payment, a subsidiary of Spain's Indra. The sale, valued at over CLP 8.9 billion, was approved by the FNE and CMF, with Minsait Payments Systems Chile S.A. now owning 100% of Nexus shares. This transaction transfers control of Nexus and concludes the banks' ownership.

title: JPMorgan Chase Is Phasing Out Safe Deposit Boxes
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is beginning to phase out safe deposit boxes, a banking feature increasingly less relevant in the digital age. The bank will no longer rent new boxes to customers, and existing boxes in branches that close will not be replaced at other locations. This move reflects a shift away from traditional banking services toward more modern solutions.

title: JPMorgan Chase & Co. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM) stock declined 1.56% to $104.50 on a Friday, underperforming the broader market indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, and its performance was mixed compared to competitors such as Bank of America Corp., Citigroup Inc., and Wells Fargo & Co. Trading volume for JPM surpassed its 50-day average.

title: Judge orders unfreezing of assets for Sam Randazzo
summary: An appellate judge has ordered the unfreezing of millions of dollars in bank accounts belonging to Sam Randazzo, a former Ohio utility regulator implicated in a public corruption scandal. While FirstEnergy claims it paid Randazzo a $4.3 million bribe, he has not been criminally charged and denies wrongdoing. The judge overturned a lower court's decision to freeze his assets, citing a lack of justification for potential "irreparable injury" and questioning the basis of the state's request.

title: People: Andrea Rossi Named M&G CEO
summary: This article reports on key personnel changes in the real estate investment sector, with a focus on executive appointments. Andrea Rossi has been named CEO of M&G, while Joy City Property and China South City have appointed new board leaders. Additionally, New World Development, Manulife US REIT, Cushman & Wakefield, and Colliers have announced various promotions and board changes.

title: CFPB Enforcement Action Latest Move Against Overdraft Fees by Financial Regulators
summary: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) recently took an enforcement action against Regions Bank for "Authorized-Positive Overdraft Fees," alleging these practices were unfair and abusive. This action is part of a growing trend among state and federal regulators to scrutinize and address overdraft and non-sufficient funds fees, which are seen as disproportionately affecting low-income consumers. Financial institutions are advised to review their policies and disclosures proactively to avoid further regulatory action and potential litigation.

title: Bradesco abre inscrições para o hackathon inovabra de Cash Management
summary: Bradesco, por meio de seu ecossistema inovabra, abriu inscrições para o 1º Hackathon de Cash Management. O evento, que aceita participantes de startups, empresas e universidades de todo o Brasil, busca soluções inovadoras em meios de pagamento. O vencedor terá a oportunidade de desenvolver uma prova de conceito remunerada com o Banco Bradesco S.A.

title: JPMorgan Chase pilots 'virtual call center' with Detroit remote workers
summary: JPMorgan Chase is piloting its first virtual call center in the nation, hiring approximately 50 remote workers from Detroit. The new full-time roles offer a starting wage of $22.50 an hour plus benefits, and the company views this as a potential model to replicate elsewhere. This initiative stems from lessons learned during the COVID-19 pandemic regarding remote work viability and is supported by collaboration with Detroit at Work.

title: Global investment banking fees drop
summary: Global investment banking fees have fallen by 32% through the first nine months of 2022 to US$83.1 billion, driven by significant declines in equity underwriting, debt underwriting, and mergers & acquisitions activity. The third quarter marked the slowest quarter since Q4 2016, with equity underwriting fees dropping by 67% year over year. JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, and BofA Securities topped the global league tables, with RBC Capital Markets remaining the top-performing Canadian investment bank.

title: The 3 Most Popular Equity Income ETFs
summary: Amidst market volatility, bear markets, and high inflation, many investors are turning to dividend stocks and related ETFs for income and less volatility. This article highlights three of the most popular equity income ETFs, detailing their inflows, investment strategies, and expense ratios. The ETFs discussed are SCHD, JEPI, and VYM, each offering distinct approaches to generating income and outperforming the broader market.

title: CD&R Appoints Former JPMorgan Chase & Co. Executive Gordon Smith as Operating Advisor
summary: Clayton, Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) announced the appointment of Gordon Smith, former Co-President and Chief Operating Officer of JPMorgan Chase & Co., as an Operating Advisor to CD&R funds. Smith will collaborate with CD&R's financial services team to identify new investments and provide guidance to portfolio companies, leveraging his nearly 40 years of financial services experience. This strategic move aims to broaden opportunities for CD&R funds and enhance the expertise available to their portfolio companies.

title: Chase Bank launches first local virtual call center in Detroit
summary: JPMorgan Chase has announced the launch of its first virtual call center in Detroit, aiming to create dozens of jobs for local residents and support financial inclusion. The initiative builds on the firm's $200 million investment in the city since 2014, offering roles with competitive pay, tuition assistance, and "second-chance" opportunities for individuals with criminal backgrounds. This move highlights Chase's commitment to inclusive growth and racial equity, with plans for potential expansion if successful.

title: Interest Rates on Ally’s Online Savings Accounts Just Hit Their All-Time High
summary: Ally Bank has increased the annual percentage yield (APY) on its online savings accounts to a record 2.25%, marking at least 13 increases since May. This trend is a result of the Federal Reserve raising the federal funds rate to combat inflation, leading banks to offer higher interest rates on deposits. Online banks like Ally and Marcus by Goldman Sachs are particularly competitive due to lower operating costs.

title: Hunt Companies Leverages Real-Time Payments
summary: Hunt Companies partnered with J.P. Morgan and Kyriba to implement Real-Time Payment and Account Balance APIs, aiming to replace expensive and time-consuming wire payments. This integration significantly increased payment efficiencies and resulted in substantial cost savings for the company. The shift to real-time payments has saved Hunt Companies an estimated 10 hours per week and reduced wire costs by 83%, offering instant confirmation and 24/7 availability for transactions.

title: A Lehman Moment for European Banks? The Market Says No.
summary: Despite rising credit risk among some European banks, including Credit Suisse and Deutsche Bank, market data suggests a "Lehman Moment" for the sector is unlikely in the short term. While credit spreads have widened significantly, capital buffers have increased, and credit-default swap (CDS) spreads do not indicate imminent widespread defaults. The market-implied six-month default probabilities for Credit Suisse and Deutsche Bank are relatively low, though longer-term concerns persist.

title: Experienced Trust Professional and More Join Pinnacle Financial Partners in the National Capital Region
summary: Pinnacle Financial Partners has announced the addition of experienced trust professional Justin Willis as a trust portfolio manager in the National Capital Region, alongside Marilyn Carrera as a financial advisor assistant and Anita Carter as a treasury management analyst. These new hires bring significant experience to the firm, strengthening its wealth management and client services in the region. The move underscores Pinnacle's commitment to building a full-service bank capable of meeting diverse client needs, leveraging the expertise and community recognition of its new team members.

title: Italy’s private equity weekly roundup. News from Atlantia, ITA Airways, Lega Calcio Serie A, NetInsurance, KPMG and more – BeBeez International
summary: This article provides a weekly roundup of private equity news in Italy, highlighting key transactions and developments. It covers the public offer for Atlantia by Schema Alfa, the extended exclusivity talks for ITA Airways' sale to Certares, and renewed private equity interest in Lega Calcio Serie A. Other news includes Poste Vita's offer for Net Insurance, KPMG's M&A report for Q3 2022, and various acquisitions and mergers involving companies like DMO Pet Care, SF Filter Group, International Food, Stain, Argea, Richetti, and MCS.

title: Report: Big U.S. Banks Are Stiffing Account Takeover Victims
summary: A report by Senator Elizabeth Warren indicates that major U.S. banks are failing to reimburse customers who are victims of account takeovers and unauthorized Zelle transactions. While banks generally don't repay victims of "fraudulently induced payments" where customers are tricked into authorizing transfers, the report highlights that even in cases of clear unauthorized fraud, banks are only refunding about 47% of the dollar amount claimed. Experts note inconsistencies in bank reimbursement policies despite CFPB guidance, suggesting potential regulatory intervention.

title: Carlyle-backed Yes Bank is now on a stressed assets hunt
summary: Yes Bank, backed by Carlyle, is actively seeking to acquire stressed assets from other lenders through its new partnership with US private-equity firm JC Flowers & Co. LLC. This move follows Yes Bank's recent sale of a large bad loan portfolio to JC Flowers’ ARC, aiming to boost profitability and shed its own legacy of stressed loans. CEO Prashant Kumar highlighted the partnership's potential to create a credible platform for managing stressed assets in India.

title: JSW arm likely to acquire National Steel and Agro Industries
summary: The Committee of Creditors (CoC) of National Steel and Agro Industries Ltd (NSAIL) has approved the resolution plan put forth by JSW Steel Coated Products Limited. NSAIL entered the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process in April after defaulting on a Rs 115 crore loan. If NCLT approves, this would be JSW Steel Coated Products Limited's second acquisition via the CIRP process.

title: With a stake in Vale, Cosan raises its bet on mining
summary: Cosan has acquired a minority stake in mining giant Vale, investing R$22 billion to reach 6.5% of the company's capital, signaling a significant bet on the mining sector's future. The move, however, raised concerns among investors and analysts regarding its financing and potential impact on Cosan's financial leverage. Cosan's executives emphasize a friendly approach and strategic alignment, viewing Vale as an "irreplicable" asset with high appreciation potential.

title: The Almost Billion Dollar Managed Futures ETF Making Waves
summary: The iMGP DBi Managed Futures Strategy ETF (DBMF) is nearing $1 billion in assets under management (AUM) due to its strong performance in a volatile market. Managed futures strategies, like DBMF, thrive during market dislocations by taking long and short positions across various asset classes. DBMF's success is attributed to replicating the average performance of top managed futures hedge funds at a significantly lower fee, offering crucial diversification when traditional assets underperform.

title: PREVIEW U.S. banks' Q3 profits set to shrink on economic risks, deal slump
summary: Major U.S. banks are projected to report significant declines in their third-quarter profits due to a slowdown in the economy and a slump in dealmaking. Investment banking activity has been hampered by turbulent markets, leading to analysts forecasting substantial profit drops for giants like JPMorgan, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley. While rising interest rates usually benefit banks, concerns about an economic downturn are prompting them to set aside more funds for potential loan losses.

title: Bank of New York Mellon Corp. stock falls Monday, still outperforms market
summary: Shares of Bank of New York Mellon Corp. (BK) dropped 0.68% on Monday, closing at $39.21. Despite the fall and the broader market decline, the stock outperformed competitors like JPMorgan Chase & Co., Citigroup Inc., and Wells Fargo & Co. This marked the fourth consecutive day of losses for Bank of New York Mellon Corp.

title: Galaxy Releases Inaugural Sustainability Report
summary: Galaxy Digital Holdings Ltd. has released its inaugural Sustainability Report, detailing the company's strategy for addressing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) objectives within the digital asset sector. This report, one of the first from a publicly traded crypto firm, emphasizes Galaxy's commitment to building equitable and inclusive communities and advancing the industry through transparent governance, social progress, and environmental stewardship. The company aims to inspire peers to adopt ESG principles, focusing on initiatives like diversity, educational resources, and reducing carbon footprints.

title: Renda fixa: CDB do Banco BV e LIG do Banco Bradesco são as recomendações da semana; confira
summary: Given the third consecutive month of deflation (IPCA falling 0.29%) and the Central Bank's resistance to interest rate cuts, analysts from the Super Renda Fixa series recommend fixed-income securities. Specifically, they suggest post-fixed titles with maturities under one year and pre-fixed titles in the middle of the curve. This week's top recommendations are the CDB Prefixado from Banco BV and the LIG Prefixada from Banco Bradesco.

title: 2022 Diversity & Inclusion award winner: JPMorgan Chase
summary: JPMorgan Chase was recognized as a 2022 Diversity & Inclusion award winner by the San Antonio Business Journal. The financial institution is committed to teaching its leadership and staff how to be more inclusive towards each other and their clients. Managing Director Robert Perales represented JPMorgan Chase & Co. for this award.

title: Coca-Cola FEMSA recompra 299.8 millones de dólares en bonos
summary: Coca-Cola FEMSA conducted a public offer to repurchase $299.8 million of its outstanding senior bonds due in 2043 and 2030. HSBC and J.P. Morgan acted as dealer managers for the offer, which initially had a cap of $250 million but was increased due to high demand. The company was advised by Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton, while the banks received legal support from Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom and Galicia Abogados.

title: Comcast Promotes CFO Mike Cavanagh to Added Role of President
summary: Comcast has promoted its Chief Financial Officer, Mike Cavanagh, to the additional role of President, making him the third person to hold this title in the company's 59-year history. Cavanagh will continue as CFO and work closely with Chairman and CEO Brian Roberts to manage Comcast's global businesses. This promotion recognizes his significant operational and financial contributions since joining Comcast seven years ago, following a distinguished career in financial services at JP Morgan Chase and The Carlyle Group.

title: Music catalog acquisitions cooling down? Not at Primary Wave: ‘We’ve never been busier.’
summary: Primary Wave has secured a significant $2 billion deal with financial giant Brookfield, establishing a "permanent capital vehicle" for catalog acquisitions. CEO Larry Mestel asserts that despite market rumors of a slowdown in music M&A due to macroeconomic factors, Primary Wave has an "unlimited supply of capital" for good deals and has never been busier. The company credits its success to a strategy of adding real value to acquired assets and maintaining strong artist relationships, distinguishing itself from competitors who may have over-leveraged.

title: Comcast Promotes CFO Mike Cavanagh to Added Role of President
summary: Comcast has promoted its chief financial officer, Mike Cavanagh, to the additional role of president, making him only the third president in the company's 59-year history. Cavanagh will work closely with chairman and CEO Brian L. Roberts to manage the company's businesses and teams while retaining his CFO responsibilities. Roberts praised Cavanagh's operational and financial expertise, highlighting his integral role in Comcast's growth.

title: Canada Post officially launches nationwide loan program with TD Bank Group
summary: Canada Post has officially launched a nationwide loan program called MyMoney in partnership with TD Bank Group. This initiative aims to provide accessible financial options, particularly for underserved Canadians in rural, remote, and Indigenous communities. The loans, ranging from $1,000 to $30,000, are intended to bridge the gap between payday lenders and traditional banks, carrying TD-determined interest rates and not requiring an existing bank account.

title: PepsiCo Defies Fears of Consumer Slowdown With Strong Earnings and Forecast (Published 2022)
summary: PepsiCo reported strong third-quarter earnings, exceeding analyst expectations and raising its full-year forecasts for revenue and profit. This performance indicates that consumers are continuing to spend on its products despite high inflation and rising prices. The company's ability to raise prices without significantly impacting sales volumes, even as the U.S. dollar's strength affected international earnings, offered a positive signal for the broader earnings season.

title: Ingreso solidario en octubre 2022: ¿Cómo cobrarlo por medio de Bancolombia?
summary: This article explains how recipients of the Ingreso Solidario government subsidy in Colombia can collect their payments through Bancolombia in October 2022. It details that payments are automatically deposited into Bancolombia accounts for existing users and how those without an account will be contacted to open one via A la mano or Nequi. The Ingreso Solidario was created during the COVID-19 pandemic to assist vulnerable families and is expected to continue until December 2022.

title: JP Morgan Chase severs ties with Kanye West following series of controversies
summary: JP Morgan Chase has reportedly decided to end its banking relationship with Kanye West's company, Yeezy LLC. This decision, announced via an alleged email shared by conservative activist Candace Owens, follows a string of controversies involving West, including his "White Lives Matter" shirt and antisemitic remarks. West had also recently terminated his partnership with GAP Inc. and Adidas was reviewing their relationship with him.

title: Carmen Kramer Finds Great Satisfaction In Solving Issues For Her Bank Clients
summary: Carmen Kramer, a Senior Treasury Management Specialist at Enterprise Bank & Trust, finds immense satisfaction in helping her clients solve their financial issues. She has a deep knowledge of banking and has been certified as an Accredited ACH Professional. Kramer, who moved to Los Alamos from Germany in 2013, is also an active volunteer in her community.

title: BlackRock Sees “Generational” Fixed Income Opportunities
summary: Robert Kapito, president of BlackRock, stated there are generational opportunities in the bond market due to rising rates and US stimulus. He highlighted that attractive yields are now available with less duration or credit risk, driving significant inflows into fixed income and bond ETFs. BlackRock also addressed its ESG strategy and Liability-Driven Investing (LDI) in the UK pension industry.

title: Chart of the Week: Advisors Find Safety Attractive
summary: Advisors are prioritizing safety and downside protection in fixed income due to rising interest rates, leading to increased interest in ultra-short bond ETFs. These ETFs offer higher yields than before, with popular options including both index-based Treasury ETFs and actively managed funds that incorporate investment-grade corporates and mortgages for better income generation. The article highlights specific ultra-short bond ETFs and their performance in the current rising rate environment.

title: Embedded finance: Who will lead the next payments revolution?
summary: Embedded finance, which integrates financial products into nonfinancial digital experiences, reached $20 billion in US revenues in 2021 and is projected to double within three to five years. The article explores how banks, payments providers, fintechs, and software firms can participate and succeed in this dynamic market by focusing on product breadth, depth, and program management support. Key success factors include choosing a strategic focus, building a modern developer experience, adapting to B2B2C/B2B2B sales, and developing robust support and risk services.

title: Big Banks’ Profits Drop, but Consumers Cushion the Blow
summary: Major banks like JPMorgan, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo reported a drop in third-quarter profits but noted that strong consumer spending is helping to mitigate the impact of financial market turbulence. While banks are bracing for an economic slowdown and bolstering reserves for potential loan losses, high employment and household savings are keeping credit card spending up and bad loans low. The profit declines were mainly attributed to a reduction in investment banking fees due to market volatility.

title: September US Class 8 Retail Sales Stay Strong
summary: U.S. Class 8 retail sales in September reached nearly 23,000 units, marking the second-highest total for the year and a significant 34.1% increase from the previous year. Industry experts note improvements in supply chain issues and anticipate normal production levels by early 2023, with demand remaining high despite forecasts of a looming recession. Many truck manufacturers experienced double-digit sales gains, and net order volume reached a record high of 53,271 in September.

title: Do credit card users want more protections? Survey says yes
summary: A LendingTree survey reveals that over 80% of credit card holders desire more protections due to rising interest rates making debt harder to manage. While sweeping changes are unlikely, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is exploring new rules for late fees, and the White House is pushing to eliminate "junk fees." Consumers are advised to pay down debt, consider 0% balance transfer cards, and ask for lower rates.

title: Iron ore price outlook clouded by global demand woes, supply risks
summary: The outlook for iron ore prices is negative, with forecasts suggesting 2022 will end at a multi-year low and 2023 will also see languishing prices. This decline is attributed to reduced steel output in China and Europe, persistent global demand weaknesses, high inflation, recession fears, and an increase in supply from major producers. Despite the challenges, some mining giants like BHP Group remain confident in China's stabilizing role due to its economic stimulus measures.

title: JPMorgan Posts Record Net Interest Income on Fed Rate Hikes
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported its highest-ever quarterly net interest income, reaching $17.6 billion, and increased its full-year guidance. This record performance was attributed to the Federal Reserve's interest-rate hikes, which boosted the bank's earnings on loans. The company also surpassed profit estimates due to lower-than-anticipated expenses.

title: Morgan Stanley profit misses estimate as deals drought extends
summary: Morgan Stanley reported a 30% slump in third-quarter profit, missing analysts' estimates, as a global dealmaking slowdown significantly impacted its investment banking business. The bank's CEO expects clarity on inflation by mid-2023, while its wealth management division surprisingly showed revenue growth. The results highlight broader challenges faced by major banks due to uncertain economic conditions and rising interest rates.

title: Surcharging and What It Means For Your Business
summary: This article explains credit card surcharging for businesses, detailing how merchants can add a fee for credit card transactions following a class action lawsuit settlement with Visa and Mastercard. It outlines eligibility criteria for the settlement, how to claim, and provides guidance on how to implement surcharging, including notification and disclosure requirements. The article also addresses frequently asked questions regarding surcharging, such as what it is, how it differs from convenience fees, and regional restrictions like those in Quebec.

title: Morgan Stanley rides wealth management as a third-quarter highlight
summary: Morgan Stanley's wealth management business was a key highlight in its third-quarter earnings, attracting $65 billion in net new assets and pushing the yearly total to $260 billion despite difficult market conditions. The company's net interest income also saw a significant boost due to rising interest rates, while investment banking revenues declined. Analysts remain bullish on the stock, citing the strength of its wealth management unit.

title: Citigroup reports $110 mln leveraged-loan loss as other banks avoid sector exposure
summary: Citigroup reported a $110 million writedown on leveraged loans in the third quarter, contrasting with other major Wall Street banks that largely avoided or reduced their exposure to the sector. This loss reflects the broader struggles in the leveraged finance market, exacerbated by rising interest rates and investor caution, which have also impacted mergers and acquisitions.

title: Bank of America profits fall as it joins other banks in setting aside money for downturn
summary: Bank of America reported an 8% decline in third-quarter profits, earning $7.08 billion, as it began setting aside money in loan-loss reserves in anticipation of a potential economic downturn. The bank allocated $378 million to these reserves, following a trend seen with other major banks like JPMorgan, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo, which are preparing for potential bad loans. Despite the profit fall, BofA saw healthy loan growth and benefited from higher interest rates, with net interest income increasing by 24%.

title: Spread the love and you could earn up to 125,000 Rapid Rewards bonus points
summary: Southwest Airlines is offering new cardholders of their Rapid Rewards® Credit Cards a chance to earn up to 125,000 bonus points through a tiered spending offer. The promotion encourages spending to unlock points, which can be redeemed for flights, gift cards, and more, providing significant value for travel. This offer is designed to attract new cardmembers and reward them for their initial spending.

title: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman: “I'm perfectly happy to see our tech spend go up”
summary: Morgan Stanley CEO James Gorman expressed satisfaction with increased tech spending, viewing it as crucial for efficiency and innovation, despite a 22% drop in bank revenues. He highlighted the importance of cloud technology, robo-advisors, and cybersecurity, while also reflecting on market recalibrations due to past "ridiculous" valuations and the return to fundamental economic principles. The bank's wealth management and fixed income sectors performed well, offsetting a decline in investment banking.

title: JPMorgan investment banking chief Hernandez to retire in 2023
summary: Carlos Hernandez, JPMorgan's executive chair of investment and corporate banking, will retire at the end of the first quarter of next year. Hernandez, a 36-year veteran at the company, has been instrumental in growing several key segments including treasury services, investor services, and global equities business. He will work with Jim Casey and Viswas Raghavan, co-heads of global investment banking, to ensure a smooth transition.

title: JPMorgan Chase becomes only bank able to accept government deposits in all 50 states
summary: JPMorgan Chase has announced its ability to accept government deposits in all 50 U.S. states, a significant milestone largely due to its expanded branch presence nationwide. This expansion allows the bank to provide financial tools and services to states and municipalities, enabling them to operate more efficiently and serve their communities better. The effort builds on JPMorgan Chase's historical engagement with governments, dating back to 1799.

title: NYCB Lends $68M on Skylight’s Latest NJ Multifamily Purchase
summary: New York Community Bank (NYCB) has provided $67.7 million in acquisition financing to Skylight Real Estate Partners and PCCP for their $116.5 million purchase of Hudson Lights, a 277-unit apartment community in Fort Lee, N.J. This marks the fourth New Jersey multifamily deal for Skylight and PCCP, highlighting the attractiveness of the Northern New Jersey market due to hybrid working trends, affordable housing demand, and office development in Western Manhattan. The property, sold by Ares Real Estate, offers various apartment configurations and amenities, with CBRE representing both buyer and seller in the transaction.

title: Jamie Dimon Praises Blockchain, Calling the Technology "Real"
summary: JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon, despite being a vocal critic of cryptocurrencies, has praised blockchain technology as "real" due to its practical applications in finance. His company, JP Morgan, uses blockchain through its Onyx platform for efficient wholesale payments. The article also suggests the Amplify Transformational Data Sharing ETF (BLOK) as an active management investment option for long-term growth in blockchain technology.

title: JPMorgan Chase’s One Paseo ‘Delivers the Firm’ to San Diego
summary: JPMorgan Chase's One Paseo office in San Diego, opened in December 2021, represents a long-term commitment to the region, bringing together Middle Market and Private Bank teams. The office, designed for accessibility and community integration, has seen significant growth in both employees and client base, and emphasizes delivering the full range of JPMorgan Chase services to San Diego businesses and residents. The firm also actively engages in philanthropic efforts through its Market Leadership Team, focusing on supporting underserved small businesses and job training programs.

title: FTI Consulting appoints Miriam Wrobel as ESG leader
summary: FTI Consulting has appointed Miriam Wrobel as the global leader of its environmental, social, and governance (ESG) and sustainability offering. Wrobel previously joined FTI's San Francisco office in 2021 as a senior managing director focusing on ESG and energy transition strategy. She will now lead a global team to address the growing demand for ESG consulting services from clients.

title: Goldman Sachs’ anti-remote-work CEO has almost brought office work back to pre-pandemic levels—but insists he ‘doesn’t want rules’
summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon, a notable opponent of remote work, has successfully brought office attendance levels close to pre-pandemic numbers, with 65% of staff now in the office compared to 75% before COVID-19. Solomon believes that in-person collaboration is crucial for the company's culture and for mentoring younger employees, who make up a significant portion of their workforce. He emphasizes fostering a culture of showing up and serving clients rather than enforcing strict rules.

title: M&T sees record profits 6 months after People's United deal
summary: M&T Bank reported record profits of $647 million in the quarter following its acquisition of People's United, despite customer service issues during the system conversion. The bank also reduced its payroll by $40 million and is now looking to fill new positions through a career fair. While M&T's deposits saw a decline, the bank is actively offering incentives to attract new customers amidst market competition.

title: DWS Appoints Dirk Goergen as Americas CEO
summary: DWS Group has appointed Dirk Goergen as its new Americas CEO, effective January 1, 2023. Goergen, who is also an Executive Board member and Global Head of Client Coverage Division, will focus on identifying growth opportunities and strengthening the firm's position in the Americas market. He succeeds Mark Cullen, who will be stepping down at the end of the year.

title: Former Celsius exec joins JPMorgan as director of crypto regulatory policy
summary: Former Celsius executive Aaron Iovine has joined JPMorgan Chase & Co as executive director of digital assets regulatory policy, despite CEO Jamie Dimon's previous criticisms of cryptocurrencies. Iovine previously served as head of policy and regulatory affairs at the now-bankrupt crypto lender Celsius. This move highlights JPMorgan's continued involvement in digital assets amidst varied opinions on their value within the financial world.

title: Jack Henry and Mastercard Expand Collaboration to Address Financial Fragmentation
summary: Jack Henry and Mastercard have expanded their collaboration to help community and regional financial institutions provide accountholders with a consolidated view of their financial experiences. This partnership utilizes Mastercard's open banking platform with Finicity services to address financial fragmentation and empower consumers and businesses with more informed financial decisions. The initiative aims to place financial institutions at the center of accountholders' financial lives, particularly as financial fragmentation increasingly complicates personal finance.

title: Capital One looks to revamp airport lounge experience
summary: Capital One is enhancing its airport lounge experience by partnering with chef José Andrés to offer elevated tapas and small plates at its new Capital One Landing lounges in New York's LaGuardia and Washington's Ronald Reagan National airports. These new lounges, strategically located closer to gates, aim to provide travelers with fresh food quickly during shorter layovers. This move follows the bank's revamp of the Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport lounge and plans for Denver and Dulles, as it competes with other banks like American Express and JPMorgan Chase in the airport lounge market.

title: Bank of Hawaii Corporation (NYSE:BOH) is largely controlled by institutional shareholders who own 75% of the company
summary: Institutional shareholders control 75% of Bank of Hawaii Corporation (NYSE:BOH), signifying their significant influence due to their substantial ownership and research capabilities. The Vanguard Group, Inc. and BlackRock, Inc. are among the largest institutional holders, while the general public holds a 23% stake. Insiders, including CEO Peter Ho, also have a meaningful stake, aligning their interests with other shareholders.

title: Employers are getting more selective and taking longer to hire, headhunter Robert Half says
summary: Robert Half International Inc.'s stock fell to a 20-month low after the company missed third-quarter profit and revenue expectations and issued a bleak outlook. The headhunter noted that clients are becoming more selective and taking longer to hire, leading J.P. Morgan analyst Andrew Steinerman to downgrade his stance due to rising recessionary risks. The CEO also highlighted a structural shift towards remote/hybrid working models among job seekers.

title: JPMorgan doubles down on gaming firm tie
summary: JPMorgan Chase has invested in Sightline Payments, a company providing payment services for the regulated gaming industry, through its payments unit. This investment aims to develop an integrated omnichannel solution for resort and online gaming companies and is part of JPMorgan Payments' broader multi-channel strategy in the gaming sector. Sightline, which previously tapped JPMorgan as its primary merchant acquirer, focuses on converting the cash-based gaming industry into a digitally-enabled one, projecting significant market expansion.

title: Follow the Money: Actuate Therapeutics Raises $11.2M to Fight Cancer, TPG Real Estate Closes $6.8B-plus Fund, Mark Cuban Backs Storage Scholars, and More
summary: This article details recent funding rounds and acquisitions in North Texas. Key highlights include Actuate Therapeutics raising $11.2 million for cancer treatment, TPG Real Estate closing a $6.8 billion fund, and Mark Cuban investing $250,000 in Storage Scholars. Other significant deals cover Sinclair Digital Services' fundraising, Darling Ingredients' $1.2 billion acquisition, and various other investments and mergers across different sectors.

title: Here are the bank branches closing (and opening) in the Louisville area
summary: U.S. Bank and JPMorgan Chase are either closing or opening branches in the Louisville area. U.S. Bank will be closing two in-store branches, while a major player in the Louisville banking market is also closing two retail branches. The article teases more details about which institutions are making these changes.

title: Denali Therapeutics Announces Closing of a $316 Million Public Offering, Including Full Exercise of Underwriters’ Option to Purchase Additional Shares
summary: Denali Therapeutics announced the closing of an upsized underwritten public offering of 11,933,962 shares of common stock at $26.50 per share, generating approximately $316 million in gross proceeds. This includes the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares. The offering was managed by Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Jefferies LLC as joint book-running managers.

title: Apple Moves iPhone 14 Production to India
summary: Apple announced it will begin manufacturing its latest iPhone 14 models in India, marking a significant step in the company's efforts to diversify production away from China. This move aligns with India's push for local manufacturing and is expected to boost India's smartphone market. Investors can capitalize on India's digital growth through ETFs like the EMQQ Global’s India Internet and Ecommerce ETF (INQQ).

title: Company Outsider: HUL Eyes Acquisitions to Beef Up its Health Foods
summary: Hindustan Unilever Ltd (HUL) is reportedly in talks to acquire majority stakes in direct-to-consumer brands Wellbeing Nutrition and Conscious Food to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing nutraceutical and health foods market. This move is part of HUL's broader strategy to expand its food portfolio and enhance its global growth contribution to its parent company, Unilever, while also streamlining deliveries to compete with online grocery wholesalers. The article also provides a summary of other significant business news, including Reliance Industries' plan to demerge its financial services, Invesco's further stake reduction in Zee Entertainment, Kotak Investment Advisors raising a real estate fund, and Vodafone Idea's bond sale to ATC Telecom Infrastructure.

title: Compañía Minera Raura obtiene crédito por 126 millones de dólares
summary: Compañía Minera Raura S.A. (Raura), a Peruvian mining company, secured a $126 million term loan from a syndicate of six banks, including Banco Santander, JPMorgan Chase Bank, Banco de Crédito e Inversiones, Citibank, ICBC Peru Bank, and Banco Internacional del Perú. The funds will be used to refinance existing debt. The transaction, which concluded on September 13th, involved legal counsel from Rodrigo, Elías & Medrano Abogados for Raura, and Clifford Chance and DLA Piper for the lenders.
