title: Costco class action alleges retailer shared customer health info with Meta
summary: Costco is facing a class action lawsuit alleging that it shared customers' personal health information with Meta through embedded tracking tools like Facebook Pixel, without consent. The lawsuit claims that this data, gathered from Costco's pharmacy website where customers manage prescriptions, is not anonymous and is linked to specific Facebook user profiles. The plaintiffs argue that Costco's actions violate HIPAA regulations designed to protect private health information.

title: Coursera class action claims company shares customer viewing history with Meta
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Coursera Inc., alleging the company shares customers' video viewing history and personally identifiable information with Meta Platforms without consent. The lawsuit claims Coursera uses an invisible tracking tool called "Meta Pixel" to facilitate this data sharing, violating the Video Privacy Protection Act. The plaintiff seeks to represent a nationwide class of individuals who viewed Coursera videos while having active Facebook accounts.

title: Walmart agrees to huge South Bay sublease deal, in lift for office market
summary: Walmart's digital unit has signed a significant sublease agreement for the 719,000-square-foot Moffett Green tech campus in Sunnyvale, a move expected to bring thousands of Walmart.com employees to the Silicon Valley location. This deal offers a substantial boost to the region's struggling office market, which has seen increased vacancies and reduced demand for office space following widespread tech layoffs and the shift to remote work. The campus was previously leased by Meta Platforms and is currently owned by CommonWealth Partners, highlighting the dynamic changes in Bay Area commercial real estate.

title: US judge trims AI copyright lawsuit against Meta
summary: A U.S. federal judge has partially dismissed a copyright lawsuit filed by comedian Sarah Silverman and other authors against Meta Platforms, concerning its AI system Llama. While the judge will dismiss allegations that Llama's text output infringes copyrights, he is allowing the authors to amend most of their claims. The core accusation that Meta infringed copyrights by using authors' books to train Llama remains unchallenged by Meta in this phase.

title: Amazon sued over 'dangerous partnership' with virtual casino apps
summary: Amazon is being sued in a proposed consumer class-action lawsuit for allegedly earning billions through an "illegal internet gambling enterprise." The lawsuit, filed by a Nevada resident, claims Amazon distributed over 30 illegal casino apps and processed payments for virtual chips, maintaining a 30% financial interest. This case is part of broader litigation targeting online social casino apps, with similar lawsuits pending against Apple, Meta, and Google regarding their payment-processing roles.

title: Autodesk Workshop XR Delivers Immersive Design Review Experience for the AEC Industry
summary: Autodesk, Inc. unveiled Autodesk Workshop XR, an immersive design review workspace connected to Autodesk Construction Cloud, aimed at the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. This new tool enables real-time collaboration on 3D models from anywhere, facilitating better decision-making and preventing costly errors. Workshop XR will be available on Meta Quest headsets, enhancing project reviews and sustainability through improved design processes.

title: FAANG Gives Way to the ‘Magnificent Seven’
summary: The "FAANG" stock group has evolved into the "Magnificent Seven," with Netflix replaced by Nvidia, and Microsoft and Tesla added to the mix of top U.S. market names. ETF issuers are beginning to launch products specifically targeting these seven stocks, while existing ETFs like the Vanguard Mega Cap Growth ETF (MGK) already hold significant concentrations of them. Investors have various options, from highly concentrated ETFs to diversified funds, to gain exposure to these influential companies.

title: Tepper’s Appaloosa dumps Apple stake and loads up on Amazon’s stock
summary: David Tepper’s Appaloosa hedge fund significantly increased its stake in Amazon.com Inc. and completely divested its position in Apple Inc. during the last quarter. The fund also raised its holdings in Google parent Alphabet Inc. and Facebook parent Meta Platforms Inc., as detailed in a recent SEC filing. This move indicates a shift in Tepper's portfolio allocation towards these tech giants.

title: ‘I was addicted to social media - now I'm suing Big Tech’
summary: Taylor Little, a 21-year-old, is among hundreds of families suing major tech companies like Meta, TikTok, Google, and Snap Inc. for allegedly designing harmful and addictive social media products for children. Taylor details their journey through social media addiction, which led to suicide attempts and depression after being exposed to graphic content and body image issues at a young age. A recent federal court ruling boosted the families' case by rejecting the tech companies' attempts to use freedom of speech and Section 230 as blanket protections.

title: AI ETFs see huge performance dispersion in 2023
summary: Artificial Intelligence ETFs have shown significant performance dispersion in 2023, with top strategies more than doubling the returns of the lowest performers. This disparity is largely attributed to the heavy weighting of certain ETFs towards US equities and the "magnificent seven" tech stocks. While these mega-cap companies have driven much of the AI theme's returns, there is still potential for pure-play AI companies to join the rally.

title: Cognizant Technology Solutions to lay off employees tied to Apple in Austin
summary: Cognizant Technology Solutions announced layoffs impacting employees linked to Apple in Austin. The contractors affected will receive pay while exploring other positions within Cognizant. This move adds to a series of technology sector layoffs in Austin, though Central Texas is noted to be somewhat sheltered from broader industry cuts.

title: Celestica stock rides another tech wave – but can it avoid a crash this time?
summary: Celestica Inc., a Toronto-based manufacturer, is experiencing a resurgence due to the AI boom, supplying equipment to data centers for major tech companies like Amazon, Google, and Meta. Despite a significant increase in stock price and revenue, questions remain about the sustainability of this growth compared to the company's past crash during the dot-com era. CEO Rob Mionis argues that Celestica is a more diversified and insulated company now, focusing on higher-margin, complex equipment and seeing sustained demand in the early stages of AI development.

title: AI Alliance Launches as an International Community of Leading Technology Developers, Researchers, and Adopters Collaborating Together to Advance Open, Safe, Responsible AI
summary: The AI Alliance has launched as an international community of over 50 founding members, including IBM and Meta, to advance open, safe, and responsible AI. The alliance aims to foster open innovation and science in AI by bringing together diverse organizations to accelerate responsible AI development, establish benchmarks, and build a vibrant AI ecosystem. Its main goal is to ensure that AI advancements are harnessed in ways that prioritize safety, diversity, economic opportunity, and benefits for all, addressing societal challenges and promoting ethical AI practices.

title: Meta Platforms, IBM create industrywide AI alliance to share technology
summary: Meta Platforms and IBM are leading an industry-wide AI Alliance of over 40 companies and organizations to promote open-source artificial intelligence development. The coalition aims to share technology, reduce risks, and focus on responsible AI development, including safety and security tools. This initiative seeks to increase open-source AI models and foster collaboration with academic researchers.

title: AMD releases new chips to power faster AI training
summary: AMD announced the availability of its new MI300 chips, including the Instinct MI300X accelerator and Instinct M1300A APU, designed to power demanding AI training and large language models. The company also unveiled the Ryzen 8040 mobile processors, which will bring enhanced AI capabilities to laptops in 2024. These releases position AMD to compete more directly with Nvidia in the booming AI chip market.

title: CastleArk Enters ETF Market With Large Growth ETF CARK
summary: CastleArk has launched its first exchange-traded fund, the CastleArk Large Growth ETF (CARK), an actively managed ETF focused on large-cap growth companies. The fund targets 25-30 leading growth companies, identifying competitive strength and seeking to optimize risk through quantitative inputs. CastleArk aims to provide an actively managed alternative to index-heavy portfolios, especially given the concentration of "Magnificent Seven" stocks in the large-cap growth sector.

title: AMD debuts new chip with eye to rival Nvidia product
summary: AMD has unveiled its new MI300 accelerator chips, aiming to compete with Nvidia in the burgeoning artificial intelligence (AI) chip market. CEO Lisa Su projected the AI chip industry could exceed $400 billion in the next four years, and mentioned Microsoft, Oracle, and Meta Platforms as customers. The company claims its new chip outperforms Nvidia's H100 in AI inference and matches it in training capabilities.

title: Salesforce’s Benioff Cashing Out at Rate of $3 Million a Day
summary: Marc Benioff, co-founder of Salesforce, has been consistently selling 15,000 shares of the company's stock, worth about $3 million, almost daily since July. This strategy has resulted in unloading over $475 million worth of shares through approximately 170 transactions this year, a practice he employs to fund charitable gifts. Experts view his systematic selling approach as a "safest" way for CEOs to diversify their holdings without significantly impacting stock prices or violating insider-trading rules.

title: What are the most visited social media platforms among Gen Z?
summary: This article analyzes the most visited and fastest-growing social media platforms among Gen Z (18-24 year olds) based on mobile app usage. It highlights YouTube as having the highest reach, while BeReal and LinkedIn are the fastest growing platforms for this demographic. The analysis also compares Gen Z's social media usage to the general population and other age groups, noting their higher engagement on most platforms except for Facebook and LinkedIn in terms of reach.

title: Breaking Through the Echo Chamber: The Dynamic Power of Out of Home + Social Media
summary: This article explores how the integration of social media and out-of-home (OOH) advertising is a game-changer for brands seeking to engage new digital audiences, particularly Gen Z. It highlights TikTok's embrace of OOH, the enhanced social media engagement driven by #sOOH, and the tangible presence OOH offers for both emerging and legacy brands. The synergy helps brands break free from digital echo chambers, foster meaningful connections, and build trust among consumers.

title: Possible IPO Stars for 2024: Private Equity Firms
summary: Despite a challenging period, private equity firms are looking towards a wave of IPOs in 2024, driven by strong returns from existing public PE companies. Firms like General Atlantic, CVC Capital Partners, Ardian, and L Catterton are reportedly considering going public, seeking capital and significant paydays for their principals. However, this move introduces greater regulatory oversight and transparency requirements, making timing critical.

title: Meta: Sell it? Buy it?
summary: Meta's stock price has experienced significant volatility in recent years, oscillating from a high of $384 in August 2021 to below $100 in October 2022, before rebounding to around $340. This article explores the company's journey from being considered a "sell" to a "buy," focusing on challenges such as Apple's privacy policy changes and competition from TikTok, and how Meta has responded by investing heavily in AI and re-evaluating its metaverse strategy. The future success of Meta is tied to its AI applications across its businesses, especially in advertising and new ventures.

title: 6 Reasons to Avoid JPMorgan (JPM) Immediately
summary: This article outlines six reasons why investors should consider avoiding JPMorgan (JPM) stock immediately. Key concerns include its expensive valuation relative to expected revenue drops, a shrinking dividend yield compared to competitors, potential economic slowdowns in an election year, the eventual departure of CEO Jamie Dimon, Dimon's recent stock sale, and the bank's focus on high-net-worth investors rather than comprehensive individual investor services. The author suggests waiting for the stock to trade lower before buying.

title: US surveillance giant’s network of operations has subsidiaries in India
summary: US surveillance giant Verint Systems has a network of operations including four subsidiaries in India, as revealed by the Cyprus Confidential investigation. One of Verint's spin-off companies, Cognyte, has faced controversy for allegedly selling spyware to "repressive regimes" and was named by Meta as a "cyber mercenary" for indiscriminately targeting journalists and dissidents. The Indian subsidiaries show significant revenue from foreign group companies and have had run-ins with the Income Tax Department.

title: GraniteShares 2x Long META Daily ETF (FBL) Dividend Yield 2026 & History $FBL
summary: The GraniteShares 2x Long META Daily ETF (FBL) offers an annual dividend of $0.67 per share, resulting in a 2.09% dividend yield. The ETF pays dividends monthly, with its most recent monthly payment of $0.6742 per share made on December 31, 2025, following an ex-dividend date of December 29, 2025. This article provides historical dividend data, payment schedules, and compares FBL's dividend performance against market averages.

title: Magazine roundup: Top 100 data centre companies
summary: Data Centre Magazine reviews its Top 100 data centre companies for 2023, highlighting their commitment to advancing technology and sustainability. The article rounds up the top 10 companies, including industry giants like AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform, detailing their founding, CEOs, and key contributions to the data centre sector. It showcases their innovative solutions, global reach, and efforts toward environmental responsibility.

title: Apple's stock underperformed top tech peers in 2023 due to longest revenue slide in 22 years
summary: Apple's stock underperformed its mega-cap tech peers in 2023, experiencing its longest revenue slide in 22 years with four consecutive quarters of declining sales. This decline was attributed to a combination of a weak economic environment for smartphones and PCs, and company-specific issues such as the lack of new iPad models and an Apple Watch sales ban. Despite a 49% stock rally for the year, Apple lagged behind competitors like Nvidia, Meta, Tesla, Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft.

title: DocuSign layoff announcement comes as tech layoffs continue to rack the industry
summary: DocuSign announced a new round of layoffs, affecting 10% of its staff, or approximately 700 employees, primarily in its field organization. This decision follows a 9% staff reduction in September and aims to position the company for profitable growth and free up resources for investments. These layoffs are part of a broader trend of continued job cuts across the tech industry, with other major companies like Google, Meta, and Amazon also announcing reductions.

title: Top-Performing Stocks of 2023
summary: The article details the top-performing stocks of 2023, highlighting Coinbase, Nvidia, DraftKings, Meta Platforms, and Palantir Technologies among others. It also identifies undervalued top performers and top-performing moat stocks and technology stocks, providing Morningstar analyst insights and key metrics for each.

title: Miami doesn’t need to be the Silicon Valley of the South
summary: Miami has been hyped as a "new Silicon Valley" or "Silicon Valley of the South," but this article argues it should be recognized for its unique strengths rather than compared to Silicon Valley. The author highlights Miami's advantages, including favorable tax laws, a supportive tech ecosystem, increasing VC attention, strong foreign investment, a focus on AI, and its role as a bridge to Latin America for nearshoring. Miami's distinct features allow it to stand as its own specialized tech hub.

title: Google and Samsung Set To Use Qualcomm's New VR Chip, Could Compete With Apple and Meta
summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) recently unveiled its new Snapdragon XR2+ Gen 2 Platform chip for virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR). Google (GOOGL) and Samsung are slated to integrate this chip into their upcoming VR/AR experiences, aiming to challenge market leaders like Apple (AAPL) and Meta Platforms (META). This development could intensify competition in the growing VR headset market, especially following Apple's Vision Pro and Meta's dominance in 2023.

title: Pinterest: The frictionless social commerce play for 2024
summary: Pinterest is positioned as a leading social commerce platform for 2024 due to its "frictionless soft sales" approach, attracting 482 million global monthly active users. The company reported strong Q3 2023 results, including a GAAP net income of $7 million and adjusted EBITDA of $185 million, with revenue growth driven significantly by Europe and increasing ARPU in the U.S. and Canada. Analysts are largely bullish on Pinterest, with several firms upgrading their ratings and issuing positive price targets.

title: Fundsmith Underperforms, Smith Takes Aim at AI Hype
summary: Terry Smith's Gold-rated Fundsmith Equity fund underperformed the MSCI World Index for the third consecutive year in 2023, growing by 12.4% against the index's 16.8%. In his annual letter, Smith questioned the market's early coronation of AI winners like Nvidia, drawing parallels to past tech leaders that faded. While the fund sold stakes in Estée Lauder, Adobe, and Amazon, it made new purchases in Procter & Gamble, Marriott, and Fortinet, maintaining its long-term investment strategy.

title: Wells Fargo’s assistant, powered by Google's AI, poised to hit 100 million interactions annually
summary: Wells Fargo's virtual assistant app, Fargo, powered by Google's AI, has handled 20 million interactions since its March launch and is projected to reach 100 million annually. The bank is aggressively deploying generative AI, including applications for back-office efficiency and a new Livesync app for financial planning. Wells Fargo emphasizes a multi-LLM, multi-cloud strategy on its "Tachyon" platform, and views multimodal LLMs and "agentic" AI as future critical developments, while navigating regulatory challenges.

title: Meta to default teen Facebook, Instagram users to most restrictive settings
summary: Meta Platforms announced it will set the default content settings for teenage users on Facebook and Instagram to the most restrictive to enhance their safety. This decision follows a lawsuit by 42 attorneys general alleging harm to teenage users by social media platforms. The update will hide more sensitive content, such as discussions of self-harm and eating disorders, and apply to both new and existing teen users.

title: How Stantec and WSP became Canada’s unlikely stock market stars — and made engineering sexy
summary: Stantec and WSP Global, two Canadian engineering firms, have become unexpected stock market stars with their shares soaring 242% and 197% respectively over five years, outperforming even major U.S. tech companies. Their success is attributed to shifting focus from fixed-price construction contracts to per-hour consulting fees, diversifying through acquisitions, expanding into areas like water infrastructure, and disciplined growth strategies focused on profitability rather than just revenue. Both companies prioritize strategic acquisitions, debt management, and maximizing workforce utilization, making engineering an attractive investment sector.

title: Musk wants 25% voting control at Tesla before fulfilling AI goal
summary: Elon Musk has stated he requires at least 25% voting control at Tesla, nearly double his current stake, before he feels comfortable scaling the company to be a leader in AI and robotics. He indicated if this voting power is not granted, he would prefer to develop AI products outside of Tesla, a stance that governance experts suggest could infringe upon his CEO duties. The billionaire sold billions of dollars worth of Tesla shares in 2022, partly to fund his acquisition of Twitter.

title: Nvidia and AMD shares hit record highs on AI chip surge
summary: AMD and Nvidia shares reached all-time highs on Thursday, driven by sustained investor demand for companies manufacturing AI-powering chips. Nvidia, the leading GPU supplier for AI, was the best-performing S&P 500 stock last year, while AMD is gaining investor confidence with new competitive chips and improved AI software. This surge aligns with strong demand reported by TSMC, their manufacturer, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's plans for large GPU purchases.

title: Mark Zuckerberg indicates Meta is spending billions of dollars on Nvidia AI chips
summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg stated that by the end of 2024, Meta's computing infrastructure will include 350,000 H100 graphics cards from Nvidia, suggesting billions of dollars in expenditure given the chips' high cost. This massive investment is driven by Meta's pursuit of artificial general intelligence (AGI) and expanding AI capabilities. Zuckerberg also mentioned plans to open-source its general intelligence development and streamline research efforts between its FAIR and GenAI teams.

title: AES positioned to provide tech sector with growing renewable energy solutions
summary: AES Corp. is strategically positioned to be a leading provider of renewable energy solutions to the technology sector, especially given the rising power demands from data centers and generative AI. The company focuses on long-term contracted revenues with credit-worthy partners and offers customized solutions to meet the unique sustainability goals of major tech firms like Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta. With significant growth projected in key markets and a strong track record of project execution, AES aims to capitalize on the increasing demand for clean energy in the tech industry.

title: T-Rex 2X Long Tesla Daily Target ETF (TSLT) Options Chain & Prices 2025
summary: This article provides a detailed options chain and pricing information for the T-Rex 2X Long Tesla Daily Target ETF (TSLT) for 2025, specifically focusing on options expiring in 2026, 2027, and 2028. It includes real-time and extended trading data, along with various call and put options, their strike prices, volumes, implied volatilities, and other relevant metrics. The page also lists related ETFs and options chain tools.

title: Oracle debuts cloud generative AI service to help enterprises deploy and fine-tune language models
summary: Oracle has launched its Cloud Infrastructure Generative AI service, enabling enterprises to leverage and fine-tune large language models like Meta's Llama 2 and Cohere's algorithms. This service supports over 100 languages, offers GPU cluster management, and provides flexible fine-tuning options, allowing businesses to integrate generative AI into their existing systems for tasks such as text generation and summarization. While analysts note the service's current limitations in model support compared to competitors, its integration with Oracle's business applications and database portfolio, alongside its cloud and on-premise deployment flexibility, could make it an attractive solution for many enterprises.

title: Online retailer eBay is cutting 1,000 jobs. It’s the latest tech company to reduce its workforce
summary: Online retailer eBay is cutting approximately 1,000 jobs, or 9% of its full-time workforce, citing that its employee count and costs have outpaced its business growth in a slowing economy. This move follows a trend of layoffs across the tech industry, where companies that rapidly expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic are now trimming expenses. CEO Jamie Iannone informed employees that the company will also reduce its alternate workforce contracts and highlighted the need for better organization and nimbleness.

title: Meta chooses new operation location in Southern Indiana
summary: Meta Platforms Inc. announced plans to build an $800 million data center campus in Jeffersonville, Indiana, which will be its 18th in the United States. The nearly 700,000-square-foot facility at River Ridge Commerce Center is expected to create approximately 100 operational jobs and will be powered by 100% renewable energy. Indiana and local authorities have offered performance-based economic incentives, including a 35-year term data center sales tax exemption, to support the project.

title: What Gentex’s Acquisition Of eSight Means For The Electronic Eyewear Market
summary: Gentex Corporation has acquired Toronto-based eSight, a move that could significantly impact the electronic eyewear market for the visually impaired. This acquisition follows a partnership that led to the eSight Go, a new electronic eyewear system that is more affordable, lighter, and offers improved performance compared to its predecessor. Gentex's expertise in electro-optical products and manufacturing capabilities is expected to drive down costs and enhance the technology for sight enhancement wearables.

title: YMAG ETF Analysis: Dividends, Returns AMEX:YMAG
summary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of YMAG ETF, the YieldMax Magnificent 7 Fund of Option Income ETFs. It details its investment strategy, which involves synthetic covered calls on the Magnificent Seven tech stocks to generate monthly income. The analysis covers key statistics, holdings, dividend history, and performance metrics, highlighting its active management and high dividend yield despite a synthetic replication method.

title: Top metaverse investors and how to start investing
summary: This article explores various ways to invest in the metaverse, including indirect investments through company stocks and ETFs, and direct investments in virtual properties and cryptocurrencies. It highlights major metaverse investors across technology platforms, gaming, chip manufacturing, and software, while also cautioning about the significant risks involved in this evolving digital realm.

title: Pinterest CEO: Big Tech must reject Big Tobacco’s model and address social media harms
summary: Pinterest CEO Bill Ready argues that the social media industry must learn from the mistakes of "Big Tobacco" and take responsibility for the harms it causes, particularly to young people. He advocates for using AI to promote positive content, improve youth online safety, and implement special protections for teens, citing Pinterest's efforts to retrain its AI for inspiring content and restrict teen accounts. Ready stresses that a business model focused on positivity is achievable and necessary to avoid social media becoming the next "Big Tobacco."

title: Unified data architectures for AI workflows
summary: In the rapidly evolving landscape of AI and ML, managing and processing various data types is critical for the quality of insights. An optimal storage strategy must account for diverse data types, their locations (on-premises, public clouds), and storage architectures (file, block, object). NetApp's intelligent data infrastructure helps overcome common AI deployment blockers like data movement and management by providing a unified approach that ensures data accessibility, efficiency, and governance across hybrid multi-cloud environments.

title: Zuckerberg Gives Impromptu Apology at Child Safety Senate Hearing
summary: During a tense Senate hearing on child safety, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg offered an unscripted apology to families of children who were victims of sexual exploitation on social media platforms. He expressed sorrow for their suffering, stating that no one should have to endure such experiences. The apology came as social media executives were being grilled by Congress over their platforms' impact on children.

title: Meta earnings after market close, will expectations for 2024 be confirmed? 📌
summary: Meta Platforms (META.US) is set to release its Q4 2023 earnings report, with high investor expectations for both past performance and the 2024 outlook, particularly after outperforming competitors in January. Analysts project strong revenues and EPS for Q4 2023, while investor attention also focuses on Meta's advancements in artificial intelligence and the potential impact of the upcoming US election year on advertising expenditures. The company's stock has seen significant growth, reflecting improved performance throughout 2023, and continued upward momentum is anticipated if expectations are met.

title: What Stock Investors Need to Know About Meta’s New Dividend
summary: Meta Platforms announced its first-ever quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share, alongside its fourth-quarter earnings, leading to a significant stock surge. While the dividend provides a more balanced capital return program, share repurchases will remain the primary method for returning cash to shareholders. The initial dividend yield is modest compared to peers and the broader market index, but Morningstar analysts expect it to grow.

title: Is calling litigation 'without merit' actually without merit?
summary: A recent federal court ruling against Pegasystems Inc. suggests that using phrases like "without merit" to describe legal actions in financial filings can be misleading and backfire. Legal experts and law firms are now advising companies to reconsider using such boilerplate language, as it could expose them to securities fraud claims. Alternative phrasing, such as "We intend to contest this matter vigorously," is recommended to signal active defense without judging legitimacy.

title: Is Meta now a value stock?
summary: Meta Platforms Inc. shares surged after a strong fourth-quarter report and dividend announcement, prompting the question of whether it can be considered a value stock. The article explores Meta's valuation, recent operational improvements, and long-term financial performance to assess if it's the best value among the "Magnificent Seven" stocks. Value stocks are typically mature companies with steady performance, dividends, and low valuations.

title: What investors need to know about Meta’s new dividend
summary: Meta Platforms Inc. has announced its first-ever quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share, which will be paid on March 26 to shareholders of record on February 22. This move is seen as a complement to existing share repurchase programs, which will remain the primary method of returning capital to shareholders. While the market reacted positively, sending Meta's stock up 20%, the initial dividend yield of less than 0.5% is modest compared to its mega-cap peers and the Morningstar Dividend Composite Index.

title: FNDX ETF: Fundamentals Are Attractive, Performance Is Not (NYSEARCA:FNDX)
summary: The Schwab Fundamental U.S. Large Company Index ETF (FNDX) tracks the Russell RAFI US Large Company Index and holds 730 companies, offering attractive valuation metrics and sector diversification. However, since its inception in 2013, FNDX has underperformed its Russell 1000 benchmark and several factor-based ETFs, despite its strong fundamental attributes. The article suggests that while the ETF's holdings show promise, its overall market performance has been lacking.

title: Why US large cap growth’s banner year didn’t look the same across index providers
summary: This article explains why US large-cap growth index performance varied significantly among providers in 2023, despite a banner year for the segment. The key differentiator is methodology, particularly how factors like momentum influence constituent classification, as exemplified by Meta's stock performance. Different index construction rules lead to varying index compositions and thus different returns.

title: Earnings To Watch: Pinterest (PINS) Reports Q4 Results Tomorrow
summary: Pinterest (NYSE: PINS) is set to report its Q4 results tomorrow afternoon, with analysts expecting revenue growth of 12.8% year-on-year to $989.6 million and adjusted earnings of $0.51 per share. The company beat revenue and user expectations last quarter, and analyst sentiment is increasingly bullish for the upcoming report. Competitors like Meta and Snap have already reported Q4 earnings, showing varied results, while Pinterest's stock has performed positively in the lead-up to its own report.

title: Google joins coalition to label AI-generated content
summary: Google has joined the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA), a standard for labeling digital content to indicate its origin and creation methods, alongside Microsoft, Meta, and Adobe. This move is significant given Google's market share with Android and YouTube, aiming to combat misinformation by making AI-generated content more transparent. While the C2PA aims for widespread adoption to make unlabeled content stand out, critics question its tamper-proof nature, suggesting that bad actors could strip or swap metadata, and it may not fully address the issue of malicious misinformation.

title: FuboTV illegally shares viewer data, class action claims
summary: A class action lawsuit alleges that FuboTV illegally shares its users' personally identifiable information and video viewing data with third parties like Facebook and Google without their consent. The lawsuit, filed by Catherine Beasley, claims FuboTV violates the Video Privacy Protection Act by failing to obtain informed written consent before disclosing this sensitive data. Beasley is seeking damages and a jury trial for herself and a nationwide class of affected consumers.

title: Should You Bet on Online Gambling Stocks Now?
summary: This article discusses the online gambling industry, focusing on companies like Flutter (FanDuel) and DraftKings, and the market potential for sports betting. It also covers Morningstar's headlines on Meta's first dividend, Boeing's quality control pause, and Novo Nordisk's strong Q4 sales. Additionally, it provides investing lessons on avoiding market timing, the importance of diversification, and minimizing political bias in investment decisions.

title: Arista Networks Q4 2023 earnings upcoming 📊 Will AI drive it again? 📈
summary: Arista Networks is set to release its Q4 2023 earnings, with investors keenly watching its 2024 outlook and the impact of AI. The company's performance is closely tied to the growth of cloud networking and demand from major clients like Meta Platforms. Analysts anticipate strong revenue growth, but the valuation of Arista's stock remains a key consideration for investors.

title: Steven Cohen's Point72 Asset Management Acquires New Stake in Annexon Inc
summary: Steven Cohen's Point72 Asset Management has acquired a new stake in Annexon Inc (NASDAQ:ANNX), purchasing almost 4.9 million shares, representing 6.20% of the company's outstanding shares. This investment, valued at $4.03 per share, signifies Cohen's confidence in the biotechnology firm's potential, aligning with Point72's focus on technology and healthcare sectors. While Annexon's stock has seen recent gains and has a strong balance sheet, value investors are advised to consider its low GF Score and profitability rank amidst the strategic backing.

title: After Earnings, Is Snap Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar maintains its $14 fair value estimate for Snap Inc (SNAP) despite mixed Q4 2023 results and a post-earnings stock decline. The stock is now considered fairly valued, trading at a discount. Analysts anticipate profitability by 2027 driven by user growth, improved engagement, and cost-cutting measures, though significant competition from Meta Platforms Inc (META) and other large social media platforms presents ongoing risks.

title: Nvidia replaces Alphabet as Wall St's third most valuable company
summary: Nvidia has surpassed Google-parent Alphabet to become the third most valuable U.S. company, with a market capitalization of $1.825 trillion. This milestone follows its recent overtaking of Amazon, driven by strong investor interest in the dominant AI chipmaker ahead of its upcoming quarterly report. Nvidia's stock has surged due to its control of about 80% of the high-end AI chip market and strong demand for its products.

title: Meta settles lawsuit over haptic feedback tech in Quest headsets
summary: Immersion, a company specializing in haptic feedback technology, has settled a lawsuit with Meta over Meta's use of touch-feedback in its Quest VR headsets. The settlement involves Meta licensing Immersion's patents for its hardware, software, VR, and gaming products, though the terms were not disclosed. Immersion has a history of pursuing patent infringement lawsuits against major tech companies like Microsoft, Sony, Apple, and Valve.

title: Applied Digital Joins AI Alliance to Collaborate with Industry Leaders to Advance Open, Safe, and Responsible AI
summary: Applied Digital (Nasdaq: APLD) has announced its membership in the AI Alliance, a collaboration of leading organizations dedicated to advancing open, safe, and responsible AI. The company, known for its next-generation digital infrastructure for High-Performance Computing and AI, aims to contribute its expertise in speed to market and digital infrastructure. Wes Cummins, CEO of Applied Digital, highlighted the importance of open innovation and ethical AI development, aligning with the alliance's mission to foster collaboration among diverse entities.

title: February 2024 The AI race makes first meaningful impact on the suppliers of optics
summary: The AI race significantly impacted optics suppliers in Q4 2023, with Coherent and Innolight reporting substantial revenue growth driven by Nvidia's demand for 800G transceivers. While Nvidia initially handles much of the optics in-house, it allocates larger volumes to these suppliers later. Major tech companies show mixed spending on infrastructure, although overall market momentum is positive with AI leading the recovery.

title: Immersion Signs License Agreement with Meta Platforms, Inc. (formerly known as Facebook, Inc.)
summary: Immersion Corporation announced it has signed a license agreement with Meta Platforms, Inc., allowing Meta to use Immersion's patents for haptic technologies in its hardware, software, VR, and gaming products. This agreement will enable Meta to deliver high-quality haptics, enhancing immersive experiences in VR gaming applications. Immersion is a leading innovator in touch feedback technology, providing solutions for various industries.

title: Tinder, other Match dating apps encourage compulsive use, lawsuit claims
summary: Match Group is facing a proposed class action lawsuit claiming its dating apps, including Tinder, Hinge, and The League, are intentionally designed to be addictive rather than help users form relationships. The plaintiffs allege a "predatory" business model that gamifies the platforms, encouraging compulsive use and prompting users to pay for subscriptions, contradicting Match's "designed to be deleted" slogan. Match Group has dismissed the lawsuit as "ridiculous" and without merit, asserting their goal is to get people on dates and off their apps.

title: Meta Licenses New Haptic Technology
summary: Meta has signed a significant licensing deal with Immersion Corporation to integrate Immersion's haptic patents into Meta's XR hardware, software, and products. This agreement could revitalize the haptic technology market, especially for VR/AR/MR applications, despite a recent lull in haptic hardware development, potentially driven by Meta's newfound quarterly profit from Reality Labs. The article also discusses advancements in haptic glove technology, such as Fluid Reality's untethered solution, and poses questions about haptics' future role in the evolving XR landscape.

title: Andreas Halvorsen's Viking Global Investors LP Bolsters Position in Verastem Inc
summary: Andreas Halvorsen's Viking Global Investors LP increased its stake in Verastem Inc (VSTM) by acquiring 75,537 shares on December 31, 2023, at $8.14 per share, bringing their total holding to 2,531,829 shares. This strategic move, which represents 9.99% ownership of Verastem, aligns with Viking Global's focus on the healthcare sector and its long-term investment philosophy in biopharmaceuticals. Despite Verastem's current stock price of $11.76 showing a significant gain since the transaction, the company faces challenges with its profitability and growth metrics, although its financial strength is more promising.

title: Chase Coleman's Tiger Global Management Reduces Stake in ATRenew Inc
summary: Chase Coleman's Tiger Global Management has reduced its stake in ATRenew Inc (RERE) by selling over 3.8 million shares, representing a 33.33% decrease in its holdings. summary: Meta Platforms has agreed to pay $1.4 billion to Texas to settle a lawsuit alleging illegal use of facial-recognition technology to collect biometric data without consent. The settlement, which Meta reached after denying wrongdoing, marks the largest accord ever by a single state and resolves a case filed under Texas' 2009 biometric privacy law. The company previously paid $650 million to settle a similar class-action lawsuit in Illinois.

summary: Patreon Inc. has agreed to pay $7.25 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging that it unlawfully shared subscribers' video viewing information and personal data with Meta Platforms Inc. without consent. summary: Digital media firm Ziff Davis (NASDAQ: ZD) is acquiring CNET from Red Ventures for over $100M, further expanding its portfolio of technology-focused online news brands. summary: Chinese ecommerce giants Temu and Shein are rapidly gaining market share in the U.S., challenging Amazon's dominance through aggressive advertising, optimized sales tactics, and innovative customer engagement strategies. They achieve this by making shopping fun with gamified elements, personalized catalogs, and influencer partnerships, despite high customer acquisition costs. title: ‘Scarcity and growth are oppositional’: How streetwear legend Supreme lost its luster
summary: Streetwear brand Supreme has seen a significant decline in its cultural cachet and financial performance, leading to its sale at a loss by VF Corp to EssilorLuxottica for $1.5 billion. Analysts attribute this decline to an attempt at aggressive expansion and growth by VF Corp, which contradicted Supreme's core value of scarcity and exclusivity. title: Amplitude Snares Private Data of Millions Via Apps, Suit Says
summary: A proposed class action lawsuit alleges that Amplitude Inc.'s technology, embedded in popular mobile apps like DoorDash, surreptitiously collects and shares millions of consumers' geolocation data and other sensitive information with third parties without consent. The complaint, filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California, states that this collected data, including names and email addresses, reveals users' locations. This practice raises significant privacy concerns about unsolicited data harvesting and sharing by analytics firms.

title: Daniel Peris: The Case for Dividend Investing
summary: Daniel Peris, a portfolio manager at Federated Hermes and author of "The Ownership Dividend," discusses the historical importance of dividends and argues for a paradigm shift back to dividend investing. He criticizes modern portfolio theory's overemphasis on share price appreciation and extreme diversification, advocating for a business-owner's perspective grounded in tangible cash flows. Peris attributes the past decline in dividends to falling interest rates, the rise of buybacks, Silicon Valley's growth, and global sociopolitical shifts, and believes a return to more normal interest rates will renew focus on cash payouts.

title: Infillion Named to Inc. 5000 List for 8th Consecutive Year
summary: Infillion, an advanced media buying platform, has been named to the 2024 Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies in America for the eighth consecutive year. The company's consistent growth is attributed to its ability to adapt to changing advertising landscapes and its recent acquisition of MediaMath, expanding its multiplatform digital advertising solutions. Infillion's founder and executive chair, Rob Emrich, and CFO, Angela Birkemeier, highlighted the team's dedication and rapid innovation.

title: Elliott Management Announces Director Candidates for the Board of Southwest Airlines
summary: Elliott Investment Management L.P. announced its intention to nominate ten independent, highly qualified candidates to the Board of Southwest Airlines, Inc. title: Big XR News from Meta, Vuzix, Pico, Apple

title: A Record 8.5% of U.S. Homes Are Worth $1 Million or More
summary: A record 8.5% of U.S. homes, totaling over 8 million, are now valued at $1 million or more, an increase from 7.6% a year ago and more than double the pre-pandemic share of 4%. This surge is driven by historically low housing inventory and rising home prices, even amidst high mortgage rates that dampen demand. While this benefits homeowners, it presents significant affordability challenges for prospective buyers, especially in high-cost areas like California metros.

title: AMD to acquire server builder ZT Systems for $4.9 billion in cash and stock
summary: AMD announced its plan to acquire server maker ZT Systems for $4.9 billion in cash and stock to expand its AI chip and hardware portfolio and bolster its competition with Nvidia. The acquisition aims to integrate ZT Systems' engineering expertise to accelerate the testing and deployment of AMD's AI GPUs for cloud computing giants, with AMD planning to divest ZT Systems' manufacturing business post-acquisition. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2025 and contribute to AMD's adjusted financial performance by the end of 2025.

title: AMD to acquire ZT Systems for $4.9B
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is set to acquire server manufacturer ZT Systems for $4.9 billion in a cash and stock transaction. This move is part of AMD's strategy to expand its AI capabilities and compete more effectively with Nvidia, leveraging ZT Systems' expertise in cloud computing design services and data center infrastructure. title: Going into earnings, is Nvidia stock a buy, a sell, or fairly valued?
summary: Morningstar assesses Nvidia (NVDA) stock ahead of its Q2 earnings report, assigning it a 3-star rating, indicating it is fairly valued at a $105 fair value estimate. title: Will Alphabet (GOOG) AI Phones Crush Apple’s AI Plans?
summary: This article examines whether Alphabet's new AI-powered Pixel phones will challenge Apple's AI ambitions, highlighting the stabilization and potential rebound of AI stocks. The piece focuses on Alphabet (GOOG), its Gemini Nano AI assistant, despite market pressures like a potential Justice Department breakup and competition from OpenAI.

title: Immersion Stock Surges as It Monetizes Haptic Technology Patents
summary: Immersion Corp. (NASDAQ: IMMR), a pioneer in haptic technology, saw its stock surge after it settled a patent lawsuit with Meta Platforms Inc. for $87.5 million and secured a licensing agreement. The company specializes in licensing its extensive patent portfolio for haptic feedback used in billions of devices and has also made a significant investment in Barnes and Noble Education Inc. Immersion continues to evolve its active sensing technology and monetize its intellectual property.

title: Classroom quitters to industry leaders: These 14 billionaires dropped out of school to chase success
summary: This article highlights 14 billionaires who dropped out of formal education to pursue their entrepreneurial dreams and achieve significant success. It spotlights individuals like Ralph Lauren, Oprah Winfrey, Bill Gates, and Mark Zuckerberg, detailing their early career decisions and current net worth according to Forbes. The piece illustrates that success is not always linear and can be achieved through ambition and unconventional paths.

title: A Dot-Com-Like Bust Isn’t in the Cards for AI Investors Who Diversify
summary: Concerns about an AI bubble akin to the dot-com bust are overblown, according to J.P. Morgan Private Bank, citing lower valuations and stronger earnings expectations for current AI leaders. While investing in an S&P 500 index fund provides some AI exposure, investors seeking outperformance should diversify across AI infrastructure (AI 1.0) and AI applications (AI 2.0), potentially including global companies and low-cost ETFs for broader exposure. A long-term perspective is crucial as AI is expected to be a multi-year or multi-decade trend.

title: The best AI fund of 2024? The S&P 500.
summary: Despite the explosive growth of AI-related companies like Nvidia and SMCI, AI-themed ETFs have largely underperformed the S&P 500. title: Global data center industry to emit 2.5 billion tons of CO2 through 2030, Morgan Stanley says
summary: The global data center industry is projected to emit approximately 2.5 billion metric tons of CO2-equivalent emissions by 2030, according to Morgan Stanley research. This surge is driven by hyperscalers like Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon expanding AI and cloud computing. The emissions are expected to accelerate investments in decarbonization solutions, clean power, and green building materials, as tech companies strive to meet climate pledges.

title: Gaia & International Yoga members may be eligible for a Share of a $2 million settlement
summary: Gaia, Inc. has agreed to a $2 million class action settlement for allegedly violating the Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA) by sharing personally identifiable information with Facebook via a tracking pixel. Users who watched videos on Gaia or Yoga International websites between September 12, 2020, and July 19, 2024, and had a Facebook account during that period, may be eligible to claim a pro rata share of the settlement fund. Claims must be submitted by December 2, 2024.

title: Nvidia Stock Is Down 15% Since Earnings. Is It a Buy?
summary: Nvidia's stock has dropped 15% since its Q2 earnings report, despite strong results and an optimistic forecast for AI investments and data center revenue. Morningstar maintains a "fairly valued" rating with a $105 fair value estimate, citing Nvidia's wide economic moat due to its GPU technology and CUDA software, and robust financial health. The primary risks include increasing competition in the AI chip market and potential diversification efforts by tech giants.

title: New Mexico accuses Snapchat of being ‘breeding ground’ for child predators
summary: New Mexico has filed a lawsuit against Snap Inc., accusing Snapchat of facilitating child sexual exploitation and becoming a "breeding ground" for predators due to its ephemeral messaging features. The state's attorney general, Raúl Torrez, stated that an undercover investigation found a "vast network" of dark websites sharing nonconsensual images from Snapchat. Snap Inc. is reviewing the complaint and maintains its commitment to making Snapchat a safe platform for young users, highlighting ongoing efforts to combat bad actors and enhance online safety tools.

title: IXP ETF: Growth Profile Not Attractive
summary: The iShares Global Comm Services ETF (IXP) carries significant concentration risk, with Meta Platforms and Alphabet constituting 42.6% of its portfolio, making its performance highly dependent on these companies' results. summary: IBM has leased the entire 320,000-square-foot office space at Domain 12 in North Austin, previously vacated by Meta Platforms. Meanwhile, Meta continues to downsize its Austin footprint as part of broader cost-cutting measures, highlighting contrasting real estate strategies between the two tech giants.

summary: Support for environmental and social resolutions in the 2024 proxy season continued to decline, while governance proposals saw a rebound. title: Big tech firms balk at Ohio electric utility demand to pay for grid upgrades
summary: Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta are resisting demands from an Ohio utility, American Electric Power Ohio, to pay for electric grid upgrades needed to support their energy-intensive AI data centers. The utility argues these payments are necessary to prevent costs from being passed on to consumers, while the tech firms deem the proposed tariff "unfair" and "discriminatory." A hearing is scheduled for October 30 to address the dispute, which highlights the increasing energy demands of AI technology and the associated infrastructure costs.

title: BuzzFeed $9 Million Facebook Settlement: Can You Claim?
summary: BuzzFeed is facing a class-action lawsuit for allegedly sharing user data with Facebook without consent, leading to a proposed $9 million settlement. Users who watched videos on BuzzFeed, HuffPost, Tasty, or Complex websites between May 16, 2021, and November 10, 2023, and were account holders or newsletter subscribers, may be eligible to claim an $8 payment and a free one-year BuzzFeed+ subscription. The deadline to file a claim is November 5th.

title: The Scoop: Philip Morris International sells inhaler company after backlash
summary: Philip Morris International (PMI) is selling Vectura, a British pharmaceutical inhaler company it acquired three years ago, due to significant backlash and "unreasonable burden of external constraints and criticism." summary: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo from TF International Securities predicts that Meta's AR glasses, Orion, could enter mass production as early as 2027, aiming to replace smartphones and tablets. This strategy provides redundancy and flexibility, enabling Intuit to leverage a unified data and AI platform to solve customer problems and future-proof its AI capabilities as the landscape evolves. title: Arkansas AG's lawsuit accuses YouTube and Google of targeting minors with harmful content
summary: Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin has filed a consumer protection lawsuit against Google, YouTube, and their parent companies, alleging they intentionally target minors with addictive and harmful content. The lawsuit, filed in Phillips County Circuit Court, claims YouTube exploits the "undeveloped capacity for self-regulation" in children's brains, leading to mental health issues and addiction. Griffin is seeking monetary damages, disgorgement of profits, and funding for prevention education and treatment for excessive social media use.

Meta is being asked for unspecified monetary damages and an order to halt alleged infringement, arguing that its AI training is protected by fair use.

summary: A former Giphy Inc. engineer, Yael Elmatad, has filed a lawsuit against Shutterstock Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc., alleging she was underpaid by over $2 million compared to her male colleagues in similar engineering roles. The lawsuit asserts that Elmatad discovered the pay disparity earlier this year through a spreadsheet revealing discrepancies in restricted stock unit award agreements. The complaint was filed in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York.

title: Oracle's Larry Ellison is getting richer, rivaling Musk, Bezos, Zuckerberg
summary: Oracle co-founder and CTO Larry Ellison's net worth has surged to an estimated $208 billion, placing him firmly among the wealthiest individuals globally, behind Elon Musk and ahead of Mark Zuckerberg and Jeff Bezos, according to Forbes. His wealth growth is largely attributed to his substantial 41% stake in Oracle, whose stock has seen a 63% increase year-to-date. Oracle's strong financial performance, with reported revenues of $13.3 billion and net income of $2.9 billion in Q1, contributes significantly to this rise, with forecasts suggesting Oracle could reach a $1 trillion market capitalization by 2030.

summary: Ubisoft is facing a class action lawsuit alleging that it unlawfully collected and shared customer data with Meta Platforms using Meta's Pixel tool without explicit consent. title: Instagram and TikTok Remain the Most Popular Social Apps Among Teens

It discusses how brands like Maybelline, BMW, and Pandora are leveraging virtual personas for campaigns, and how the entertainment sector is seeing success with virtual performers. The author emphasizes the importance of ethical practices and transparency as the line between real and virtual content blurs, urging brands to carefully consider the limitations, purpose, and value-add of these technologies.

title: Which AI Stocks Are Leading the Market to New Highs?
summary: After a sharp selloff, AI-related stocks, including Nvidia, Apple, and Amazon, are once again driving the market to new highs, contributing significantly to recent gains. While the Morningstar Global Next Generation Artificial Intelligence Index is up 30.94% this year, it's also trading at a premium, raising questions about future growth and prompting Morningstar strategists to suggest opportunities might lie in undervalued small-cap and value stocks. This current tech-led recovery mirrors earlier market trends since October 2022, with technology and financial services sectors consistently leading the way.

title: Sui Launches ‘Incubator’ Hub in Dubai for ‘On the Spot’ Solution Engineering
summary: The Layer 1 blockchain Sui has launched an "incubator" hub in Dubai, positioning it as the first in a global series. This hub aims to support blockchain developers and entrepreneurs, with a vision to facilitate "on-the-spot" solution engineering, particularly for government entities requiring rapid blockchain-based proofs of concept. The initiative is a collaboration with Ghaf Group and looks to capitalize on Dubai's clear regulatory environment for Web3 technologies.

title: MAGS: An Efficient Way To Invest In The Magnificent Seven (NASDAQ:MAGS)
summary: The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) offers a diversified, quarterly rebalanced investment strategy focused on the Magnificent Seven tech giants, which are expected to lead market growth. Despite some bubble concerns, MAGS has shown strong performance, appreciating 45.01% in 2024, with reasonable valuations and expected earnings growth of 47.17% over two years. While MAGS carries risks like concentration and derivative-related imbalances, it presents a compelling investment opportunity in a favorable economic environment.

title: Paltalk, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:PALT) 28% Dip Still Leaving Some Shareholders Feeling Restless Over Its P/SRatio
summary: Paltalk, Inc. (PALT) shares have dropped 28% in the last month, yet its Price-to-Sales (P/S) ratio of 1.9x still stands above the industry average of 1.2x, causing concern among shareholders. The company's revenue is declining, and analysts predict further decreases, making its current high P/S ratio questionable. Despite warnings from analysts about future revenue declines, many investors appear to be holding onto their stock, potentially risking significant investment.

title: OpenAI launched a new browser to challenge Google's market position, causing Alphabet's stock price to fall.
summary: OpenAI launched its new AI-powered browser, ChatGPT Atlas, directly challenging Google's Chrome and causing a fluctuation in Alphabet's stock price. The new browser features an intelligent assistant and agent mode, prompting speculation about its potential impact on Chrome's market share. This launch comes amidst an increasingly competitive AI browser landscape and a recent antitrust ruling against Google, further intensifying competition among tech giants.

title: Internet Ad Spending Could Be Key for These ETFs
summary: The article discusses how internet ad spending, particularly from Meta Platforms (META) and Alphabet (GOOG), could be a key factor for ETFs like Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM) during upcoming earnings reports. Analyst commentary suggests Meta continues to gain market share in advertising, while Alphabet's YouTube and Google Search could also see strong growth driven by AI enhancements. The performance of these tech giants' advertising revenues will offer insights into broader market trends.

title: Instagram poised to crack Korean webcomics market
summary: Instagram is rapidly gaining traction in the South Korean webcomics market, with its usage among Korean users rising significantly, surpassing Kakao Webtoon to become the fourth most-used digital comics platform. This rise is attributed to Instagram's lower barriers for creators and users, as well as its support programs for webcomics. The increased presence of global big tech companies like Instagram and Google in the Korean webcomics market is putting pressure on local platforms, prompting Kakao Entertainment to incorporate AI to enhance its competitiveness.

title: Pinterest faces EU privacy complaint over tracking ads
summary: Pinterest is facing a privacy complaint in the EU from the nonprofit noyb, which alleges the visual discovery engine is breaching GDPR by tracking users for advertising without consent. The complaint, filed with France’s data protection authority, also accuses Pinterest of failing to provide adequate information in response to a data access request. Pinterest rejects the accusations, stating its approach to personalized advertising is GDPR compliant.

title: DUET Acquisition Corp. faces Nasdaq delisting over holder rule
summary: DUET Acquisition Corp., a SPAC, is appealing a Nasdaq delisting decision due to non-compliance with the Minimum Public Holders Rule. The company, which is based in Miami, Florida, has yet to file a registration statement for its proposed business combination with Fenix 360 Pte. Ltd., casting doubt on its ability to meet compliance requirements by January 19, 2025. Despite the delisting threat, DUET's stock trades near its 52-week high, although InvestingPro identifies a high P/E ratio as a potential concern.

title: Twitter Names Marjorie Scardino to Board
summary: Twitter has appointed Marjorie Scardino, former CEO of Pearson PLC, to its board of directors, addressing previous criticism regarding the absence of women on its all-male board. Scardino, 66, was the first woman to lead a FTSE 100 company and joins the board alongside CEO Dick Costolo and co-founder Jack Dorsey. Her appointment comes after Twitter faced scrutiny, similar to Facebook, for its lack of board diversity.

title: Zumba Fitness Shared Users’ Data With Meta, Pinterest, Suit Says
summary: A proposed class-action lawsuit alleges that Zumba Fitness LLC unlawfully shared users' personal information and viewing history with Meta Platforms Inc. and Pinterest Inc. without consent. The suit claims Zumba's website used Meta Pixel software to track activity and disclose data, including names and email addresses, violating a federal video privacy law. The complaint was filed in the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida.

title: Is Deckers Stock a Buy After Its Beat-And-Raise Quarter?
summary: Deckers Outdoor (DECK) stock rose after reporting strong fiscal second-quarter earnings, beating expectations and raising its full-year profit forecast, driven by significant growth in its Hoka brand. Wall Street analysts maintain a "Buy" rating for DECK, anticipating further upside based on continued product innovation and market segmentation. The company's robust performance year-to-date and positive outlook for the holiday season suggest ongoing growth potential.

title: While other people build all the LLMs, we will make sure it works for people: Nandan Nilekani
summary: Nandan Nilekani, co-founder of Infosys, believes India should focus on becoming the "use case capital for AI" rather than building large language models (LLMs). He highlights how digital public infrastructure (DPI) can provide a foundation for AI to grow rapidly and address issues like inclusion and education, leveraging existing AI tools to solve real-world problems for a billion people in a frugal manner. Nilekani advocates for a balanced approach to responsible AI and innovation.

title: How Nvidia Overtook Apple as World's Most Valuable Company
summary: Nvidia briefly surpassed Apple to become the world's most valuable company, driven by the immense demand for its specialized AI chips crucial for advanced AI applications. This shift highlights the growing importance of AI-driven technologies in the tech market, with Nvidia benefiting significantly from the race among tech giants to dominate AI. While Apple later regained its lead, Nvidia's surge underscores the impact of AI on market valuations and investment trends.

title: Generative AI agent startup Sierra Technologies raises $175M at $4.5B valuation
summary: Sierra Technologies, an AI startup co-founded by ex-Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, has secured $175 million in funding, pushing its valuation to $4.5 billion. The company develops AI-powered virtual assistants for customer service, featuring personalized conversational models capable of utilizing business data to resolve customer issues and reduce human agent intervention. Sierra differentiates itself through customizable AI agent personalities and a "constellation" approach to large language models for enhanced reliability.

title: COPT plans 1GW data center campus outside Des Moines, Iowa
summary: COPT Defense Properties is planning a 1GW data center campus near Des Moines, Iowa, after acquiring a 365-acre land parcel for $32 million. The campus is projected to include 15 buildings totaling 3.3 million square feet and will serve an existing Fortune 100 cloud computing tenant. This expansion leverages Des Moines' attractive land values, power availability, renewable energy access, and tax incentives.

title: Is the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) Ready to Perform?
summary: The ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), led by Cathie Wood, has shown sideways movement in 2024 but is now gaining attention after clearing its April 2024 highs. Despite past underperformance, recent outperformance against the S&P 500, improved momentum, and a pending golden cross suggest a potential turning point. While the fund's top holdings in e-commerce, robotics, metaverse, and online gambling show promise, their individual performance needs to solidify for ARKK to confirm a sustained upward trend.

title: Meta Reports Third Quarter 2024 Results
summary: Meta Platforms, Inc. reported strong Q3 2024 financial results, with total revenue reaching $40.59 billion, marking a 19% increase year-over-year. The company's net income rose to $15.69 billion, a 35% increase, driven by progress in AI across its applications and business. Meta also provided optimistic financial guidance for Q4 2024, projecting revenue between $45-48 billion, while expecting continued significant investments in Reality Labs and infrastructure.

title: Meta Earnings: Strong Q3 and Promising AI Developments | Morningstar UK
summary: Meta reported strong third-quarter results with revenue up 19% year over year and improved profitability, driven by its advertising engine and significant AI investments. The company's AI-powered ad opportunities are enhancing user engagement and monetization, while progress in Threads and Reality Labs, particularly with Ray-Ban AR glasses, also contributed to growth. Despite elevated capital expenditures for AI, Morningstar maintains a $560 fair value estimate, considering Meta's shares fairly valued.

title: Microsoft names Jay Parikh as a member of the senior leadership team
summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced that Jay Parikh is joining Microsoft's senior leadership team, reporting directly to Nadella. Parikh previously served as global head of engineering at Facebook (now Meta) and CEO of Lacework, bringing extensive experience in scaling technical teams and driving innovation. His role will focus on enhancing Microsoft's capabilities in security, quality, and AI innovation.

title: BlackRock launches ETF that expands beyond the ‘Magnificent Seven'
summary: BlackRock's iShares has launched the iShares Top 20 U.S. Stocks ETF (TOPT) to offer investors diversification beyond the "Magnificent Seven" tech giants. This new ETF comprises the 20 largest U.S. stocks by market capitalization, aiming to provide a broader and more diversified investment in leading U.S. companies. The move comes as some investors worry about the concentration of the Magnificent Seven in the S&P 500 and their high valuations.

title: Tech layoffs tracker 2024: Dropbox, Meta, Tidal cut jobs in October
summary: In October 2024, significant tech companies like Dropbox, Meta, and Tidal continued to announce job cuts, affecting thousands of employees. While these layoffs are devastating, overall numbers for tech layoffs in 2024 are down compared to 2023, with 142,532 employees laid off from 484 companies this year versus 264,220 from 1,193 companies last year. Dropbox, for instance, cut 20% of its workforce, citing softening demand and an overly complex organizational structure.

title: Bay Area tech layoffs hit Upwork, Coursera, Kraken and other companies
summary: Several major Bay Area tech companies, including Coursera, Kraken, dYdX Trading, Miro, and Upwork, announced significant layoffs in October, impacting hundreds of employees. Reasons for the workforce reductions vary from aligning costs with business goals and declining revenue projections to strategic shifts and decreased demand for services that boomed during the pandemic. These companies are aiming for greater efficiency, profitability, and renewed focus as they navigate changing economic landscapes.

title: Analysts Offer Insights on Communication Services Companies: IAC/InteractiveCorp. (IAC) and Meta Platforms (META)
summary: Analysts from TD Cowen and Goldman Sachs have issued bullish sentiments on IAC/InteractiveCorp. and Meta Platforms, respectively, within the Communication Services sector. John Blackledge of TD Cowen maintained a Buy rating on IAC with a $60 price target, while Eric Sheridan of Goldman Sachs reiterated a Buy rating on Meta Platforms with an $815 price target. Both companies also received positive consensus ratings and price targets from other analysts, indicating potential upside from current levels.

title: After Earnings, Is Meta Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar maintains its fair value estimate of $560 for Meta Platforms after strong third-quarter earnings, viewing the stock as fairly valued despite heavy AI investments. The company's core advertising business continues to perform robustly, driven by increased ad impressions and prices, alongside growing user engagement from AI tools. While acknowledging uncertainty from investments in generative AI and Reality Labs, Morningstar highlights Meta's wide economic moat, strong financial health, and long-term monetization opportunities in Asia.

title: United States Supreme Court to Hear Two Securities Cases This Term
summary: The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear two securities cases, Facebook, Inc. v. Amalgamated Bank and NVIDIA Corp. v. E. Ohman J:or Fonder AB and Stichting Pensioenfonds PGB, both concerning the pleading standard in securities fraud class actions. These cases will clarify whether companies must disclose past instances of risk materialization and further define the heightened pleading standards for scienter and falsity under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. The outcomes could significantly impact future securities fraud litigation and the role of expert opinions in such cases.

title: Arista Earnings: Impressive Performance Continues
summary: Morningstar has raised its fair value estimate for Arista Networks (ANET) to $300 per share, up from $270, due to exceptional growth in AI networking environments. Arista surpassed Q3 expectations and raised full-year guidance, with anticipated strong performance into 2025 fueled by high capital investment in AI from major customers like Microsoft and Meta Platforms. Despite robust results, the stock experienced a post-earnings dip, which Morningstar attributes to overly high expectations already priced into the AI market.

title: Lumen’s CEO delivers the bad news first, then the good news
summary: Lumen's CEO Kate Johnson outlined the company's challenging legacy telecom business but presented a positive pivot towards AI-driven growth. The company reported an additional $3 billion in Private Connectivity Fabric (PCF) sales, aiming to be the backbone for the AI economy and cloudify telco networks. Lumen plans to cut costs by $1 billion by 2027 by unifying its network architectures, while betting on AI and its NaaS platform for future revenue generation.

title: Exploring high growth characteristics of META PLATFORMS INC-CLASS A (NASDAQ:META).
summary: This article identifies META Platforms Inc-Class A (NASDAQ:META) as a potential breakout candidate due to its high technical and setup ratings from ChartMill. It highlights META's strong performance, positive financial metrics like increased quarterly earnings, revenue growth, and robust operating margins, alongside a conservative debt-to-equity ratio and consistent EPS beats. The analysis suggests strong prospects for further price appreciation based on both technical and fundamental indicators.

title: Apple’s Next Device Is an AI Wall Tablet for Home Control, Siri and Video Calls
summary: Apple is preparing to launch a new wall-mounted AI tablet, code-named J490, designed to be a smart home command center. The device will control appliances, handle video calls, and leverage the new Apple Intelligence AI platform, positioning Apple to compete with rivals like Amazon and Google in the smart home market. A more advanced, robotic version with an AI personality is also in development, potentially priced up to $1,000.

title: APUE: This Sophisticated ETF Still Has To Prove Itself (APUE)
summary: The ActivePassive U.S. Equity ETF (APUE) combines active and passive management strategies, showing fundamental metrics slightly superior to its benchmark but nearly identical performance. With a short track record since its launch in May 2023, the ETF's strategy remains unproven, appearing average when compared to lower-fee competitors.

title: PHARMACIES, PIXELS, AND PRIVACY: Costco’s Prescription for Legal Trouble
summary: A federal court has largely allowed a lawsuit against Costco to proceed, challenging its use of Meta's tracking pixel on its pharmacy website. The lawsuit alleges that Costco illegally collected and shared sensitive prescription-related data, potentially violating federal and California privacy laws. The court's decision emphasizes that prescription searches are considered protected content, raising significant liability concerns for healthcare providers using similar tracking tools.

title: EU fines Meta 797 mln euros over abusive practices benefiting Facebook Marketplace
summary: The European Commission has fined Meta Platforms €797.72 million ($840.24 million) for breaching EU antitrust rules. The fine relates to abusive practices that benefited Facebook Marketplace, specifically tying its online classified ads service to Facebook and imposing unfair trading conditions on other providers. Meta has stated it will appeal the decision but will comply in the interim to launch a solution.

title: AEP, Hyperscalers, Data Center Coalition Mull Energy Tariff Plan for Ohio Cloud Cluster
summary: American Electric Power of Ohio (AEP) entered into a negotiation with hyperscalers and the Data Center Coalition regarding a new energy tariff plan for data centers in Ohio. This follows AEP's initial proposal to the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (PUCO) for a new rate structure that would require data centers to pay for 90% of planned power usage, which was met with industry opposition. A joint stipulation and subsequent settlement agreement, involving various stakeholders, proposes an 85% commitment for new 25 MW+ data centers, along with other provisions to balance economic growth and reliable energy supply in Central Ohio.

title: UBS: Raymond James Financial (RJF) Is A Bottom-Ranked Quant Stock
summary: UBS has identified Raymond James Financial (RJF) as a bottom-ranked quant stock in a report evaluating various sectors including AI, IT, and healthcare. While the banking sector faces market shifts and changes in investment activity, the article highlights the performance of other major tech companies in the AI space and broader market trends. UBS maintains an optimistic outlook on the US stock market, anticipating continued growth in AI investments and positive impacts from potential Fed rate cuts.

title: Coca-Cola Co: Alignment of Stated Corporate Values with Political and Electioneering Expenditures
summary: A letter signed by investors with $63 billion in assets raised concerns with Coca-Cola's sponsorship of a conference featuring Chris Rufo, arguing it contradicts the company's stated values on diversity and inclusion. Shareholders request that the Coca-Cola Board of Directors publish a report analyzing the negative impacts of associating its brand with politically divisive events and outline policies to avoid such risks in the future.

title: Costco Membership Fees Are What Makes It Profitable
summary: Costco's membership fees, while only 2% of annual revenue, are crucial to its profitability because they contribute 66% of the retailer's bottom line due to their presumed zero cost. The company recently raised its membership fees for the first time in seven years, impacting 52 million members. This move significantly boosts Costco's net income, which rose 17% to $7.37 billion in the last fiscal year.

title: Qurate’s new strategy banks on streaming, social media platforms
summary: Qurate Retail Group, parent company of QVC and HSN, is rebranding to QVC Group and shifting its focus to live social shopping across streaming and social media platforms. The company aims to generate $1.5 billion in revenue from these new channels within three years, despite recent struggles with falling sales and Nasdaq compliance issues. This strategic pivot includes leadership changes and a push to tailor content for platforms like TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, Netflix, and Hulu.

title: Meta, Netflix Get Hit With Lawsuit Over Streaming Video Market
summary: Meta Platforms Inc. and Netflix Inc. are facing a proposed class action lawsuit. Two Netflix subscribers allege the companies engaged in an anticompetitive agreement, where Meta refrained from directly competing in the streaming-video market in exchange for Netflix's subscriber data. This alleged agreement is claimed to have caused consumers to pay inflated prices for streaming services.

title: FBY: One Of My Favorite Santa's Income Plays
summary: The author sees an opportunity to invest in big tech, particularly META, after a recent market sell-off, citing strong leadership and innovation. FBY, a YieldMax ETF for META, is highlighted as a favorable pick for high dividends and potential capital gains, especially in anticipation of a "Santa rally."
