summary: Colgate-Palmolive announced it would review the name of its "Darlie" toothpaste, a popular brand in Asia, which translates to "Black people toothpaste." This decision follows renewed criticism over racial inequality and stereotyping, and comes after similar moves by other American brands to reassess offensive branding. The product, co-owned with Hawley & Hazel, had previously changed its name and logo from "Darkie" and a minstrel singer in blackface in 1989 due to public backlash.

title: Johnson & Johnson drops skin-whitening creams
summary: Johnson & Johnson announced it would stop selling skin-whitening creams in Asia and the Middle East, citing renewed social pressure amidst global discussions on racial inequality. The company stated that product names suggesting "fair" or "white" as better contradict their view that "healthy skin is beautiful skin." This decision affects product lines like Clean & Clear Fairness and Neutrogena Fine Fairness, though existing stock may still be available on shelves.

title: Unilever, Johnson & Johnson will pull or rebrand skin-lightening creams in India
summary: Unilever, Johnson & Johnson, and L'Oreal are rebranding or discontinuing some of their skin-lightening products in India and Asia following growing controversy and global protests against racial discrimination. Hindustan Unilever will remove the word "Fair" from its "Fair & Lovely" brand, while Johnson & Johnson has already pulled products with "Fairness" labels. L'Oreal is also removing terms like "white," "fair," and "light" from similar products, aiming for a more inclusive vision of beauty.

title: Coca-Cola pauses advertising on all social media platforms globally
summary: Coca-Cola announced it would pause advertising on all social media platforms globally for at least 30 days to reassess its policies and demand greater accountability from its partners. This decision comes amidst a growing advertiser boycott, #StopHateForProfit, against platforms like Facebook and Instagram over their handling of hate speech and misinformation. Other major companies, including Unilever, Levi's, Dockers, and Hershey's, have also announced similar advertising pauses or spending cuts.

title: EPA approves 2 Lysol products as first to effectively kill novel coronavirus on surfaces
summary: The US Environmental Protection Agency has approved two Lysol products, Lysol Disinfectant Spray and Lysol Disinfectant Max Cover Mist, as effective against SARS-CoV-2, the virus causing COVID-19. These are the first products to be directly tested and proven to kill the virus on hard, non-porous surfaces within two minutes. The announcement emphasizes the importance of proper cleaning practices, as a CDC survey revealed many people were cleaning more but often incorrectly, leading to potential health issues.

title: Kraft Heinz Canada Announces New VP, Supply Chain
summary: Kraft Heinz Canada has appointed Anna Petrova as its new Vice President, Supply Chain, effective July 6, 2020. Petrova brings over 25 years of leadership experience, having previously led supply chains for Conagra and Ferrero in Canada, and other major companies globally. Her expertise spans various aspects of supply chain management, and she is expected to drive continuous improvement for Kraft Heinz Canada.

title: What cleaning products are approved to kill coronavirus? Lysol, Microban 24, Clorox
summary: The EPA has approved several cleaning products to be effective against the coronavirus, with Lysol being the first surface disinfectant directly tested and approved for COVID-19. Other products like Microban 24 and various Clorox items are also on the EPA's "List N" due to their effectiveness against similar viruses, with Clorox demand surging by 500% at the start of the pandemic. While Lysol has been directly tested against COVID-19, other products on the list are considered effective due to their action against similar viruses.

title: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® Elects Gilbert Dávila to Board of Directors
summary: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. (Nasdaq: CBRL) announced the election of Gilbert Dávila to its Board of Directors, effective immediately. Mr. Dávila, founder and CEO of DMI Consulting, brings extensive experience in multicultural marketing, diversity & inclusion, market segmentation, and digital marketing from his leadership roles at The Walt Disney Company, Sears & Roebuck Company, Coca-Cola USA, and Procter & Gamble. This appointment supports Cracker Barrel's strategic focus on digital and multicultural engagement.

title: Anna Petrova Named Supply Chain VP at Kraft Heinz Canada
summary: Anna Petrova has been appointed Vice President of Supply Chain at Kraft Heinz Canada. She brings extensive experience from previous roles at Conagra Brands, Ferrero, Mondelēz, BAT, Procter & Gamble, and Mars. Her appointment is expected to bolster continuous improvement in Kraft Heinz Canada's supply chain, logistics, and operations.

title: Diageo unveils paper bottles for Johnnie Walker
summary: Diageo announced the creation of paper-based bottles for its Johnnie Walker whisky, set to launch in 2021. The bottles are made from sustainably sourced pulp and are expected to be 100% plastic-free and fully recyclable. Diageo partnered with Pilot Lite to form Pulpex, a sustainable packaging technology company, which has also formed a consortium with other FMCG companies like Unilever and PepsiCo to develop similar paper bottle solutions.

title: Invest in companies with strong and sustainable moat
summary: This article explains the concept of an economic moat, coined by Warren Buffett, which refers to a company's sustainable competitive advantage. It discusses how to identify such companies through strong brands, long-term profitability growth, high switching costs for customers, and low production costs. The author advocates investing in these "moat companies" for long-term wealth creation, providing examples like Colgate Palmolive and Nestle India with their financials.

title: Mattel Appoints Diana Ferguson to Its Board of Directors
summary: Mattel Inc. has appointed Diana S. Ferguson, CFO of Cleveland Avenue LLC, to its board of directors, effective July 21, 2020. Ferguson, who brings extensive experience in corporate financial management and strategic planning, will serve on the board’s audit committee and become its chair on September 1. This appointment supports Mattel's strategy to transform into an IP-driven, high-performing toy company and drive shareholder value.

title: Clorox tops corporate reputation ranking as demand soars over COVID-19
summary: Clorox has risen to the No. 1 spot on the annual Axios-Harris Poll 100 Corporate Reputation Rankings due to soaring demand for its disinfectant products amid the COVID-19 pandemic. Consumers rewarded companies that provided essential goods and services during the crisis, leading to a shift in rankings where health and safety became paramount. Other companies focused on essentials like Hershey, Publix, and Proctor & Gamble also saw strong showings, while those that faced safety concerns or failed to meet consumer needs, such as Boeing and Juul Labs, significantly dropped.

title: 7 Dental Stocks to Buy for Long-Term Gains: SDC, XRAY, HSIC
summary: Despite a near-term decrease in demand for dental services due to the pandemic, this article identifies seven dental stocks with long-term growth potential. The author, Will Ashworth, provides a contrarian view to analyst expectations, suggesting that investors should buy these stocks while they are out of fashion. The article details the financial performance and prospects of each company, including Henry Schein (HSIC), 3D Systems (DDD), Dentsply Sirona (XRAY), Patterson Companies (PDCO), Procter & Gamble (PG), SmileDirectClub (SDC), and Envista Holdings (NVST).

title: New Clorox CEO brings female leadership of top companies to record 38
summary: Linda Rendle will become the new CEO of The Clorox Company in September, raising the number of female Fortune 500 leaders to a record 38. This appointment follows a 15% sales spike for Clorox during the initial months of the coronavirus pandemic. Rendle plans to expand the company's brand into wellness and nutraceuticals and enhance the disposability of cleaning wipes.

title: Hair Oil Market Research Report is Projected to Witness Considerable Growth by 2027 | Unilever plc, Marico Limited, Dabur India Limited, Emami Group, Procter & Gamble
summary: The Hair Oil Market is anticipated to experience considerable growth by 2027, driven by increasing consumer focus on personal care and the rising trend of professional hair care products. The report highlights the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the market, causing initial disruptions but also presenting opportunities for supply chain re-evaluation. Key segments covered include different types of hair oil, applications, distribution channels, and major market players like Unilever plc and Procter & Gamble.

title: Survey reveals newfound family time around the breakfast table
summary: A new General Mills survey indicates that while the pandemic disrupted morning routines for 80% of U.S. parents, it has also led to more family time at the breakfast table. The survey, commissioned by Big G cereals, found that 73% of families with school-aged children are now spending more time together before work or school. This trend highlights the role of breakfast, particularly cereal, in fostering family connection during challenging times.

title: P&G puts more of Gillette’s Fort Point land up for sale
summary: Procter & Gamble plans to sell a 2.5-acre parking lot adjacent to Gillette's World Shaving Headquarters in Fort Point, Boston, according to an announcement on Tuesday. This action follows the 2019 sale of 6.5 acres to Related Beal for $218 million and is part of a broader strategy to capitalize on the neighborhood's development wave, particularly in life sciences. The site is the last P&G parcel in the city’s 100 Acres Plan, and its development could be influenced by factors such as the Massachusetts Turnpike running beneath it and the need for resilient construction against rising sea levels.

title: P&G to sell off more of Gillette’s South Boston campus
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is continuing to sell off portions of its former Gillette campus in South Boston. The consumer-goods giant has previously sold over 9 acres of the property for a combined total of at least $314 million. This article highlights P&G's ongoing strategy to divest parts of the Gillette campus.

title: P&G trials Olay refill pods: ‘Small steps can lead to monumental change’, says exec
summary: Procter & Gamble is launching Olay refill pods for its Regenerist Whip moisturiser on Amazon UK, marking its first European foray after a North American trial. These recyclable pods aim to reduce plastic waste and promote sustainability in beauty. P&G views this initiative as a "first step" towards more sustainable packaging and is partnering with Young Women's Trust, donating £5 from each purchase to support young women.

title: Ecolab CEO joins Mayo Clinic Board of Trustees
summary: Douglas M. Baker, Jr., Chairman and CEO of Ecolab Inc., was elected as a public trustee to the Mayo Clinic Board of Trustees. He brings decades of national and global leadership experience to the board. Baker's extensive background includes leadership roles at Ecolab and board positions with Target Corporation and the National Association of Manufacturers.

title: Procter and Gamble Plant Technician Internship Programme 2020
summary: Procter & Gamble is offering a Plant Technician Internship Programme in Ibadan, Nigeria, for students passionate about manufacturing world-class brands. The internship targets Ordinary National Diploma (OND) holders in Electrical/Electronic engineering, Mechanical engineering, and Science Lab Technology with recent results and approved IT letters. Interns will gain hands-on experience in manufacturing standards, safety, quality, and leadership within the Ariel manufacturing team.

title: EY and Procter & Gamble team up on supply chain offering
summary: EY and Procter & Gamble (P&G) have broadened their alliance to offer supply chain expertise, combining their strengths to help businesses navigate challenges, particularly those exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic. This collaboration will address various supply chain processes, including strategy, planning, and distribution, leveraging advanced tools and joint teams. P&G, recognized for its leading supply chain operations, aims to share its successful methodologies with clients through EY to enhance responsiveness, productivity, and cost savings.

title: Procter & Gamble appoints first black woman Debra Lee to Board of Directors
summary: Procter & Gamble has appointed Debra Lee, former Chairman and CEO of Black Entertainment Television (BET), to its Board of Directors, making her the first Black woman to hold such a position on P&G's board. Her appointment increases the number of female board members to 50 percent, recognizing her extensive experience and advocacy for equality and inclusion, including founding Leading Women Defined, Inc. Lee's governance expertise from other major boards like Marriott, Burberry, and AT&T was highlighted as a key reason for her selection.

title: Health and Wellness Enthusiast Megan Call Helps Women Find Balance
summary: Megan Call, a health and wellness enthusiast residing in Hawaii, inspires women to lead healthy and carefree lifestyles. She teaches women to balance family life and work by operating businesses from home, as she does with her luxury hair and skincare brand. Megan advocates for innovation and utilizing the internet to expand businesses and reach a wider audience.

title: P&G names Monica Turner president of North America sales
summary: Procter & Gamble has appointed Monica Turner as its new president of North America sales. Turner is a 30-year veteran of the company, having started her career as a sales representative. This promotion marks a significant leadership change in P&G's North American sales division.

title: P&G carries out expansion at its production plant in the State of Mexico
summary: Procter and Gamble (P&G), Health Division, announced the expansion of its production plant in Naucalpan, State of Mexico, reinforcing its three-decade presence in the region. This expansion is expected to create new employment opportunities and increase the company's production capabilities, manufacturing state-of-the-art tablets. The State of Mexico's economic development minister praised P&G's continued investment, highlighting the state's competitive advantages for business.

title: P&G CEO David Taylor sells $3.6 million in stock
summary: David Taylor, the CEO of Procter & Gamble, a Cincinnati-based consumer package goods company, has recently sold $3.6 million worth of company stock. This transaction highlights executive activity within the major corporation, with the sale being reported in the Cincinnati Business Courier. The article briefly mentions this sale alongside other P&G related news.

title: Shweta Shukla Named Senior Director and Head, Corporate Affairs, Asia Pacific, Middle East, and Africa for Kellogg’s
summary: Kellogg Company has appointed Shweta Shukla as Senior Director and Head of Corporate Affairs for Asia Pacific, Middle East, and Africa. In this role, Shukla will oversee Sustainability, Philanthropy, Government Affairs, and Communications, leveraging her 20 years of experience from companies like Unilever, Procter & Gamble, and Kimberly-Clark. Her focus will include Kellogg's Heart & Soul Sustainability Strategy, which pledges to support climate-smart farming, cut food waste, and utilize responsibly sourced ingredients.

title: Colgate-Palmolive Co. stock rises Thursday, outperforms market
summary: Colgate-Palmolive Co. (CL) stock increased by 0.52% on Thursday, closing at $79.06, outperforming the broader market indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The stock closed just shy of its 52-week high and showed mixed performance compared to competitors, with Unilever PLC ADR (UL) and Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC (RBGPF) also rising, while Procter & Gamble Co. (PG) declined. Trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: P&G: CEO David Taylor's pay climbs to $22.9M
summary: Procter & Gamble CEO David Taylor received a 12% raise, increasing his total compensation to $22.9 million, according to new federal disclosures. His compensation included a salary, a bonus with cash, stock options, and deferred compensation, along with stock and option awards. The perks also covered personal use of a company jet, a company car, home security, and other personal benefits.

title: Procter & Gamble: US, Asian sales power rebound
summary: Procter & Gamble has seen a significant sales rebound in recent years, driven primarily by strong performance in its core U.S. and Asian markets, particularly China. This resurgence has boosted the company's stock to near all-time highs. While international sales faced some headwinds from lagging growth in regions like India, the Middle East, and Africa, and unfavorable exchange rates, growth in key markets has compensated for these challenges.

title: Warren Buffett auctioned off a wallet containing a stock tip for $210,000 in 1999
summary: Billionaire investor Warren Buffett auctioned off his wallet for $210,000 in 1999 to benefit the Omaha charity Girls Inc. The wallet contained a Geico business card, an expired Hooters discount pass, and a stock tip for First Industrial Realty Trust. The winning bidder shared the stock tip with others who donated to the charity, and Buffett himself invested $43 million in the company before eventually selling his stake.

title: Digimarc at Center of Pan-European Development of Digital Watermarking for Improved Plastic Sortation and Recycling
summary: Digimarc Corporation's platform has been selected as the primary technology for the "HolyGrail 2.0" initiative, a pan-European effort to enhance plastic sortation and recycling rates. This industry-led project, facilitated by AIM, involves over 85 companies including major brands like P&G, Nestle, PepsiCo, and Danone. The Digimarc Platform uses digital watermarking to improve the identification and sorting of plastic packaging, helping manufacturers meet sustainability goals and advance the circular economy in Europe and beyond.

title: Digimarc to serve as principal technology for HolyGrail 2.0 initiative
summary: Digimarc's automatic identification platform has been selected as the principal technology for the "HolyGrail 2.0" initiative. This cross-value chain effort aims to evaluate how digital watermarking can improve the sorting and recycling rates for packaging within the European Union. Major brands like P&G, Nestle, PepsiCo, and Danone are leading the initiative with over 85 participating companies.

title: Graduate Hotels partners with P&G, Cleveland Clinic and hotel association on cleaning protocols
summary: Graduate Hotels has announced a partnership with Procter & Gamble Co., the Cleveland Clinic, and the American Hotel & Lodging Association. This collaboration aims to enhance the health and safety protocols for guests, particularly after the reopening of its Graduate Cincinnati hotel. The initiative focuses on implementing robust cleaning procedures across their properties.

title: Shareholders mount class action lawsuit against Coty
summary: Coty, Inc. and some of its officers are facing a class action lawsuit from shareholders. The lawsuit claims the company provided misleading information and overpaid for its acquisitions of the P&G specialty beauty business and Kylie Cosmetics, and lacked adequate infrastructure to integrate them. The lawsuit seeks damages for alleged violations of federal securities laws.

title: Procter & Gamble Talks the Talk on Diversity, But Fails to Walk the Walk
summary: As You Sow announced a shareholder resolution against Procter & Gamble for its refusal to disclose details on the effectiveness of its diversity and inclusion programs. Despite P&G's extensive advertising campaigns on race relations, the company has not provided metrics on promotion, recruitment, and retention of protected employee classes, leading to investor concerns about the practical impact of its stated commitments. This stands in contrast to other major companies that have agreed to increase their diversity reporting.

title: Big Indian companies shy away from solving the plastic waste crisis, says report
summary: A report from The Changing Markets Foundation, "Talking Trash: The Corporate Playbook of False Solutions," reveals that the plastics industry, consumer brands, and retailers, particularly their Indian subsidiaries, are using tactics to delay and derail effective legislation against plastic use. The report criticizes the lack of transparency and impact of voluntary initiatives by major plastic polluters like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo, stating these efforts are negligible compared to the plastic they generate. It proposes 12 measures for India, including stricter legislation, phasing out multi-layered plastics, and banning harmful plastic materials, to effectively address the plastic waste crisis.

title: DuPont Human Microbiome Venture and P&G to research next-generation probiotics
summary: DuPont Human Microbiome Venture and Procter & Gamble (P&G) have formed a research partnership to discover and develop next-generation probiotics (NGPs) for human health, initially focusing on dietary supplements. Both companies have conducted extensive research in this area and aim to accelerate innovation in metabolic health. This collaboration seeks to leverage their combined capabilities to benefit consumers affected by metabolic health issues.

title: Activist investor takes stake in Comcast, calling the company’s stock ‘undervalued’
summary: Activist investor Trian Fund Management has acquired a 0.4% stake in Comcast, arguing that the company's stock is undervalued. Trian, founded by Nelson Peltz, often pushes for changes like cost-cutting or selling business units to deliver more value to investors, though influencing family-controlled Comcast could be challenging. The news initially boosted Comcast's stock, and analysts like Craig Moffett also believe Comcast is undervalued, particularly its cable business compared to its media segments.

title: DuPont and P&G to tackle metabolic health in new probiotic-focused deal
summary: DuPont's Human Microbiome Venture and Procter & Gamble (P&G) have partnered to research how probiotics can address metabolic health conditions like obesity and type 2 diabetes. The collaboration aims to develop next-generation microbe-based products, initially as supplements, leveraging both companies' expertise. This initiative builds on DuPont's previous metabolic health research and P&G's existing work with microbiome-focused brands and probiotic supplements.

title: P&G shares diversity data after its own marketing raises expectations
summary: Procter & Gamble has released its diversity data following increased expectations generated by its marketing campaigns. The article, published on September 22, 2020, by Jack Neff, highlights how the company is responding to the discourse around diversity and inclusion.

title: Callaway taps Kevin Nealon to tee up new clubs as interest in golf surges
summary: Callaway has partnered with Kevin Nealon for a new campaign promoting their Big Bertha B21 clubs to address golf slices. The campaign features an eight-minute short film and a "Slicers Anonymous" webpage, capitalizing on increased interest in golf during the pandemic and a surge in Google searches for "golf slice." This initiative highlights Callaway's strategy to engage new and returning golfers with a humorous approach that acknowledges common challenges in the sport.

title: Do you own stock in Procter & Gamble?
summary: This article urges Procter & Gamble (P&G) shareholders to vote "FOR" Shareholder Proposal #5 by the October 13th deadline. Proposal #5 requires P&G to develop a plan to increase efforts to eliminate deforestation and forest degradation from its supply chains, and to publicly disclose this plan. The article provides detailed instructions on how shareholders can vote, including methods like internet, phone, and mail, and guidance on finding their control numbers and qualifying as a shareholder of record.

title: Procter & Gamble at 1,400 workers in West Virginia and still hiring
summary: Procter & Gamble's Berkeley County manufacturing facility in West Virginia has grown to 1,400 employees and is still looking to hire another 100 to 200 workers despite challenges in recruitment due to the pandemic. The plant, which began construction in 2015, has expanded rapidly, quadrupling production in its last year, and is becoming one of P&G's largest manufacturing sites globally, operating 24/7 with automated systems supported by skilled human workers. The company emphasizes its commitment to the community and long-term presence in the area.

title: Procter & Gamble calls for change to annual TV ad-buying process
summary: Procter & Gamble's top marketing executive, Marc Pritchard, is advocating for significant changes to the annual TV upfront ad-buying process, calling it antiquated and inefficient. P&G is requesting a later upfront marketplace and more flexibility in ad purchasing closer to air dates, criticizing how current practices allow networks to leverage client budget forecasts to maintain high rates despite declining TV ratings. Pritchard also called for social media platforms to better regulate content to avoid government intervention.

title: Pritchard: P&G is taking control in the media supply chain — and so can other marketers
summary: Procter & Gamble's Chief Brand Officer Marc Pritchard has outlined a vision for overhauling the legacy media supply chain, advocating for greater control for brand marketers, increased diversity, and improved cross-platform measurement. P&G is implementing these changes by avoiding traditional TV upfronts, increasing programmatic and direct buys, and partnering with minority-owned media companies. Pritchard urged all marketers to demand a validated, scalable cross-platform measurement pilot by next year’s ANA Media & Measurement conference to create a more equitable and efficient media ecosystem.

title: Procter & Gamble, Unilever and Colgate-Palmolive top chart as ‘world’s worst offenders’ for plastic pollution
summary: Procter & Gamble, Unilever, and Colgate-Palmolive have been identified as some of the top global plastic polluters in a report by The Changing Markets Foundation. The report, titled 'Talking Trash: The Corporate Playbook of False Solutions,' criticizes these companies for allegedly obstructing plastic waste legislation while their initiatives fall short of addressing the crisis. The companies are accused of producing substantial amounts of plastic packaging annually and using the pandemic to push for increased plastic use.

title: Amazon launches "Climate Pledge Friendly" program
summary: Amazon is launching "Climate Pledge Friendly," a new program labeling over 25,000 products with sustainability certifications, making it easier for customers to find eco-friendly options. The initiative includes a new certification called "Compact by Design" which focuses on product efficiency to reduce carbon emissions through better packaging and design. This program supports Amazon's commitment to be net-zero carbon by 2040 and aligns with the Paris Agreement.

title: Clorox’s new CEO is racing to keep wipes on store shelves
summary: Linda Rendle, the new CEO of Clorox, is focused on ramping up production of cleaning products like disinfecting wipes and sprays to meet unprecedented demand fueled by the coronavirus pandemic. At 42, Rendle is one of the youngest Fortune 500 CEOs and the first woman to lead Clorox. Prior to the pandemic, she was tasked with boosting flagging sales, but now her primary mission is to overcome severe product shortages.

title: By any other name? P&G to re-brand skin lightening creams
summary: Procter & Gamble plans to re-brand its skin lightening and whitening creams, but will not cease their sale. This decision comes as the global skin lightening market was valued at US$8.3 billion in 2018, and despite P&G's involvement in anti-racism campaigns. Other companies like Johnson & Johnson have exited the category, while Unilever and L'Oréal have also rebranded.

title: Worried about more shortages, grocery stores are stockpiling goods
summary: Grocery stores across the U.S. are stockpiling products like paper towels, Clorox wipes, and even holiday turkeys and cold remedies to avoid shortages during a potential second wave of coronavirus. This strategy shifts from stocking weeks to months worth of supplies, driven by consumer hoarding and ongoing demand, which has also led to higher prices. Manufacturers like Clorox anticipate shortages well into 2021 despite increased production efforts.

title: P&G Cleans Up Act After Bounty Paper Towel-Sponsored TikToks Prompt NAD Inquiry
summary: The National Advertising Division (NAD) investigated Procter & Gamble (P&G) regarding Bounty paper towel advertisements on TikTok, where influencers promoted the product. The NAD raised concerns because the #BountyPartner disclosure, indicating a paid sponsorship, did not consistently transfer when videos were shared from TikTok to other platforms like Instagram, violating FTC guidelines. P&G addressed the issue by requiring influencers to embed disclosures directly into their videos to ensure they persist across platforms.

title: Colgate-Palmolive Supports the World Health Organization (WHO) #SafeHands Effort in Papua New Guinea and Around the World to Help Stop the Spread of COVID-19
summary: Colgate-Palmolive is supporting the World Health Organization's (WHO) #SafeHands initiative by donating 25 million bars of soap globally, with 250,000 bars specifically allocated to Papua New Guinea. This effort aims to combat the spread of COVID-19 by promoting proper handwashing, especially in vulnerable communities lacking access to quality soap and knowledge. UNICEF PNG will manage the distribution of these soaps to schools, health centers, and communities across various districts.

title: P&G rolls out 'Ninjamas' brand of nighttime underwear under Pampers
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched a new brand of nighttime underwear called 'Ninjamas' under its Pampers umbrella. This expansion aims to target the nighttime incontinence market. The initiative was announced by the Cincinnati Business Courier.

title: How to Show a VC That Your Startup Will Be Profitable
summary: Even with venture capital still available, startups face intense competition. Betsy Bluestone of P&G Ventures and Vanessa Dawson of Vinetta Project offer five key tips for perfecting a VC pitch: highlighting market opportunities, offering "no trade-off" products, building strong teams, showing customer benefits, and protecting intellectual property. These strategies help early-stage companies stand out and secure funding for growth.

title: Icahn Automotive Appoints Elisa Bannon-Jones Chief People Officer and Deborah Brundage Chief Marketing Officer
summary: Icahn Automotive has announced the appointment of Elisa Bannon-Jones as Chief People Officer and Deborah Brundage as Chief Marketing Officer. Bannon-Jones will lead human resources strategy, while Brundage will direct marketing, communications, and customer experience. These appointments are part of an ongoing plan to separate Icahn Automotive into distinct Parts and Service companies, strengthening leadership for the Service division.

title: Procter & Gamble can do better!
summary: This article by the Rainforest Action Network criticizes Procter & Gamble (P&G) for its alleged involvement in human rights abuses, deforestation, and contributions to climate change through its supply chains. Specifically, it highlights forced labor in palm oil production linked to P&G, the destruction of critical forests for paper products like Charmin, and the company's overall impact on the climate crisis. The article urges shareholders to vote for Shareholder Proposal #5 to prioritize people and the planet over profits.

title: Campaign Spotlight: Private Sector launches "Ingat Angat Tayong Lahat" campaign for consumer confidence and economic recovery
summary: The private sector in the Philippines has launched the "Ingat Angat Tayong Lahat" campaign to restore consumer confidence and aid economic recovery amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. This initiative encourages businesses to maintain strict safety standards while increasing operations and urges Filipinos to safely resume activities outside their homes. The campaign, supported by numerous major corporations and media partners, emphasizes public-private sector cooperation and adherence to minimum health protocols to protect both lives and livelihoods.

title: P&G Shareholders Send Resounding Message Calling for Diversity Disclosure
summary: Procter & Gamble shareholders voted 37% in favor of a resolution from As You Sow, demanding greater disclosure on diversity data related to employee promotion, recruitment, and retention. Investors are concerned P&G's extensive advertising campaigns on race relations may be perceived as exploitative without accompanying internal diversity metrics. This shareholder action highlights a demand for concrete data to demonstrate the effectiveness of P&G's diversity, equity, and inclusion programs, contrasting with other companies that have agreed to increased reporting.

title: P&G Declines to Share Diversity Data, It’s Like My Favorite Superhero Turning Out to Be a Villain
summary: Robert Xavier Snaer-Williams, speaking on behalf of As You Sow, moved a proposal requesting Procter & Gamble publish an annual report on its diversity and inclusion efforts. He expressed disappointment that P&G, which has promoted racial justice in its marketing, declines to share key inclusion statistics like recruitment, retention, and promotion rates for its own workforce. Snaer-Williams argues that P&G's lack of transparency creates an unnecessary business risk and undermines its advertising efforts aimed at diverse consumers.

title: P&G shareholders push board to publish report on deforestation
summary: Procter & Gamble shareholders have voted in favor of a proposal requiring the company to publish a report on its efforts to combat deforestation, despite opposition from its board. The decision highlights increasing investor pressure on corporations regarding environmental issues, particularly P&G's timber sourcing for its tissue products from Canada's Northern Boreal Forest. Environmental groups like the Natural Resources Defense Council argue that P&G's current sustainability practices are insufficient.

title: P&G names president of division in charge of new business - Cincinnati Business Courier
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced Guy Persaud as the new president of its New Business division, effective January 1, 2021. This division focuses on creating new lines of business for the Cincinnati-based consumer goods giant. The appointment aims to further P&G's innovation and market expansion strategies.

title: Disposable Razor Blades Market Share, Size, Report, 2032
summary: The global disposable razor blades market, valued at USD 3.39 billion in 2019, is projected to reach USD 5.45 billion by 2032, growing at a CAGR of 3.84%. Europe held the largest market share in 2019, driven by high disposable income and grooming trends, while the shift towards eco-friendly products and impact of COVID-19 on grooming habits are notable trends affecting demand. The market is segmented by blade count (1&2, 3&4, 5&more), end-user (men, women), and distribution channel (hypermarkets, online, others), with key players including Procter & Gamble, Edgewell Personal Care, and BIC Group.

title: P&G to Grow DTC Presence as E-commerce Sales Jump 50%
summary: Procter & Gamble reported a 9% net sales increase to $19.3 billion in fiscal Q1, driven by a 50% surge in e-commerce sales, which now account for 11-12% of total sales. The company plans to expand its direct-to-consumer (DTC) presence to better understand consumer needs, while maintaining a channel-agnostic approach. Organic sales grew across most core segments, with innovation and increased demand for home care and personal cleansing products being key drivers, though baby care saw a slight decline.

title: Procter & Gamble beats estimates as sales jump 9%, raises forecast amid strong demand
summary: Procter & Gamble reported a strong fiscal first-quarter, with sales rising 9% due to increased demand for household products during the pandemic. The company exceeded Wall Street expectations for both earnings per share and revenue, prompting them to raise their sales and core earnings per share growth outlook for fiscal 2021. P&G saw significant organic sales growth across all five business segments, particularly in fabric and home care, and plans to increase stock buybacks.

title: P&G Rises as It Reports Broad Growth, Raises 2021 Forecast
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported its best organic sales growth since 2005, driven by increased at-home consumption of its household products. The company raised its full-year forecast, predicting strong sales to continue until a COVID-19 vaccine becomes available. Sales grew across all business units, particularly in the fabric and home care segment.

title: Procter & Gamble shows that increasing spending during a recession is worth it
summary: Procter & Gamble's recent earnings report highlights the strategy of increasing spending in key areas during a recession, rather than cutting indiscriminately. The company boosted marketing efforts while competitors reduced theirs, leveraging its strong brand recognition during the pandemic. This approach, supported by research from Harvard Business School and Boston Consulting Group, resulted in a significant stock rebound, reinforcing the idea that strategic investment during downturns can lead to greater success.

title: P&G sales surge amid pivot to digital, $100M investment in advertising
summary: Procter & Gamble saw its revenue increase by 9% to $19.3 billion in Q1 2021, driven by a nearly 50% surge in e-commerce sales, which now account for 11% to 12% of total sales. The company boosted its marketing spending by over $100 million during the quarter, simultaneously cutting overhead costs, as it strategically reinvests in advertising to capitalize on increased demand for cleaning, health, and hygiene products amid the pandemic. Analysts attribute P&G's growth to its marketing approach, product innovation, and structural changes that prepared it for a more digital-focused market, with these shifts in consumer behavior expected to persist post-pandemic.

title: How Clorox’s new CEO plans to turn disinfectant wipes into future wins
summary: New Clorox CEO Linda Rendle aims to leverage the increased demand for disinfectant wipes during the COVID-19 pandemic to accelerate the company's multiyear "Ignite" growth plan. This strategy focuses on innovation, expanding into new markets like professional cleaning, and building on its health and wellness product portfolio. The article highlights how Clorox is adapting to capitalize on current trends while maintaining its long-term objectives for revenue growth and profitability.

title: P&G’s Lysol Competitor Wins EPA Approval to Fight Covid-19
summary: Procter & Gamble's Microban 24 sanitizing spray, a competitor to products like Lysol, has received EPA approval for its effectiveness against the virus causing Covid-19. Introduced just before the pandemic, the product has seen a surge in demand due to increased need for cleaning supplies. This approval marks a significant validation for P&G's entry into the germ-killing household product market amidst the public health crisis.

title: J.M. Smucker selling Crisco to Green Giant owner for $550 million
summary: J.M. Smucker Co. is selling its Crisco brand to B&G Foods Inc. for $550 million in a cash deal. This divestiture aligns with Smucker's strategy to exit the U.S. baking category and focus on pet food, coffee, and snacks. Crisco generated approximately $270 million in sales for Smucker's 2020 fiscal year.

title: Rawlings Picks Up Easton
summary: Rawlings Sporting Goods is set to acquire Easton Diamond Sports, forming a leading provider of baseball and softball equipment. This acquisition will allow for greater investment in research and development, product innovation, and expanding customization options for players. Both companies emphasize their commitment to growing the games of baseball and softball through enhanced partnerships and an improved value proposition for all stakeholders.

title: CEW Honors C-suite’s Next Generation With Top Talent Awards
summary: CEW recognized eight honorees for its 2020 Top Talent Awards, celebrating the next generation of C-suite executives in the beauty industry who have demonstrated agility and adaptability amid changing consumer behaviors. These leaders from companies like L’Oréal, Estée Lauder, P&G, Nars, Ulta Beauty, Symrise, and Nügg Beauty shared insights on how the pandemic has accelerated digital transformation, personalized consumer engagement, and emphasized self-care and sustainability within the beauty sector. The honorees highlighted their strategies for innovation in technology, merchandising, fragrance, and brand communication to meet evolving demands.

title: Ecolab’s Doug Baker to Retire After 16-Year Run as CEO
summary: Doug Baker, CEO of Ecolab for 16 years, will retire on January 1st, with President and COO Christophe Beck taking over. Baker is credited with significantly growing the company's global sales, overseeing major acquisitions, and playing a prominent role in the Minnesota business community and St. Paul's community life. Christophe Beck, an Ecolab veteran since 2007, is set to continue Baker's vision for the company.

title: ­Clorox lifts forecast after best sales jump in over 20 years
summary: ­Clorox reported its strongest quarterly sales growth in over two decades, leading the company to raise its full-year sales and profit forecasts. This surge is attributed to increased demand for disinfectants and other cleaning products due to the Covid-19 pandemic, as well as higher sales of products like Glad trash bags and charcoal. Despite running factories round the clock, Clorox, like its peers, is still struggling to fully meet the elevated consumer demand.

title: Wet Tissue and Wipe Market Size, Share 2020: Global Industry Trends, Growth, Segmentation, Future Demands, Latest Innovation, Sales Revenue by Regional Forecast to 2024 | Technavio
summary: The wet tissue and wipe market is projected to grow by USD 6.64 billion between 2020 and 2024, exhibiting a CAGR of over 7%. This growth is primarily driven by product premiumization through innovation and portfolio extension, along with increasing concerns regarding hygiene. Technavio's report provides a holistic analysis, including market sizing, forecast, trends, growth drivers, challenges, and vendor analysis, considering the impact of COVID-19.

title: P&G subsidiary picks CR Dua as chair
summary: CR Dua, chairman and founder of Dua Associates, has been appointed to chair the board of Procter & Gamble (P&G) Hygiene and Health Care for a five-year term. P&G Hygiene and Health Care is an India-based company known for popular household brands such as Ariel, Duracell, and Gillette. The article notes that this content is exclusively for subscribers.

title: Sodexo, P&G Professional, Clorox Healthcare and GOJO Launch
summary: Sodexo, P&G Professional, Clorox Healthcare, and GOJO have partnered to launch the "Safer Together" pilot program in select Care New England hospitals. This initiative aims to boost consumer confidence in hospital safety through enhanced cleaning, disinfection, and hand hygiene practices using trusted brands. The program addresses patient concerns about hospital cleanliness, integrating well-known products and signage to reassure visitors.

title: Cleco honored for diversity and inclusion efforts at Cenla Chamber Bizzy Awards
summary: Cleco was honored with the Procter & Gamble Diversity and Inclusion Award at the 2020 Bizzy Awards in Alexandria, becoming its inaugural recipient. The company was recognized for its commitment to diversity and inclusion, with a focus on hiring diverse employees, fostering an inclusive work environment, and valuing different perspectives. Cleco's diversity and inclusion strategy, which began in 2018, aims to enhance employee engagement, innovation, and customer satisfaction.

title: Rodolfo Spielmann joins NatureSweet as president and CEO
summary: Rodolfo Spielmann has been appointed president and CEO of NatureSweet Tomatoes in San Antonio. He brings over 23 years of experience from major consumer packaged goods companies, including Proctor & Gamble, Heinz, Del Monte, and Mars, where he focused on growth and development. Spielmann recently attended the Fresh Summit to engage with customers and explore partnership opportunities.

title: Vicks Sinex Nasal Spray Recalled for Bacterial Contamination
summary: Procter & Gamble has voluntarily recalled three lots of its Vicks Sinex nasal spray in the US, Germany, and the UK due to bacterial contamination with B. cepacia. Although no illnesses have been reported, this bacteria could pose a serious risk to individuals with compromised immune systems or chronic lung conditions. P&G discovered the contamination during routine quality control and believes it's limited to one raw material batch.

title: Diversey Care Launches Oxivir 1 Disinfectant Cleaner Wipes to Lead its Disinfectant Portfolio
summary: Diversey Care has launched Oxivir®1 ready-to-use disinfectant wipes, powered by Accelerated Hydrogen Peroxide® (AHP®). These wipes are highly effective against 75 key pathogens, including bacteria, viruses, TB, and fungi, in one minute or less, while also being safe for use without personal protective equipment. Designed for healthcare environments, they offer a one-step cleaning and disinfecting solution, improving compliance and reducing turnover time.

title: |Tesla to Join S&P 500 Next Month as Largest-Ever New Member
summary: |Tesla Inc. (TSLA) is set to join the S&P 500 index on December 21, becoming the largest company ever added to the gauge. This announcement follows months of speculation and a significant rally in the stock this year, elevating the electric vehicle pioneer's market value to nearly $390 billion. Tesla's inclusion is expected to greatly broaden its investor base and make it one of the index's most influential constituents.

title: AKQA, Grey merger naming sparks employee uproar and 'upsets' P&G
summary: The article reports on the significant dissatisfaction among employees and client Procter & Gamble regarding the naming of the newly merged AKQA and Grey advertising agencies. WPP CEO Mark Read is mentioned in relation to this merger. The controversy highlights potential internal and external repercussions of the agency consolidation.

title: Thermo Fisher Scientific Elects New Director to Board
summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. has announced the election of R. Alexandra "Alex" Keith to its board of directors, increasing the board's total to 13 members. Ms. Keith currently serves as CEO of Procter & Gamble's global Beauty business and brings extensive experience in leadership and brand-building. Chairman and CEO Marc N. Casper highlighted her visionary leadership and focus on results as key assets for Thermo Fisher Scientific's global brand strategy.

summary: The online beauty & personal care products market is projected to grow by USD 57.79 billion between 2020 and 2024, at a CAGR of approximately 15%. This growth is primarily driven by increasing internet penetration and the expansion of distribution channels through omnichannel strategies. Inc., and Henkel AG & Co. KGaA.

title: Pantene, Head & Shoulders partner on STEM scholarships
summary: Pantene and Head & Shoulders, two Procter & Gamble brands, are partnering through a new initiative to support Black women pursuing STEM degrees. In collaboration with CVS, they will award $200,000 in scholarships to students at Historically Black Colleges and Universities and UNCF member schools. This effort aims to increase diversity in STEM fields and empower future Black female innovators.

title: Amazon is price gouging cleaning products for the second COVID wave
summary: During the second COVID-19 wave, Amazon sellers are price gouging cleaning products from name brands like Clorox, Bounty, and Charmin, while generic alternatives remain relatively more stable. Clorox wipe prices, for instance, have surged over 200% since January, reaching as high as $50 for a pack. This practice is occurring despite earlier efforts by companies like Clorox to address price gouging on the platform.

title: PMI wins U.S. Department of Homeland Security award
summary: Philip Morris International (PMI) received a Partnership Award from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's National Intellectual Property Rights Coordination Center for its campaign against fraudulent goods, particularly personal protective equipment (PPE), during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company also secured three Platinum MarCom Awards for its illicit trade prevention efforts. These recognitions highlight PMI's commitment to collaborating with public and private sectors to combat counterfeit products.

title: Johnson & Johnson, Mars, WD-40 E-Commerce Experts Pack CGSM 2020 DTC Panel
summary: Experts from Johnson & Johnson, Mars, Inc., and WD-40 Company are set to speak on a direct-to-consumer (DTC) e-commerce panel at the Consumer Goods Sales and Marketing Summit (CGSM) 2020. The panel will discuss how consumer goods brands are leveraging DTC strategies to meet evolving consumer needs as e-commerce accelerates due to the pandemic. The session will highlight the collaborative team approach required for success in the DTC space.

title: NAA asks P&G to pay Rs 241 crore in penalties for not passing GST rate cut to consumers
summary: The National Anti-profiteering Authority (NAA) has directed Procter & Gamble to pay Rs 241.5 crore for reportedly not passing on the GST rate reduction to consumers. The NAA found that P&G failed to reduce prices commensurate with the GST rate cut from 28% to 18% in November 2017 and instead allegedly increased prices of 1,383 goods. P&G maintains it has not violated the law and will explore all legal options, asserting it passed on the benefits through consumer promotion schemes.

title: P&G taps JLL to sell South Boston site
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has enlisted JLL to sell a site in South Boston. The property, currently a parking lot, has the potential to accommodate 500,000 square feet of future development. This move by P&G opens up a significant development opportunity in the Fort Point Channel area.

title: P&G sells Newbridge plant to Mapaex
summary: Procter & Gamble has sold its Newbridge, Co Kildare plant to Mapaex. Employees are expected to retain their jobs, terms, and pension rights and the deal includes a 10-year supply agreement for P&G’s oral care and Braun business. P&G stated the facility was "under-utilised" and the sale will enable the site to take on additional work.

title: Huggies launches biodegradable baby wipes in step towards plastic-free goal
summary: Huggies, owned by Kimberly-Clark, has introduced its first biodegradable baby wipes in the UK, aiming to eliminate plastics from its wipe range over the next five years. These new Huggies Pure Biodegradable wipes are made from 100% natural fibers and are designed to break down in landfill conditions within 15 days, contributing to a significant reduction in plastic usage. This initiative follows pressure from consumers and media to address the environmental impact of wet wipes, aligning with Huggies' "Tiniest Footprint" Mission and WRAP’s UK Plastic Pact.

title: coca-cola, PepsiCo and nestlé named top plastic polluters for third consecutive year
summary: Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, and Nestlé have been identified as the world's leading plastic polluters for the third year in a row, according to a report by Break Free From Plastic. The organization's annual brand audit collected plastic waste from 55 countries, highlighting the significant contribution of these corporations to global plastic pollution. Despite claims of working towards solutions, these companies continue to produce harmful single-use plastic packaging, prompting calls for them to adopt robust reuse systems and reduce plastic production.

title: Insights on the Global Electric Toothbrush Market 2020-2024: COVID-19 Analysis, Drivers, Restraints, Opportunities, and Threats - Technavio
summary: The electric toothbrush market is projected to grow by USD 2.34 billion, achieving an 8% CAGR between 2020-2024, driven primarily by the rising prevalence of periodontal diseases. North America is expected to contribute 45% of this growth, largely due to increased oral health awareness, despite the high cost of electric toothbrushes posing a restraint. Technavio's report details market assessments, key company strategies, and effects of COVID-19.

title: Colgate-Palmolive’s Developed Markets Remained a Drag in 1Q17
summary: Colgate-Palmolive's sales in developed markets, including North America and Europe, experienced a decline in 1Q17, largely due to falling volumes and lower pricing, impacting overall financial performance. While North America was hit hardest, European sales showed a sequential improvement despite adverse currency fluctuations. The company maintained market leadership in oral care and saw success with new product launches despite these challenges.

summary: The oral care market is projected to grow by USD 11.84 billion between 2020 and 2024, at a CAGR of over 4%, driven primarily by increasing awareness of oral health and technological innovations leading to product premiumization. Key companies contributing to this growth include Amway Corp., Church & Dwight Co. Inc., and Colgate-Palmolive Co. title: WPP announces winners of its inaugural Extraordinary Awards
summary: WPP announced the winners of its first Extraordinary Awards, celebrating outstanding work from its agencies across five categories: Communications, Experience, Commerce, Technology, and the top prize for Creative Transformation. The awards recognized projects that demonstrated creativity's power to drive change for clients and communities, with winning campaigns including Boots' "Breaking the Mould of Christmas," Burger King's "The Moldy Whopper," and P&G's "Rabbi Bot by Always."

title: Procter & Gamble Announces CFO Transition
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced that Andre Schulten will succeed Jon Moeller as Chief Financial Officer, effective March 1, 2021. Moeller will remain as Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer, overseeing Enterprise Markets and other functional areas. Schulten, currently Senior Vice President–Baby Care, North America, was praised for his leadership and financial expertise by CEO David Taylor.

title: P&G names Andre Schulten as CFO replacing Jon Moeller
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced Andre Schulten, currently senior vice president of its North America baby care unit, will replace Jon Moeller as the new chief financial officer. Schulten will assume the role on March 1, 2021. Moeller, who has been CFO since 2009, will continue as vice chairman and chief operating officer, focusing on operational roles and leading the enterprise markets unit.

title: Selena Gomez Wins Startup of the Year at Beauty Inc Awards
summary: Selena Gomez's Rare Beauty won Startup of the Year at the 2020 Beauty Inc Awards, which were held virtually. Other notable winners included Byredo's makeup line, Sharon Chuter of Uoma Beauty for founding Pull Up for Change, and The Estée Lauder Cos. for social responsibility. The article details all the winners across various categories.

title: Coca-Cola kicks off massive agency review to 'fundamentally transform' its marketing
summary: Coca-Cola has launched a comprehensive global review of its media and creative planning and buying practices, along with its agency appointments. This initiative aims to enhance effectiveness and efficiency across various marketing investments, including media, creative, and production, as part of the company's digital transformation. While expected to generate cost savings, the primary goal is a fundamental redesign of its marketing model and consolidation of third-party agencies.

title: Coca-Cola tops list of 10 corporate plastic polluters of 2020
summary: For the third consecutive year, Coca-Cola has been identified as the leading global plastic polluter among major brands, according to the "Branded Volume III" report by the Break Free From Plastic movement. The report lists Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Nestlé, and seven other corporations as the biggest contributors to plastic waste, urging them to reduce single-use plastics and reinvent their delivery systems. Despite some companies joining initiatives like the New Plastics Economy Global Commitment, their reduction in virgin plastic use has been minimal.

title: International Flavors & Fragrances Inc. stock rises Wednesday, outperforms market
summary: International Flavors & Fragrances Inc. (IFF) stock rose 1.07% on Wednesday, outperforming the broader market. Despite a mixed trading session for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones, IFF achieved its second consecutive day of gains. The stock closed below its 52-week high but showed a mixed performance compared to competitors like Procter & Gamble Co., L'Oreal S.A. ADR, and Estee Lauder Cos. Cl A.

title: P&G Commits to 2,021 Acts of Good in 2021 and Inspires Millions Through Lead With Love Campaign
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has pledged 2,021 "acts of good" for 2021, commencing with significant contributions of health, hygiene products, PPE, and financial aid for COVID-19 relief. This initiative is part of their "Lead with Love" campaign, which encourages collective action for communities, equality, and the environment. P&G will highlight these efforts through various brand programs and a new film titled "Emotions," aiming to inspire people to do more and better in the new year.

title: Procter & Gamble names new CFO from within its ranks
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has announced Andre Schulten as its new chief financial officer. Schulten will replace Jon Moeller, who has served in the CFO role since 2009 and will continue as P&G's vice chairman and COO. The appointment marks an internal promotion for the company.

title: P&G Reveals the Power of Purpose
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is highlighted for its commitment to sustainability, driven by Chief Sustainability Officer Virginie Helias. The company emphasizes how a focus on purpose and sustainability is crucial for both being a force for good and a force for growth, with consumer expectations increasingly aligning with brands that demonstrate social responsibility. P&G collaborates across industries and leverages technology to drive positive change in areas like waste and climate change, making sustainable lifestyles more accessible and appealing to consumers.

title: Costco Wholesale Corporation (NASDAQ:COST) Pays Huge Dividends
summary: Costco (NASDAQ: COST) has continued to pay lucrative dividends to shareholders, despite the COVID-19 pandemic, due to its success in selling essential goods. The company's unique membership-based business model allows it to sell inventory at cost, providing a competitive advantage. Outstanding financial results, including a 17% year-over-year increase in same-store sales and an 86% rise in e-commerce revenue, have enabled Costco to issue a record $4.4-billion special distribution to shareholders, contributing to a 32% year-to-date increase in COST stock.

title: Procter & Gamble Had a Strong 2020. Here’s What Could Boost the Stock After the Pandemic.
summary: Procter & Gamble experienced strong performance in 2020 due to increased demand for cleaning products during the pandemic. Despite potential waning demand for these specific products post-pandemic, the company is still positioned for continued growth. The article suggests factors that could contribute to P&G's success even after the immediate impact of the pandemic subsides.

title: P&G terminates plan to acquire razor startup Billie following FTC lawsuit
summary: Procter & Gamble has terminated its planned acquisition of the women’s beauty products startup Billie after the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) sued to block the deal. The FTC argued that the merger would eliminate competition in the wet shave razor market, particularly given Billie's growing presence and planned expansion into physical retail. Both P&G and Billie expressed disappointment but agreed to terminate the agreement rather than engage in a prolonged legal challenge, with the FTC commending the decision as beneficial for consumers.

title: P&G, Billie Cancel Deal After FTC Suit
summary: Procter & Gamble's planned acquisition of women’s shaving brand Billie has been called off after the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) filed a suit to block the deal, citing concerns over competition. Both companies agreed not to pursue a prolonged legal challenge. This follows a similar FTC intervention that led to the cancellation of Edgewell Personal Care's acquisition of Harry's.

title: P&G Launches Oral Health Education and Sustainability Program
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) Oral Care has launched "Healthy Smiles. Healthy Lives. Healthy Planet." a program aimed at promoting healthy oral care habits and reducing environmental impact. The initiative, led by brands like Oral-B and Crest, seeks to educate and enable 2 billion people to adopt healthy oral care habits by 2030 while also focusing on sustainable practices like 100% recyclable packaging by 2025 and reduced greenhouse gas emissions. P&G Oral Care emphasizes innovation for both human and planetary health, including products designed to reduce plastic waste and improve energy efficiency in its operations.

title: Get High Dividend Exposure with the HDEF ETF
summary: The article discusses the Xtrackers MSCI EAFE High Dividend Yield Equity ETF (HDEF) as an option for investors seeking high dividend exposure with international diversification. HDEF offers exposure to developed markets outside the U.S., focusing on high-dividend stocks while hedging against currency risk. This strategy aims to provide stable dividend payments, exemplified by its top holding, Unilever PLC.

title: Kroger and Cintas halt political contributions, P&G may change future support
summary: Kroger and Cintas announced they are halting political donations following the riots in Washington, D.C., with Kroger reviewing its PAC-giving philosophy and Cintas reviewing its criteria and strategy. Procter & Gamble also signaled it might change its future political support based on actions undermining democratic processes. These Cincinnati-based companies join a growing list of corporations rethinking their financial support for politicians after the Capitol riot.

title: P&G Commits to Sustainable Oral Care for Patients and Products
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) Oral Care has launched "Healthy Smiles. Healthy Lives. Healthy Planet," a new platform outlining its sustainability commitments. P&G aims to educate 2 billion people on healthy oral care habits by 2030, while simultaneously reducing its environmental footprint through initiatives like recyclable packaging and improved energy efficiency. The company's brands, Oral-B and Crest, will focus on education, access to products, and innovation to support these goals, aligning with P&G's Ambition 2030 Sustainability Program and UN Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Clearwater Paper Corporation raises 4.79% on January 12
summary: Clearwater Paper Corporation saw its shares jump 4.79% on January 12, closing at $41.78. The company, which manufactures private label tissue, paperboard, and pulp-based products, traded approximately 127,201 shares. The gain increased its market cap to $692.43 million, with shares trading between $43.16 and $11.89 over the past year.

title: Procter & Gamble wants to reinvent how you clean your home
summary: Procter & Gamble is introducing new cleaning products like Dawn Powerwash Dish Spray, designed to reduce water usage and adapt to evolving consumer habits. This shift is driven by the increasing awareness of water scarcity and changes in how people clean their homes, especially with more frequent, smaller clean-ups rather than large soaks. The company aims to innovate the user experience of cleaning, aligning with current disruptions and changing consumer expectations.

title: How A Satanic Rumor Almost Ruined Procter And Gamble
summary: In the early 1980s, a widespread rumor claimed that Procter & Gamble's president admitted to worshipping Satan on a talk show and that the company's logo contained satanic symbols. This led to P&G facing numerous calls and eventually lawsuits against individuals spreading the false information. Despite changing its logo and winning a significant lawsuit against Amway distributors who perpetuated the rumor, the company continued to battle these claims for decades, highlighting the damaging impact of conspiracy theories on businesses.

title: P&G's newest product is unlike anything its done before
summary: Procter & Gamble showcased its new EC30 waterless technology at the Consumer Electronics Show. This product represents a significant departure from the company's traditional offerings, highlighting an innovative approach for the consumer goods giant. The announcement was made by Andy Brownfield of the Cincinnati Business Courier.

title: P&G raises forecast after earnings top expectations, fueled by 8% jump in sales
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) raised its fiscal 2021 outlook for the second consecutive quarter after its Q2 revenue rose 8%, exceeding expectations. This growth was driven by increased demand for cleaning, grooming, and household products due to pandemic-driven at-home consumption trends. The company reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.64 and revenue of $19.75 billion, both surpassing analyst estimates.

title: Indian Toothpaste Market Size, Share, Growth, Industry Analysis, Opportunities and Forecast 2020-2026
summary: The Indian toothpaste market is projected to grow significantly at a CAGR of 7.2% from 2020 to 2026, driven by increasing disposable income, urbanization, and the growing popularity of ayurvedic products. Manufacturers are expanding their offerings in the ayurvedic segment and leveraging strong ad campaigns to increase product penetration. Key players in the market include Colgate-Palmolive Co., Patanjali Ayurveda, Procter & Gamble Co., and Dabur India Ltd.

title: Procter & Gamble’s Always teams up with Walmart to encourage girls to stay in sports
summary: Procter & Gamble's Always brand has partnered with Walmart to launch the #KeepHerPlaying campaign, encouraging girls to remain involved in sports for personal growth. The initiative, promoted by Olympic gymnast Laurie Hernandez, includes a $250,000 donation to the Women's Sports Foundation with a potential additional $250,000 based on campaign video views. The program aims to bolster girls' confidence, leadership, and teamwork skills, especially given the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on extracurricular activities.

title: UBS Asset Management acquires 7,977 sqm office asset in Paris
summary: UBS Asset Management's Real Estate & Private Markets has acquired a 7,977 sqm office asset called Union Square in Paris from AEW. Located in the Rueil-sur-Seine business district, the building is over two-thirds let and will undergo an enhancement program to increase its appeal and secure full occupancy. This acquisition aligns with UBS-AM's value-add investment strategy, targeting income potential and strong market demand for quality office space.

title: Harry's Inc Launches Haircare Brand Headquarters
summary: Harry's Inc., initially a direct-to-consumer razor brand, has launched a new haircare line called Headquarters, signaling an expansion beyond its core shaving products. This move comes after its planned $1.4 billion acquisition by Edgewell fell through due to FTC intervention, leaving Harry's as an independent entity. The company aims to differentiate itself by looking beyond traditional marketing and merger strategies.

title: How Procter & Gamble Is Committing to 2,021 Acts of Good This Year
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched a new campaign called "Lead With Love" with the ambitious goal of performing 2,021 acts of good in the coming year. This initiative builds on P&G's support for the UN Global Goals, covering areas like community impact, environmental sustainability, and racial equity. The campaign encourages individuals to participate through P&G Good Everyday, where their actions trigger donations to various causes, and aims to inspire kindness and positive change globally.

title: Reckitt invests in Bombay Shaving Co
summary: Reckitt Benckiser has led a Rs 45-crore strategic investment in Bombay Shaving Company, demonstrating large consumer goods companies' interest in youth-oriented digital brands. This investment will help Bombay Shaving Co expand into offline retail and leverage Reckitt's expertise in market understanding and R&D. The grooming startup aims to reach 50,000 stores in 30 cities by the end of 2021 and plans to launch new personal care brands to broaden its market beyond male grooming.

title: Forget Procter & Gamble: Here Are 3 Better Dividend Stocks
summary: This article suggests three dividend stocks—Stag Industrial, JPMorgan Chase, and American Electric Power—as better options than Procter & Gamble for income-focused investors. It highlights Stag Industrial's REIT structure and solid tenant base, JPMorgan Chase's financial resilience and growth in corporate/investment banking, and American Electric Power's strong dividend growth and proactive shift towards renewable energy sources. Each company's dividend yield, growth rate, and competitive advantages are detailed.

title: Kroger on Middle Tennessee Blvd. closing in February; pharmacy, fuel center will remain open
summary: Kroger announced the closure of its Middle Tennessee Boulevard grocery store at the end of February due to diminishing profitability, though its pharmacy and fuel center will remain open. Affected employees will be offered positions at other Kroger locations in the area. The company has invested over $30 million locally in recent years, including opening new stores and remodeling existing ones.

title: P&G has a new ad urging men to close the 'chore gap'
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched a new ad campaign, "Come Clean to Close the Chore Gap," through its Dawn and Swiffer brands, encouraging men to take on more household chores. The campaign, which includes a Super Bowl pre-game ad, highlights that in 65% of homes, most chores fall to one person, often women, and aims to promote more equitable division of labor, a message particularly relevant during the COVID-19 pandemic. This initiative continues P&G's strategy of integrating socially conscious messages into its advertising, following previous campaigns addressing "toxic masculinity" and racism.

title: P&G campaign asks for greater equality in household chores
summary: Procter & Gamble's Dawn dish soap and Swiffer cleaning products have launched a campaign called "Come Clean to Close the Chore Gap" to encourage more equal sharing of household chores. The campaign, which includes a Super Bowl pregame ad, highlights that most household work in 65% of U.S. families is done by one person, with women disproportionately affected, especially during the pandemic. P&G is also using the campaign to drive sign-ups to its rewards program, collecting first-party data and donating cleaning products for every registration.

title: Global Feminine Hygiene Products Market to Grow by $7.11 Billion During 2020-2024 | 32% Growth to Come From APAC | Technavio
summary: Technavio projects the global feminine hygiene products market to grow by $7.11 billion from 2020-2024, at a CAGR of over 4%. APAC is expected to contribute 32% of this growth, driven by key markets like China and Japan. The sanitary napkins segment will see significant growth due to government initiatives promoting hygiene awareness.

title: Abercrombie & Fitch elects Kenneth Robinson to its Board of Directors
summary: Abercrombie & Fitch has elected Kenneth Robinson as an independent director to its Board of Directors, where he will also serve on the audit and finance committee. Robinson brings over 40 years of consumer retail experience, including roles at Exelon Corporation and Procter & Gamble. His election expands the board to 13 members, and he expressed enthusiasm for the company's progressive stance on sustainability and diversity.

title: Top Secret: P&G selects two big brands for refillable deodorant launch
summary: Procter & Gamble has chosen its major brands, Secret and Old Spice, to introduce a new line of refillable deodorant products. This initiative marks a significant step for P&G in the sustainable consumer goods market. The launch is featured in the Cincinnati Business Courier.

title: P&G Appoints B. Marc Allen to Board of Directors
summary: The Procter & Gamble Company has appointed B. Marc Allen, Chief Strategy Officer and Senior Vice President of Strategy and Corporate Development at The Boeing Company, to its Board of Directors, effective February 10, 2021. Mr. Allen brings extensive experience in international operations, trade, law, government relations, strategy, and corporate development. P&G Chairman, President, and CEO David Taylor highlighted Allen's capabilities as a valuable addition to the Board as P&G continues to strengthen its global market position.

title: P&G continues forest degradation practices despite shareholder vote
summary: Despite a clear mandate from two-thirds of its voting shareholders to cease deforestation practices, Procter & Gamble (P&G) has failed to announce an action plan over 100 days later. The company continues to source from mills linked to significant forest degradation in Canada and has not shown meaningful progress in addressing human rights violations and deforestation in its palm oil supply chain. Environmental groups are urging P&G to reduce virgin fiber use, ensure supplier compliance with environmental and human rights standards, and engage with impacted communities.

title: P&G's newest deodorant is 10 years in the making
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched a new deodorant and antiperspirant product called Derma under its Secret brand. This product is the culmination of a decade of research and development. The launch signifies P&G's continuous innovation in personal care.

title: Procter & Gamble Co. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. (PG) stock fell 1.86% on Friday, closing at $127.12, underperforming the broader market and its competitors. The decline ended a three-day winning streak, and the stock closed $19.80 below its 52-week high. Competitors such as Johnson & Johnson, L'Oreal S.A. ADR, and Estee Lauder Cos. Cl A also saw declines but generally smaller percentages.

title: P&G CEO expects higher demand for cleaning products to outlast pandemic
summary: Procter & Gamble CEO David Taylor anticipates that elevated demand for cleaning and hygiene products will persist beyond the Covid-19 pandemic. He notes that consumers have ingrained new habits of cleaning and valuing the home, which will likely sustain for an extended period. This prediction is shared by other industry leaders, such as Clorox CEO Linda Rendle, as both companies have raised their sales outlooks.

title: Tristan Walker Sold His Multimillion-Dollar Brand to Procter & Gamble. Here's What He Wants Every Young Entrepreneur to Know
summary: Tristan Walker, founder of Walker & Company, discusses the inspiration behind his entrepreneurial journey, emphasizing the importance of leveraging unique lived experiences. His company, which sells grooming products for people of color, was acquired by Procter & Gamble and launched its Bevel hair care line in Walmart. Walker encourages young entrepreneurs to recognize and celebrate their distinct backgrounds as a source of strength and authenticity in business.

title: Top Women Profile: Tabata Gomez
summary: Tabata Gomez, Chief Marketing Officer at Stanley Black & Decker, shares her journey from cosmetics to power tools and her efforts to promote diversity and gender equality in the hardware industry. She discusses the successful re-launch of the Craftsman brand, challenges to unconscious bias, and Stanley Black & Decker's commitment to gender parity. Gomez also reflects on teaching her son about breaking stereotypes and achieving success.

title: Hershey threatens to suspend non-compliant suppliers in effort to cut deforestation
summary: Hershey has implemented a companywide policy to eliminate deforestation across its raw material supply chain by 2030, threatening to suspend or remove non-compliant suppliers. This new holistic approach replaces its previous commodity-by-commodity strategy and is part of a broader ESG agenda that includes reducing Scope 3 emissions and packaging weight. The policy outlines specific requirements for suppliers, including commitments to reforest, respect human rights, and avoid illegal harvesting, with a focus on high-risk commodities like cocoa, palm oil, soy, and pulp and paper.

title: Kimberly-Clark Names Robert Long as Chief Research and Development Officer
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corporation announced the appointment of Robert Long as its new Chief Research and Development Officer, effective March 15, 2021. In this newly created role, Long will oversee global research, development, innovation, and quality functions, reporting directly to CEO Mike Hsu and serving on the executive leadership team. Long brings over four decades of experience from companies like The Coca-Cola Company and Procter & Gamble, where he held senior R&D and innovation leadership positions.

title: Kimberly-Clark Names Coca-Cola Vet Robert Long Its 1st Chief R&D Officer
summary: Kimberly-Clark has appointed Robert Long, a veteran from The Coca-Cola Company and Procter & Gamble, as its first chief research and development officer, effective March 15. In this new global role, Long will oversee research, development, innovation, and quality functions, reporting to chairman and CEO Mike Hsu. Hsu anticipates Long will drive growth by enhancing brands and expanding markets, leveraging his extensive experience in R&D within the consumer goods sector, including Coca-Cola's innovation and P&G's various product categories.

title: P&G targets fastest-growing sports market with new Gillette sponsorship
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is expanding its marketing reach into the rapidly growing esports industry through a new Gillette brand sponsorship. This move targets the professional video gaming audience, which represents the fastest-growing segment in live event viewing globally. The initiative aims to connect the Gillette brand with this burgeoning market.
