title: Procter & Gamble Stock: 3 Reasons to Buy After the Recent Dip
summary: Despite being a recent underperformer in the S&P 500, Procter & Gamble (PG) presents a compelling investment opportunity. The company has demonstrated strong organic sales growth, outpacing competitors, and is capitalizing on a growing market for cleaning, health, and hygiene products. Furthermore, P&G boasts robust cash flows, enabling significant cash returns to investors through dividends and share buybacks, with expectations for its 64th consecutive dividend increase.

title: Stick to the Fundamentals with the Value-Focused 'VTV'
summary: The article highlights the Vanguard Value ETF (VTV) as a promising investment option for those looking to capitalize on the ongoing value stock comeback. VTV focuses on large-cap value stocks, offering stability during downturns and capturing upside potential in a recovering economic climate. The fund, which tracks the CRSP U.S. Large Cap Value Index, is up significantly in the past year and provides a convenient way to invest in large value stocks with stable revenues and dividend potential.

title: P&G jumps on crypto trend that's taking the art world by storm
summary: Procter & Gamble, known for its consumer goods, has entered the cryptocurrency space by releasing the world's first-ever toilet paper crypto collection. This move sees the company joining the non-fungible token (NFT) trend that is gaining traction in the art world and beyond. The initiative involves P&G's Charmin brand, leveraging its iconic bear mascot.

title: PureCycle Technologies completes business combination with Roth CH Acquisition I Co. and will begin trading on Nasdaq
summary: PureCycle Technologies has completed its business combination with Roth CH Acquisition I Co. and will begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "PCT." This transaction provides PureCycle with increased capital market access to scale its proprietary recycling process for polypropylene, transforming plastic waste into virgin-like resin. The company aims to revolutionize polypropylene recycling, a material with broad applications but a low current recycling rate.

title: Who will replace Procter & Gamble's CEO David Taylor?
summary: This article discusses the potential succession planning for Procter & Gamble's CEO David Taylor, who is nearing retirement age. While there's no immediate pressure for a change given P&G's strong performance, the article identifies Jon Moeller, the current COO, as a frontrunner and also highlights several other key executives, including three women and two Asia-born leaders, who are being groomed for top positions. It also details the recent financial performance of various P&G business units and touches on Taylor's tenure and the company's past challenges and successes.

title: P&G’s Marc Pritchard Is Using 'Constructive Disruption' to Reinvent Brand Building
summary: Marc Pritchard, Procter & Gamble's chief brand officer and Adweek's Performance Marketer of the Year, has championed "constructive disruption" to reinvent brand building amidst the challenges of 2020. P&G focused on leveraging data and technology for precision marketing, utilizing tools like search and one-to-one consumer engagement through apps and loyalty platforms. This approach allowed them to adapt to changing consumer behaviors during the pandemic and integrate purpose-driven marketing effectively.

title: Procter & Gamble Company
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is the world's largest consumer goods company, founded over 180 years ago. The company attributes its longevity and success to leadership, innovation, and citizenship, emphasizing responsible governance, transparency, and environmental protection. P&G aims to be a workplace where employees can take pride in their contributions.

title: P&G's SK-II opens film studio to elevate purpose-driven marketing
summary: P&G's skincare brand SK-II has launched SK-II Studio, a film division and content hub, to create purpose-driven marketing focused on social pressures affecting women. This initiative is part of its #ChangeDestiny campaign and will release eight original films in 2021, starting with "The Center Lane" about swimmer Ikee Rikako. SK-II will donate $1 for every view, up to $500,000, to organizations supporting women, aiming to elevate brand building beyond traditional advertising and meet consumer expectations for brands that take a stand on social issues.

title: Table of Experts: Women Who Lead
summary: This article features a "Table of Experts" discussion with four prominent women leaders: Megan Mikolaichik (Panera Bread), Kathy Osborn (Regional Business Council), Marcela Manjarrez Hawn (Centene Corp.), and Lisa Rock (National Medical Billing Services). They discuss navigating challenges, particularly during the past year, their management styles, prioritizing daily tasks, and the specific challenges women face in leadership roles. The experts also share insights on what younger generations bring to corporate culture, effective communication strategies, key traits for career advancement, and how their companies promote gender parity, offering advice for women in their careers.

title: Great News! Wilkinson Sword Bans Badger-Hair Brushes
summary: Edgewell Personal Care, the parent company of Wilkinson Sword and Schick, has banned badger-hair brushes following an exposé by PETA US on the cruel badger-hair industry. This move helps PETA in encouraging the personal-care sector to adopt more ethical practices. The article highlights the severe psychological distress and abuse badgers face on farms and in illegal captures, advocating for other companies to switch to cruelty-free alternatives.

title: Procter & Gamble’s New ‘Widen The Screen’ Program Aims To Diversify The Portrayal Of Black People In Advertising And Entertainment
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched "Widen The Screen," a new program aimed at increasing the accurate and diverse portrayal of Black people in advertising and entertainment. The initiative seeks to invest in Black directors, actors, crews, and media, fostering greater representation within the creative and media supply chain. P&G is partnering with various companies and organizations, including Spring Hill, Saturday Morning, and the Tribeca Film Festival, and also increasing investment in Black-owned media companies.

title: P&G Aims to Improve Portrayal of “Black Life” on Screen, Expands Inclusion Efforts for Black Creators
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has launched "Widen The Screen," an initiative to improve the portrayal of Black life in advertising, film, and television by increasing Black creators' inclusion and investment in Black-owned media. The program includes new films, talent development platforms, and partnerships aimed at combating stereotypes and fostering more diverse storytelling. This expands on P&G's previous efforts to promote racial equity and aims to create more accurate and dynamic representations of Black individuals.

title: Better Buy: Procter & Gamble or All 30 Dow Jones Stocks?
summary: This article argues that due to current market conditions, which are becoming a "stock picker's market," Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG) is a better investment than the entire Dow Jones Industrial Average. P&G offers safety, reliability, and stability, with its consumer staples products and low beta making it less susceptible to market-wide downturns. The author suggests adjusting portfolios to prioritize defensive stocks like P&G given perceived market overvaluation and potential for correction.

title: P&G amps up opportunities for Black creators across advertising, film and TV
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched "Widen The Screen," a new platform aimed at increasing the inclusion of Black creators in advertising, film, and television industries. This initiative includes an anthem film, new productions with diverse storytellers, and partnerships to support Black creators and combat misrepresentation. P&G also plans to increase its investments in Black-owned and -operated companies and collaborate with various organizations and production houses to drive real change in the industry.

title: P&G’s ‘Widen The Screen’ Ad Aims To Diversify ‘Black Life’ Onscreen
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched a new short film called "Widen The Screen" as part of its initiative to diversify the portrayal of Black people in media, advertising, TV, and film. The campaign aims to challenge existing stereotypes by showcasing the full spectrum of Black experiences beyond common tropes of struggle or triumph. P&G is partnering with production companies and investing in Black-owned media to foster systemic change and eliminate bias both in front of and behind the camera.

title: Colgate taps into the ‘oral beauty’ trend with new sub-brand for Gen Zers
summary: Colgate-Palmolive launched Co. by Colgate, a new oral care sub-brand targeting Gen Z consumers, sold exclusively through Ulta Beauty and its DTC site. The brand aims to tap into the "oral beauty" trend by merging oral care with self-care, as Gen Z increasingly views beauty as a way to fulfill self-care needs. Co. by Colgate features seven products priced from $8-$129 and plans to donate a portion of sales to charity, while also focusing on understanding and engaging with its target demographic.

title: Shoppers Start to See Effect of Higher Commodity Costs
summary: Consumers are beginning to experience the impact of rising commodity prices as manufacturers, including Kimberly-Clark, General Mills, and Hormel, pass increased costs onto shoppers. Kimberly-Clark specifically announced plans to raise prices across its North America consumer-products business to offset higher raw-material expenses. This trend reflects the strain Felt by companies as commodity prices climb.

title: Procter & Gamble’s environmental controversy escalates with protest in company’s hometown
summary: Activists from Stand.earth recently escalated their protest against Procter & Gamble in Cincinnati, broadcasting radio messages and holding demonstrations to highlight the company's alleged role in deforestation and human rights abuses through its supply chains. This protest occurred after P&G's "inadequate plans" to address these issues were announced, following a shareholder directive raised in October 2020. The activists accuse P&G of greenwashing and failing to commit to ending relationships with suppliers involved in destroying critical primary forests and violating human rights.

title: Kimberly-Clark says Cottonelle, Scott toilet paper price hikes coming
summary: Kimberly-Clark announced price increases "in the mid-to-high single digits" for Cottonelle, Scott toilet paper, and other baby/adult care products in North America, effective by late June. This move is necessary to offset significant commodity cost inflation. The announcement comes amidst recent concerns over potential toilet paper shortages due to the Suez Canal blockage and prior pandemic-induced stockpiling.

title: General Motors Pledges to Devote More Ad Dollars to Black-Owned Media
summary: General Motors announced its commitment to significantly increase its advertising spending with Black-owned media outlets, quadrupling the percentage from 2% to 8% by 2025. This decision follows pressure from Black media leaders and aims to foster greater diversity and inclusion in its marketing efforts. GM will also launch an "upfront" process for diverse media owners to submit business proposals.

title: P&G, Dove Push for More Equitable Representation in Media
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched "Widen the Screen," a platform to increase inclusion of Black creators and improve portrayals of Black life in media through new films, initiatives, and investments in Black-owned media. Simultaneously, Dove South Africa is challenging other brands to adopt more diverse talent in their ad campaigns by offering to subsidize booking costs, building on its years of promoting broader representations of beauty. Both companies aim to drive more equitable representation and challenge narrow beauty ideals within the advertising and media industries.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | P&G Worked With China Trade Group on Tech to Sidestep Apple Privacy Rules
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) collaborated with a Chinese trade group on a new technology, called CAID, to gather iPhone data for targeted ads. This effort aims to bypass Apple's new iOS 14.5 privacy features, which require user permission for app tracking. The technique, using device fingerprinting, would allow advertisers to continue tracking users despite Apple's policies, which explicitly prohibit such methods.

title: P&G reportedly testing Chinese workaround to Apple’s privacy changes
summary: Procter & Gamble is participating in a test in China of a method to collect iPhone data for ad targeting, as a potential way to circumvent Apple's new privacy features. This initiative, developed with the China Advertising Association, uses "device fingerprinting" technology (CAID) to track online consumers, which violates Apple's app rules. As a major advertiser, P&G is seeking alternative audience tracking methods to maintain ad efficiency given that many consumers are expected to opt out of device tracking.

title: Major League Soccer lands a top corporate sponsorship with Procter & Gamble
summary: Major League Soccer (MLS) has secured a five-year corporate sponsorship deal with Procter & Gamble (P&G), estimated to be worth between $80 million and $100 million. This partnership aims to help MLS recover from significant Covid-19 losses and leverage P&G's brand strength to promote the league to a growing North American soccer audience. P&G will sponsor key MLS events and use its product brands like Gillette, Old Spice, and Crest to promote the league, aligning with MLS's strategy to appeal to younger, diverse sports fans.

title: P&G Declares Dividend Increase
summary: The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG) announced an increased quarterly dividend of $0.8698 per share, representing a 10% increase from the previous dividend. This marks the 65th consecutive year P&G has increased its dividend and the 131st consecutive year it has paid a dividend. The company highlighted its commitment to returning cash to shareholders.

title: Procter & Gamble Kicks Off Major League Soccer Sponsorship
summary: Procter & Gamble has signed a multiyear advertising deal with Major League Soccer to broaden its appeal to younger demographics and the Hispanic market. This agreement includes sponsoring the Mexican National Team's U.S. Tour and supporting P&G's hometown MLS club, FC Cincinnati, as part of a strategy leading up to the 2026 FIFA World Cup. This marks P&G's significant entry into soccer marketing.

title: P&G Professional and Northland Properties Corporation Launch Partnership to Help Elevate Health & Safety
summary: P&G Professional has partnered with Northland Properties Corporation, Canada's largest privately-owned hospitality company, to enhance their PureClean programs. This collaboration will integrate P&G Professional's trusted cleaning brands like Tide Professional, Dawn Professional, and Health Canada-approved disinfectants Spic and Span and Comet into Northland's hotels, resorts, and restaurants to elevate health and safety standards for guests and staff. The initiative aims to build customer confidence by using well-known, effective cleaning solutions for increased hygiene in high-touch and heavily trafficked areas.

title: P&G’s “It’s Our Home” Shows How Small Actions at Home Can Make A Big Difference for Our Planet
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is launching a new "It's Our Home" campaign to highlight how small, sustainable actions at home can significantly impact the planet. Inspired by a study showing that most people want to be more sustainable but don't know how, P&G brands like Tide, Oral-B, and Gillette aim to make eco-friendly choices easier through product innovations and consumer education. The initiative underscores P&G's commitment to reducing environmental impact and helping consumers achieve a more sustainable lifestyle.

title: Fragrance Creators to Present Sean Broderick of Procter & Gamble With Extraordinary Leadership Award
summary: Fragrance Creators Association will present Sean Broderick of Procter & Gamble with a special Extraordinary Leadership Award for his instrumental role in helping the industry navigate and continue operations during the COVID-19 pandemic. Broderick facilitated coordination among key industry organizations and served as a vital resource for the fragrance value chain, providing guidance and data during bi-weekly leadership meetings. The award will be formally presented at Fragrance Creators' 2021 Mid-Year Business Meeting on July 22, 2021.

title: Procter & Gamble Splashes $3bn on Supplier Diversity
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has announced plans to spend $3 billion with diverse-owned businesses by 2030, building on its prior investment of $2.8 billion between 2008 and 2020. This initiative aims to increase diversity within its own supply base and encourage its suppliers to also diversify their networks, particularly increasing investment in women-owned businesses globally. P&G views a diverse supply chain as a critical element for innovation, market growth, and creating positive socio-economic impacts.

title: Procter & Gamble earnings beat as consumers hang on to pandemic cleaning habits; price hikes ahead
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) exceeded Wall Street's expectations for its fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue, driven by sustained consumer demand for cleaning supplies and revitalized interest in beauty products. The company announced upcoming price hikes on some products in autumn to offset rising commodity and freight costs. Despite the positive earnings, shares dipped slightly in premarket trading.

title: Procter & Gamble Will Raise Prices On Baby And Feminine Care Products In September
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it will raise prices on baby care, feminine care, and adult incontinence products starting in September to offset rising commodity prices. This move follows similar announcements from competitors Kimberly-Clark and Coca-Cola, as companies expect a short-term bump in inflation as the economy recovers. The price increases will be mid-to-high single-digit percentages and will vary by brand.

title: Procter & Gamble will raise prices in September to fight higher commodity costs
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it will increase prices on baby care, feminine care, and adult incontinence products starting in September to counter rising commodity costs. This move follows similar announcements from competitors like Kimberly-Clark and Coca-Cola, as companies aim to protect their profit margins. P&G stated the price increases would be in the mid-to-high single-digit range and that it is assessing other categories for potential future increases.

title: Procter & Gamble Will Raise Prices in September
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it will increase prices on various household staples, including baby products, adult diapers, and feminine-care brands, starting in September. This move, making it the latest and largest consumer-products company to do so, is a response to rising costs for raw materials like resin and pulp, as well as higher transportation expenses. The price increases come as the company reports slowing growth in its latest financial quarter.

title: Procter & Gamble announced as Major League Soccer sponsor
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has inked a multi-year, multifaceted sponsorship deal with Major League Soccer (MLS). This partnership will see P&G sponsor key MLS events like the All-Star Game and Campeones Cup, as well as the Mexico men’s national team’s US tour. The collaboration aims to leverage P&G's brand portfolio to connect with fans and help make soccer more accessible.

title: Procter & Gamble to raise prices on some paper products
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it will increase prices on certain paper products, such as Pampers diapers and Tampax tampons, by 5% to 9% starting in mid-September, citing rising commodity costs. This move follows a similar announcement by competitor Kimberly-Clark. Despite these cost pressures, P&G reported a strong financial quarter with a $3.3 billion profit and increased sales.

title: Sherwin-Williams Shareholders Elect New Director
summary: The Sherwin-Williams Company announced that Aaron M. Powell was elected to its Board of Directors at the company's Annual Meeting of Shareholders. Powell, currently President, Asia-Pacific Consumer Business for Kimberly-Clark Corporation, will also serve on the Board's Audit Committee. John G. Morikis, Chairman, President and CEO of Sherwin-Williams, highlighted Powell's extensive experience in global markets, operations, sales, marketing, and digital expertise.

title: P&G plans to quickly scale e-commerce capabilities as digital sales grow 50%
summary: Procter & Gamble reported a 50% year-over-year growth in e-commerce sales during its fiscal third-quarter, now accounting for 14% of global sales. This growth is driving P&G to rapidly scale its e-commerce capabilities, influencing areas like packaging design, to meet evolving consumer trends accelerated by the pandemic. Other major CPGs like Unilever are also increasing investments in high-growth digital segments.

title: Procter & Gamble Acquires Voost Vitamins
summary: Procter & Gamble has acquired Voost, an Australian brand specializing in effervescent vitamins, for an undisclosed sum. This move allows P&G to expand its portfolio in the growing vitamins, minerals, and supplements industry, particularly targeting the Australian market. Voost, founded in 2013, has achieved significant year-on-year sales growth of 50 percent, making it a leader in the effervescent vitamins subcategory in Australia.

title: Procter & Gamble Is One of the 2021 TIME100 Most Influential Companies | TIME
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) was recognized as one of the 2021 TIME100 Most Influential Companies due to its significant performance during the pandemic. The company saw a banner year with $71 billion in sales, a 6% increase, driven by high demand for its household products like Charmin and Tide. Additionally, P&G repurposed its manufacturing capabilities to produce hundreds of thousands of face shields for healthcare workers.

title: Procter & Gamble opens detergent factory in Romania
summary: Procter & Gamble has opened a new detergent factory in Romania. This investment signals continued growth and manufacturing presence for the consumer goods giant in the Romanian market, focusing on products within the chemicals and consumer goods industries.

title: PureCycle to invest $363 million in plastic recycling facility
summary: PureCycle Technologies LLC is investing $363 million to build a plastic recycling facility in Ironton, Ohio, creating 51 new jobs. This facility will recycle over 100 million pounds of polypropylene plastic annually, addressing the growing demand for recycled plastics and contributing to a solution for plastic waste. The project, supported by JobsOhio and other local economic development entities, will utilize PureCycle's proprietary technology to produce virgin-like recycled polypropylene.

title: WWD Beauty Inc ranks Top 10 beauty companies for 2020
summary: WWD Beauty Inc released its Top 100 rankings for 2020, highlighting the performance of major beauty multinationals and the impact of Covid-19. The report reveals that while many large companies faced declines, mass brands and those with diverse portfolios like L'Oréal and L Brands fared better. The top 10 list shows only four companies achieving double-digit billion-dollar revenues, with L'Oréal leading at US$31.95 billion, and includes financial figures for makeup, skincare, haircare, suncare, and deodorants.

title: PureCycle to invest $363 million, create 51 jobs in Ironton
summary: PureCycle Technologies LLC plans to invest $363 million to construct a polypropylene recycling plant in Lawrence County, Ohio, creating 51 high-wage jobs. The facility, located at a former Dow Chemical plant site, will revitalize existing buildings and produce over 105 million pounds of ultra-pure recycled polypropylene annually. This investment is part of PureCycle's U.S. expansion to meet demand for recycled polypropylene and address the plastics waste crisis, leveraging a proprietary process licensed from Proctor and Gamble.

title: Diapers, Cereal and, Yes, Toilet Paper Are Going to Get More Expensive (Published 2021)
summary: Major consumer goods companies like Procter & Gamble, Kimberly-Clark, and General Mills are raising prices on essential products due to increased commodity costs, supply-chain issues, and freight expenses. This shift reflects a change in how companies are responding to demand during the pandemic, with retailers now passing on higher costs to consumers rather than absorbing them as they did pre-pandemic. The pandemic-induced chaos in global shipping and a rapid shift in consumer buying habits are cited as primary drivers for these price increases.

title: When It Comes to Investing in Product Innovation, Large CPG Companies Could Learn a Lot from Their Smaller Competitors
summary: Large consumer packaged goods (CPG) companies spend significant amounts on R&D without seeing the sales boosts experienced by smaller competitors. Research by Gregory Carpenter and colleagues suggests that large CPG firms should focus on incremental innovation driven by consumer insights, rather than chasing blockbuster breakthroughs. This approach, exemplified by companies like Reckitt Benckiser, leads to more consistent sales growth and better stock performance.

title: Procter & Gamble raising prices on baby care, feminine care products
summary: Procter & Gamble announced price increases on baby care, feminine care, and adult incontinence products, including popular brands like Pampers, Luvs, Tampax, and Always. These price hikes, expected to be in the mid-to-high single-digit percentages, will begin in September to offset rising commodity costs and supply bottlenecks. Other companies like 3M and Coca-Cola are also implementing similar price adjustments.

title: The Stockout: Raising prices on disinfectants during COVID is not gouging
summary: Clorox is facing significant challenges, including rising input, manufacturing, and logistics costs, which have led to a contraction in its gross margin for the first time in 10 quarters. Despite these pressures, the company has been hesitant to raise prices on its cleaning products to avoid perceptions of price gouging during the pandemic. Other CPG companies like Procter & Gamble and Kimberly-Clark have announced price increases, suggesting Clorox may eventually follow suit, especially as widespread cost pressures could mitigate market share loss.

title: P&G’s Charmin Brand Dabbles with AI Digital Doppelganger
summary: P&G's Charmin brand has introduced BRB Bot, an AI-powered digital doppelganger that allows users to step away from video calls without anyone noticing. The bot uses machine learning and natural language processing to mimic real-time reactions and was unveiled with Niecy Nash and Juju Smith Schuster. While currently in beta, there are no immediate plans for a public release, as Charmin explores innovative bathroom technology to "Enjoy the Go."

title: Honest Co. CEO ready to face big-name competition like P&G and Revlon with 'clean' brand strength
summary: Honest Co.'s shares soared in its Nasdaq debut, but the company faces significant competition from established players like P&G and Revlon. Despite the successful IPO, one research group considers the stock 'overvalued,' indicating potential challenges ahead. The CEO is prepared to leverage the strength of its 'clean' brand to compete in the market.

title: Kroger Celebrates Small Business Week and Offers Retail Partnership Guidebook to Advance Supplier Inclusion
summary: Kroger announced new initiatives and progress in its supplier inclusion program, achieving $4.1 billion in diverse supplier spend in 2020 and introducing 107 new diverse suppliers. The company launched a Small Business Resource Guide and held its 3rd annual Supplier Inclusion Innovation Summit to further support diverse-owned enterprises. Kroger is also piloting a Multicultural Entrepreneurship Development program and will launch a Go Fresh & Local Supplier Accelerator.

title: Metro East distribution center to undergo $7M expansion
summary: TriStar Properties is investing $7 million to expand a distribution center in Edwardsville, Illinois, leased by Phillips 66. The project will add 60,000 square feet to the existing 102,500-square-foot facility within the Gateway Commerce Center. This expansion is expected to increase the building's value to approximately $18 million once completed in October.

title: Meghan Markle Partnering With Company She Challenged 28 Years Ago
summary: Meghan Markle and Prince Harry's Archewell Foundation has announced a multi-year global partnership with Procter & Gamble. This partnership will focus on gender equality, inclusive online spaces, and paralympic athletics. Notably, this comes 28 years after Meghan Markle, as an 11-year-old, successfully campaigned for Procter & Gamble to change a soap advertisement she deemed sexist.

title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's non-profit teams up with Procter & Gamble
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's Archewell Foundation announced a multi-year partnership with consumer goods giant Procter & Gamble. The collaboration will focus on gender equality, fostering inclusive online communities, and promoting "resilience and impact" through sports, though financial details were not disclosed. This partnership adds to the couple's various ventures in social work and media content creation since stepping away from royal duties.

title: How Meghan Markle’s Procter & Gamble Partnership Follows Woke-Washing Claim
summary: Meghan Markle and Prince Harry's Archewell Foundation announced a multiyear partnership with Procter & Gamble, a move that harks back to Markle's childhood criticism of the company's sexist advertising. This partnership is now drawing attention for P&G's recent "woke washing" marketing strategies, where it promotes social causes to sell products. Critics, including Piers Morgan, have previously taken issue with P&G's socially conscious campaigns, such as Gillette's toxic masculinity ad, raising questions about the authenticity of such corporate efforts.

title: How Proctor & Gamble Reacted to News Meghan Markle Called Out Sexist Ad
summary: Proctor & Gamble reacted positively to Meghan Markle's childhood letter calling out sexist advertising, noting they were "moved" by her activism for gender equality. The company has now partnered with Meghan and Prince Harry's Archewell Foundation to work on gender equality initiatives, underscoring their commitment to using advertising as a force for good. This collaboration follows Markle's successful campaign as a schoolgirl in 1993, which led P&G to change a sexist commercial.

title: Harry and Meghan partner with P&G — 28 years after she ripped its ‘sexist’ ads
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's Archewell Foundation has announced a global partnership with Procter & Gamble, focusing on gender equality, inclusive online spaces, and impact through sport. This partnership comes 28 years after Meghan Markle, as an 11-year-old, famously led a letter-writing campaign against P&G's "sexist" Ivory dish soap advertisement. Markle's childhood activism influenced the company to change its ad, a story she has often highlighted as foundational to her commitment to justice and equality.

title: Short seller's report targets PureCycle
summary: Hindenburg Research, a short seller, has published a report alleging that PureCycle Technologies is an example of executives enriching themselves while presenting unproven technology and unrealistic financial projections to public markets. PureCycle, a publicly traded company licensing PP purification technology from Procter & Gamble, immediately denied the allegations. The report led to a significant drop in PureCycle's stock price, prompting law firms to seek to represent investors who lost money.

title: Meghan Markle and Prince Harry Team Up With Procter & Gamble on a Multi-Year Partnership
summary: Meghan Markle and Prince Harry, through their Archewell Foundation, have announced a multi-year global partnership with Procter & Gamble. The initiative will focus on gender equality, creating more inclusive online spaces, and promoting resilience through sport. This collaboration comes nearly three decades after Meghan, at age 11, successfully campaigned for P&G to change a sexist dish soap advertisement.

title: Here's Why You Should Hold on to AptarGroup (ATR) Stock Now
summary: AptarGroup (ATR) is expected to continue benefiting from increased demand for hygiene products and vaccine components due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The company's strong Q1 earnings, positive Q2 guidance, strategic acquisitions, and innovative product launches further strengthen its investment profile. AptarGroup currently holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) and a VGM Score of B, indicating favorable investment potential when combined with its rank.

title: Diversity Demands from NYC Pension Overseer OK’d at DuPont, Union Pacific
summary: Two shareholder proposals from the NYC comptroller requiring DuPont and Union Pacific to disclose their workforce diversity by race, ethnicity, and gender have passed with overwhelming support. This marks a significant victory for investors and pension holders, with similar proposals expected for other companies like American Express and Procter & Gamble. The move aims to increase transparency and accountability in corporate diversity and inclusion efforts.

title: Why Google, Procter & Gamble veteran will lead IRI
summary: Kirk Perry, a veteran of Google and Procter & Gamble, has been appointed President and CEO of IRI. The article highlights his experienced background from major companies, signaling a new leadership direction for IRI. No further details are provided in this snippet regarding the "why" of his appointment.

title: Pampers & UNICEF: Pioneering Partnership Helps Save Estimated One Million Newborn Lives
summary: Pampers and UNICEF celebrated 15 years of their partnership, which has been instrumental in saving an estimated one million newborn lives globally from maternal and neonatal tetanus (MNT). This collaboration has also helped eliminate MNT in 26 countries and protected 100 million women and their babies. The initiative, funded through Pampers pack purchases, is highlighted as a best-in-class example of a cause-related partnership.

title: McDonald’s, Byron Allen dispute continues amid scrutiny into QSR ad-spending practices
summary: McDonald's announced plans to more than double its investments in diverse media partners following a discrimination lawsuit filed by Byron Allen's Allen Media Group. The lawsuit alleges racial stereotyping and refusal to contract based on race, seeking $10 billion in damages and claiming McDonald's operates a tiered advertising structure. McDonald's aims to increase its national advertising spending with Black-, Hispanic-, Asian Pacific American-, women- and LGBTQ-owned platforms to 10% by 2024, specifically boosting allocation for Black-owned businesses from 2% to 5%.

title: P&G Earns Seventh Straight Gartner Supply Chain Mastery Award
summary: P&G has received its seventh consecutive Gartner Supply Chain Mastery Award, an achievement that highlights its long-term excellence in supply chain management. This recognition comes despite the extreme disruptions caused by the pandemic, which tested P&G's supply chain significantly. P&G is one of only five companies, including Apple, Amazon, McDonald’s, and Unilever, to be recognized in the elite "Master" category, which acknowledges consistent top performance over many years.

title: Demand grows for grooming products, travel items as lockdown eases
summary: As pandemic lockdowns ease and vaccinations increase, demand for grooming products such as deodorant, teeth whitener, and perfume is on the rise. Sales of travel-related items like luggage, swimsuits, and even alarm clocks are also surging. Consumers are investing in personal care and apparel again, signaling a return to pre-pandemic routines and a desire to "pamper themselves" as they prepare to go out.

title: Procter & Gamble Co. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. (PG) stock saw a slight loss of 0.22% on Wednesday but still outperformed some competitors, despite the overall market experiencing a favorable trading session. The company's shares closed below its 52-week high, and trading volume was slightly below its 50-day average. Its performance was mixed compared to rivals like Johnson & Johnson and L'Oreal, while Estee Lauder saw a gain.

title: Amy Chang and Calvin McDonald Elected to The Walt Disney Company Board of Directors
summary: The Walt Disney Company announced the election of Amy Chang and Calvin McDonald to its Board of Directors, effective immediately. Robert A. Iger highlighted their expertise in technology, consumer experience, and scaling businesses. Both Chang and McDonald expressed excitement about contributing to Disney's innovation and growth.

title: Procter & Gamble named official presenting sponsor of annual Bayou Classic
summary: Procter & Gamble has been named the Official Presenting Sponsor of the 48th Annual Bayou Classic, extending its corporate partnership agreement with Grambling University Foundation, Inc. and Southern University System Foundation, Inc. This sponsorship, part of a multiyear agreement, allows P&G to further demonstrate its support for Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and promote its brands through the Bayou Classic's various platforms. The event, ranked as the No. 1 HBCU Classic in the nation, will take place on November 27, 2021, in New Orleans.

title: One way companies are concealing higher prices: Smaller packages
summary: Companies are increasingly using "shrinkflation"—reducing product size while maintaining or increasing prices—to offset rising labor and material costs. This strategy allows them to pass on expenses to consumers without overtly raising prices, leading to smaller packaging for various household staples. Experts anticipate this trend will continue to grow in the coming months.

title: Giant Food Partners With P&G and Kellogg’s for Pride Month
summary: Giant Food is partnering with Procter & Gamble and Kellogg's to celebrate Pride Month throughout June, featuring a dedicated e-commerce experience with exclusive recipes by celebrity chef Elizabeth Falkner and spotlighting LGBT-owned brands. The initiative also includes special offers on P&G products, the limited-edition "Together With Pride" cereal from Kellogg's and GLAAD, and a matching donation of $25,000 to benefit the "Can't Cancel Pride 2021" event. This effort builds on Giant Food's ongoing commitment to supporting the LGBTQ+ community and businesses.

title: MacNeill Pride Group Appoints CEO
summary: MacNeill Pride Group (MPG) has appointed Keith Bornholtz as its new CEO, bringing over 30 years of experience in consumer products to the role. Concurrently, MPG announced the addition of four new directors to its Board: David Tanner, Jessica Klodnicki, Kevan Talbot, and Joe Steranka, strengthening its leadership with diverse industry expertise. MPG is a portfolio company of Centre Partners and includes brands such as ORCA and GCI Outdoor.

title: What P&G Can Learn from its Peers
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is criticized for its slow progress in addressing deforestation and intact forest degradation in its supply chain, receiving an 'F' grade from Rainforest Action Network (RAN). The article highlights how other consumer goods giants like Unilever and Mars are implementing more robust sustainability policies, including enhanced traceability, accountability, and commitments to human rights and emissions reduction. P&G is urged to adopt similar practices to catch up with its peers and meet environmental, social, and corporate governance leadership expectations.

title: Justin Baldoni’s Wayfarer Studios to Launch ‘The Man Enough Podcast’ in Deal With Procter & Gamble (Exclusive)
summary: Justin Baldoni's Wayfarer Studios is launching 'The Man Enough Podcast' next Monday in a significant partnership with Procter & Gamble. This deal also includes P&G co-financing and co-producing other film, TV, and new media projects with Wayfarer Studios. The podcast, inspired by a video series and book, will feature conversations on topics like fatherhood and body image with guests such as Matthew McConaughey and Shawn Mendes.

title: General Mills, Mars, Target among brands committed to GroupM's Black-owned media initiative
summary: GroupM announced that 20 major clients, including General Mills, Mars, and Target, have committed to allocating at least 2% of their annual media budgets to Black-owned media companies as part of its Media Inclusion Initiative (MII). This move reflects a broader industry push toward diversity, equity, and inclusion in advertising, spurred by recent calls for racial justice. Target has pledged an even higher commitment of 5% of its budget towards Black-owned media starting in 2022.

title: Digital Watermarking Technology Optimizes Packaging Line Efficiencies at P&G
summary: Procter & Gamble has implemented Digimarc's digital watermarking technology on its Dawn and Fairy liquid soap bottles to enhance packaging line efficiencies and store enterprise data. This technology uses covert codes on labels that can be read by various devices, allowing for faster inspection speeds and reduced camera requirements. The pilot program, conducted across facilities in the Czech Republic, UK, and U.S., demonstrated significant improvements in productivity.

title: Is Polypropylene Recycling Hitting Its Stride in 2021?
summary: The article discusses the significant strides being made in polypropylene (PP) recycling in 2021, highlighted by increased collaboration between CPG companies, suppliers, and recycling organizations. The Recycling Partnership's Polypropylene Recycling Coalition has issued grants to enhance PP sortation at MRFs and consumer education. Additionally, Procter & Gamble's long-term investment in PP recycling has led to a collaboration with PureCycle to commercialize a proprietary purification process, aiming to produce over 1 billion lbs of recycled PP annually.

title: How Procter & Gamble Plans to ‘Widen the Screen’ for Black Creators and Media Companies
summary: Procter & Gamble's chief brand officer, Marc Pritchard, has launched a new initiative titled "Widen the Screen" to promote racial equity within the advertising and media industries. This program aims to support Black creators and media companies by connecting ad spending and CPMs to equity. The initiative kicks off with P&G's continued partnership with Queen Latifah on the third season of her documentary series, Queen Collective.

title: Who was George Cates? Civic leader built a company, helped shape modern Memphis | Evanoff
summary: George E. Cates, a Memphis civic leader and real estate entrepreneur, passed away at age 83. He founded Mid-America Apartment Communities Inc. (MAA), one of the nation's largest apartment owners, and was a significant philanthropist who contributed to the city's growth, including the Grizzlies pro basketball team and the Crosstown Concourse. His legacy extends through his family and the company culture he fostered, emphasizing community and sustainable growth.

title: NAD Performs a Check-up on P&G’s Claims for Crest Whitening Emulsions
summary: The National Advertising Division (NAD) reviewed claims made by Procter & Gamble (P&G) for its Crest Whitening Emulsions product, following a challenge from SmileDirectClub, LLC. The NAD found some claims, such as "100% whiter" and "virtually no sensitivity," to be substantiated but recommended modifications or discontinuations for others like "best in class results" and "stays on teeth 10x longer." P&G agreed to comply with the NAD's decision.

title: Procter & Gamble, PepsiCo, Unilever Are Developing 'False' Solutions To Plastic Pollution, Reveals Report
summary: A report by the non-profit Break Free From Plastic movement reveals that major FMCG companies like Procter & Gamble, PepsiCo, and Unilever are largely investing in "false solutions" to plastic pollution. Out of 265 corporate projects analyzed from 2018 to April 2021, only 15% focused on proven methods like reuse, refill, and alternative delivery systems, with the vast majority being ineffective or even damaging. Environmental advocates urge these companies to end their reliance on single-use plastics and scale up genuine reuse-based systems instead of promoting misleading initiatives.

title: Clorox CEO Linda Rendle talks candidly about rising to the top
summary: Clorox CEO Linda Rendle discusses her journey to becoming a chief executive, emphasizing the importance of diverse leadership styles and the support of mentors. She aims to change the narrative of what a CEO should be, highlighting how her introverted nature and active listening skills have been assets. Rendle also shares advice for young women, encouraging them to recognize and leverage their unique strengths.

title: Marc Pritchard: ‘Choose equality as the systemic way of bringing creativity to life’
summary: Procter & Gamble's chief brand officer, Marc Pritchard, emphasized the critical role of diversity, equality, and inclusion in the creative ecosystem during Cannes Lions. He urged brands to integrate equality into every aspect of creativity, rather than treating it as an afterthought. Pritchard outlined a three-step approach—start inside, use your voice, and change the system—to achieve sustainable progress in this area.

title: P&G's Europe president on scaling better consumer products for a more sustainable planet
summary: Loic Tassel, President of P&G Europe, discusses the company's commitment to climate neutrality by 2030 and its efforts to scale sustainable products and practices. Europe plays a crucial role as a "lighthouse" for pioneering innovations and setting sustainability trends, which also helps P&G prepare for upcoming regulations like the European Green Deal. Tassel emphasizes educating consumers for more sustainable product use and highlights his personal commitment to environmental responsibility.

title: P&G’s Lela Coffey on ‘mirroring the consumers we’re trying to serve’
summary: This article features Lela Coffey of Procter & Gamble, discussing the importance of reflecting the consumer base. It highlights her perspective on serving consumers, likely presented as part of the "Leading Women 2021" series by Ad Age. The piece focuses on P&G's strategy as articulated by Coffey.

title: P&G debuts Nervive line focused on nerve pain
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched a new line of daily supplements called Nervive in the U.S., inspired by its international top-selling nerve care brand, Neurobion. The Nervive line aims to address nerve care and provide relief for occasional nerve aches, weakness, and discomfort often associated with aging. Products include Nerve Health, Nerve Relief, and Nerve Relief PM, formulated to support nerve function.

title: Be Seen, Be Heard: Driving Visibility of the LGBTQ+ Community
summary: P&G's Global LGBTQ+ Equality Program Leader, Brent Miller, discusses the importance of authentic LGBTQ+ representation in advertising and media to foster equality and inclusion. He highlights P&G's 4R Framework for engaging diverse consumers and their ongoing commitment to LGBTQ+ visibility, including campaigns for brands like Pantene and a partnership with GLAAD for The Visibility Project. The article emphasizes that while progress has been made, continuous effort is needed to ensure meaningful engagement and support for the LGBTQ+ community.

title: The startup helping P&G, Mercedes-Benz replace petrochemicals
summary: Twelve, a carbon transformation company formerly known as Opus 12, has secured $57 million in Series A funding to scale its electrolysis technology. This technology converts industrial CO2 emissions into ingredients for various products, aiming to replace petrochemicals in items from sneakers to detergents, and is already being used by P&G and Mercedes-Benz. The company plans to use the new capital to transition its systems from pilot size to industrial scale, offering a solution for businesses to achieve climate goals while maintaining product performance.

title: P&G Declares Quarterly Dividend
summary: The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG) has declared a quarterly dividend of $0.8698 per share, payable on or after August 16, 2021. This dividend marks 131 consecutive years of payments and 65 consecutive years of dividend increases, showcasing P&G's commitment to returning value to its shareholders. The company serves consumers globally with a strong portfolio of trusted brands across various categories.

title: Procter & Gamble: A Force for Good? - The Understory
summary: The Rainforest Action Network critiques Procter & Gamble's environmental and human rights record, highlighting its significant contribution to deforestation through the sourcing of ingredients like palm oil and pulp & paper. The article argues that despite shareholder pressure, P&G lags behind competitors in adopting and implementing No Deforestation, No Peat, No Exploitation (NDPE) policies. It calls for P&G to suspend sourcing from problematic suppliers, respect Indigenous rights, and commit to ending deforestation across its supply chains to become a true "force for good."

title: Focus: Getting the cap on the bottle: Inside P&G's robot ambitions
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is using advanced robotics and automation to maintain its competitive edge in the consumer goods market by reducing manufacturing costs and improving efficiency. Despite being known for branding, P&G develops its own automation solutions, focusing on tasks like precise packaging and handling diverse product shapes. This push for automation is also driven by the need for social distancing during the pandemic and labor shortages, with P&G continuously exploring new robotic applications for its factories.

title: Procter and Gamble launches first paper Lenor bottle with Paboco
summary: Procter and Gamble (P&G) has partnered with Paboco to introduce the first paper bottle for its Lenor fabric softener brand, which will be trialed in Western Europe next year. This initiative aligns with P&G's goal to reduce virgin plastics by 2030 and explores more sustainable packaging options, following Lenor's existing use of recycled plastic. The paper bottle is made from FSC-certified paper and includes a thin plastic barrier from post-consumer recycled PET.

title: P&G pivots approach to office space post-pandemic: PHOTOS - Cincinnati Business Courier
summary: Procter & Gamble is changing its approach to office space in the wake of the Covid-19 pandemic, accelerating a shift that began by taking cues from Silicon Valley startups. This change is highlighted with photos of P&G's innovative office environments. The article by Andy Brownfield details how the consumer goods giant is adapting its workplace strategy.

title: Why your cereal boxes and ice cream cartons are shrinking
summary: The article discusses "shrinkflation," a tactic where manufacturers reduce product sizes while maintaining or increasing prices, often seen during periods of inflation. Consumers are less likely to notice size reductions compared to direct price hikes. The piece provides examples like cereal and ice cream, noting that companies justify these changes due to rising costs for ingredients, transportation, and labor.

title: Campbell’s commemorates updated soup can labels with NFT collection
summary: Campbell's is launching a 100-piece NFT collection by artist Sophia Chang to celebrate the redesign of its iconic soup can labels. The collection, titled "AmeriCANa — Sophia Chang X Campbell's," will benefit Feeding America, and the brand is partnering with Ntwrk and Aerial to offset the carbon footprint of the NFTs. This initiative ties into current marketing trends by engaging with NFTs, addressing sustainability, and updating the brand's connection to art and popular culture.

title: Procter & Gamble names Jon Moeller as new CEO, will replace current chief David Taylor in November
summary: Procter & Gamble announced Jon Moeller will become CEO in November, replacing current chief David Taylor, who will transition to executive chairman. Moeller, currently COO and vice chairman, has been with P&G since 1988. Taylor's leadership saw a proxy battle with investor Nelson Peltz in 2017.

title: Ex-Staples chief Sandy Douglas to become new UNFI CEO
summary: J. Alexander (Sandy) Miller Douglas, former chief executive officer of Staples Inc., is set to become the new CEO of United Natural Foods Inc. (UNFI), succeeding the retiring Steven Spinner. Douglas will begin his role on August 9, with Spinner transitioning to an advisory position. This appointment follows a ten-month search to find a replacement for Spinner, who has led UNFI since 2008 and oversaw the significant acquisition of Supervalu Inc.

title: Strong Leadership to Take P&G Forward
summary: P&G announced significant leadership changes with Jon Moeller elected as President and Chief Executive Officer, effective November 1, 2021, succeeding the current CEO. Shailesh Jejurikar was also elected Chief Operating Officer, effective October 1, 2021. The outgoing CEO will transition to Executive Chairman, supporting the new leadership team.

title: Procter & Gamble CEO David Taylor to Step Aside
summary: Procter & Gamble CEO David Taylor will step down after a six-year tenure, during which he navigated an activist investor, revived sales, and led the company through a pandemic. He will be succeeded by his top deputy, Jon Moeller, on November 1st. Moeller has served as COO for the past two years and was previously the company's finance chief.

title: Vittorio Cretella left school at 17 to join the Italian Army. Now he’s CIO at Procter & Gamble.
summary: Vittorio Cretella, CIO of Procter & Gamble, discusses his unconventional career path from the Italian Army to leading digital transformation at the $300+ billion CPG company. He emphasizes the importance of diversity and inclusion in hiring, along with the pervasive role of digital transformation, machine learning, and cloud adoption in P&G's strategy. Cretella also highlights his work with NPower, a non-profit helping veterans and underserved youth find careers in tech, and P&G's neurodiversity hiring program.

title: Procter & Gamble earnings beat, but company warns cost pressure will weigh on future profits
summary: Procter & Gamble exceeded quarterly earnings and revenue expectations, driven by increased sales of premium health and personal care products. However, the company cautioned that rising commodity and freight costs could negatively impact future profits by approximately $1.9 billion. In response to these escalating costs, P&G plans to implement price increases on some of its products this fall.

title: 5 things to know before the stock market opens Friday
summary: On Friday, July 30, the stock market was poised for a lower open, with Nasdaq futures leading declines due to Amazon's revenue miss. Despite this, all three major benchmarks were still on track for solid monthly gains. Investors were also digesting the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, which came in slightly below estimates, and mixed earnings reports from Dow companies like Chevron, Caterpillar, and Procter & Gamble.

title: Procter & Gamble Stock Climbs. Earnings Show Headwinds.
summary: Procter & Gamble reported strong quarterly results with sales and earnings exceeding expectations, leading to a climb in its stock. However, the company also warned that higher commodity prices and freight costs would negatively impact profits in the upcoming fiscal year.

title: 5 takeaways from P&G's leadership change
summary: Procter & Gamble announced Jon Moeller will become the new CEO in November, replacing David Taylor, who will become executive chairman. This transition is seen as a logical pick for a smooth shift in strategy, given Moeller's extensive involvement in major company decisions over the last decade. The article highlights Moeller's unusual path to CEO through finance, the challenges ahead for P&G including economic uncertainties and potential executive departures, and the concurrent promotion of Shailesh Jejurikar to COO to retain top talent.

title: How P&G's $140 billion man cemented his legacy
summary: David Taylor, CEO of Procter & Gamble, is set to step down in November after three months. He leaves the company in its strongest financial health in decades. The article discusses his legacy and P&G's future outlook under new leadership.

title: Eastman enters into partnership with Procter & Gamble
summary: Procter & Gamble has partnered with Eastman to incorporate Eastman Renew materials into its products and packaging, aiming to reduce reliance on virgin plastics and promote a circular economy. The collaboration will also focus on advocacy and infrastructure development to increase plastic recycling rates, particularly for hard-to-recycle plastics. Eastman plans to open a large molecular recycling facility in 2022 to process over 200 million pounds of plastic scrap annually.

title: P&G Ventures Among Top 20 Best Workplaces for Innovators According to Fast Company
summary: P&G Ventures, Procter & Gamble's internal startup studio, has been recognized by Fast Company as one of the top 20 Best Workplaces for Innovators for 2021, ranking 19th. The studio was honored for its unique business model that fosters innovation by partnering with entrepreneurs and startups to develop new fast-moving consumer goods brands in categories outside P&G's current portfolio. This recognition highlights P&G Ventures' success in launching brands like Zevo, OPTE, Bodewell, and Kindra through a collaborative approach combining startup agility with P&G's resources.

title: Procter & Gamble’s path to constructive disruption
summary: P&G CEO David Taylor discusses the concept of "constructive disruption" and how it influences the company's innovation, growth, and sustainability strategies. He highlights P&G's efforts in R&D, supply chain resilience, reducing environmental impact through new formulations and packaging, and fostering a culture of passionate collaboration and diversity. The interview also covers challenges in reducing packaging and water usage, along with evolving consumer expectations regarding ESG.

title: The end of the Nelson Peltz era at P&G? Hedge fund manager exits board
summary: Hedge fund manager Nelson Peltz is exiting Procter & Gamble's board of directors, four years after a significant proxy fight to influence the company. While his firm, Trian Fund Management, remains a major investor, Peltz will retire from the board at the upcoming annual meeting. This departure comes as incoming CEO Jon Moeller prepares to take over and after a period of healthy sales and profit growth for P&G.

title: Eastman Enters into Partnership with Procter & Gamble
summary: Eastman and Procter & Gamble have partnered to accelerate the transformation of plastic packaging and collaborate on recycling solutions to enable a circular economy. P&G will integrate Eastman Renew materials, made from molecular recycling technologies using waste plastic, into select products and packaging. The collaboration also aims to expand the collection of hard-to-recycle plastics and drive critical changes in recycling infrastructure.

title: Eastman CEO touts P&G partnership as company tries to change the 'whole game' around recycling
summary: Eastman CEO Mark Costa highlights a partnership with Procter & Gamble as a crucial step in a new approach to plastic recycling. This initiative, called "molecular recycling," aims to tackle the 70% of plastic waste that currently ends up in landfills. Costa states that this method creates an "infinite life" for plastics, transforming waste into valuable, high-quality material for a circular economy.

title: P&G and Coke’s pandemic performances prove it: You don’t cut ad spend in a crisis
summary: This article argues that companies should not cut ad spending during a crisis, using Procter & Gamble and Coca-Cola's pandemic performances as examples. P&G doubled down on marketing and saw revenues surge, while Coca-Cola cut ad spend and experienced dwindling revenues. The author, Mark Ritson, emphasizes that maintaining advertising investment during downturns leads to stronger brand health and competitive advantage.

title: Procter & Gamble set to dethrone Amazon as world’s biggest advertiser
summary: Procter & Gamble is projected to surpass Amazon as the world's largest advertiser. This report from Ad Age Datacenter indicates a significant shift in global advertising spending.

title: PureCycle technology to head to South Korea
summary: PureCycle Technologies Inc. has signed an MOU with South Korea-based SK Global Chemical to explore building and operating a facility in South Korea to recycle polypropylene scrap into ultra-pure polypropylene resin. This partnership aims to advance plastic circularity in the Asia Pacific region, leveraging PureCycle's solvent-based recycling technology. Both companies express a strong commitment to reducing plastic waste and creating a circular economy for plastics.

title: How I went from chemical engineer to CEO of P&G Beauty
summary: Alex Keith, CEO of Procter & Gamble's Global Beauty business, shares her unconventional career path from chemical engineer to CEO, her experiences leading during a pandemic, and insights on retaining diverse talent. She discusses the importance of mentorship, stepping outside one's comfort zone, and fostering an inclusive culture within a company. Keith also reflects on how her perspective on being over 50 has changed and the lessons she learned about human connection and leadership flexibility during the pandemic.

title: RPM International names new president of its Consumer Group
summary: RPM International Inc. has appointed Bill Spaulding as the new president of its Consumer Group, effective September 1, succeeding Terry Horan. Concurrently, Jeff Ackerberg will become president of Rust-Oleum, and Mark Heird will take over as president of DAP. These leadership changes involve promoting several veteran executives within RPM's subsidiaries.

title: How I went from chemical engineer to CEO of P&G Beauty
summary: Alex Keith, CEO of P&G's Global Beauty business, discusses her non-traditional career path from chemical engineer to leading a $13.4 billion portfolio. She shares insights on overcoming barriers as a woman in a top leadership role, the challenges and solutions for retaining diverse talent, and key leadership lessons learned while managing a global team during the pandemic. Keith also reflects on evolving perceptions of women over 50 in the workforce.

title: Procter & Gamble regains its title as top global advertiser
summary: Procter & Gamble has reclaimed its position as the world's top advertiser, surpassing Amazon, with a marketing expenditure of $11.5 billion in its last fiscal year. This resurgence highlights the CPG giant's strategy of maintaining ad spending even during difficult economic times, a move that brand consultants argue has consistently benefited the company. While Amazon has the capacity to increase its ad spending significantly, P&G's continued investment in marketing has proven effective in sustaining its brand presence and sales growth.

title: Coty Escapes Class Action Claims That it Misled Investors With $12.5 Billion P&G Beauty Deal
summary: Coty and its officers successfully fended off a class action lawsuit alleging they misled investors regarding its $12.5 billion P&G Specialty Beauty Business acquisition. A New York federal court dismissed the amended complaint, finding that shareholders failed to plausibly allege actionable omissions or fraudulent intent concerning integration issues, marketing disclosures, or delayed goodwill impairment. The court sided with Coty, stating the company consistently updated investors on challenges.

title: Procter & Gamble has a brand problem
summary: A survey by Fortune and Civis Analytics reveals that Procter & Gamble has a significant generational favorability gap, with only 36% of 18–34 year olds having a favorable view compared to 87% of those over 65. This gap is largely attributed to younger Americans not having heard of P&G, despite the company's efforts in environmental sustainability and its massive advertising budget for individual brands like Tide and Crest. While P&G has the largest net favorability gap, its overall net favorability score remains high at +50 points.

title: Powell picked as Pizza Hut’s new CEO
summary: Aaron Powell has been appointed chief executive officer of the global Pizza Hut division at Yum! Brands, Inc., effective Sept. 20. He will oversee Pizza Hut's growth strategies, franchise operations, and performance worldwide. Powell brings over 25 years of experience from Kimberly-Clark Corp. and other companies, specializing in business-to-business and consumer packaged goods sectors.

title: P&G’s Board Must Be Accountable for Forest Destruction
summary: Ten months after Procter & Gamble's shareholders called on the company to address its impacts on climate-critical forests and Indigenous rights, P&G has failed to take meaningful action. This article details P&G's continued role in driving deforestation and human rights violations through its tissue and palm oil supply chains, and calls for investors to hold the Board of Directors accountable by voting against Angela Braly and James McNerney.

title: Yum! Brands Appoints Pizza Hut Division Chief Executive Officer to Drive Global Brand Strategies and Growth
summary: Yum! Brands announced the appointment of Aaron Powell as the global Pizza Hut Division Chief Executive Officer, effective September 20, 2021. Powell, former President of Kimberly-Clark Corporation’s Asia-Pacific Consumer Business, will be responsible for driving Pizza Hut's growth strategies and franchise operations worldwide. This appointment aims to further implement best practices and continue growth for franchisees and shareholders, with Kevin Hochman and Vipul Chawla reporting to Powell.

title: 2021 Annual Report
summary: This document is the 2021 Annual Report for Procter & Gamble, detailing financial highlights, strategic approaches, and citizenship efforts. It outlines the company's performance, winning strategy centered on a strong portfolio and superiority, and its commitment to ESG principles. The report also highlights P&G's leadership and organizational culture.

title: Citizenship at P&G
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) highlights its commitment to "Citizenship," encompassing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) efforts. The article details P&G's progress and future goals in environmental sustainability, equality & inclusion, community impact, and ethical governance, emphasizing its belief in being "a force for good and a force for growth." This includes reducing carbon emissions, promoting diversity, providing clean drinking water, and advocating for social equity.

title: A Strong & Focused Portfolio
summary: Procter & Gamble's strategy is built on a strong, focused portfolio of 10 daily-use product categories where performance is key to brand choice. These categories, including Fabric Care, Home Care, and Personal Health Care, are financially attractive and leverage P&G's strengths, holding leading or significant market positions. The company continuously aims to enhance the superiority of its offerings across these performance-driven categories.

title: Procter & Gamble Taps NFL in Bid to Boost New Tide Habit
summary: Procter & Gamble is partnering with the NFL to promote its "cold water wash" initiative for Tide detergent, aiming to change household laundry habits to save energy and money. Sixteen NFL teams, including the Cincinnati Bengals, will participate by washing their jerseys in cold water with Tide, providing a powerful endorsement for the campaign. This collaboration builds on previous successful advertising partnerships between Tide and the NFL, utilizing traditional TV ads, digital elements, and even sweepstakes with talking washing machines.

title: Why Procter & Gamble is giving Steve Chabot the cold shoulder
summary: Procter & Gamble has withheld donations to Republican Congressman Steve Chabot's 2022 campaign, a departure from their long-standing support, presumably due to his vote to overturn the 2020 election results. This decision follows a January announcement by P&G to reconsider support for politicians who voted against certifying the election. Chabot's campaign argues that P&G should continue supporting "results-oriented Republican leaders" who advocate for pro-growth policies.

title: P&G promotes leaders to key positions
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced key leadership changes, naming Monica Turner as president of its North American business and Carolyn Tastad as CEO of its healthcare division. These promotions highlight P&G's focus on strengthening leadership in its largest and most profitable region and its healthcare sector.

title: P&G promotes three women to top executive ranks as new CEO prepares to take over
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced several top executive promotions and retirements as Jon Moeller prepares to take over as CEO on November 1st. In a significant move, three women have been promoted to key leadership roles, potentially positioning them as future CEO candidates for the company, which has never had a female chief executive. These changes involve shifts in leadership for major business units like Family Care, Health Care, and North American operations, impacting divisions responsible for significant portions of P&G's total sales.

title: Commercial Metals Company Announces Appointment Of Gary E. McCullough To Board Of Directors
summary: Commercial Metals Company (NYSE: CMC) announced the appointment of Gary E. McCullough to its Board of Directors, effective October 12, 2021. Mr. McCullough brings over 30 years of business experience, including leadership roles at ARI Packaging, Career Education Corporation, and senior positions at Abbott Laboratories, Wm. Wrigley Jr. Company, and Procter & Gamble. He will serve on the Compensation and Finance Committees, bringing the total number of directors to 10.

title: Introducing Michelle Reynolds, Reddit’s Chief Accounting Officer
summary: Reddit has announced the appointment of Michelle Reynolds as its first Chief Accounting Officer. Reynolds brings over 15 years of experience from Snap Inc. and other companies, and will be responsible for improving financial and accounting processes, and developing reporting practices. She will report directly to Reddit’s CFO Drew Vollero, with a focus on building a world-class financial team as the business continues to grow.

title: Kroger unveils new citrusy shopping cart icon
summary: Kroger has unveiled a new shopping cart-inspired icon featuring a citrusy basket, aligning with its "Fresh for Everyone" slogan and refreshed logo. This new visual aims to create an instant association with freshness for the Kroger Family of Companies. The company also reported Q2 results with a 43% profit drop but raised its annual profit forecast, while its stock saw a 7.5% decline.

title: Procter & Gamble to invest US$5.8 million dollars to increase Argentina production
summary: Procter & Gamble plans to invest US$5.8 million (600 million pesos) to modernize and expand its production lines in Argentina. This investment will improve its plant in Pilar, Buenos Aires, and double razor production at its Villa Mercedes plant, aiming to localize manufacturing of previously imported products and reduce foreign exchange spending.

title: ​​Tom’s of Maine False Advertising Claims Dropped As Colgate Exits Class Action Lawsuit
summary: Colgate and lead plaintiff Angela Munsell have ended a class action lawsuit alleging false advertising of Tom’s of Maine brand toothpastes as natural. The lawsuit, originally filed in 2019, claimed the products contained synthetic ingredients despite being marketed as "natural." This dismissal follows a previous settlement where Tom's of Maine agreed to cease "all natural" advertising for three years.

title: The company behind Tide and Bounty pledges net zero emissions by 2040
summary: Procter & Gamble announced a new climate goal to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions across its operations and supply chain by 2040. This plan addresses Scope 3 emissions, which account for about 10 times the company's operational emissions, and includes interim 2030 goals for reductions and efforts to educate consumers on sustainable product use. The company is also working with partners to develop low-carbon technologies and sustainable materials while emphasizing "no deforestation" in its supply chain.

title: P&G Steps Up Climate Change Actions to Cut Most Emissions Across Supply Chain
summary: Procter & Gamble has intensified its climate change efforts, setting a goal to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across its operations and supply chain by 2040. The company also detailed interim 2030 targets, including a 50% reduction in operational emissions and a 40% reduction in supply chain emissions. P&G plans to prioritize cutting emissions throughout its value chain and address residual emissions with natural or technical carbon removal solutions.

title: Florida Polytechnic University plans for first tenant in campus research park
summary: Florida Polytechnic University gained approval for its first tenant, International Flavors & Fragrances (IFF), in its campus research park. This public-private partnership will offer internships and job opportunities for students, foster faculty research, and potentially bring significant economic growth to the region. IFF plans to establish a cutting-edge innovation center focused on citrus, leveraging the university's academic expertise.

title: P&G Accelerates Action on Climate Change Toward Net Zero GHG Emissions by 2040
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) announced a comprehensive plan to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across its operations and supply chain by 2040, setting interim 2030 goals. The plan includes reducing operational emissions by 50% and supply chain emissions by 40%, with a strong focus on transitioning to renewable electricity, decarbonizing logistics, and developing new low-carbon technologies and materials. P&G also aims to collaborate with consumers and industry partners to reduce emissions from product use and promote sustainable homes.

title: \u2018Bachelor\u2019 Finalist Hannah Ann Sues P&G, CVS Over Use of Image
summary: Hannah Ann Sluss, a former "Bachelor" contestant, has filed a lawsuit against Procter & Gamble, CVS Pharmacy, Walmart, and Target. She alleges that these companies continued to use her image to promote Downy detergent even after her licensing agreement had expired. The complaint states that P&G exceeded the scope of her original license by featuring her image on multiple products and packaging materials.

title: The Climate Pledge announces 86 new signatories
summary: The Climate Pledge, co-founded by Amazon and Global Optimism, has announced 86 new signatories, bringing the total to over 201 companies committed to achieving net-zero carbon by 2040, ten years ahead of the Paris Agreement. These new additions, including major businesses like Nespresso, ASOS, Procter & Gamble, HP, and Salesforce, represent various industries across 21 countries and are collectively expected to significantly mitigate carbon emissions. The initiative emphasizes collaboration and real business changes in response to the urgent climate crisis highlighted by recent IPCC reports.

title: The Climate Pledge Announces 86 New Signatories, Including Procter & Gamble, HP, and Salesforce, Signaling Their Commitment to Achieving Net-Zero Carbon by 2040 or Sooner.
summary: The Climate Pledge has announced 86 new signatories, including major companies like Procter & Gamble, HP, and Salesforce, bringing the total to over 200 global organizations. These companies commit to achieving net-zero carbon by 2040, a decade ahead of the Paris Agreement, and are collectively expected to mitigate 1.98 billion metric tons of carbon emissions annually by 2040. The announcement emphasizes the urgency of collective action by businesses to address climate change based on recent IPCC findings.

title: Procter & Gamble 'retiree' Pete Carter launches agency-matching consultancy
summary: Former Procter & Gamble executive Pete Carter has launched a new agency-matching consultancy. The new venture aims to connect brands with suitable agencies for their marketing needs. This move comes after his retirement from P&G.

title: Tide Cleaners Signs Franchise Group to Open Five Locations in California
summary: Tide Cleaners, the on-demand dry cleaning and laundry service, has signed its first multi-unit agreement in California with Jon and Megan Mut of Clean Rock Ventures, LLC. The couple plans to open five Tide Cleaners locations in the San Fernando Valley area of Los Angeles County, with the first expected within a year. This expansion marks a significant step for Tide Cleaners into one of the largest states, leveraging the trusted Tide brand.

title: Sabir Sami Promoted to KFC Division CEO, Effective January 1, 2022
summary: Yum! Brands, Inc. announced the promotion of Sabir Sami to KFC Division Chief Executive Officer, effective January 1, 2022. Sami, currently KFC Division Chief Operating Officer and Managing Director of KFC Asia, will succeed Tony Lowings, who is retiring. Additionally, Dyke Shipp has been promoted to KFC Division President, reporting to Sami.

title: Progressive names 3M executive Remi Kent as its new chief marketing officer
summary: Progressive Corp. has appointed Remi Kent, a 3M executive, as its new chief marketing officer, effective Nov. 1, 2021. Kent will succeed long-serving CMO Jeff Charney and will report directly to President and CEO Tricia Griffith. Her appointment comes as Progressive continues to invest heavily in advertising, building on the success of iconic campaigns.

title: Procter & Gamble's New Storytelling Campaign
summary: Procter & Gamble has reframed its Employee Value Proposition (EVP) to "P&G + Me = Mutual Success," emphasizing the reciprocal relationship between employees and the company. This new EVP, inspired by employee feedback, highlights P&G's commitment to values, superior brands, and a great work environment. The campaign invites employees to share their personal "P&G + Me" stories, illustrating how they have grown and made an impact within the company.

title: Yum! Brands appoints Sabir Sami as global division CEO of KFC
summary: Yum! Brands has appointed Sabir Sami as the global division chief executive officer of KFC, effective January 1, 2022. Sami, previously KFC Asia managing director, will be responsible for driving KFC's global brand strategy and performance, succeeding Tony Lowings.
