His experience in leading KFC Asia's high-growth region, particularly India, positions him well for this new role at Yum!'s largest brand.

title: Linda Rendle: age, family, education, salary, career, songs, profiles, net worth
summary: This article profiles Linda Rendle, the first woman CEO of The Clorox Company, detailing her age, education, career progression, and estimated salary. It highlights her journey from a sales analyst to a top executive in a male-dominated field, emphasizing her achievements and recognition as a powerful woman in business.

title: Dozens protest vaccine mandate at P&G in Cape Girardeau Co.
summary: Dozens of people protested a new COVID-19 vaccine mandate at Procter & Gamble in Cape Girardeau County, Missouri, on Monday. P&G recently announced that employees must be fully vaccinated, obtain an approved exemption, or undergo weekly testing, a policy set to begin on November 1. Protesters, including P&G employees, their families, and friends, stated that their demonstration was not anti-vaccine but rather in support of the individual's right to choose.

title: This Course Lets Undergraduates Act As Brand Managers — And Solve Real Problems
summary: Indiana University's Kelley School of Business offers a Brand Management Practicum where undergraduates work with major companies like Clorox on real-world business problems. This hands-on course, initiated by adjunct lecturer Kelly King, allows students to gain invaluable professional feedback and experience, which helps them secure jobs in the industry. The practicum has grown significantly due to its practical relevance and success in preparing students for careers in brand management.

title: Procter & Gamble heirs say company's "production is coming at a terrible price to the planet"
summary: Two sixth-generation descendants of Procter & Gamble co-founder James Gamble, Justine Epstein and Jules Feeney, are pushing the company to adopt more sustainable practices, citing concerns about its environmental impact, particularly its sourcing of wood pulp from Canada's Boreal Forest for products like Charmin. They sent a letter to P&G's CEO, signed by 88 descendants, expressing deep concern about the company's production at a "terrible price to the planet," and advocating for increased use of recycled materials. This pressure follows a shareholder resolution that passed with 67% approval, urging P&G to enhance efforts to eliminate deforestation, despite the company's current stance on needing virgin forest fiber.

title: Procter & Gamble’s descendants call out family’s business for wasteful resources
summary: Descendants of Procter & Gamble co-founder James Gamble are publicly criticizing the company for its unsustainable practices, particularly its use of "virgin fiber" from critical forests for tissue products like Charmin. Siblings Jules Feeney and Justine Epstein, along with 96 other family members, sent a letter urging P&G to adopt sustainable alternatives, highlighting the environmental impact of cutting down essential ecosystems for single-use products. Environmental groups like the NRDC have also given P&G an "F" for sustainability, pressing the $350 billion company to address its role in forest destruction.

title: Procter & Gamble Sustainability Awards
summary: Procter & Gamble recently celebrated its employees' contributions to sustainability during the "It's Our Home Awards," as the company aims for net-zero emissions by 2040. The awards highlighted innovations in supply chain sustainability, such as reusable packaging in China, and advancements in sustainable brand packaging like Gillette's switch to recyclable cardboard. Jack Mcaneny, VP of Global Sustainability, received the inaugural John Pepper Excellence and Mastery Sustainability Award for his significant leadership in the company's sustainability efforts.

title: Cottonelle Wipes Maker Inks Deal to End Clogged Sewer Claims in Nationwide Class Action
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corp., maker of Cottonelle wipes, has reached a deal with sewage system operators to address claims that its "flushable" wipes clogged sewers nationwide. The agreement, which has received preliminary judicial approval, mandates that Kimberly-Clark improve product performance and labeling to meet national flushability standards by May 2022. While this settlement resolves injunctive relief claims, it does not preclude claims for damages from other municipalities or defendants in the ongoing lawsuit.

title: Top Women in Convenience Awards Gala Honors Change Champions
summary: The 2021 Top Women in Convenience (TWIC) Awards Gala celebrated 74 outstanding women from the convenience store industry, including five Women of the Year. Held in Chicago, the event highlighted themes of resilience, leadership, and the importance of mentorship, particularly for women in historically male-dominated fields. Honorees shared personal reflections on their careers, the impact of COVID-19 on women, and the ongoing progress and challenges in achieving gender equality within the industry.

title: Procter & Gamble must stop the destruction of forests around the world
summary: Over 100 environmental groups have urged Procter & Gamble's shareholders to address the company's negative impact on forests, specifically pinpointing its palm and pulp supply chains. Despite a previous shareholder vote for increased efforts to mitigate deforestation, P&G has not made adequate commitments and has even increased pulp purchases from Canada. The groups recommend shareholders oppose Angela Braly's re-election to P&G's board and call for the company to commit to using more forest-free fibers, reducing supply chain emissions, and enforcing ethical sourcing protocols regarding Indigenous rights and human rights violations.

title: Court Preliminarily Approves Settlement In Charleston, SC, Flushable Wipes Sewer Damage Class Action
summary: A federal judge has preliminarily approved a settlement in a class action lawsuit filed by the Charleston Water System against Kimberly-Clark Corp. The lawsuit alleged that Kimberly-Clark marketed wipes as "flushable" when they were not, causing damage to sewer systems. The settlement includes enhanced product performance, testing, improved labeling, and public outreach regarding flushable wipes.

title: Christopher Kempczinski, President and CEO of McDonald’s Corporation Newly Elected to P&G Board of Directors at 2021 Annual Meeting
summary: Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG) announced the election of Christopher Kempczinski, President and CEO of McDonald’s Corporation, to its Board of Directors, effective immediately, at its 2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders. All 12 director nominees, including Mr. Kempczinski, received over 90 percent support. The company also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.8698 per share, continuing its 131-year history of dividend payments and 65 consecutive years of increases.

title: P&G dogged by controversy on forests, human rights at annual meeting for third year in a row
summary: Environmental advocacy groups protested Procter & Gamble's annual general meeting for the third consecutive year, raising concerns about the company's supply chain issues, particularly its sourcing of pulp from Canadian boreal forests and palm oil from Indonesian and Malaysian tropical forests. Activists called for greater accountability regarding forest destruction, human rights, and climate change, with shareholders voting to keep board member Angela Braly despite pushback. The groups emphasize that pressure on P&G will continue until substantial improvements are made in its sourcing practices and policy.

title: Outgoing P&G CEO David Taylor cautions 'headwinds will continue;' Peltz leaves board
summary: At his final shareholder meeting as CEO, David Taylor expressed confidence in Procter & Gamble's future while acknowledging ongoing challenges from the pandemic, including rising commodity costs and supply chain issues. P&G posted a $14.3 billion profit on $76.1 billion in sales for the fiscal year, with organic sales up 6%. Nelson Peltz, along with other long-term board members, retired from the board, as Taylor prepares to transition to executive chairman and Jon Moeller takes over as CEO.

title: P&G Declares Quarterly Dividend, Elects Kempczinski to Board of Directors
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) held its 2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders, where Christopher Kempczinski, President and CEO of McDonald's Corporation, was elected to the Board of Directors along with 11 incumbent directors. Shareholders also passed both Board proposals and the Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.8698 per share, continuing its 131 consecutive years of dividend payments and 65 consecutive years of dividend increases. CEO David Taylor highlighted the company's strong performance and strategic choices during a challenging year.

title: Why Procter & Gamble Is a Buy
summary: Demitri Kalogeropoulos and Brian Withers discuss why Procter & Gamble (PG) is a manufacturing giant worth investing in due to its competitive advantages, global presence, and strong financial performance. They highlight P&G's market leader position in numerous product categories, efficient manufacturing, innovative packaging, and growing operating profits, making it an attractive stock despite recent market underperformance. The company is a dividend aristocrat with great cash flow and an opportunity to expand margins.

title: The Global Laundry Care Market is expected to grow by $
summary: The global laundry care market is projected to grow by $21.88 billion during 2021-2025, progressing at a CAGR of 4.22%. This growth is attributed to product innovation, portfolio extension, and a shift from traditional laundry care products, as well as improved packaging solutions. The market analysis covers product and distribution channel segments across various geographies and includes a vendor analysis of approximately 25 companies.

title: Jewelers for Children Announces Board of Directors; Reeds’ Alan Zimmer Named Chair
summary: Alan Zimmer, President and CEO of Reeds Jewelers, has been elected as the new chair of the Jewelers for Children board of directors, succeeding Debra Puzio. The organization also announced the addition of eight new directors and the re-election of seven others to its board. These changes coincide with the start of the organization's fiscal year on October 1.

title: P&G to increase prices further as commodity, freight costs bite
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it will further increase prices on some grooming, oral, and skin care products in the U.S. to offset rising commodity and freight costs. These price hikes are in addition to earlier increases on products like Pampers and Always. The company raised its commodity and freight cost impact forecast for the fiscal year to $2.3 billion and expects these additional expenses to reduce full-year earnings per share by 90 cents.

title: Procter & Gamble warns of price increases as inflation continues to bite
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it will raise prices on a wide range of its consumer products, including beauty, oral care, and grooming items, to combat rising costs of raw materials and increased transportation expenses. This follows previous price hikes on paper-based products and comes as inflation remains at 30-year highs. P&G expects to spend an additional $2.1 billion on transport and raw materials for the current fiscal year and is implementing strategies like hiring backup suppliers and limiting retailer supplies to manage the situation.

title: Procter & Gamble hikes prices, tries to ease supply chain clogs
summary: Procter & Gamble announced price increases on various home goods due to rising transportation costs and raw material shortages impacting supply chains. The company is implementing strategies like identifying backup suppliers and reformulating products to mitigate inflation and ensure product availability. Other retailers are also getting creative, including chartering their own vessels, to navigate supply chain disruptions and maintain consumer confidence.

title: P&G’s Global Scale Helping Mitigate Supply Chain Woes
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) reported a 4% increase in organic sales for its fiscal first quarter, surpassing expectations, despite facing challenges from rising commodity and supply chain costs. The company is mitigating these issues by raising prices across categories in the U.S. and leveraging its global scale for flexible sourcing and inventory management. P&G's strong e-commerce growth, now representing 14% of total sales, also contributes to its ability to manage supply chain disruptions and optimize costs.

title: P&G to raise prices on more products
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) announced it would increase prices on specific oral care, skin care, and grooming products in the first half of its fiscal year 2022. This decision comes as P&G faces significant increases in commodity costs, estimated at $2.1 billion, and an additional $200 million in freight costs. The company hopes these price hikes will offset rising expenses and improve earnings in the latter half of its fiscal year.

title: Procter & Gamble says it's raising prices on some grocery items
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it is raising prices on certain grooming, beauty, and oral care products to offset higher costs for raw materials and transportation. This is the latest in a series of price hikes by the company and other major manufacturers; P&G expects to spend $2.3 billion more on freight and commodity costs for its 2022 fiscal year. While these increases will first affect retailers, consumers are expected to see the impact soon, although P&G and Albertsons noted that consumer shopping patterns have not significantly changed yet.

title: Procter & Gamble says it's raising prices on some grocery items
summary: Procter & Gamble announced its latest round of price increases on certain grooming, beauty, and oral care products for retail customers, effective in the next 90 days. This decision is driven by higher costs for raw materials and transportation, with the company now expecting to spend $2.3 billion more on freight and commodity costs for its 2022 fiscal year. Despite the price hikes, P&G and grocery chain Albertsons note that consumers have not changed their shopping patterns.

title: P&G: Marketing efficiency breeds effectiveness, leading to more investment
summary: Procter & Gamble plans to maintain current marketing investment levels, aiming to support growth as consumers favor trusted brands. The company focuses on marketing efficiency through digital reach and better targeting to offset increased costs, with e-commerce now contributing 14% of total sales. P&G's strategy has resulted in strong sales, partially due to investments in digital marketing, helping it gain market share amidst rising prices and supply chain challenges.

title: P&G shifts suppliers, product formulas to avoid supply chain issues
summary: Procter & Gamble is proactively addressing supply chain disruptions and inflation by utilizing alternate suppliers and reformulating products. CFO Andre Schulten stated that these strategies help optimize costs and maintain product availability without impacting quality for consumers. Other companies like Levi's are also employing global sourcing strategies to mitigate similar issues.

title: The Coca-Cola Company and PepsiCo named top plastic polluters for the fourth year in a row
summary: For the fourth consecutive year, The Coca-Cola Company and PepsiCo have been identified as the world's leading plastic polluters by Break Free From Plastic's annual Brand Audit. The report also highlights Unilever rising to become the third-worst polluter, drawing criticism given its role as a principal partner for COP26. The audit, based on global volunteer cleanups, underscores that these corporations' voluntary commitments are having minimal impact and calls for governments to implement policies to reduce plastic production and hold producers accountable.

title: Diaper, Tissue, Toilet Paper Prices Likely to Rise, Kimberly-Clark Warns
summary: Kimberly-Clark, the maker of Huggies and Kleenex, has warned that prices for diapers, tissues, and toilet paper are likely to increase due to inflation and persistent supply chain issues. The Irving-based company also revised its annual earnings forecast downwards for the third consecutive quarter, citing a "volatile and difficult macro environment." This signals potential higher costs for everyday household products for consumers.

title: Coca-Cola raises profit forecast as strong soda sales counter cost pressures
summary: Coca-Cola Co raised its full-year profit forecast, driven by higher prices and strong global demand for its sodas. Despite anticipating continued strong demand, CFO John Murphy acknowledged that the company is not immune to cost inflation in 2022 or potential business impacts from new COVID-19 lockdowns. Coca-Cola plans to increase marketing expenditure and prices to navigate these potential challenges.

title: Big brands are world’s top plastic polluters for the fourth time
summary: A new study by Break Free from Plastic revealed that major brands like Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Unilever, Nestlé, and P&G are the world's top corporate plastic polluters for the fourth consecutive year. The report, based on audits conducted by volunteers in 45 countries, highlights the continued failure of these companies to adopt sustainable practices despite the climate crisis and the pandemic. Environmental groups are urging lawmakers to pass single-use plastic bans and hold these corporations accountable for their environmental impact.

title: New York pension fund joins exit from Unilever over Israel restrictions
summary: New York's $268 billion state pension fund has restricted its holdings in Unilever Plc due to sales limits imposed by its Ben & Jerry's brand in Israeli-occupied Palestinian territories. The fund's comptroller stated that a review found Unilever and its subsidiary "engaged in BDS activities." Other U.S. states have taken similar actions following Ben & Jerry's July decision, which Unilever said was made independently and did not signify support for the BDS movement.

title: Arm & Hammer, OxiClean parent plans price hikes
summary: Church & Dwight Co., the parent company of Arm & Hammer and OxiClean, is implementing price increases across 80% of its product portfolio to counter rising input and transportation costs. These hikes follow previous actions in July and October, with further increases expected in 2022 due to ongoing inflationary pressures. Despite a drop in gross margin caused by various cost factors, the company reported strong third-quarter profits and expects a positive full-year performance.

title: Top 4 Features Driving the Adoption of Toilet Paper, 2021
summary: The global toilet paper market is projected to reach USD 38.34 billion by 2027, growing at a CAGR of 4.9% from 2020-2027. This growth is driven by increased personal hygiene consciousness due to the COVID-19 pandemic, rising commercial and residential infrastructural development, a growing consumer preference for eco-friendly products, and the expanding influence of the e-commerce industry. Manufacturers are focusing on innovative, quality products to meet evolving consumer demands for hygiene and luxury.

title: Procter & Gamble’s Digital Sales Strengthen During Pandemic
summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Procter & Gamble experienced a significant boost in e-commerce sales, with digital transactions up 16% year-over-year and 66% compared to 2019. The company's focus on health, hygiene, and home cleaning products, coupled with consumers staying home, drove increased demand for items like paper towels and toilet paper. Despite supply chain challenges, P&G has implemented price increases on certain products to offset revenue losses, leveraging its strong brand presence in the digital marketplace.

title: a2 Milk and The Hershey Company to release co-branded chocolate milk
summary: The a2 Milk Company and The Hershey Company announced a partnership to release co-branded Hershey’s/The a2 Milk Company chocolate milk, scheduled to hit shelves in January 2022. This collaboration pairs Hershey’s iconic chocolate with a2 Milk's premium A2 protein milk, aiming to capture the market for natural, high-quality chocolate milk that may help avoid stomach discomfort. The initiative marks Hershey's first partnership with a premium milk company and is seen as an expansion into "better-for-you" categories.

title: 'Mr. P&G' takes over: Jon Moeller takes helm of company he helped rebuild
summary: Jon Moeller officially takes over as CEO of Procter & Gamble Co. on November 1st, having been a 33-year veteran of the company. His appointment on July 29th was met positively by investors, resulting in the share price reaching an all-time high. Moeller played a significant role in rebuilding the company, earning him the moniker "Mr. P&G."

title: P&G Sells Old Spice Antiperspirant Containing Cancer-causing Benzene, Says Class Action
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Procter & Gamble (P&G) alleging that the company sells Old Spice antiperspirant and body sprays containing benzene, a known human carcinogen. The plaintiffs, Matthew Lopez, Erik Velasques, and Frank Ortega, claim P&G failed to disclose this contamination, which was highlighted by an independent analytical pharmacy, Valisure. They seek to represent a nationwide class for economic loss and medical monitoring for consumers affected by benzene exposure.

title: P&G Will Not Patent New Packaging Designed for People With Disabilities
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has developed a new Easy Open lid for its Olay North America products, designed to enhance accessibility for people with disabilities. The company will not patent this design and plans to share it with other manufacturers, encouraging broader adoption across the industry. This initiative aligns with P&G's goal of creating more inclusive products and packaging, and is part of a larger trend in the consumer goods sector towards collaborative innovation for social and environmental benefits.

title: Cardinal Health is Ohio’s biggest company; what others make the top 10?
summary: The article highlights Ohio's largest companies based on the 2021 Fortune 500 list, with Cardinal Health securing the top spot. It details the top 10 companies, including their revenue, overall Fortune 500 ranking, headquarters, and number of employees. The report also notes changes from the 2020 list, such as companies joining or dropping off the Fortune 500.

title: P&G ‘will grind to a halt': Anti-vax group claims to be employees in YouTube video
summary: An anti-vaccination group claiming to be Procter & Gamble employees released a YouTube video protesting the company's vaccine mandate and warning of production shutdowns. P&G announced in September that its 26,000 U.S. employees must provide proof of vaccination, get an exemption, or submit to weekly testing. P&G stated that the video distorts its policy, noting that roughly 75% of its workforce is vaccinated, and is proceeding with compliance with the federal mandate.

title: P&G Wraps Launch Of Super C Supplement Brand In Co-Packaging With DayQuil And NyQuil OTCs
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched its Super C supplement brand, strategically co-packaging it with DayQuil and NyQuil OTCs to boost sales in the immunity supplement sector. This approach could potentially test FDA regulations regarding drug and supplement combination policies. The article also mentions related content discussing FDA warnings on supplement/drug combinations and corporate acquisitions in the consumer health market.

title: As General Electric splits apart, does GE Aviation become Greater Cincinnati's newest Fortune 500 company?
summary: General Electric is splitting into three stand-alone companies: aviation, healthcare, and energy. This move positions GE Aviation, based in Evendale, as a potential new Fortune 500 company for Greater Cincinnati, given its $22 billion in 2020 revenues. The split aims to provide stronger focus and better financial flexibility for each resulting business.

title: Procter & Gamble executive: ‘Sustainability is good business’
summary: Virginie Helias, Procter & Gamble's chief sustainability officer, discussed how sustainability drives good business practices through product innovations that delight customers while reducing environmental impact. She highlighted initiatives like reduced-weight diapers and cold-water detergents, emphasizing that these efforts also improve the company's bottom line. Helias stressed the importance of tailored solutions for different regions and "radical collaboration" across industries, governments, and activists to address environmental concerns effectively.

title: Clorox turns to contract suppliers, manufacturers to bolster inventory
summary: Clorox is increasing its reliance on third-party manufacturers and suppliers to meet high demand for its products, with contract manufacturers now handling approximately 50% of shipments, up from 20% historically. This strategy, while costly, helped Clorox avoid raw material shortages and rebuild inventory, positioning them well on supply. However, the company views these additional measures as temporary, planning to scale back and take manufacturing back in-house once demand stabilizes and they can find cost savings.

title: Herbal Essences packaging incorporates Eastman Renew
summary: Herbal Essences is launching new product packaging made from Eastman Renew molecular-recycled plastic, becoming the first P&G brand to do so. This initiative leverages a collaboration between P&G and Eastman Chemical Co. to advance circular economy goals by reducing reliance on virgin plastic and encouraging recycling. The new packaging will feature How2Recycle labels and continue to be part of TerraCycle's national recycling program.

title: Procter & Gamble Buys Farmacy Beauty
summary: Procter & Gamble has acquired Farmacy Beauty, a "farm-to-face" skin care brand, to strengthen its presence in the specialty retail channel and appeal to a younger consumer base. The acquisition allows P&G to expand its skin care portfolio, which already includes Olay, SKII, and First Aid Beauty, while enabling Farmacy to scale its operations globally. Founder David Chung will remain an adviser for a year, and current VP of global marketing Mina Chae will become president and CEO.

title: P&G to pack Herbal Essences in molecular-recycled plastic
summary: Procter & Gamble has partnered with Eastman to use its Renew molecular-recycled plastic for the primary packaging of its Herbal Essences brand. Herbal Essences will be the first P&G brand to incorporate this material, starting with five bio:renew sulfate-free collections this month and two new collections in January 2022. This initiative aims to reduce dependence on virgin plastic and encourage recycling behavior through standardized How2Recycle labels.

title: Back-to-school Market Size & Share | Growth Analysis - 2030
summary: The global back-to-school market is projected to reach $131.1 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 4.8%. This growth is driven by innovations in products like backpacks and stationery, government initiatives in education, and NGO efforts, particularly in Asia-Pacific and LAMEA. The stationery segment held the largest market share in 2020, while the e-commerce distribution channel is expected to show the highest growth.

title: Procter & Gamble to acquire Farmacy
summary: Procter & Gamble has reached a deal to acquire the indie skincare brand Farmacy Beauty. The deal terms were not disclosed, but Farmacy is expected to report net sales of US$80 million this year. Farmacy's founder emphasized the need for P&G's resources for further growth, while P&G highlighted the brand's science-backed and natural "farm to face" positioning.

title: Exponential Growth Expected for Adult Nappy Market With Complete SWOT Analysis by Forecast From 2021 to 2027: Kimberly Clark, SCA, Unicharm, Hartmann
summary: The Adult Nappy Market is expected to see exponential growth between 2021 and 2027, according to a report by Worldwide Market Reports. The report provides detailed insights into market shares, growth opportunities, and competitive landscape, profiling key players like Kimberly Clark, SCA, and Unicharm. It also analyzes the impact of COVID-19 and offers growth prospects across various segments and regions.

title: Waldencast acquires beauty brands Obagi and Milk Makeup in three-way US$1.2 billion deal
summary: Waldencast, a special-purpose acquisition company, has acquired skincare brand Obagi and makeup and skincare company Milk Makeup in a three-way deal valued at US$1.2 billion. This acquisition is the first step in Waldencast's strategy to build a global multi-brand beauty and wellness platform. Michel Brousset, Founder and CEO of Waldencast, will lead the new entity, with Co-founder Hind Sebti serving as Chief Operating Officer.

title: These 3 stocks can weather a market crash: STORE Capital, AGNC Investing, Proctor & Gamble
summary: This article identifies three stocks – STORE Capital (NASDAQ: STOR), AGNC Investment (NASDAQ: AGNC), and Proctor & Gamble (NYSE: PG) – that are well-positioned to withstand a market crash. The author, Brent Nyitray, CFA, explains that while crashes are unpredictable, investors can plan by choosing defensive stocks that will be least affected. Each company is highlighted for its specific defensive characteristics, such as long-term leases and non-discretionary goods for STORE Capital, government-guaranteed mortgage-backed securities for AGNC Investment, and consumer staple products for Proctor & Gamble.

title: Pental rides the COVID tidal wave to new ecommerce-driven, eco-friendly heights
summary: Pental Ltd (ASX:PTL), an Australian household product manufacturer, leveraged local procurement during COVID-19 to meet increased demand in the cleaning product market. The company is now focusing on e-commerce and sustainability, acquiring "Hampers with Bite" and developing eco-friendly products, leading to increased profits and a strong financial position. Pental aims for at least 50% of its products to be fully recyclable by 2025 and is exploring new markets and acquisitions.

title: Unilever to sell Lipton Tea owner to CVC Capital for $5 Billion
summary: Unilever is selling its tea business, ekaterra, which includes brands like Lipton and PG tips, to CVC Capital Partners for 4.5 billion euros ($5.1 billion). This sale is part of Unilever CEO Alan Jope's strategy to refocus the company's portfolio on higher-growth areas and follows a period of declining demand for traditional tea. The transaction is expected to be completed in the second half of 2022.

title: Procter & Gamble Buys Farmacy Beauty
summary: Procter & Gamble has acquired Farmacy Beauty, a cult "farm-to-face skincare" brand, to expand its skincare portfolio and attract younger consumers. P&G aims to leverage Farmacy's science-based sustainable products and D2C presence, along with its existing retail channels like Sephora, QVC, and Amazon. The deal is expected to help Farmacy grow beyond its current $80 million net sales, with brand founder David Chung remaining as an advisor and Mina Chae becoming the new President and CEO.

title: Procter & Gamble acquires prestige indie brand Farmacy Beauty for undisclosed sum
summary: Procter & Gamble has acquired Farmacy Beauty, a "farm-to-face skincare" brand founded by David Chung, for an undisclosed sum. This acquisition aims to attract younger consumers through responsible and clean beauty brands and complements P&G's existing skincare portfolio. Farmacy Beauty's founder will remain in an advisory role for a year, as P&G plans for international expansion while allowing the brand to maintain its distinct direction, similar to its strategy with First Aid Beauty.

title: Procter & Gamble Issue Voluntary Recall of Certain Old Spice, Secret Products
summary: Procter & Gamble has issued a voluntary recall of specific Old Spice and Secret brand aerosol antiperspirants and Old Spice Below Deck aerosol spray products due to the detection of benzene. This action follows findings by Valisure, a private pharmaceutical company, which identified benzene in various antiperspirant body sprays, leading to concerns about potential health risks despite no reported adverse events to date. The recall highlights broader issues concerning raw material quality and the need for independent testing in the consumer healthcare product supply chain.

title: Some Old Spice and Secret deodorants are recalled. Here’s what you need to know
summary: Procter & Gamble has issued a voluntary recall for specific Old Spice and Secret aerosol antiperspirants and sprays due to the detection of benzene, a human carcinogen. While no adverse reactions have been reported, the company is urging consumers to discard the affected products, offering refunds, and has removed them from store shelves. The recalled items have an expiration date before September 2023.

title: Schick Owner Edgewell Personal Care Buys Women’s Razor Brand Billie
summary: Edgewell Personal Care, maker of Schick razors, has acquired women’s razor brand Billie for $310 million. This acquisition comes after federal regulators blocked a previous attempt by Procter & Gamble (Gillette's parent company) to acquire Billie due to antitrust concerns. Billie, founded in 2017, targets younger consumers with affordable products and campaigns that challenge traditional beauty standards.

title: Edgewell acquires shaving disruptor Billie for $310m
summary: Edgewell has acquired the female-first shaving and body care brand Billie for $310 million in cash. Billie, known for its subscription service and campaign against the "pink tax," was previously targeted for acquisition by Procter & Gamble, a deal that was blocked by the US Federal Trade Commission. This acquisition is expected to enhance Edgewell's position in the women's shave category and accelerate Billie's expansion into brick-and-mortar retail in the US.

title: Disney names Susan Arnold as its first woman chair
summary: Walt Disney Co. has appointed Susan Arnold as its new chairman of the board, making her the first woman to hold the role in the company's 98-year history. Arnold, a board member for 14 years, will replace Bob Iger on December 31, who steps down after serving as CEO for 15 years and will leave the company at the end of the month. This appointment aligns with a growing trend among corporations to separate the roles of CEO and board chairperson.

title: Susan Arnold named chairman of the board for Walt Disney Co.
summary: Susan E. Arnold, a 14-year member of the Walt Disney Co.'s board of directors, has been named chairman of the board, effective December 31, 2021. She will succeed Robert A. Iger, who departs Disney at the end of the year. Arnold brings extensive public-company board experience and knowledge in brand management, marketing, and finance to her new role.

title: Procter & Gamble and A.S. Watson Co-Create New Skin Care Brand
summary: Procter & Gamble and A.S. Watson Group have collaborated to launch a new clean beauty skincare brand called "aio." The brand, featuring a fully-recyclable packaging and an Oxyniacine formula, will be sold in Watson's brick and mortar stores and online in Greater China. This partnership marks a new approach for P&G Beauty in co-creating products with retail partners.

title: Disney appoints its first female board chair
summary: Susan E. Arnold has been elected as the first woman to chair the Walt Disney Co. board, succeeding Robert Iger, effective December 31st. With 14 years on the board and executive experience from Procter & Gamble and the Carlyle Group, Arnold steps into this lead role during a significant period of change for the entertainment industry. Disney is also focusing on streaming services and redefining its female characters to be strong and independent.

title: How Sumaira Latif brought accessible design to P&G
summary: Sumaira Latif, Accessibility Leader at Procter & Gamble, spearheaded efforts to integrate accessible design into P&G's products and packaging after realizing the challenges faced by disabled consumers, drawing from her own experience as a blind person. She initiated the People with Disabilities Network and the Disabilities Challenge to immerse colleagues in the realities of product accessibility, leading to innovations like tactile indicators on Herbal Essences bottles and the adoption of NaviLens QR codes on Pantene products. Latif advocates for industry-wide collaboration and the inclusion of disabled consumers in the design process, emphasizing that accessible design benefits everyone and presents a significant business opportunity.

title: P&G Breaks Into Prestige Hair Care With Jen Atkin Deal
summary: Procter & Gamble has acquired Ouai, celebrity hairstylist Jen Atkin’s hair care and lifestyle brand, marking P&G's entry into the prestige hair care market. Atkin and CEO Colin Walsh will remain with Ouai, which is projected to exceed $50 million in sales for 2021, and they plan to continue product innovation and geographical expansion. This acquisition follows other recent deals by P&G Beauty in the fast-growing prestige segment, with Ouai set to operate separately from the larger P&G business.

title: Edgewell Personal Care Acquires Billie in $310 Million Deal
summary: Edgewell Personal Care has acquired the female personal care brand Billie in a $310 million all-cash transaction, significantly strengthening its position in the women's shaving category. This acquisition enhances Edgewell's digital capabilities and market presence while providing Billie with broadened retail distribution and marketing channels. The deal follows a previous attempt by Procter & Gamble to acquire Billie, which was blocked by the FTC due to antitrust concerns.

title: Three Class Actions Claim Companies Failed To Disclose Benzene Contamination In Personal Care Products
summary: Three new class-action lawsuits have been filed against HRB Brands, Edgewell Personal Care Company, and The Village Company. These lawsuits allege that the companies failed to disclose benzene contamination in their personal care products, including antiperspirant sprays, body sprays, and sunscreens. The lawsuits follow an independent study by Valisure, an analytical pharmacy, which found benzene, a known human carcinogen, in several products.

title: P&G and Herbal Essences' PET Bottles Move to 50% Chemically Recycled PCR
summary: P&G's Herbal Essences brand is introducing shampoo and conditioner bottles made with 50% certified recycled plastic from Eastman Renew resins, utilizing advanced molecular recycling technology. This initiative is part of a broader collaboration between P&G and Eastman to advance recycling efforts and reduce virgin plastic use, with a focus on difficult-to-recycle materials. The new packaging also incorporates How2Recycle® labels to encourage consumers to recycle.

title: Procter & Gamble to enter prestige hair space with acquisition of Ouai
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced its planned acquisition of Ouai, a prestige hair care brand. Celebrity hairstylist Jen Atkin will remain as Founder and Chief Creative Officer, and Colin Walsh will continue as CEO, with plans for geographical expansion. The deal's terms were not disclosed, but analysts estimate Ouai's 2021 sales at US$50 million.

title: Procter & Gamble to Acquire Jen Atkin's Ouai
summary: Procter & Gamble has signed an agreement to acquire Ouai, the haircare brand founded by celebrity hairstylist Jen Atkin in 2015. This acquisition marks P&G's strategic entry into the prestige haircare sector, a rapidly growing category. Ouai, which has expanded into body products, fragrances, and more, is expected to continue operating separately with its current team, including Atkin as founder and Chief Creative Officer, and Colin Walsh as CEO.

title: P&G Issues Voluntary Recall of Aerosol Dry Conditioner Spray Products and Aerosol Dry Shampoo Spray Products
summary: The Procter & Gamble Company has issued a voluntary recall for aerosol dry conditioner and dry shampoo products from brands like Pantene, Aussie, Herbal Essences, and Waterl<ss due to the detection of benzene. While benzene is not an ingredient, unexpected levels were found from the propellant, a human carcinogen. P&G has not received reports of adverse events and is conducting this recall out of an abundance of caution, offering reimbursements for affected products.

title: P&G recalls some conditioner, shampoo sprays on finding carcinogens
summary: Procter & Gamble Co (PG.N) has voluntarily recalled some dry conditioner and shampoo sprays from several brands, including Pantene and Herbal Essences, in the United States and Canada due to the detection of a cancer-causing chemical, benzene. While the company stated that daily exposure to the detected benzene levels is not expected to cause negative health consequences, the products represented less than 1% of its overall hair care portfolio. This recall follows a similar action earlier in the year by Johnson & Johnson, which also detected benzene in some of its sunscreen products.

title: Procter & Gamble issues a recall on 32 hair care products on ingredient cancer concern
summary: Procter & Gamble issued a recall for 32 aerosol dry shampoos and conditioners due to the presence of benzene, a carcinogen. The recall affects popular brands like Pantene, Aussie, and Old Spice. Consumers are advised to stop using the products and can return them for a refund.

title: Throw Out These Procter & Gamble Hair Care Products With Cancer-Causing Chemicals, FDA Says
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has issued a voluntary recall of several aerosol dry shampoo and conditioner sprays from brands like Pantene, Herbal Essences, Old Spice, Aussie, and Waterless. This recall follows the discovery of unexpected levels of benzene, a known carcinogen, which P&G states came from the propellant used in the sprays, not an active ingredient. Consumers who have purchased these recalled products are advised to stop use immediately, dispose of them, and contact P&G for reimbursement.

title: Shampoo, conditioner recall: Procter & Gamble sprays could contain cancer-causing chemical
summary: Procter & Gamble is recalling several dry conditioner and dry shampoo aerosol products from brands including Pantene, Aussie, and Herbal Essence due to the detection of benzene, a cancer-causing chemical. The recall is voluntary and being conducted out of an abundance of caution, with P&G offering reimbursements to consumers. People are advised to stop using the products and dispose of them.

title: P&G recalls over 30 aerosol spray products due to benzene
summary: Procter & Gamble has issued a recall for over 30 aerosol spray products, including dry shampoos and conditioners from brands like Pantene, Aussie, and Herbal Essences, due to detected traces of benzene. While benzene is not an ingredient, it was found in the propellant used in these products. P&G states that adverse health effects are not expected at the detected levels, and they have not received any related reports, advising customers to discard affected items for reimbursement.

title: Blackstone Buys Majority Stake in Sunscreen Brand Supergoop
summary: Blackstone Inc.'s growth fund is acquiring a majority stake in Supergoop, a 15-year-old sunscreen brand, in a deal estimated to value the company at $600 million to $700 million. Supergoop's founder and CEO will retain significant equity, and the investment aims to fuel product and regional expansion, including into China. This acquisition highlights a trend of larger players buying clean beauty brands to attract younger, ingredient-conscious consumers.

title: Procter and Gamble Recalls Dry Shampoo and Conditioner Products Over Cancer-Causing Chemicals
summary: Procter & Gamble has voluntarily recalled over 30 aerosol dry shampoo and conditioner products from brands like Pantene, Aussie, Herbal Essences, and Waterl<ss due to the detection of benzene. While benzene is not an ingredient, it was found in the propellant used to spray the products. P&G states the detected levels are not expected to cause adverse health consequences and is offering a full refund to affected consumers.

title: P&G harnesses the power of partnerships to drive innovation and impact
summary: P&G is leveraging partnerships to achieve its net-zero greenhouse gas emissions goal by 2040, focusing on innovation in its Fabric and Home Care sector, particularly with its Tide brand. These collaborations, including with NASA and suppliers, aim to develop sustainable products and processes, reduce supply chain impacts, and drive consumer behavior change towards more environmentally friendly practices like cold water washing. P&G emphasizes that such partnerships are crucial for tackling the climate crisis and meeting consumer expectations for sustainable solutions.

title: Procter & Gamble recalls 32 dry shampoo and conditioner products over benzene concern
summary: Procter & Gamble has issued a voluntary recall for 32 of its dry shampoo and conditioner products, including brands like Pantene and Herbal Essences, due to the detection of "unexpected" levels of benzene, a known carcinogen. The company stated that it has not received any reports of adverse events and is conducting the recall out of an abundance of caution, offering reimbursement to consumers. This action follows recent reports of benzene found in aerosol products, with P&G identifying the carcinogen in the propellant used to spray its products.

title: The Walt Disney Company Extends Chief Financial Officer Christine M. Mccarthy’s Contract Through June 30, 2024
summary: The Walt Disney Company has extended the contract of Chief Financial Officer Christine M. McCarthy through June 30, 2024. CEO Bob Chapek highlighted McCarthy's indispensable leadership during a period of disruption and transformation, praising her contributions to the company's growth and navigation through the pandemic. McCarthy, a 22-year Disney veteran and CFO since 2015, expressed her privilege in the role and her commitment to delivering shareholder value.

title: P&G’s Tide is Headed to Space with NASA and SpaceX!
summary: P&G's Tide brand is collaborating with NASA to develop the first space-specific laundry detergent solution, Tide Infinity, which is set to launch on SpaceX CRS-24 to the International Space Station. This fully degradable detergent aims to solve malodor, cleanliness, and stain removal problems in resource-constrained environments, with potential applications for water-scarce areas on Earth. Further experiments for stain removal and detergent stability will be conducted in early 2022 aboard Northrop Grumman CRS-17, including tests on Tide To Go products in zero-gravity.

title: P&G shampoo recall is only the latest for benzene in spray products
summary: Procter & Gamble has issued a recall for aerosol dry shampoo and conditioner spray products due to the presence of benzene, a known carcinogen. This recall affects several brands including Aussie, Herbal Essences, Pantene, and Waterless, and is part of a larger trend of benzene contamination in various spray products, such as sunscreens and hand sanitizers. P&G states that exposure to the detected levels of benzene in their products is not expected to cause adverse health consequences, and they are offering reimbursement for recalled items.

title: Lawsuits mount against Procter & Gamble over cancer-causing chemical in Old Spice, Secret sprays
summary: Procter & Gamble is facing at least 17 federal lawsuits, including six class-action suits in Cincinnati, alleging its Old Spice and Secret antiperspirant sprays are contaminated with dangerous levels of benzene, a known carcinogen. These lawsuits follow a November report by Valisure, an independent lab, which found high levels of benzene in various body-spray products, prompting P&G to voluntarily recall several aerosol products. P&G states benzene is not an ingredient in their products but came from the propellant, and despite claims of low risk, they issued recalls "out of an abundance of caution."

title: STEM Professionals Are ReLaunching Careers With P&G
summary: P&G's ReLaunch program is successfully bringing STEM professionals who have taken career breaks back into the workforce. The program, which started in 2020 and has expanded globally, offers flexibility and support, appealing to individuals seeking meaningful careers and work-life balance. It highlights how career breaks can bring valuable maturity and diverse experiences to companies.

title: P&G cancels live appearances at CES tech show amid COVID-19 concerns
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced it is canceling its live appearances at the upcoming CES tech show in Las Vegas due to rising concerns over the coronavirus' omicron variant. Instead of a physical presence, P&G will host an all-virtual event on its pglifelab.com website, prioritizing the health and well-being of its employees and partners. This decision follows similar moves by other major companies like Amazon and Meta, despite CES's plans to continue the in-person event from January 5-8.

title: Shed Concentration Risk With Equal-Weight ETFs
summary: This article discusses the increasing concentration risk in cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500, primarily due to the large market capitalization of a few tech giants like Apple and Microsoft. It advocates for equal-weight exchange-traded funds (ETFs), such as the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP), as a solution to provide comparable returns with superior diversification. The article highlights how equal-weight ETFs mitigate the risks associated with an over-reliance on a few mega-cap stocks.

title: Shun Concentration Risk With Equal-Weight ETFs
summary: This article discusses the increasing concentration risk in cap-weighted S&P 500 indexes due to the massive market capitalization of a few tech giants like Apple and Microsoft. It promotes equal-weight ETFs, such as the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP), as a solution to this problem, highlighting their comparable performance with superior diversification. The piece draws historical parallels to the tech bubble, emphasizing the benefits of a less concentrated portfolio.

title: More than words
summary: Plastic packaging producers worldwide are increasing investments to close the loop on their products, acknowledging the historically low recycling rates for plastic compared to other materials. These investments span various forms, from traditional scrap collection and processing to advanced recycling technologies, driven by regulatory pressure, corporate sustainability goals, and shareholder activism. The article highlights major players like Alpla Group, Amcor, Sealed Air Corp., Ineos Styrolution, and PureCycle Technologies, emphasizing efforts in PET, HDPE, and PP, and discussing the debate around the economic viability and environmental impact of chemical recycling.

title: P&G takes first step into the metaverse with BeautySphere
summary: P&G Beauty has entered the metaverse with the launch of BeautySphere, a virtual storytelling world accessible via desktop, which debuted at CES. This platform enables consumers to interact with P&G's brands through live content, panel discussions, and gamified challenges, focusing on the company's "Responsible Beauty" initiatives. BeautySphere aims to engage digitally-savvy consumers on a nascent virtual landscape, bridging virtual experiences with real-world impact, such as planting trees for reforestation efforts.

title: P&G VENTURES ANNOUNCES LADY PATCH AS WINNER OF THE 2022 VIRTUAL CES INNOVATION CHALLENGE
summary: P&G Ventures announced Lady Patch as the winner of its 2022 Virtual CES Innovation Challenge. Lady Patch, a drug-free feminine patch for bladder leaks, received a $10,000 grand prize and an opportunity to partner with P&G Ventures. Additionally, for the first time, three other finalists—Cybele Microbiome, Kushae Naturals, and Ryp Labs—were awarded $5,000 each for their innovative products.

title: P&G Targets Metaverse in Search for Future Customers
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. is venturing into the metaverse to attract new customers, showcasing its strategy at CES. This includes a digital platform called BeautySPHERE featuring virtual tours of Kew Gardens to educate consumers on plant-derived ingredients in products like Herbal Essences. P&G is also pledging real-world tree planting in Mexico for participants who complete the virtual experience.

title: Mars taps former J.M. Smucker Co. executive to lead pet nutrition innovation
summary: Mars Petcare has appointed Alejandro “Alex” Cedeno as Senior Vice President of Research and Development for its Pet Nutrition North America team. Cedeno, formerly of The J.M. Smucker Company, will lead innovation aligned with Mars' commitment to pets and will replace Michel Oostwal, who is retiring. He will be responsible for strategic and operational leadership in R&D, focusing on food safety, sustainability, and product innovation.

title: Patent Pick: P&G's Dissolvable Solid Fibrous Shampoo
summary: Procter & Gamble has developed a dissolvable solid fibrous shampoo designed to overcome drawbacks associated with liquid shampoos, such as controlling dosage and product delivery. This innovative solid format, detailed in patent application WO/2021/262912, quickly dissolves into a smooth composition, providing a consumer-acceptable amount of lather. The formulation includes a polymeric structurant, a surfactant system (substantially free of sulfate-based surfactants), and a pH adjuster.

title: P&G Declares Quarterly Dividend
summary: The Procter & Gamble Company announced its Board of Directors declared a quarterly dividend of $0.8698 per share. This dividend is payable to shareholders of record by January 21, 2022, on or after February 15, 2022. P&G highlights its long history of paying dividends for 131 consecutive years and increasing them for 65 consecutive years, underscoring its commitment to shareholder value.

title: SC firm files suit against Procter & Gamble over cancer-causing chemical in products
summary: A South Carolina law firm, Anastopoulo Law Firm, has filed a class-action lawsuit against Procter & Gamble. The suit alleges that Old Spice and Secret aerosol spray antiperspirants, and Old Spice Below Deck aerosol spray products, contained dangerous levels of benzene, a chemical linked to various cancers and blood disorders. Though P&G issued a recall, the firm claims the "damage was already done" and seeks justice for affected consumers.

title: Oral Care Market Size to Surpass US$ 99.78 Billion by 2030
summary: The global oral care market is projected to reach US$ 99.78 billion by 2030, growing at an 8.1% CAGR from 2021 to 2030, driven by an increasing prevalence of dental disorders and rising awareness of cosmetic dental treatments. Despite challenges like lack of awareness for herbal products and adverse effects of certain treatments, the market is poised for growth due to the shift towards online sales channels. North America is the fastest-growing region, while Asia-Pacific holds the largest market share.

title: Razor Blade Market 2022 – Major Players Analysis Forecast
summary: A new report titled "Razor Blade Market 2022" provides comprehensive insights into the global razor blade market. The report details the market's dynamics, characteristics, key players, segmentation by application and product type, and regional analysis. With major players like Gillette(P&G) and Energizer dominating, the market was valued at USD 2546 million in 2020 and is projected to reach USD 2583.8 million by 2027, growing at a CAGR of 0.2%.

title: Procter & Gamble says the prices of Tide laundry products and personal-care items are going up soon
summary: Procter & Gamble announced additional price hikes set to take effect on February 28, impacting its Fabric Care portfolio, including Tide, Gain, Downy, Bounce, and Unstopables. This move follows other companies like General Mills in raising consumer product prices. The increases will apply to all forms of these products, such as liquid and unit dose detergents, scent beads, liquid fabric softeners, and dryer sheets.

title: Procter & Gamble’s sales jump as consumers brush off rising prices.
summary: Procter & Gamble reported a significant jump in its second-quarter earnings, with revenue increasing 6 percent to $21 billion and earnings up 9 percent to $4.2 billion, driven by higher prices on consumer products. The company plans further price increases on fabric and personal care items in February and April. This financial growth signals that consumers are largely absorbing increased costs despite rising inflation.

title: Eastman unveils plans for $1B polyester depolymerization plant
summary: Eastman is planning to build a $1 billion polyester depolymerization facility in France to chemically recycle up to 160,000 metric tons of hard-to-recycle plastic annually. Several global brand owners, including Procter & Gamble and L'Oréal, have signed letters of intent to purchase the recycled resin. This investment, announced by Eastman CEO Mark Costa alongside French President Emmanuel Macron, marks a significant step in the company's circular economy strategy and will reduce its carbon footprint in Europe.

title: Eastman to invest $1 billion in ‘world’s largest’ molecular plastics recycling facility
summary: Eastman plans to invest up to $1 billion in a molecular recycling facility in France, aiming to recycle 160,000 metric tonnes of hard-to-recycle plastic waste annually using its polyester renewal technology. The project, which includes an innovation center, is supported by the French government and major brands like LVMH Beauty and Procter & Gamble, and is expected to create 350 direct and 1,500 indirect jobs. The facility and innovation center are projected to be operational by 2025.

title: Kraft Heinz price increase: Oscar Mayer hot dogs and Velveeta cheese are about to get more expensive
summary: Kraft Heinz plans to raise prices on dozens of its products, including Oscar Mayer cold cuts and Velveeta cheese, starting in March due to ongoing inflation and increased costs. These increases range from 5% to 30%. This follows similar announcements from other consumer goods companies like Procter & Gamble and Conagra, as the US consumer price index rose 7% annually in December.

title: ESG Risk Management Makes Sense, but ESG Impact Is Less Straightforward
summary: This article distinguishes between ESG risk management and ESG impact, arguing that while managing ESG risks directly affects valuation, measuring and achieving positive ESG impact is far more complex and less directly tied to financial returns. It highlights challenges companies like Unilever face when prioritizing sustainability impact at the expense of core business fundamentals, and discusses the difficulty in objectively measuring the benefits of impact spending and aligning diverse investor values.

title: Colgate-Palmolive Co. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Colgate-Palmolive Co. (CL) stock underperformed on Tuesday, shedding 0.64% to $81.92, despite an overall favorable trading session for the broader market. The stock also closed below its 52-week high and displayed mixed performance compared to competitors like Procter & Gamble Co., Unilever PLC ADR, and Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC, all of which also saw slight declines. Trading volume for Colgate-Palmolive Co. exceeded its 50-day average.

title: P&G Website Not Accessible To Blind Individuals, Class Action Claims
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Procter & Gamble, alleging that its website, sk-ii.com, is not fully accessible to blind and visually-impaired individuals. Plaintiff Robert Weekes, who is legally blind, claims the website's screen reader fails to read item descriptions and stops abruptly, preventing him from making purchases. The lawsuit asserts that this violates Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA) and the New York City Human Rights Law.

title: WPP gains early access to Instacart ad products in latest retail media bet
summary: WPP has partnered with Instacart, giving its clients early access to Instacart's new ad formats and analytics tools. This collaboration positions WPP as Instacart's first Analytics API partner, allowing for in-depth data integration and the co-development of an Instacart Ads agency certification program. The move highlights WPP's strategic focus on retail media, leveraging the boom in e-commerce and the increasing demand for effective advertising as third-party tracking methods decline.

title: Beijing Olympics sponsor Procter & Gamble silent on Uyghur genocide after calling out US 'systemic racism'
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G), a sponsor of the 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing, is facing criticism for its silence on China's genocide of Uyghur Muslims. This silence contrasts sharply with the company's vocal stance on "systemic racism" in the U.S. P&G has reportedly downplayed its Olympics involvement and lobbied against legislation targeting corporate sponsors of the Games, prioritizing its significant revenue from the Chinese market.

title: Love thyself more this Valentine's Day with P&G x Lazada's #WinWithLove campaign
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is launching the #WinWithLove Super Brand Day campaign on Lazada to encourage self-love this Valentine's Day. The campaign features a partnership with TikTok influencer thefakeoppa in a humorous video demonstrating self-care using P&G products. This initiative includes a 24-hour shopping event on LazMall across six Southeast Asian markets with exclusive offers on various P&G brands.

title: Mumbai based, Boch & Fernsh, 360 creative agency expands during the pandemic
summary: Boch & Fernsh Inc., a 360 creative agency based in Mumbai, successfully expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, acquiring major clients like Alcon, 7 eleven, Acuvue, Ganit Inc., and DePuy Synthes. The company, founded in 2005, attributes its growth to its data-driven approach, digital-first mindset, and ability to transfer best practices across industries. CEO Chirag Shah noted that the pandemic provided an opportunity for Indian agencies to go global due to their creativity, analytical skills, and adaptability.

title: The Most Durable Baby Wipes for Everyday Mess Management
summary: This article identifies and reviews ten of the most durable and effective baby wipes available, emphasizing their versatility beyond just diaper changes. It highlights key considerations for parents, such as durability, size, ingredients (scented vs. unscented), and environmental impact, including options for compostable and reusable wipes. The selections range from essential oil infused to water-based, catering to various needs and skin sensitivities.

title: A sustainability champion at a global giant
summary: This article profiles Virginie Helias, Procter & Gamble's Chief Sustainability Officer, highlighting her journey and contributions to integrating sustainability into P&G's business practices. It details her career progression, her pivotal role in various green initiatives like the recycled plastic Head & Shoulders bottle, and P&G's commitment to net-zero targets and science-based reduction goals under her leadership. Helias is portrayed as a passionate and authentic leader who has driven significant environmental changes within a global corporate giant.

title: Colgate® Launches its Groundbreaking Recyclable Toothpaste Tube with "Recycle Me!" Packaging in the U.S.
summary: Colgate is introducing its breakthrough recyclable toothpaste tube in the U.S., featuring "Recycle Me!" packaging to raise awareness. Made from HDPE, the same plastic as milk bottles, this new tube is designed to be recycled alongside plastic bottles without extra steps. Colgate-Palmolive is also collaborating with peer companies and recycling facilities to pilot educational efforts and define best practices for tube recycling.

title: Colgate Porter Five Forces Analysis
summary: This article provides a Porter Five Forces analysis of Colgate, evaluating the threat of new entrants, substitute products, bargaining power of buyers and suppliers, and competitive rivalry. It concludes that while some forces like competitive rivalry are high, Colgate's market leadership and brand loyalty position it favorably, though continuous innovation is crucial.

title: For Companies, Winning in China Now Means Losing Somewhere Else (Published 2022)
summary: The 2022 Beijing Olympics have forced global companies, particularly sponsors, into a difficult position due to the strained U.S.-China relationship. Companies like Procter & Gamble have had to engage in lobbying efforts to mitigate negative fallout from their association with an event seen as legitimizing China's authoritarian government. This situation highlights a growing dilemma where business interests in one country increasingly become liabilities in the other.

title: Effervescent health: P&G launches VÖOST Vitamins in major retailers in Singapore
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has launched its Australian effervescent supplement brand, VÖOST Vitamins, in major Singaporean retailers following its acquisition in April 2021. The range includes seven SKUs of single vitamins and multi-ingredient supplements, targeting immunity, nervous system health, and overall wellness for various consumer groups. P&G aims to expand product offerings and sales channels, leveraging accessible formats, attractive packaging, and influencer marketing to grow brand awareness in the region.

title: Pantene and Stubb's will be sold in reusable containers at some Kroger stores
summary: Kroger, through its Fred Meyer stores, is partnering with Loop to offer Pantene, Stubb's, and other major brand products in reusable packaging with a refundable deposit. This initiative aims to gauge consumer interest in sustainable alternatives that require a behavior change, with a pilot program launching in 25 Portland-area Fred Meyer locations. The move reflects growing concerns about plastic pollution and a shift towards more sustainable retail practices.

title: James Hurley, a basketball and business trailblazer, dies at 76
summary: James "Jim" Hurley, a trailblazer in both basketball and business, passed away at 76. Hurley was known for breaking racial barriers, integrating schools and basketball programs, and rising as a Black leader at Procter & Gamble Co. Throughout his life, he was admired for his genuine interest in others and his commitment to making a positive difference.

title: Surabhi Pokhriyal Named Chief Digital Growth Officer at Church & Dwight
summary: Church & Dwight has appointed Surabhi Pokhriyal as its Chief Digital Growth Officer, where she will lead the company's digital transformation and e-commerce initiatives. Pokhriyal, previously with Colgate-Palmolive and other major consumer goods companies, is tasked with accelerating digital momentum, including e-commerce penetration and M&A integration. She is excited to leverage the company's nimble structure and focused talent to elevate its digital capabilities and expand its brand footprint.

title: Wide Moat Stocks Can Get Their Grooves Back
summary: The VanEck Vectors Morningstar Wide Moat ETF (MOAT) has shown durability amid market turbulence in early 2022 and is outperforming the S&P 500. Analysts believe wide moat equities have the ingredients for continued success, with the ETF's valuation methodology identifying stocks trading at attractive multiples despite their inherent quality. MOAT's sector-agnostic approach and diversified holdings, including non-tech stocks, are helping to buffer against current tech sector weaknesses.

title: What impact will Ukraine crisis have on Procter & Gamble Co.?
summary: The article discusses the potential impact of the Ukraine crisis and Russian sanctions on Procter & Gamble Co., referencing past currency-related losses and P&G's current preparedness. While P&G's sales and profits from Russia and Ukraine are small, the economic slowdown in Europe could significantly affect P&G and other multinationals, prompting warnings to businesses about engaging with Russian entities.

title: Leveraging Technology to Improve The Lives of P&G Consumers
summary: P&G utilizes advanced data-processing technologies like machine learning and artificial intelligence to enhance its products, understand consumer behavior, and streamline operations. This technology-driven approach, which began over five years ago, impacts everything from product development and quality control to personalized consumer communication and supply chain logistics. P&G's strategy focuses on connecting data, facilitating data scientists' work, and developing talent to continuously improve products and consumer experiences.

title: P&G to invest $110M in North Carolina facility, create 46 jobs
summary: Procter & Gamble plans to invest $110 million in its North Carolina manufacturing facility on Swing Road in Greensboro. This expansion is expected to create 46 new jobs. The investment highlights P&G's continued growth and presence in the region.

title: P&G ending new capital investments, reducing portfolio in Russia
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) announced it is halting all new capital investments in Russia and significantly scaling back its product portfolio to focus on essential hygiene, health, and personal care items. This decision comes as major investors urge companies to reconsider operations in Russia due to its invasion of Ukraine. P&G is also suspending all advertising and promotional activities in Russia and has proactively ceased operations in Ukraine, offering support to its employees there.

title: Procter & Gamble To Invest $110M In North Carolina Expansion
summary: Procter & Gamble will invest $110 million to expand its consumer products manufacturing facility in Greensboro, North Carolina. This expansion will add 80,000 square feet to the facility and create 46 new jobs. Local officials expressed enthusiasm for the economic development and job creation in the community.

title: Colgate-Palmolive Co. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Colgate-Palmolive Co. (CL) stock experienced a 0.88% loss on Monday, closing at $76.68, amidst a broader market downturn where the S&P 500 fell 2.95% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 2.37%. Despite this decline, Colgate-Palmolive's stock outperformed several key competitors, including Procter & Gamble Co. (PG), Unilever PLC ADR (UL), and Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC (RBGPF), which all experienced larger percentage losses. The stock closed $8.93 below its 52-week high reached earlier in January.

title: Russian invasion of Ukraine: P&G halting Russian investment and advertising, cutting product offering
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it is significantly cutting back its product offerings in Russia, ceasing all new marketing and investment in the country due to the invasion of Ukraine. The company has also suspended operations in Ukraine and is providing extensive support to its employees there. P&G, which considers Russia one of its top-10 markets, is adjusting its operations while prioritizing employee safety.

title: P&G halts investments, cuts back product sales in Russia
summary: Procter & Gamble is reducing its operations in Russia by halting new capital investments, suspending advertising, and significantly cutting back its product portfolio to focus on essential health, hygiene, and personal care items. This decision comes in response to the war in Ukraine, with P&G also providing relief efforts and support for its employees in Ukraine. The company joins a growing list of global corporations scaling back Russian operations, though some consumer giants like Nestle and Pepsi have yet to follow suit.

title: Procter & Gamble announces new Specialty Beauty division
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has announced the creation of a new Specialty Beauty division, signaling its renewed intent to become a major force in the prestige beauty market. This new division will house recently acquired upmarket skincare brands like Farmacy and Tula Skincare, premium hair brand Ouai, and existing prestige brands such as SK-II and in-house developed brands. The Specialty Beauty division will focus on skin health and operate through specialty retail stores, prestige bricks-and-mortar stores, and direct-to-consumer channels.

title: P&G announces new Specialty Beauty division
summary: Procter & Gamble has established a new Specialty Beauty division under its global P&G Beauty business to house high-end products. This new division will include recent acquisitions like Ouai, Tula Skincare, and Farmacy, as well as First Aid Beauty, and brands incubated in-house such as SeeMe Beauty and KeepItAnchored, alongside SK-II’s North American operations. P&G veteran Chris Heiert will lead the division, reporting to CEO Alex Keith.

title: Huggies Maker to Keep Selling Products in Russia
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corp., the maker of Huggies diapers, announced it will continue selling essential products like baby diapers and feminine pads in Russia, citing the humanitarian nature of these items. However, the company will halt capital spending and advertising in the country and has suspended investments in its Stupino, Russia, facility. This decision comes as other major consumer companies face pressure to cut ties with Russia following its invasion of Ukraine.

title: Nestle, tobacco groups, gamemaker Sony join move away from Russia
summary: Nestle, Philip Morris, and Sony are among the multinational companies ceasing or scaling back operations in Russia, reflecting increasing consumer pressure in the West following the invasion of Ukraine. While some companies pledged to continue providing essentials or gradually reduce manufacturing, others, like Sony, completely halted shipments and operations. The exodus has prompted warnings from Russian officials about potential nationalization of foreign assets, as Russia faces widespread sanctions and economic isolation.

title: VP at Procter & Gamble shares advice with students in leadership course
summary: Jeanie Knuth, VP of Research & Development at Procter & Gamble and a Mizzou Engineering alumna, shared her insights on leadership and career development with students in the new Engineering Leadership and Strategic Communications course. She emphasized the importance of experiential learning, mentorship, and networking, crediting her own Mizzou experiences for her success. Knuth also highlighted her commitment to mentoring others, particularly those facing biases, and giving back to her alma mater.

title: Schick ditches the script for rebrand targeted at everyday men
summary: Schick has launched a rebranding campaign, "Be You. No One Else Can.," focusing on authentic representation of everyday men and what facial hair means to them, rather than using models or celebrities. Developed with Partners & Spade, the campaign features unscripted conversations in black-and-white ads directed by Mike Mills, along with digital extensions on Reddit and TikTok. This initiative aims to resonate with consumers who prioritize authenticity, following a survey indicating that 85% of men prefer to see real people in ads and that personal grooming contributes to self-expression.

title: P&G’s Plan to Get Into Prestige Beauty
summary: Procter & Gamble is re-entering the prestige beauty market seven years after selling off numerous beauty brands, launching a new specialty beauty division and acquiring brands like Tula, Farmacy, and Ouai. The company plans to leverage these acquisitions to expand its presence in the high-growth skin and hair care sectors, despite increased competition from other CPG giants and digital-native brands. P&G aims to support these brands with its R&D and marketing expertise while allowing them to maintain operational autonomy.

title: Chemical industry under pressure to cut ties with Russia
summary: Following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, major chemical companies like BASF, Dow, Solvay, Clariant, LyondellBasell, and DuPont are facing increasing pressure to disengage from Russian business. Many have announced suspensions of new business, investments, and supply of non-essential goods, while some continue to provide products for essential needs like food and hygiene. The conflict has also impacted potential deals, such as Borealis abandoning the sale of its fertilizer business to EuroChem due to sanctions.

title: MSG Entertainment Names Lucas Watson President, MSG Sphere
summary: Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp. announced the appointment of Lucas Watson as President, MSG Sphere, effective March 28. In this role, Watson will lead the business strategy and execution for MSG Sphere, the company's planned immersive entertainment venues, including go-to-market planning and bookings. The first MSG Sphere venue is scheduled to open in Las Vegas in the second half of 2023, and Watson will also oversee the global development of the MSG Sphere brand.

title: Consumer Staples: 5 Things To Know About This Defensive Sector
summary: This article provides an overview of consumer staples stocks, highlighting their defensive nature, consistent dividend payments, and potential drawbacks like modest growth and susceptibility to inflation. It categorizes consumer staples into five subcategories and explains how investors can gain exposure through individual stocks or ETFs. The piece emphasizes their stability during market volatility and their role as a cushion for investor portfolios.

title: Western companies wrestle with Russia 'half-exits'
summary: Western companies providing essential goods like food and medicine in Russia are caught between balancing the Russian government's demands and calls from Ukraine supporters to fully withdraw. While over 400 companies have exited Russia, about 80, including consumer and pharmaceutical giants, maintain a presence, citing humanitarian concerns and potential repercussions for their employees. These firms are devising strategies like donating Russian profits to humanitarian aid or seeking buyers for local operations, as they face growing pressure to fully disengage while navigating legal, operational, and ethical dilemmas.

title: Through Group Black, P&G Pledges Nine-Figure Advertising Buy in Black-Owned Media
summary: Procter & Gamble has committed a nine-figure advertising investment to Group Black, a collective dedicated to accelerating Black-owned media. This significant pledge is the largest single investment Group Black has received since its debut, with the collective aiming to deploy $500 million in Black-owned media by the end of the year. The investment will support Group Black's dual mission of strengthening the Black media landscape through its ecosystem of members and its accelerator for Black-owned media brands.

title: Russia remainers say leaving would hand Putin an easy win
summary: Some companies, despite condemning the invasion of Ukraine, are choosing to scale back operations in Russia rather than fully exit, arguing that leaving entirely would hand an easy win to Putin.
