summary: This article by Ad Age investigates how major brands such as McDonald's, P&G, Coca-Cola, and GM are allocating their advertising budgets towards Black-owned media companies. The content is based on a survey conducted by Ad Age focusing on the spending patterns of these large brands.

title: Always®, International Paper, and Period Heroes Join Forces to Advocate for Federal Action to Help #EndPeriodPoverty in the U.S.
summary: Always, International Paper, and Period Heroes convened in Washington D.C. to support Congresswoman Grace Meng's Menstrual Equity for All Act, aiming to end period poverty by ensuring access to free period products in federal buildings and schools. The initiative highlights that 1 in 5 girls miss school due to lack of period products and advocates for systemic change beyond product donations. This effort stresses the importance of legislative action to address the widespread issue of period poverty and its impact on education and confidence.

title: Unilever posts 20% increase in revenue
summary: Unilever Ghana PLC reported a 20% increase in revenue, reaching GH¢632 million in 2022, up from GH¢530 million in 2021. The company's profit surged significantly to GH¢15 million from GH¢0.4 million the previous year, despite global economic challenges. This growth is attributed to strategic price increases, continuous innovation, and the resilience of its workforce.

title: 2022’s Top Advertisers: P&G, Comcast Join Radio’s $200 Million Club.
summary: Procter & Gamble and Comcast Corp. both surpassed $200 million in radio ad spending in 2022, securing their positions as top advertisers. P&G increased its radio allocation by 48% and Comcast by 35%, while other significant spenders included Deutsche Telekom, the U.S. Government, Berkshire Hathaway, and Pfizer, with Pfizer showing the fastest growth among major advertisers. The article also highlights shifts in ad spending across different media, with AVOD and local radio seeing significant increases.

title: A Discussion With P&G's Chief Sustainability Officer
summary: This article features an interview with Virginie Helias, P&G's Chief Sustainability Officer, discussing the evolution of sustainability at P&G and their strategies to tackle the plastic waste crisis. Helias highlights P&G's shift from regulatory compliance to embedding sustainability across all business functions and emphasizes the importance of partnerships and collaboration to achieve circularity goals, particularly in developing markets. She details P&G's progress towards reducing virgin plastic and increasing recyclable packaging, and outlines their efforts to create a more sustainable and equitable plastics value chain through responsible sourcing and community engagement.

title: Perrigo Appoints Patrick Lockwood-Taylor as President and CEO
summary: Perrigo Company plc has appointed Patrick Lockwood-Taylor as its new President, Chief Executive Officer, and Board member, effective June 30, 2023. Mr. Lockwood-Taylor brings over 25 years of experience in global consumer product leadership, previously serving in a dual role at Bayer AG as President of Bayer U.S. and Regional President of Consumer Health North America, where he achieved significant growth and market share recovery. The company's Chairman, Orlando D. Ashford, highlighted Lockwood-Taylor's experience and proven track record as ideal for executing Perrigo's "Optimize & Accelerate" strategy.

title: Procter & Gamble's Jeff Kent Discusses AI and Machine Learning
summary: Jeff Kent, VP of Smart Platforms Technology & Innovation at Procter & Gamble, detailed the company's application of AI and machine learning to cut manufacturing costs and improve operations. P&G aims for significant efficiency gains and cost reductions using its "WISE" initiative, including the SmartBox edge device, and is implementing thousands of machine learning algorithms across its global sites. The company is strategically moving beyond the traditional Purdue model to achieve more direct and agnostic communication in its push for digitalization and Industry 4.0.

title: Candle Market Size to Grow by $2.8 Billion from 2022 to 2027: Technavio
summary: The global candle market is projected to grow by $2.8 billion from 2022 to 2027, driven by evolving lifestyles, increased home decor demand, and a CAGR of 5.79%. North America is expected to contribute 28% to this growth, fueled by festive demand, natural essential oil candles, and eco-friendly attributes like wooden wicks. Key market players are implementing various growth strategies in this fragmented market.

title: VF Taps Gaming Tech Exec to Be CEO
summary: VF Corp. has appointed Bracken Darrell, former CEO of Logitech, as its new president and CEO, effective July 17. Darrell is known for his history of successful turnarounds, including doubling Logitech’s revenue and increasing its market cap tenfold during his 10-year tenure. He takes over a company where some brands like Vans and Dickies have struggled, though the Vans turnaround is reportedly on track.

title: VF Corporation Appoints Bracken Darrell as President and CEO
summary: VF Corporation (NYSE: VFC) has appointed Bracken Darrell as its new President and CEO, effective July 17, 2023. Darrell previously served as President and CEO of Logitech International for 10 years, where he significantly expanded revenue and market capitalization. Richard Carucci has been named Chair of the Board, and interim CEO Benno Dorer will remain a Board member.

title: Better Buy: Procter & Gamble vs. Clorox
summary: This article compares Procter & Gamble (PG) and Clorox (CLX), concluding that P&G is the better buy primarily due to its significantly larger marketing budget and ability to dominate competitive markets. While Clorox leads in niche categories, P&G's financial muscle allows it to consistently out-promote competitors and maintain an "unfair advantage" in consumer staples. The article emphasizes that P&G's size allows it to better navigate consumer price sensitivity and market competition.

title: P&G’s Vanished Forest Degradation Commitment
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has removed its commitment to prohibit forest degradation from its latest forest sourcing policy, despite previous investor pressure. This move suggests a backtracking on responsible sourcing claims, leaving P&G as a continued driver of degradation in Canada's boreal forests, which has significant climate and biodiversity impacts. The NRDC highlights that P&G's previous claims were misleading and calls for a genuine commitment to eliminate forest degradation.

title: Toothpaste Market size to grow by USD 3.99 billion from 2021 to 2026| Rising dental issues in the children and elderly population to drive the market - Technavio
summary: The global toothpaste market is projected to grow by USD 3.99 billion from 2021 to 2026, driven by an increase in dental issues among children and the elderly and rising awareness of oral hygiene. APAC is expected to contribute 60% to this growth. The market is fragmented with vendors competing on technological advancements and product pricing, while the growth of e-commerce is identified as a key trend.

title: SAP SE Appoints Pinar Dolen as Vice President, Chief Analytics Officer
summary: SAP SE has appointed Pinar Dolen as Vice President, Chief Analytics Officer to lead its global analytics organization and support its transformation into an intelligent, sustainable enterprise. Dolen brings extensive experience in digital transformation from her previous roles at Procter & Gamble and Louis Dreyfus Company. She will leverage advanced analytics to drive SAP's strategic objectives.

title: Despite a decade of effort, P&G can’t please activists on deforestation
summary: Procter & Gamble has struggled for a decade to satisfy environmental activists regarding its deforestation policies, despite implementing sustainable sourcing targets and grievance trackers. Activists criticize P&G's continued sourcing from areas tied to deforestation and forest degradation, particularly in the Canadian boreal forest and its palm oil supply chain. Descendants of P&G's founders are also engaging with the company and activists to advocate for more responsible environmental practices, highlighting the complexity of balancing business needs with ecological concerns.

title: Focus: P&G drops forest pledge, drawing ire of green groups, investors
summary: Procter & Gamble has removed a prior pledge from its corporate policy to not purchase wood pulp from degraded forests, a move that has drawn strong criticism from environmental groups and some investors. P&G stated this change was made because a widely applied definition of forest degradation is unavailable, and affirmed it will comply with an upcoming EU deforestation law. However, environmental NGOs and investors argue there is a broad understanding of forest degradation and are pushing back against the policy change.

title: Unilever appoints chairman of Compass Group Meakins as chair designate
summary: Unilever announced the appointment of Ian Meakins, chairman of Compass Group, as its chair designate, set to replace Nils Andersen. Meakins will join the board on September 1 and become chairman on December 1, while Andersen will step down at the company's Annual General Meeting in May 2024 after nine years of service. Meakins brings a strong background from executive and non-executive roles in various industries, including prior positions at Diageo, Bain & Company, and Procter & Gamble.

title: P&G Beats Profit and Sales Estimates on Higher Prices
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) surpassed profit and sales estimates for its fiscal 2023 fourth quarter, driven by higher prices for its products, even while facing increased costs. Shares rose over 3% following the announcement. However, the company's outlook for fiscal 2024 fell below forecasts due to anticipated macroeconomic challenges.

title: Will inflation make consumers abandon their favorite brands?
summary: Procter & Gamble is being cautious about its 2024 outlook despite better-than-expected quarterly earnings, driven by concerns that inflation may cause consumers to abandon their favorite brands for cheaper alternatives. While brand loyalty is strong due to habit, P&G mitigates this risk by offering a range of brands at different price points, allowing consumers to trade down within its own product portfolio.

title: P&G Trimming SKUs As Part of Collaborative Commerce Strategy
summary: Procter & Gamble is reducing its SKU count, leveraging POS data and proprietary algorithms to optimize product offerings and improve service levels. This initiative is part of a larger collaborative commerce strategy with retail partners, aiming to drive efficiencies, productivity, and maximize overall sales throughput, as other CPG companies like Mondelez and Unilever have also done. The company views SKU rationalization as both a cost-saving and top-line growth opportunity, enhancing its evolving omnichannel strategy.

title: Procter & Gamble sales rise slightly, fueled by higher prices
summary: Procter & Gamble exceeded Wall Street's earnings and revenue expectations for its fiscal fourth quarter, thanks to increased prices on products like Crest and Pampers. Despite this, the company's fiscal 2024 sales forecast fell short of analyst estimates, and it saw its fifth consecutive quarter of volume decline, particularly as consumers in some markets traded down to cheaper alternatives. P&G anticipates volume to start increasing again in fiscal 2024, with only slight price rises.

title: P&G price hikes drive 2023 sales
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) reported sales exceeding $82 billion in 2023, primarily fueled by strategic price increases implemented throughout the year. These price hikes led to a 7% organic sales growth, with a strong performance from the beauty segment, particularly Skin and Personal Care. Despite success in pricing, challenges such as lowered demand in Asia, especially China, partially offset growth in categories like Hair Care.

title: Procter & Gamble Executive Joins Barton School Dean’s Advisory Board
summary: Tadd Fowler, Senior Vice President, Treasurer and Global Taxes at The Procter & Gamble Company, has joined the Barton School Dean’s Advisory Board at Wichita State University. An alumnus of the Barton School, Fowler brings extensive expertise in global treasury and tax matters from his role at P&G, where he manages over $10 billion in annual global tax contributions. This addition is expected to significantly enhance the student experience and curriculum innovation at the Barton School of Business.

title: GSK will close its factory in Nigeria and move to third party direct distribution
summary: GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) Consumer Nigeria is shutting down its manufacturing operations and moving to a third-party distribution model, impacting 290 employees. While Nigerian media link this to foreign exchange shortages, the article suggests GSK's decision is more influenced by its corporate demerger with Haleon and a strategic review of African operations, exemplified by similar moves in Kenya. This transition follows a trend of multinational companies restructuring their presence in Nigeria due to economic challenges and strategic shifts.

title: Detergent Market Size to Grow by $31.5 Billion from 2022 to 2027: Technavio
summary: The global detergent market is projected to grow by $31.5 billion between 2022 and 2027, driven by factors such as the increasing generation of industrial waste and product innovation. North America, with Procter and Gamble dominating, is expected to contribute significantly to this growth. Emerging trends include new packaging designs focusing on flexibility and sustainability, while high price wars pose a significant challenge to market expansion.

title: With 66% ownership of the shares, The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG) is heavily dominated by institutional owners
summary: Institutional investors hold a significant 66% ownership in The Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG), making them the dominant shareholder group and influencing the company's stock price and board decisions. The two largest institutional shareholders are The Vanguard Group, Inc. and BlackRock, Inc. Retail investors, through the general public, own 34% of the company's shares.

title: Colgate-Palmolive and P&G lag behind Unilever at cutting back emissions
summary: A new study by Planet Tracker indicates that Unilever is outperforming Colgate-Palmolive and Procter & Gamble (P&G) in achieving climate transition goals, with the latter companies' projected emissions to 2030 being seven times higher than recommended levels. The report emphasizes the significant financial risks associated with continued high emissions for these FMCG companies, particularly concerning Scope 3 emissions. While Unilever has a more comprehensive mitigation strategy and includes downstream Scope 3 emissions in its targets, all companies still face challenges in meeting stricter climate objectives.

title: Top Analyst Reports for Procter & Gamble, AbbVie & Walt Disney
summary: This article summarizes top analyst reports from Zacks Research Daily on Procter & Gamble (PG), AbbVie (ABBV), and The Walt Disney Company (DIS). It details the financial performance, challenges, and growth prospects for each company, highlighting key drivers and headwinds. Additionally, it mentions other noteworthy reports on HSBC, Boston Scientific, and Duke Energy.

title: P&G enlists IoT, predictive analytics to perfect Pampers diapers
summary: Procter & Gamble is leveraging IoT and predictive analytics, specifically Microsoft's IoT and edge analytics platform, to enhance the production of Pampers diapers. This initiative, dubbed Hot Melt Optimization, uses proprietary sensors and machine learning to predict and prevent manufacturing failures, significantly reducing waste and improving efficiency. The system has eliminated 70% of flawed diapers in 11 plants, showcasing the impact of data-driven innovation in manufacturing.

title: P&G Board of Directors – Rajesh Subramaniam
summary: This article introduces Rajesh Subramaniam, President and CEO of FedEx Corporation, as an independent director on the P&G Board of Directors since 2022. It details his extensive career at FedEx, highlighting his leadership in operations, marketing, global experience, and digital transformation skills, which are valuable to P&G's strategic goals. The piece also lists his other board memberships and advisory roles.

title: P&G Board of Directors – Sheila Bonini
summary: This article introduces Sheila Bonini, an independent director on the P&G Board since 2023. It highlights her extensive background in environmental sustainability and private sector engagement, including her current role as Senior Vice President at World Wildlife Fund and previous leadership at The Sustainability Consortium. Her experience in finance and consulting is also noted, emphasizing her contribution to the Board's environmental, marketing, and regulatory insights.

title: Behind the brand: Knorr – the global taste sensation with the local touch
summary: Knorr, a Unilever brand, has grown from its 1838 origins in Germany to become the world's fifth-largest consumer packaged goods brand, known for its "glocal" approach that tailors global food technologies to local tastes. The brand emphasizes healthy and sustainable eating, promoting plant-based meals, sustainable sourcing, and fortifying products to combat malnutrition. Knorr continues to innovate with salt-free bouillon and campaigns like "Eat for Good Day," while also making packaging more environmentally friendly.

title: Cosmetics Market to Hit USD 417.24 Billion by 2030 | With a CAGR of 4.2%
summary: The global cosmetics market, valued at USD 299.77 billion in 2022, is projected to reach USD 417.24 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 4.2%. This growth is driven by increasing awareness of physical appearance, demand for anti-aging products, and a rise in self-care and grooming trends. Key players in the market are focusing on organic products and strategic partnerships, with Asia Pacific expected to dominate due to its growing geriatric population.

title: Dishwashing Products Market Size, Growth Trends, Forecasts,
summary: The global dishwashing products market is projected to reach over US$ 30.8 billion by 2030, growing at an annual rate of 5.8% from its 2022 valuation of US$ 19.6 billion. The report by RationalStat highlights the importance of these products for hygiene, their diverse formats, and the growing demand driven by convenience, particularly for automatic dishwasher detergents. North America is expected to dominate the market regionally, while the liquid segment is forecast to hold the largest share by type.

title: Shareholding descendants of P&G founders blast company leadership on forest degradation policy
summary: Descendants of Procter & Gamble's founders, who are also shareholders, have publicly criticized the company's leadership for removing pledges against forest degradation in its supply chain. These nine shareholders contend that P&G's current policies expose it to significant financial and regulatory risks, prompting calls for leadership changes within the company.

title: J.M. Smucker to Purchase Hostess Brands in $5.6 Billion Deal
summary: J.M. Smucker Co. is acquiring Hostess Brands for $5.6 billion, including debt, aiming to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing snack market. This strategic move is expected to enhance Smucker's presence in the convenience store channel and meet the increasing consumer demand for on-the-go snack options. Hostess, known for Twinkies and Ding Dongs, has a history of financial struggles but its acquisition aligns with Smucker's ongoing diversification into various consumer goods sectors like coffee and pet food.

title: Active Ingredient in Hundreds of Cold and Flu Meds Is ‘Entirely Ineffective,’ Class Action Says
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against fourteen companies for selling over-the-counter cold and flu medicines containing phenylephrine, an active ingredient that an FDA advisory panel deemed "entirely ineffective" at treating nasal congestion. The lawsuit claims that these companies, including makers of popular brands like Tylenol and Sudafed, have long marketed their products as effective despite knowing the ingredient works no better than a placebo. This legal action follows a unanimous FDA advisory committee vote that phenylephrine does not work to treat nasal congestion, raising questions about its continued use in numerous products.

title: Better Stock Buy: Coca-Cola vs. Procter & Gamble
summary: This article compares Coca-Cola and Procter & Gamble, two major consumer staples companies, to determine which is a better stock buy. It highlights their similarities in business resilience and dividend history, while scrutinizing their differences in product offerings and, critically, their current valuations based on price-to-sales, price-to-earnings, and price-to-book ratios. The analysis concludes that Coca-Cola appears more attractively priced historically compared to P&G.

title: The Price Of Procter & Gamble Company Is Simply Too High (NYSE:PG)
summary: The article argues that Procter & Gamble, despite its strong position as a consumer staple leader with consistent revenue, EPS growth, and a 67-year dividend increase streak, is currently overvalued. While it offers promising growth opportunities and shareholder commitment, its high valuation leaves no margin of safety, especially in uncertain economic conditions. The author, a dividend growth investor, is seeking new investment opportunities but finds PG's current price unattractive.

title: CMO 50 2023: Procter & Gamble’s long-term investments in sustainability reap rewards with younger generations
summary: Procter & Gamble's long-term focus on sustainability and environmental responsibility has helped it gain favor with younger generations, despite their skepticism towards large corporations. The company's marketing strategy integrates ESG principles into its core business, leading to authentic sustainability messages that resonate with consumers and address "big is bad" sentiments. This approach ensures P&G's brands are seen as not just promising, but actively delivering on their commitments to a more sustainable future.

title: Clorox Hack Opens Door For Competitors to Grab Market Share
summary: Clorox Co. is facing a significant risk of losing market share to competitors following a cybersecurity attack that disrupted its US factories and caused product shortages. While most factories have resumed production, some remain offline, leading to empty shelves and opportunities for rival brands to capture market share that may persist. This situation impacts various Clorox products, from bleach to cat litter, and is expected to bolster competing brands.

title: Procter & Gamble brushes off 'vote no' campaign from shareholding descendants over deforestation
summary: Procter & Gamble is facing criticism from a group of shareholders regarding its deforestation policies, leading to a "vote no" campaign against the re-election of company leaders, including Chairman Jon Moeller. P&G has responded to these criticisms. This article previews the situation, highlighting that P&G has pushed back against these shareholder concerns.

title: P&G Leadership - Susan Street Whaley
summary: Susan Street Whaley is the Chief Legal Officer and Secretary at Procter & Gamble, where she leads a global legal organization responsible for legal, compliance, government relations, public policy, and brand protection functions. She also advises P&G's Board of Directors on governance and securities issues, leveraging her extensive experience with the company since 1999. Whaley is known for her strategic counsel, advocacy for equality, and commitment to improving the employee value equation.

title: Undervalued by 30%, This Wide-Moat Dividend Stock Is a Buy
summary: Morningstar identifies Campbell Soup (CPB) as an undervalued wide-moat dividend stock, projecting annual dividend increases at a mid-single-digit rate over the next decade. Despite near-term challenges like increasing competition and cost pressures, the company's strategic focus, brand intangible assets, and cost advantage support a long-term bullish outlook. Morningstar's fair value estimate is $61, suggesting the stock is currently undervalued by 30%.

title: Dividend Aristocrats may shine again if the Fed causes another bad year for the stock market
summary: The article suggests that Dividend Aristocrats, which performed well during the 2022 market downturn, could again be a strong investment if rising interest rates lead to another challenging year for the broader stock market. With investors becoming nervous due to increasing long-term rates, dividend stocks are presented as a potential safe haven. The piece indicates that the S&P Dividend Aristocrats, defined by S&P Dow Jones Indices, may warrant increased investor consideration.

title: Coty Starts Trading on Euronext Paris
summary: Coty Inc. began trading on the professional segment of Euronext Paris on Thursday, marking a step towards its planned double listing alongside its existing presence on the New York Stock Exchange. The stock closed down slightly at 10.39 euros on its first day. This strategic move aims to attract European investors, especially given the significant portion of beauty and luxury companies listed on the Paris Stock Exchange, and the company intends to use the proceeds to reduce its outstanding debt.

title: Clorox advances circular packaging, but virgin material reduction still a challenge
summary: Clorox made progress in its circular packaging goals, with 88% of its plastic packaging now reusable, recyclable, or compostable, partly by removing non-recyclable labels. However, the company is falling behind its virgin material reduction target, achieving only a 9% reduction toward a 50% goal by 2030. Extended producer responsibility policies could significantly increase costs for Clorox if national regulations are adopted.

title: Procter & Gamble makes Forbes' World's Best Employers list for 2023
summary: Procter & Gamble, the Cincinnati-based consumer goods giant, has been named to Forbes' list of the world's best employers for 2023. It is the only local company from Cincinnati to achieve this recognition. The article highlights P&G's continuous prominence in business and employment rankings.

title: Procter & Gamble, Cintas lead list of Cincinnati’s most valuable public companies by market capitalization
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. maintains its position as the largest Greater Cincinnati company by market capitalization. While Cintas Corp. ranks second, LSI Industries showed the most significant market cap growth among the region's 21 locally based public companies this year.

title: St. Bernard Soap Co. slashes half its workers after P&G trims contract manufacturing firms
summary: St. Bernard Soap Co. is set to cut 127 jobs, roughly half its workforce, after Procter & Gamble decided to consolidate its contract manufacturing partners. P&G is moving production from external contractors, including St. Bernard Soap Co., to its own facilities. The company filed a notice with the state of Ohio regarding these impending job cuts.

title: Higher Prices Drive Procter & Gamble's Better-Than-Expected Earnings
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported stronger-than-expected Q1 FY 2024 earnings, with sales up 6% and profit up 17% year-over-year, primarily driven by higher product prices. While some segments saw declining sales volume due to these price increases, the overall financial performance remained robust. The company's successful management of prices and margins has been crucial in navigating inflation, leading to a significant increase in gross margin for the quarter.

title: Procter & Gamble Earnings: Sales and Margins Pop, but Competitive and Macro Headwinds Loom
summary: Procter & Gamble reported strong Q1 results with organic sales jumping 7% and gross margins surging, driven by higher prices and lower commodity costs. Morningstar expects to slightly increase its fair value estimate for P&G stock but notes that shares are not a bargain, advising investors to watch for a potential dip. Despite competitive and macro headwinds, P&G's strategic investments in R&D and marketing are expected to maintain its competitive edge.

title: Colgate-Palmolive Opens AI-Infused Plant to Propel Hill’s Growth
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has opened a new 365,000-square-foot AI-infused manufacturing plant in Tonganoxie, KS, for its Hill’s Pet Nutrition brand to overcome capacity constraints and drive growth. The advanced facility utilizes artificial intelligence, automation, and robotics, including automated guided vehicles and autonomous mobile robots, to enhance efficiency and food safety. This investment aims to boost Hill's Pet Nutrition's rapid growth, which has consistently been a strong performer for Colgate-Palmolive, and expand its presence in the wet pet food category.

title: Empowering Employee ‘P&G + Me’ Stories
summary: This article highlights several P&G employees who share their personal experiences and reasons for loving their careers at the company. It emphasizes P&G's commitment to employee growth, compassion, and fostering a supportive work environment. The testimonials showcase how P&G enables personal and professional development, values diverse voices, and connects employees' passions with their purpose.

title: How Cincinnati public company CEOs rank by shareholder return
summary: An analysis by the Cincinnati Business Courier ranked Dr. August Troendle, CEO of Medpace Holdings, as the top-performing CEO among Greater Cincinnati public companies based on total shareholder return relative to the S&P 500 during his tenure. The article previews how other local public companies, including P&G and Kroger, performed in this ranking.

title: P&G Leadership - Gary Coombe
summary: This article profiles Gary Coombe, CEO of Grooming at P&G and Executive Sponsor of Corporate Wellbeing. It details his 35+ year career at P&G, from a sales representative to leading global brands like Gillette, Venus, and Febreze, and his role in driving diversity and inclusion efforts. The profile highlights his passion for coaching future leaders and his various affiliations and recognitions.

title: Unilever’s Plan to Restore Market Share Underwhelms Investors
summary: Unilever's new CEO, Hein Schumacher, announced a plan to revive the company's struggling market share by focusing on top brands and ruling out major acquisitions, a strategy that underwhelmed investors as shares fell. The plan includes overhauling division heads and naming a new CFO, with Schumacher emphasizing a return to core business and divesting non-core assets like Dollar Shave Club, while moving away from the previous CEO's focus on brand social purpose. Investors were disappointed by the lack of significant portfolio restructuring and the absence of a clear mention of breaking up underperforming businesses.

title: Colgate-Palmolive raises prices again and says the consumer is ‘resilient’
summary: Colgate-Palmolive (COL) reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings after raising prices by an average of 9.5% globally. This move, similar to Procter & Gamble (PG), helped boost profit margins by combating inflationary pressures. The company has repeatedly increased prices over the past year.

title: Procter & Gamble introduces 'blowout-proof' Pampers diaper - Bizwomen
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched a significant innovation in its Pampers Swaddlers line, introducing a "Blowout Barrier" designed to prevent up to 100% of leaks. This improvement, which is the biggest for the brand since 2018, aims to alleviate parents' fears about diaper blowouts, a common issue affecting millions of U.S. parents weekly. The company enlisted celebrity endorsements and highlighted survey data on the widespread impact of blowouts to market the new product.

title: Procter & Gamble introduces innovative Pampers diaper with blowout protections
summary: Procter & Gamble has launched a new version of its Pampers Swaddlers diapers featuring a "Blowout Barrier," marking its most significant innovation for the brand since 2018. This product aims to provide enhanced protection against blowouts.

title: Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway Sells Out of GM, P&G, Johnson & Johnson, and Other Longtime Holdings
summary: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A, BRK.B) engaged in significant selling activity during the third quarter, offloading $5.7 billion in equities. Notable divestitures included entire stakes in GM, Johnson & Johnson, Procter & Gamble, and Activision Blizzard, alongside reductions in Chevron and HP. The company also acquired new positions primarily due to corporate actions by Liberty Media and continued investments in Japanese trading houses.

title: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire sheds General Motors, Procter & Gamble as it builds cash
summary: Berkshire Hathaway has sold off its stakes in General Motors and Procter & Gamble, and reduced its Amazon holdings, while increasing its cash reserves to a record $157.2 billion. The company also divested from Celanese, Mondelez International, and United Parcel Service, reflecting a broader trend of net stock sales throughout 2023. These changes come as Berkshire Hathaway seeks confidential treatment for certain investments, a practice previously used for major stakes in IBM and Exxon Mobil.

title: Berkshire sheds GM, Johnson & Johnson, Procter & Gamble as it amasses cash
summary: Berkshire Hathaway has sold off its holdings in General Motors, Johnson & Johnson, and Procter & Gamble, while also trimming its stake in Amazon.com, according to a recent regulatory filing. These moves have contributed to the conglomerate's record cash pile of $157.2 billion. Berkshire's net stock sales for 2023 totaled $23.6 billion, significantly increasing its cash reserves.

title: LPGA, ESPN Agree to New Two-Year Deal Through 2025
summary: The LPGA and ESPN have signed a new two-year agreement to stream Featured Group coverage at eight LPGA Tour events live and exclusively on ESPN+ through the 2025 season. This deal expands ESPN's commitment to golf and women's sports, offering fans more opportunities to watch LPGA athletes. The agreement includes coverage of this week’s CME Group Tour Championship and the 2024 CME Group Tour Championship.

title: P&G: Stop Forest Destruction
summary: Rainforest Action Network (RAN) criticizes Procter & Gamble (P&G) for weakening its Forest Commodity Policy, which now permits forest degradation from industrial logging in its wood pulp supply chain. RAN is pressuring P&G to cease ties with Royal Golden Eagle (RGE) due to land grabs in Indigenous territories and to uphold Indigenous land rights by requiring Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC). The organization escalated its campaign, leading protests and actions culminating in a large rally and banner drop before P&G's Annual General Meeting to demand an end to forest destruction.

title: The Relative Strength Index (RSI) Indicator: Does It Work?
summary: This article explores the effectiveness of the Relative Strength Index (RSI) as a technical analysis indicator for predicting stock movements. It delves into the RSI's calculation, demonstrates its application using Python with examples like Coca-Cola and Omnicell, and analyzes its performance across the Russell 3000. The author concludes that while RSI alone offers modest returns, its effectiveness significantly improves when combined with fundamental analysis, especially when applied to mean-reverting or high-risk stocks, and can even be reversed for "breakout" stocks.

title: ‘Effectiveness breeds spending’: Procter & Gamble moves to take more marketing in-house
summary: Procter & Gamble is continuing its strategy of taking more marketing functions in-house, shifting media planning duties for several brands from Dentsu's Carat to internal teams. This move aligns with CEO Jon Moeller's philosophy that greater marketing efficiency leads to more spending and drives market growth. P&G has already increased its marketing spend and plans further investment as it aims to return to pre-pandemic ad levels, focusing on digital reach and targeting improvements.

title: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway sells off shares of Procter & Gamble - Cincinnati Business Courier
summary: Warren Buffett's investment conglomerate, Berkshire Hathaway, has sold all of its shares in the Cincinnati-based consumer goods company, Procter & Gamble. The brief article, published in the Cincinnati Business Courier, reports on this significant financial move. The exact reasons for the liquidation were not detailed in the provided content.

title: What they are saying about development on and around the Dayton International Airport
summary: The area around Dayton International Airport has seen significant commercial development over the past decade, driven by logistics, distribution, and increasingly, aerospace manufacturing companies. This growth has brought new jobs, tax revenue, and the need for substantial infrastructure investments. Local officials and business leaders emphasize the region's strategic location and the diverse job opportunities this development provides.

title: Household Cleaning Products Market to Reach US$ 355 Billion
summary: The global household cleaning products market is projected to reach US$ 355 billion by 2030, growing at an annual rate of over 4.8% from its 2023 valuation of US$ 255.7 billion. This growth is driven by increasing demand for effective hygiene and home care solutions, coupled with innovations in convenient and user-friendly products. Laundry detergents hold the largest market share, with the Asia Pacific region being dominant, influenced by factors like home improvement trends and rising disposable incomes.

title: Surface Disinfectant Market size worth $ 1424.76 Million, Globally, by 2030 at 8.38% CAGR: Verified Market Research®
summary: The global surface disinfectant market is projected to reach USD 1424.76 million by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 8.38% from 2023. This growth is driven by an increase in surgical procedures worldwide and a rising demand for infection prevention. The market is segmented by formulation, type, application, end-user, and geography, with Asia-Pacific holding the largest market share in 2019.

title: S&P turns negative on Clorox after cyberattack causes shortages
summary: S&P Global Ratings lowered its outlook for Clorox Co. to negative due to stock shortages and lost distribution following a cyberattack earlier this year. The attack led to widespread operational disruptions, switching to manual processes, and a significant 26% drop in sales volumes by September 30. While S&P affirmed Clorox's BBB+ rating, analysts expressed concerns about the lengthy recovery process and potential long-term impacts on shelf space and market share.

title: Warren Buffett-Led Berkshire Hathaway Sells Its Entire Procter & Gamble Stake. Should You?
summary: Berkshire Hathaway fully exited its small position in Procter & Gamble, likely due to consolidating its portfolio and P&G's premium valuation compared to other opportunities like Apple. Despite Berkshire's sale, P&G is still considered a worthwhile investment for risk-averse individuals due to its strong brand development, pricing power, and commitment to shareholder returns through dividends and buybacks. The article suggests that while P&G's valuation is high, its other characteristics make it a solid choice for passive income and portfolio stability.

title: P&G to Record Up to $2.5 Billion in Charges Related to Gillette Business, Restructuring
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it would record up to $2.5 billion in charges over two fiscal years. These charges are linked to writing down the value of its Gillette business, which it acquired in 2005, and restructuring efforts in certain markets like Argentina and Nigeria. The company attributed these charges, which include a $1.3 billion non-cash impairment charge on Gillette, partly to a stronger US dollar and difficult macroeconomic conditions.

title: P&G to record up to $2.5 bln in Gillette writedown, operations rejig
summary: Procter & Gamble announced it would record up to $2.5 billion in charges over two fiscal years, including a $1.3 billion non-cash impairment charge on its Gillette business and $1 billion to $1.5 billion related to restructuring operations in Argentina and Nigeria. These charges are attributed to writing down the value of Gillette and difficult macroeconomic conditions compounded by a stronger dollar. The consumer goods giant expects these charges to be recognized in fiscal years 2024 and 2025, leading to a 2% drop in its shares.

title: P&G Will Take Up to $2.5 Billion in Charges for Restructuring, Gillette Impairment
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. announced charges of up to $2.5 billion over the next two fiscal years for restructuring operations in certain enterprise markets, including Argentina and Nigeria, and a non-cash impairment related to its Gillette business. The company's shares fell 3.5% following the announcement. P&G warned that while Gillette's performance is strong, future adverse conditions could lead to further impairment charges.

title: P&G shares slump amid $2B+ in reported charges for restructuring, Gillette write down
summary: Procter & Gamble announced a $1 billion write down of Gillette's market value and restructuring moves on Dec. 5. This decision comes as the U.S. dollar continues to strengthen against other currencies, impacting P&G's shares. The write down contributes to over $2 billion in reported charges for the company.

title: Jim Cramer explains why he's sticking with Procter & Gamble despite its 2023 dip
summary: Jim Cramer remains confident in Procter & Gamble (PG) despite its underperformance in 2023 compared to the S&P 500. He describes the company as a "dividend aristocrat" with solid fundamentals that he believes the market is currently misunderstanding due to temporary currency impacts. Cramer, whose Charitable Trust holds PG, highlighted its strong track record of delivering value and good yield.

title: Kellanova Paves Way to Less Plastic: A Glimpse Into Innovative Packaging
summary: Kellanova is making significant strides in reducing plastic waste by implementing innovative packaging solutions for its snack brands, resulting in a substantial reduction of plastic and corrugated cardboard. These efforts align with the company's "Kellanova Better Days Promise" to achieve 100% reusable, recyclable, or compostable packaging by 2030, emphasizing a circular economy approach and consumer education on recycling. The company's initiatives reflect a broader industry trend towards sustainable packaging, driven by environmental concerns and consumer demand.

title: Procter & Gamble Co. stock rises Wednesday, still underperforms market
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. (PG) shares rose 0.08% on Wednesday, closing at $146.06. Despite this gain, the stock underperformed the broader market, with the S&P 500 Index rising 0.14% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average increasing 0.30% during the same session. This marked the fourth consecutive day of gains for the company's stock.

title: 5 Reasons to Avoid Procter & Gamble Stock (PG) Without Hesitation
summary: This article outlines five reasons why investors may want to avoid buying Procter & Gamble stock (PG), despite its reputation as a safe consumer products company. The reasons include its expensive valuation at 24 times earnings, potential for slower earnings-per-share growth due to higher input prices, consumer shift to cheaper generic brands during a recession, a "good but not great" dividend yield of 2.59%, and alleged environmental issues related to sourcing. The article suggests holding existing shares but advises against new purchases.

title: P&G Earnings Show Its Pricing Power Endures
summary: Procter & Gamble continues to demonstrate strong pricing power as consumers accept higher prices for its premium brands like Tide, despite a slip in sales volumes. The company successfully raised prices by 7% in the June quarter, following two consecutive quarters of approximately 10% year-over-year increases. This strategy has helped prop up P&G's sales, indicating consumers' willingness to pay more for essential goods from the company.

title: Storied former P&G soap factory shutting down in March
summary: The St. Bernard Soap Co., a former Procter & Gamble subsidiary and contractor known for producing iconic bar soaps like Ivory, will cease operations by mid-March, leading to 118 job losses. This decision follows P&G's strategy to consolidate contract manufacturing and shift production to its Boston plant. The Ivorydale facility, where St. Bernard Soap Co. operated, has a long history dating back to 1886.

title: Patrick Industries buys Minnesota manufacturer Sportech for $315 million
summary: Patrick Industries has acquired Sportech, a Minnesota-based manufacturer of vehicle component parts for motorcycles, snowmobiles, and ATVs, for $315 million. This acquisition will expand Patrick Industries' presence in the powersports and off-roading markets, complementing its core business in recreational vehicles and boats. Sportech's customers include major brands like Polaris, Kawasaki, and Honda.

title: P&G beauty line needs a makeover, analysts say
summary: Analysts suggest that Procter & Gamble's beauty care business, which accounts for nearly a quarter of its revenue, needs a significant turnaround to reignite sales growth. The beauty segment, anchored by major brands like Pantene, Wella, and Olay, posted flat organic sales growth for the year in the March quarter, marking its worst performance since the Great Recession. Newly-returned CEO A.G. Lafley is expected to address these challenges as the company prepares to release its annual earnings.

title: Which companies are ‘Most Admired for HR’? Here are the leaders
summary: The 19th annual "Most Admired for HR" list, compiled by Korn Ferry and HRE, shows significant shifts, with DHL Group rising to No. 1. Megabanks and semiconductor companies also saw substantial climbing in rankings, while perennial leaders like Apple maintained high positions. The report highlights trends like emphasizing learning and development, strategic workforce planning, and a focus on culture alignment with business objectives for HR excellence.

title: Media reports: Johnson & Johnson reaches settlement to resolve talc baby powder investigations
summary: Johnson & Johnson has reportedly reached a $700 million settlement with over 40 states investigating whether the company misled the public about the safety of its talc-based baby powder. This settlement addresses investigations stemming from over 50,000 lawsuits due to asbestos contamination in talc, which can cause life-threatening illnesses. Although J&J stopped selling talc-based baby powder in 2020 and now uses a cornstarch alternative, the company still faces individual consumer lawsuits, highlighting the ongoing need for stricter regulation of consumer products by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

title: P&G: ‘Now Is Not The Time To Be Pulling Back On Investments In Marketing.’
summary: Procter & Gamble reported a 4% increase in organic sales for its fiscal quarter ending December 2023, with CEO Jon Moeller attributing success to superior innovations and effective marketing. Moeller emphasized that P&G will continue to invest heavily in marketing and commercialization, stating that now is not the time to pull back on such investments, especially given the continuous product innovation. The company rigorously analyzes its marketing spend to ensure maximum return on investment, maintaining its position as a top advertiser in channels like radio.

title: «There’s No White Knight for the Global Economy»
summary: Bryan Whalen, Co-Chief Investment Officer at TCW, warns that despite market optimism, a global recession is practically inevitable due to aggressive interest rate hikes and ongoing economic stresses. He points to declining capital expenditures, tightening lending conditions, and rising consumer delinquencies as red flags, arguing that the US Federal Reserve's policy will remain restrictive, making a "soft landing" unlikely. Whalen advises bond investors to be long interest rate duration, particularly in the front end of the curve, and defensive with corporate credit.

title: Progressive was the 2nd-best performing stock among major Ohio companies last week
summary: Progressive Corp. was the second-best performing stock among major Ohio companies last week, with a 5.5% increase in share price. The top performer was Procter & Gamble Co., which saw a 5.8% rise. The article lists eleven Ohio companies that experienced significant stock price gains, including four from the Cleveland-Akron area.

title: Coca-Cola pilot removes labels from Sprite bottles to ease recycling
summary: Coca-Cola has launched a limited trial of label-less 500mL Sprite and Sprite Zero bottles in British supermarkets to further ease recycling and reduce packaging material. The initiative follows the company's 2022 move to switch Sprite bottles from green to clear PET to improve bottle-to-bottle circularity. The company aims for all its packaging to be recyclable by 2025 and to cut 3 million metric tons of virgin plastic by 2025 from a 2020 baseline.

title: 2027 the Target for Transition Away from 1D GTIN, Toward Digital Link 2D Barcodes
summary: The packaging industry is targeting 2027 for a significant transition from the traditional 1D GTIN barcode to the more versatile Digital Link 2D barcode. This shift, driven by increasing consumer demand for information, regulatory requirements, and supply chain traceability needs, will enable a single QR code to provide different information to various stakeholders (consumers, retailers, supply chain partners). The "Sunrise 2027" program aims to prepare the necessary infrastructure, primarily software changes, for this industry-wide adoption.

title: In Depth: The power of prestige beauty
summary: Despite global challenges like a pandemic and cost-of-living crisis, the prestige beauty market continues to thrive, driven by consumer desire for small luxuries and emotional purchases. Major beauty companies like Shiseido, Unilever, and Estée Lauder are heavily investing in this sector through acquisitions and strategic developments, recognizing its robust growth potential and attractive profit margins compared to mass-market brands. This trend, often linked to the "lipstick effect," is expected to continue with more investments and acquisitions in 2024 and beyond.

title: Waldencast Names Manuel Manfredi as CFO
summary: Waldencast plc announced the appointment of Manuel Manfredi as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective April 1, 2024. Manfredi brings nearly 25 years of financial leadership experience in the beauty and consumer products industries, most recently serving as CFO for L’Oréal Spain and Portugal. Michel Brousset, Waldencast's CEO, will act as interim CFO until Manfredi's start date, succeeding Philippe Gautier who is departing the company.

title: Artificial Intelligence at Procter & Gamble
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is scaling its AI initiatives across various departments, focusing on clear business purposes, organizational AI fluency, and standardized development. The article highlights two key AI use cases: supply chain optimization using the KNIME platform for predictive analytics and consumer behavior analysis through real-time data from smart products like the Oral B iO toothbrush to inform product development. These applications aim to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance customer satisfaction for the multinational goods corporation.

title: Neighbors oppose P&G expansion at former Iowa City Kirkwood campus
summary: Neighbors in Iowa City are opposing Procter & Gamble's proposed expansion onto the former Kirkwood Community College campus, citing concerns about environmental justice and potential health impacts from increased industrial activity. Residents, including Anne Marie Kraus, fear the expansion will exacerbate existing issues like air pollution and argue that the area, which has a higher percentage of low-income and minority residents, should not be disproportionately affected by industrial development. The Iowa City Council is set to consider rezoning the 6.8-acre property from neighborhood public to general industrial, despite P&G stating they have no immediate plans for the site beyond potential expansion of oral care operations, not chemical production.

title: General Mills rolls out MillsChat, an internal generative AI tool
summary: General Mills has launched MillsChat, a private generative AI tool built on Google's PaLM 2 model, for its employees in the U.S., Canada, U.K., and India. The tool is designed to assist with writing, summarizing, and brainstorming in a secure environment. This initiative reflects General Mills' increasing investment in AI, having grown its data science headcount fortyfold since 2018, and aligns with other food brands like Kraft Heinz, Coca-Cola, and Procter & Gamble that are also integrating generative AI into their operations to improve business outcomes and operational efficiencies despite a challenging consumer landscape.

title: P&G CEO would change debate from 'social justice to winning' to bolster diversity
summary: Procter & Gamble CEO Jon Moeller advocates for reframing the conversation around diversity from "social justice" to "winning" to make a more powerful argument for women and diverse individuals in leadership roles. He emphasized that linking diverse representation to business success is fundamental for attracting and serving a diverse consumer base. Moeller expects that P&G will eventually have a female CEO, acknowledging that a significant portion of their consumer base is women.

title: The Clorox Company Tops Barron’s 2024 List of The 100 Most Sustainable US Companies
summary: The Clorox Company has topped Barron’s 2024 list of the 100 Most Sustainable US Companies for the second consecutive year, achieving a final score of 77 based on 230 environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance indicators. Other notable companies from the beauty, cleaning, and personal care industries, including Procter & Gamble, Ecolab, The Estée Lauder Companies, and Colgate-Palmolive, also made the list. Clorox highlighted its accomplishments in pay equity, ESG governance, board diversity, its climate action plan, renewable energy use, and waste reduction efforts.

title: Nestlé, P&G, and Walmart reveal their 2024 talent retention secrets
summary: Nestlé, Procter & Gamble, and Walmart are focusing on talent retention in 2024 by enhancing employee benefits, offering stock options, and promoting internal growth through structured career development and access to AI tools. P&G, for instance, emphasizes continuous learning within the company, with employees typically taking on five different roles in their first decade. This strategy aims to counteract high job-switching rates and foster a "Big Stay" environment.

title: Kroger and P&G open applications for the 2024 Game Changers Scholarship
summary: Kroger's Columbus Division and The Procter & Gamble Company have opened applications for their 2024 Game Changers Scholarship program. The scholarship aims to support underrepresented female students pursuing higher education in business, science, technical, and liberal arts fields. One local scholarship of $2,000 will be awarded by Kroger, contributing to a national total of over $45,000 for 23 women, administered by the Ohio Foundation of Independent Colleges and Scholarship Management Resources.

title: Procter & Gamble SVP Named Barton School’s Executive-in-Residence
summary: Tadd Fowler, Senior Vice President at Procter & Gamble and an alumnus, has been named the Spring 2024 Executive-in-Residence for the W. Frank Barton School of Business at Wichita State University. He will deliver a public keynote address, mentor students, and guest lecture, discussing P&G's transformation and relevancy. This initiative aims to provide students and the public with insights from a distinguished executive.

title: Microsoft, P&G, Unilever and Walmart among 239 companies to miss net-zero deadline
summary: The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) has reclassified 239 companies, including Microsoft, P&G, Unilever, and Walmart, as "commitment removed" for net-zero goals because they failed to submit science-based targets for validation within the 24-month deadline. A significant obstacle for these companies is the difficulty in reducing Scope 3 emissions, which relate to indirect emissions from customers and supply chains. Despite the reclassification, these major corporations maintain that they are continuing to pursue aggressive emissions reduction targets and are in various stages of reviewing or updating their strategies to align with SBTi standards, with many still holding near-term validated targets.

title: The First Brands acquisition: Marking 25 years
summary: The article reflects on the 25th anniversary of The Clorox Company's acquisition of First Brands Inc., a pivotal event that doubled Clorox's size and brought iconic brands like Glad and Scoop Away into its portfolio. It highlights the transformation and innovation that followed, including the development of advanced products like Glad's ForceFlex™ and OdorShield® technologies and Scoop Away's enhanced features. The piece also acknowledges the integration of First Brands' facilities and, most importantly, its employees into the Clorox family, celebrating the enduring legacy of the acquisition.

title: Procter & Gamble Brings Relief to Residents Affected by Tornadoes in Ohio and Indiana
summary: Procter & Gamble, in partnership with Walmart and Matthew 25: Ministries, is providing disaster relief to communities in Ohio and Indiana affected by recent tornadoes. Beginning March 18, 2024, at the Church of God in Russells Point, Ohio, they will offer free laundry services via the Tide Loads of Hope Mobile Laundry Unit, hot showers from a dedicated trailer, and distribute personal care kits and cleaning supplies. These services aim to help families and first responders in their recovery efforts.

title: P&G’s Former Chair Bob McDonald: ‘Life Is A Series Of Starting Over’
summary: This article features insights from former P&G CEO and U.S. Secretary of Veterans Affairs, Bob McDonald, as discussed in the Corporate Competitor Podcast with Don Yaeger. McDonald emphasizes the importance of an "abundance mindset" and the confidence to embrace new beginnings throughout life and career. He shares his journey from a high-ranking military career to leading P&G and later the Department of Veterans Affairs, highlighting his purpose-driven approach and leadership philosophy centered on serving others.

title: Dow, Procter & Gamble partnering to develop new recycling technology
summary: Dow and Procter & Gamble have formed a joint development agreement to create a new recycling technology. This initiative aims to efficiently convert hard-to-recycle plastic packaging into near-virgin quality recycled polyethylene with a low greenhouse gas emissions footprint. The partnership seeks to advance a circular economy by enabling the reuse of recycled polymers in consumer packaging.

title: Dow and P&G partner to create new plastics recycling technology
summary: Dow and Procter & Gamble (P&G) have formed a joint development agreement to create new proprietary recycling technology for hard-to-recycle plastic waste. This collaboration aims to convert challenging packaging, including rigid, flexible, and multilayer plastics, into high-quality recycled polyethylene (PE) using a dissolution process. The goal is to produce near-virgin quality PCR PE with reduced greenhouse gas emissions, which P&G plans to integrate into its consumer packaging to foster a circular economy.

title: Rolaids® Bolsters Presence in Convenience Stores Through Strategic Partnership with Lil’ Drug Store Products
summary: Lil’ Drug Store Products (LDSP) has partnered with Procter & Gamble (P&G) to become the primary distributor of Rolaids® to convenience and travel retailers nationwide. This collaboration aims to make Rolaids the #1 antacid brand in the convenience sector by 2028, leveraging P&G's investment and targeting the significant overlap between convenience store consumers and heartburn sufferers. LDSP has already resumed distribution of Rolaids products, which will feature flavor and texture upgrades under P&G's ownership.

title: Kimberly-Clark to reorganize business, incur $1.5 bln in costs
summary: Kimberly-Clark announced a reorganization into three business units to simplify operations and cut costs, expecting to incur about $1.5 billion in related costs over the next three years, with half of that from workforce reductions. The move comes as the company faces waning benefits from price hikes and increased competition from private-label alternatives. The restructuring aims to generate over $3 billion in gross productivity and $500 million in working capital savings, expecting completion by the end of 2024.

title: New Balance President and CEO Joe Preston and Procter & Gamble-Gillette Vice President Karan Dyson to Deliver Commencement Addresses at Bentley University
summary: Bentley University announced that New Balance President and CEO Joe Preston will deliver the keynote address for the undergraduate commencement, and Procter & Gamble-Gillette Vice President Karan Dyson will speak at the graduate commencement. Both executives are recognized for their leadership and will receive honorary Doctor of Commercial Science degrees. The ceremonies, celebrating over 1,500 students, will take place on May 17th and 18th, 2024.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Berkshire Hathaway, Procter & Gamble, Adobe, Advanced Micro Devices and AstraZeneca
summary: This Zacks Analyst Blog highlights research reports on major stocks including Berkshire Hathaway, Procter & Gamble, and Adobe, along with Advanced Micro Devices and AstraZeneca PLC. It provides an overview of each company's recent performance, key financial drivers, and potential headwinds. The article emphasizes Zacks Investment Research's stock-picking strategies and their strong historical performance.

title: Dear Younger Self: 3 Lessons From a P&G Executive
summary: Fama Francisco, CEO of Global Baby, Feminine and Family Care at P&G, shares three key lessons learned over her 35-year career. These lessons include persevering when faced with setbacks, embracing one's unique authentic self and flexing different skills, and prioritizing personal well-being to avoid burnout. Her experiences highlight P&G's commitment to employee development and a diverse, inclusive workplace.

title: Cereal giant Post is bringing a distribution center to North Texas
summary: Post Consumer Brands, a division of Post Holdings Inc. (NYSE: POST), known for cereals like Fruity Pebbles and Honeycomb, is establishing a 1.1 million-square-foot distribution center in Wilmer, near Dallas. This move follows the company's expansion, including recent pet food brand acquisitions, and aims to optimize its distribution network. The deal represents the largest industrial lease in the DFW region for 2024 so far.

title: P&G vendió las marcas Magistral y Ariel a Dreamco S.A.
summary: Dreamco S.A. has completed the acquisition of P&G's fabric and dish care business in Argentina, including the brands Magistral and Ariel. This transaction involved the transfer of a plant and distribution center in Pilar, Buenos Aires, along with equipment and specific usage permits. Bruchou & Funes de Rioja advised Dreamco on labor aspects and on securing a syndicated loan from Banco de Galicia and Banco BBVA Argentina for working capital and asset structuring.

title: 2023 Top 100: Why Procter & Gamble’s Beauty Business Grew Across the Board
summary: Procter & Gamble's beauty division experienced significant growth in 2023 across most brands and geographies, despite economic headwinds. The mass hair business showed steady growth, while the Specialty Beauty division, including acquired brands like Mielle Organics and Native, saw sales swell over 70 percent. Olay's skincare innovations contributed to moderate growth, though high-end brand SK-II faced sales declines due to geopolitical factors.

title: Procter & Gamble Co: Disclosure of PFAS-Related Risk Management Practices
summary: A shareholder resolution requests Procter & Gamble to publish a report detailing its management of health and environmental risks associated with PFAS chemicals in its products. This request follows concerns about PFAS detection in Tampax products and the broader health and litigation risks linked to these chemicals. Other personal care companies are already taking steps to minimize PFAS and disclose their efforts.

title: Procter & Gamble's strategic pricing shift should accelerate business growth this year
summary: Procter & Gamble is adjusting its pricing strategy to prioritize volume growth over price increases, responding to inflation-weary consumers. This shift is expected to accelerate business growth, with analysts anticipating improved volumes due to more stable pricing. Wall Street is closely watching P&G's upcoming fiscal 2024 third-quarter earnings report for signs of this strategy's impact.

title: P&G’s stock falls after a sales miss, as baby and health-care volumes declined
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. (P&G) stock fell after the company reported fiscal third-quarter sales that missed forecasts, primarily due to weakness and volume declines in its baby, feminine, and family-care segments. Despite the sales miss, P&G beat quarterly profit expectations and subsequently raised its full-year outlook. Prices increased at the slowest rate in over two years, while volume remained flat for the second consecutive quarter.

title: Procter & Gamble Stock Slips Despite Earnings Beat as Q3 Sales Miss Estimates
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported third-quarter earnings that surpassed estimates, but revenue fell short of expectations, leading to a slight dip in share price. Despite missing sales estimates, the company maintained its full-year sales growth outlook and increased its EPS projections. Organic sales remained strong across most segments, driven by a 3% price increase.

title: P&G lifts annual profit forecast on strong US consumer demand, easing costs
summary: Procter & Gamble raised its annual profit forecast due to lower commodity costs and continued strong consumer demand, especially in the U.S. and Europe. This comes despite a slight miss on third-quarter net sales expectations. The company also anticipates a higher benefit from favorable commodity costs for fiscal year 2024.

title: Huggies backpedals on ad claims after challenge from Pampers parent P&G
summary: Huggies has retracted certain ad claims following a challenge from Procter & Gamble, the parent company of competitor Pampers. The contested campaign, created by Quality Meats, featured diverse baby bottoms. This development highlights ongoing competitive dynamics in the diaper market.

title: Fifth Third's Somalya on Diversity in Governance
summary: Saema Somalya, deputy general counsel at Fifth Third, emphasizes the critical role of board diversity for corporate competitiveness and economic well-being. She highlights that diverse perspectives are essential for anticipating trends and strengthening oversight, citing Fifth Third's recent addition of Linda Clement-Holmes to its board as an example of a qualifications-based approach leading to increased diversity. Somalya also anticipates increased shareholder activism around board diversity, driven by ESG-focused investing.

title: Inside the 2024 CEW Achiever Awards
summary: The 2024 CEW Achiever Awards honored several prominent women in the beauty industry, including executives from Estée Lauder Cos., Shiseido, Ulta Beauty, and L'Oréal. The event, which drew around 1,000 attendees, also recognized the founder of Supergoop as the keynote speaker, emphasizing themes of passion, purpose, and people. Award recipients shared insights on career growth, the importance of diversity and inclusion, and the impact of mentorship and community in their professional journeys.

title: Procter and Gamble descendant proposes bill to stop the type of animal testing P&G has done
summary: A descendant of Procter & Gamble founders, State Rep. Sara Carruthers (R-Hamilton), has introduced House Bill 495 in Ohio to end most cosmetics animal testing, a practice P&G still engages in despite claiming to be cruelty-free. The bill aims to save animals and boost the cruelty-free cosmetic market, but it faces opposition from medical experts like Sharona Hoffman, who warns of potential negative impacts on medical advancements and research for conditions like burn victims or reconstructive surgeries. While Carruthers argues for cheaper, modern testing alternatives, Hoffman contends that animal studies are crucial for understanding complex biological interactions.

title: West Chester business picks up work after P&G subsidiary closes
summary: ASIC Corp. in West Chester Twp. has taken over the controls piece of the injection molding business after iMFLUX, a Procter & Gamble subsidiary, shut down its Symmes Road operations last year. ASIC, a family-owned business, has hired three former iMFLUX employees and is now responsible for machine sales, training, and service for the control systems, working in conjunction with P&G to advance the imflux technology. They provide replacement parts and integrate the imflux system into various OEM machines for any industry.

title: Changing culture will be key to attracting more women professionals, says AlphaSimplex's Kathryn Kaminski
summary: Kathryn Kaminski of AlphaSimplex Group, who has an engineering background, believes that cultural changes are crucial for attracting more women into the asset management industry. The article highlights this perspective and includes several other financial news snippets covering topics like private credit, endowments, private equity, and pension funds.

title: P&G shifts focus to brands for Paris Olympics ads
summary: Procter & Gamble is changing its advertising strategy for the upcoming Paris Olympics, moving away from its traditional corporate "Thank you, Mom" campaigns to focus on individual brands like Pampers and Gillette. This shift means P&G will launch advertising for over 30 brands, more than ever before, with a particular emphasis on European retailers. The company's chief brand officer stated that this new approach is designed to align with what consumers are more familiar with.

title: P&G Details Cost-Cutting Productivity Enhancements Across Supply Chain, R&D, and Marketing
summary: Procter & Gamble is achieving significant cost savings and productivity gains through digital transformation efforts across its supply chain, R&D, and marketing departments. These enhancements include using technology for faster product reformulation, defect detection in manufacturing, and optimizing marketing strategies. CFO Andre Schultenn expects annual savings of $1.5 billion from supply chain improvements and $500 million from R&D and marketing optimizations.

title: Procter & Gamble announces marketing plans for Paris 2024
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has unveiled its marketing strategy for the Olympic and Paralympic Games Paris 2024, leveraging its status as a Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic Partner. The plan includes Olympic-themed brand marketing, in-store promotions, athlete partnerships, and complimentary products and services for athletes. Brands like Venus and Gillette are launching specific campaigns to highlight product performance in an Olympic context.

title: P&G Honours Suppliers Driving Excellence in Supply Chains
summary: P&G recognized its external business partners at the 2024 Partner of the Year Awards, highlighting their exceptional contributions to supply chains, consumer satisfaction, environmental sustainability, and equality and inclusion. The company awarded five suppliers with the Supplier Impact Award and acknowledged many others for their vital roles in enabling P&G's global operations. Chief Purchasing Officer Ana Elena Marziano emphasized the critical nature of these partnerships for innovation, problem-solving, and mutual business growth.

title: Procter & Gamble, Mondelēz, and Nestlé Are Among 10 of the Leading Consumer Brands Driving Global Deforestation
summary: This article highlights how major consumer brands, including Procter & Gamble, Mondelēz, and Nestlé, are significantly contributing to global deforestation and human rights abuses despite public commitments. A report by the Rainforest Action Network (RAN) graded ten multinational corporations, finding none achieved an 'A' grade, with several performing poorly due to insufficient policies, lack of third-party verification, and continued engagement in practices harmful to forests and communities. The author calls for genuine commitment, transparent reporting, and comprehensive NDPE policies across all supply chains to combat the climate crisis.

title: Procter & Gamble’s Ranya Shamoon brings growth to a tough European baby care market
summary: Ranya Shamoon of Procter & Gamble has successfully driven consistent growth for the company's baby care division in Europe over the past three years. This achievement is particularly notable given the challenging market conditions in the region. The article highlights her role in navigating these difficulties to ensure sustained progress for P&G's baby care portfolio.

title: How Walmart, P&G, General Motors, PepsiCo and other big marketers are spending on Black-owned media
summary: This article discusses how major marketers like Walmart, P&G, General Motors, and PepsiCo are increasing their advertising spend on Black-owned media channels. Based on an Ad Age survey of Black-owned media companies, these brands significantly boosted their investment in 2023. The piece highlights a trend among large companies to support Black-owned media.

title: McCormick adds former Procter & Gamble exec to board
summary: McCormick has appointed a former Procter & Gamble executive to its board of directors, increasing the board's size to 13 members. This article previews the announcement and provides links to related stories about McCormick's executive compensation, new product lines, sales performance, and previous board additions.

title: Campbell Soup Company Shakes Up Supply Chain
summary: Campbell Soup Company is investing $230 million through fiscal year 2026 to modernize its supply chain operations, creating 210 new jobs. This includes significant investments in plants in Maxton, North Carolina; Hanover, Pennsylvania; and Franklin, Wisconsin, along with expanding Goldfish cracker production in Richmond, Utah. The company will also close its Tualatin, Oregon plant and shift production in Jeffersonville, Indiana, as part of its strategy to increase efficiency and drive business growth.

title: Western Companies U-Turn on Russia Exit Plans – FT
summary: Western companies are reconsidering their plans to exit Russia due to high Kremlin-imposed exit costs, difficulties in finding suitable buyers, and a resurgence in consumer activity, according to the Financial Times. While 1,610 foreign companies have left or scaled back operations, 2,175 still remain, with some openly discussing their intentions to stay. Challenges to exiting include mandatory 50% discounts on assets, a 15% exit tax, and the need for Moscow-approved, unsanctioned Russian buyers.

title: Huggies Owner Kimberly-Clark Exits Africa’s Most Populous Market
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corp., the maker of Huggies diapers and Kotex sanitary pads, is ceasing operations in Nigeria after almost 15 years, citing economic developments and a shift in global strategic priorities. This marks its second exit from the country in recent years, following a relaunch in 2022. The departure is part of a larger trend of global conglomerates leaving Nigeria due to currency crises, high operating costs, and unreliable infrastructure.

title: Procter & Gamble to build plant in Poland
summary: Procter & Gamble announced plans to construct a €38m cosmetics plant in Aleksandrow Lodzki, Poland, with an investment of $50m by 2012 and the creation of 300 jobs. This move is part of a broader trend of multinational companies investing in Eastern European markets due to increasing disposable income and booming cosmetics sales. P&G, which already has a strong presence in Poland, expects the factory to be operational by 2009.

title: Aerosol can recycling has confounded consumers. There’s a push to fix that by 2030.
summary: The Aerosol Recycling Initiative, involving the Can Manufacturers Institute and Household and Commercial Products Association, aims to improve aerosol can recycling in the U.S. by 2030. Key goals include achieving an 85% recycling access rate and ensuring 90% of cans are labeled as recyclable with proper instructions. The initiative also seeks to include aerosols in state-wide Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) programs and educate Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) to overcome perceived fire risks, despite data showing such risks are rare when cans are emptied.

title: Kimberly-Clark Is on a Roll with New Forest Policy and Goals
summary: Kimberly-Clark, maker of Kleenex and Scott tissue products, has announced a new Forests, Land, and Agriculture Policy and a goal to eliminate natural forest fiber from its entire product line. This move sets a higher standard in the industry, aiming to reduce forest degradation, particularly in critical northern forests, and includes commitments to Indigenous communities' rights. The policy puts pressure on competitors like Procter & Gamble and aligns with increasing global regulatory scrutiny on deforestation and forest degradation.

title: P&G Exec Named Top Women in Grocery's CPG Trailblazer
summary: Mindy Sherwood, President of Global Walmart and Chief Sales Officer at Procter & Gamble (P&G), has been recognized as a CPG Trailblazer for Top Women in Grocery. The article highlights her 35-year career at P&G, her leadership philosophy focusing on empowering team members, and her insights on overcoming challenges faced by women in male-dominated industries. Sherwood also shares advice for young professionals starting their careers, emphasizing curiosity, continuous learning, and making a significant impact.

title: Bloomberg: Western Multinationals Fleeing Nigeria Being Replaced by Asian, Turkish Firms
summary: Western multinationals are exiting Nigeria due to economic challenges like currency fluctuations, high inflation, and economic mismanagement, but Asian and local firms are stepping in to fill the void. Companies like Tolaram Group Inc. are succeeding by localizing production and sourcing materials within Nigeria to mitigate currency risks. Despite ongoing difficulties, this shift is creating opportunities for domestic manufacturing and exports to other African countries.

title: Consumer Reports finds unclear ingredients in seven brands of baby wipes
